G0576.d: ἀπο-βαίνω to step off, disembark: Luk.5:2, Jhn.21:9; metaphorically, of events, to issue, turn out (Field, Notes, 74): Luk.21:13, Php.1:19 (MM, see word).† (AS)

G0577.d: ἀπο-βάλλω to throw off: Mrk.10:50; metaphorically, to lose, let go (Field, Notes, 231 f.; MM, see word): Heb.10:35.† (AS)

G0578.d: ἀπο-βλέπω to look away from all else at one object; hence, to look steadfastly: Heb.11:26 (cf. ἀφοράω).† (AS)

G0579.d: ἀπό-βλητος, -ον (ἀποβάλλω), [in Aq.: Lev.7:18, al.; Sm.: Hos.9:3 (טָמֵא) ;] to be thrown away, rejected: 1Ti.4:4 (Hom., Plut.).† (AS)

G0580.d: ἀπο-βολή, -ῆς, ἡ (ἀποβάλλω); __1. a throwing away, rejection: opposite to πρόσλημψις, Rom.11:15. __2. a losing, loss: Act.27:22.† (AS)

G0581.d: ἀπο-γίνομαι (cl. -γίγν-) __1. to be away, removed from. __2. to depart life, to die (MM, see word): τ. ἀμαρτίαις, i.e. with ref. to sins, 1Pe.2:24 (Cremer, 149, 668).† (AS)

G0582.d: ἀπο-γραφή, -ῆς, ἡ (ἀπογράφω) __1. a written copy. __2. As law term, a deposition (Demos.). __3. In late writers, a register, enrolment, census (MM, see word; Deiss., LAE, 160, 268 f.): Luk.2:2, Act.5:37.† (AS)

G0583.d: ἀπο-γράφω __1. to write out, copy. __2. to enrol; mid., to enrol oneself: Luk.2:1 (M, Pr., 162; but. see ICC, in l), Luk.2:3, 5; pass., Heb.12:23 (see reff, see word ἀπογραφή ).† (AS)

G0584.d: ἀπο-δείκνυμι __1. to bring out, show forth, exhibit (Lft., Notes, 200; ICC, in l): 1Co.4:9. __2. to declare, show: Act.2:22 __3. to prove: Act.25:7. __4. As frequently in late Gk., to proclaim to an office: before ὅτι, 2Th.2:4 (Milligan, in l; MM, see word; Lft., Notes. 113.)† (AS)

G0585.d: ἀπό-δειξις, -εως, ἡ (ἀποδείκνυμι) __1. a showing off. __2. As used by Gk. philosophers, demonstration, certain proof: 1Co.2:4 (see ICC, in l; MM, see word; Lft., Notes, 173).† (AS)

G0586.d: ἀπο-δεκατοω, __1. with accusative of thing(s), to tithe, pay a tenth of: Mat.23:23, Luk.11:42. __2. C. accusative of person(s), to exact tithes from: Heb.7:5. __3. to decimate (Socr., HE, 573 A; see Kennedy, Sources, 117).† (AS)

G0588.d: ἀπο-δέχομαι to accept gladly, welcome, receive: Luk.8:40 9:11, Act.18:27 21:17 28:30; metaphorically, with accusative of thing(s), Act.2:41 24:3 (MM, see word; Cremer, 688).† (AS)

G0589.d: ἀπο-δημέω, -ῶ (ἀπόδημος), to be or go abroad (M, Pr., 130, 2): Mat.21:33 25:14-15, Mrk.12:1, Luk.15:13 20:9.† (AS)

G0590.d: ἀπό-δημος, -ον gone abroad (RV, sojourning in another country): Mrk.13:34.† (AS)

G0591.d: ἀπο-δίδωμι to give up or back, restore, return: Mat.27:58, Luk.4:20 9:42 19:8; esp. of wages, debts, oaths, etc. (MM, see word), to render what is due, to pay (Deiss., LAE, 334 f.): absol., Mat.18:25, 28, Luk.7:42. with accusative, Mat.5:26 18:29-30, 34 20:8 21:41 22:21, Mrk.12:17, Luk.10:35 12:59 20:25, Rom.13:7, Heb.12:11, Rev.22:2; ὅρκους, Mat.5:33 (cf. Num.30:3, Deu.23:21 al.); of conjugal…

G0592.d: ἀπο-δι-ορίζω (διορίζω, ἅρος, a limit), to mark off, hence metaphorically to make separations: Ju 19 (Cremer, 806).† (AS)

G0593.d: ἀπο-δοκιμάζω to reject: Mat.21:42 (LXX), Mrk.8:31 12:10" (LXX) Luk.9:22 17:25 20:17" (LXX), Heb.12:17, 1Pe.2:4 2:7" (LXX) (Cremer, 701; MM, see word).† (AS)

G0594.d: ἀπο-δοχή, -ῆς, ἡ (ἀποδέχομαι), acceptance, approbation (Field, Notes, 203): 1Ti.1:15 4:9 (Cremer, 686; MM, see word).† (AS)

G0596.d: ἀπο-θήκη, -ης, ἡ (ἀποτίθημι), a storehouse, granary: Mat.3:12 6:26 13:30, Luk.3:17 12:18, 24.† (AS)

G0597.d: ἀπο-θησαυρίζω to treasure up, store away: 1Ti.6:19.† (AS)

G0599.d: ἀπο-θνῄσκω, to die: of natural death, Mrk.5:35, al.; of violent death (pass. of ἀποκτείνω), esp. of Christ, Mat.26:35, Jhn.12:33, Heb.10:28, al.; of spiritual death, Jhn.6:50, Rom.8:13, al.; with dative ref., Rom.6:2, 10 14:7, 8, Gal.2:19; accusative, ὅ, Rom.6:10; before ἐν, Mat.8:32, Jhn.8:21, 24 1Co.15:22, Heb.11:37, Rev.14:13; before ὑπέρ, περί, Jhn.11:50, 51 18:14, Rom.5:6-8 14:15, 1Co.15:3,…

G0600.d: ἀπο-καθ-ίστημι (ἀποκαθιστάω, Mrk.9:12, Rec., -ιστάνω, LTTr.; cf. Act.1:6; -κατιστάνω, WH), __1. to restore, i.e. to a former condition: of health, Mat.12:13, Mrk.3:5 8:25, Luk.6:10; of social or political affairs, Mat.17:11, Mrk.9:12, Act.1:6. __2. to give back, bring back: Heb.13:19 (so in π., MM, see word; cf. also Cremer, 312).† (AS)

G0601.d: ἀπο-καλύπτω __1. in general sense (cl.), to reveal, uncover, disclose, __(a) of things: Mat.10:26, Luk.2:35 12:2, 1Co.3:13; __(b) of persons: pass., Christ, Luk.17:30; Antichrist, 2Th.2:3 2:6 2:8 __2. In LXX and NT, in special sense of divine revelation: Mat.11:25 (on the tense, see M, Pr., 136), ib. Mat.11:27 16:17, Luk.10:21-22, Jhn.12:38, Rom.1:17-18 8:18, 1Co.2:10 14:30, Gal.1:16 3:23,…

G0602.d: ἀπο-κάλυψις, -εως, ἡ (ἀποκαλύπτω), an uncovering, laying bare (Plut.). Metaphorical, a reveal­ing, revelation: a disclosure of divine truth, or a manifestion from God: Luk.2:32 Rom.2:5 8:19 16:25, 1Co.1:7 14:6 14:26, 2Co.12:1 12:7, Gal.1:12 2:2, Eph.1:17 3:3 2Th.1:7 1Pe.1:7 1:13 4:13, Rev.1:1.† SYN.: ἐπιφάνεια, παρουσία, φανέρωσις (see Tr., Syn., xciv; Lft., Notes, 102, 178; Westc, Eph., 178 f.;…

G0603.d: ἀπο-καραδοκία, -ας, ἡ (ἀποκαραδοκέω, used by Aq. in Psa.37:7 for חוּל; ἀπό, κάρα the head, δοκέω, in Ion., to watch), to watch with outstretched head, watch anxiously (Polyb., π.; see Deiss., LAE, 374.5, 377 f.), Rom.8:19, Php.1:20 (Lft., in l; Cremer, 177).† (AS)

G0604.d: ἀπο-κατ-αλλάσσω (cf. καταλλάσσω: ἀπό here signifies completely, see Lft., Col., l.with; Ellic., Eph., l.with; but also Mey., Eph., l.with), to reconcile completely: Eph.2:16, Col.1:20-21.† (AS)

G0605.d: ἀπο-κατά-στασις, -εως, ἡ (ἀποκαθίστημι), restoration: Act.3:21 (in τ. of repairs and restorations of temples, see MM, see word).† (AS)

G0606.d: ἀπό-κειμαι to be laid up, in store, laid away: Luk.19:20. Metaphorical, C. dative of person(s), to be reserved (Dem., Plat.; and see MM, see word): Col.1:5, 2Ti.4:8, Heb.9:27.† (AS)

G0607.d: ἀπο-κεφαλίζω (ἀπό, κεφαλή), to behead: Mat.14:10, Mrk.6:16, 28 Luk.9:9.† (AS)

G0609.d: ἀπο-κόπτω to cut off: Mrk.9:43, 45, Jhn.18:10, 26 Act.27:32. Mid., to mutilate oneself, have oneself mutilated: Gal.5:12 (cf. Deu.23:1 LXX; and see Cremer, 751; MM, see word).† (AS)

G0610.d: ἀπό-κριμα, -τος, τό (ἀποκρίνω); __1. prop., a judicial sentence: 2Co.1:9, R, mg. __2. an answer (see Thayer, see word): 2Co.1:9, R, txt. (In FlJ, Ant., xiv, 10, 6, of a rescript of the Senate; in Inscr. of an official decision, Deiss., BS, 257; a reply to a deputation, MM, see word: cf. also Cremer, 3'75).† (AS)

G0611.d: ἀποκρίνω, ἀποκρίνομαι, in cl., __1. to separate, distinguish. __2. to choose. Mid., to answer: Mat.27:12, Mrk.14:61, Luk.3:16 23:9, Jhn.5:17, 19 Act.3:12. In late Gk. the pass, also is used in this sense, and pass. forms are the more frequently in NT (M, Pr., 39, 161; MM, see word); __(a) in general sense: absol., Mrk.12:34; with accusative of thing(s), Mat.22:46; with dative of person(s),…

G0612.d: ἀπό-κρισις, -εως, ἡ (ἀποκρίνομαι), an answering, an answer: Luk.2:47 20:26, Jhn.1:22 19:9.† (AS)

G0613.d: ἀπο-κρύπτω to hide, conceal, keep secret: with accusative, Luk.10:21; pass., 1Co.2:7, Eph.3:9, Col.1:26 (MM, see word).† (AS)

G0614.d: ἀπόκρυφος, -ον (ἀποκρύπτω), hidden: Mrk.4:22, Luk.8:17, Col.2:3 (see Lft., in l; MM, see word).† (AS)

G0615.d: ἀπο-κτείνω (also in late forms -κτέννω, Mat.10:28, a1., LTTr., -κτεννύω, Mrk.12:5, WH), to kill: Mat.14:5, al.; before instr. ἐν (which see), Eph.2:16, Rev.2:23, al. Metaphorical: Rom.7:11; τ. ἔχθραν, Eph.2:16; τὸ γράμμα ἀποκτείνει 2Co.3:6 (on the perfective force of this verb, see M, Pr., 114) (AS)

G0616.d: ἀπο-κυέω (Rec. -κύω), -ῶ (ἀπό, κυέω or κύω, to be pregnant), prop., "the medical word for birth as the close of pregnancy" (Hort, Ja., 26 f.). In κοιν, "an ordinary syn. of τίκτω, but definitely 'perfectivised' (M, Pr., 111 ff.; MM, see word) by the ἀπό, and so implying safe delivery," to bring forth, give birth to: Jas.1:15, 18.† (AS)

G0617.d: ἀπο-κυλίω (see: κυλίω), to roll away: Mat.28:2, Mrk.16:3, Luk.24:2.† (AS)

G0618.d: ἀπο-λαμβάνω __1. to receive from another; absol., to receive as one's due: Luk.16:25 18:30 (seel. λάβῃ) Luk.23:41, Rom.1:27, Gal.4:5, Col.3:24, 2Jn.8. __2. to receive back: Luk.6:34 15:27. __3. to take apart or aside: Mrk.7:33 (cf. use in π. of the recluses of the Serapeum; MM, see word).† (AS)

G0619.d: ἀπόλαυσις, -εως, ἡ (ἀπολαύω, to take of, enjoy a thing) enjoyment: 1Ti.6:17, Heb.11:26 (for late exx., see MM, see word).† (AS)

G0620.d: ἀπο-λείπω __1. to leave, leave behind (in π. a term. techn. in wills; see MM, see word): 2Ti.4:13 4:20, Tit.1:5; pass., to be reserved, remain: Heb.4:6, 9 10:26. __2. to desert, abandon: Ju 6.† (AS)

G0621.d: ἀπο-λείχω (for ἐπιλ-, which see), to lick up: Luk.16:21, Rec.† (AS)

G0622.d: ἀπ-όλλυμι and ἀπολλύω . __1. Act., __1 to destroy utterly, destroy, kill: Mk 124, 922, al.; τ. ψνχήν, Mat.10:28, al.; __2 to lose utterly: Mat.10:42, al.; metaphorically, of failing to save, Jhn.6:39 18:9. __2. Mid., __1 to perish; __(a) of things: Mat.5:29, Jhn.6:12, Heb.1:11 (LXX, al.; __(b) of persons: Mat.8:26, al. Metaphorical, of loss of eternal life, Jhn.3:15-16 10:28 17:12, Rom.2:12,…

G0623.d: Ἀπολλύων, -οντος, ὁ (present ptcp. of ἀπολλύω), Apollyon, i.e. the Destroyer: Rev.9:11 (cf. Ἀβάδδων). (Cremer, 453; DB, i, 125, 172.) † (AS)

G0624.d: Ἀπολλωνία, -ας, ἡ Apollonia, a city of Macedonia: Act.17:1.† (AS)

G0625.d: Ἀπολλώς, -ώ, ὁ (perh. contr. from Ἀπολλώνιος, Act.18:24 D) Apollos: Act.18:24 19:1, 1Co.1:12 3:4-6 3:22 4:6 16:12, Tit.3:13.† (AS)

G0626.d: ἀπολογέομαι, -οῦμαι (ἀπό, λόγος), __1. to defend: with accusative, Rom.2:15. __2. to defend one's self: absol., Luk.21:14, Act.26:1; before ὅτι, Act.25:8; τί, to adduce something in one's defence, Luk.12:11, Act.26:24 (ταῦτα) Act.24:10 (τὰ περὶ ἐμαυτοῦ); περί, with genitive of thing(s), and ἐπί, with genitive of person(s), Act.26:2; with dative of person(s), Act.19:33, 2Co.12:19.† (AS)

G0627.d: ἀπολογία, -ας, ἡ (ἀπολογέομαι), a speech in defence: Act.25:16, 2Co.7:11, Php.1:7, 16, 2Ti.4:16; with dative of person(s), 1Co.9:3, 1Pe.3:15; before πρός, Act.22:1.† (AS)

G0628.d: ἀπο-λούω to wash off, wash away; mid., metaphorically, with accusative of thing(s), to wash off oneself: ἀμαρτίας, Act.22:16; absol., ἀπελούσασθε, ye washed yourselves clean (cf. Cremer, 406), 1Co.6:11.† (AS)

G0629.d: ἀπο-λύτρωσις, -εως, ἡ (ἀπολυτρόω, to release on payment of ransom, cf. λύτρον), release effected by pay­ment of ransom, redemption, deliverance; metaphorically, Heb.11:35; of deliverance thr. Christ from evil and the consequences of sin: Luk.21:28, Rom.3:24 (Vau., in l) 8:23, 1Co.1:30, Eph.1:7, 14 4:30, Col.1:14, Heb.9:15. (On the extent to WH. the word retains the sense of ransom, see ICC,…

G0630.d: ἀπο-λύω __1. to set free, release: Luk.13:12, Jhn.19:10, al.; a debtor, Mat.18:27; metaphorically, of forgive­ness, Luk.6:37. __2. to let go, dismiss (Field, Notes, 9 f.): Mat.15:23, Luk.2:29 9:12, Act.19:41, al.; of divorce, τ. γυναῖκα: Mat.1:19 5:31-32 19:3, 8 19:10 Mrk.10:2, 4 10:11, Luk.16:18; with ref. to Gk. and Rom. (net Jewish) custom, τ. ἄνδρα: Mrk.10:12. Mid., to depart: Act.28:25 (MM,…

G0630G.d: ἀπο-λύω __1. to set free, release: Luk.13:12, Jhn.19:10, al.; a debtor, Mat.18:27; metaphorically, of forgive­ness, Luk.6:37. __2. to let go, dismiss (Field, Notes, 9 f.): Mat.15:23, Luk.2:29 9:12, Act.19:41, al.; of divorce, τ. γυναῖκα: Mat.1:19 5:31-32 19:3, 8 19:10 Mrk.10:2, 4 10:11, Luk.16:18; with ref. to Gk. and Rom. (net Jewish) custom, τ. ἄνδρα: Mrk.10:12. Mid., to depart: Act.28:25 (MM,…

G0630H.d: ἀπο-λύω __1. to set free, release: Luk.13:12, Jhn.19:10, al.; a debtor, Mat.18:27; metaphorically, of forgive­ness, Luk.6:37. __2. to let go, dismiss (Field, Notes, 9 f.): Mat.15:23, Luk.2:29 9:12, Act.19:41, al.; of divorce, τ. γυναῖκα: Mat.1:19 5:31-32 19:3, 8 19:10 Mrk.10:2, 4 10:11, Luk.16:18; with ref. to Gk. and Rom. (net Jewish) custom, τ. ἄνδρα: Mrk.10:12. Mid., to depart: Act.28:25 (MM,…

G0631.d: απο-μάσσω (μάσσω, Att... -ττω, to touch, handle), to wipe off, wire clean: mid., Luk.10:11.† (AS)

G0632.d: ἀπο-νέμω (νέμω, to distribute), to assign, apportion: 1Pe.3:7. (In π. of a Prefect who renders to all their dues; see MM, see word)† (AS)

G0633.d: ἀπο-νίπτω to wash off: mid. (reflex.), τ. χεῖρας, Mat.27:24.† (AS)

G0635.d: ἀπο-πλανάω, -ῶ to cause to go astray; metaphorically, of leading into error: Mrk.13:22; pass., to be led astray: 1Ti.6:10.† (AS)

G0637.d: ἀπο-πλύνω to wash off: seel. for πλύνω, Luk.5:2, Rec.† (AS)

G0638.d: ἀπο-πνίγω to choke: Mat.13:7, Luk.8:7; pass., of drowning (= καταποντίζομαι), Luk.8:33.† (AS)

G0639.d: ἀπορέω, -ῶ (ἄπορος, ἀ- neg., πόρος, a way, resource), to be at a loss, be perplexed: absol., Mrk.6:20 (ἐποίει, R, mg.); mid., be in doubt: absol., 2Co.4:8; with accusative, Act.25:20; before περί, Luk.24:4; ἐν, Gal.4:20; περὶ τίνος λέγει, Jhn.13:22.† SYN.: διαπορέω, διακρίνομαι, διστάζω, μετεωρίζομαι (see DCG, i, 491) (AS)

G0640.d: ἀπορία, -ας, ἡ (ἀπορέω), perplexity: Luk.21:25 (MM, see word; on the construction, see Field, Notes, 74 f.).† (AS)

G0641.d: ἀπο-ρίπτω (Rec. -ρρίπτω, c1.), to throw away, cast forth: reflexively, Act.27:43 (BV, cast themselves overboard; see MM, see word).† (AS)

G0642.d: ἀπ-ορφανίζω (ἀπό, ὀρφανός), to be bereaved (prop., of a parent, Lft., Notes, 36); metaphorically, 1Th.2:17 (where Field thinks it = χωρισθέντες, Notes, 199).† (AS)

G0643.d: ἀπο-σκευάζω to pack and carry off; mid., to pack and remove one's goods: Act.21:15, Rec. (see ἐπισ-).† ἐπι-σκευάζω, to equip, make ready; mid., to make one's preparations: Act.21:15.† (AS)

G0644.d: ἀπο-σκίασμα, -τος, τό (ἀποσκιάζω, to cast a shadow; v,s. σκία) a shadow: Jas.1:17 (MM, see word).† (AS)

G0645.d: ἀπο-σπάω, -ῶ to draw off or away, tear away (MM, see word): Act.20:30; μάχαιραν, draw a sword, Mat.26:51; pass., to be parted or withdrawn (Field, Notes, 134; but see Thayer, see word), Luk.22:41, Act.21:1.† (AS)

G0646.d: άποστασία, -ας, ἡ (ἀφίστημι), defection, apostasy, revolt; in late Gk. (MM, Exp., viii; Lft., Notes, 111; Cremer, 308) for cl. ἀπόστασις, frequently in sense of political revolt, in LXX (e.g. Jos.22:22, 2Ch.29:19, Jer.2:19) and NT always of religious apostasy: Act.21:21, 2Th.2:3.† (AS)

G0647.d: ἀποστάσιον, -ου, τό (ἀφίστημι), __1. in cl., only in phrase ἀποστασίου δίκη, an action against a freedman for forsaking his προστάτης (Dem.). __2. In LXX, βιβλίον ἀποστασίου, a bill of divorce: Mat.19:7, Mrk.10:4; in same sense ἀ. alone (MM, see word), Mat.5:31 (for other late exx., see MM, l.with; Kennedy, Sources, 121).† (AS)

G0648.d: ἀπο-στεγάζω (στέγη), [in Sm.: Jer.29:11 * ;] to unroof: Mrk.2:4.† (AS)

G0649.d: ἀπο-στέλλω, prop., to send away, to dispatch on service; __1. to send with a commission, or on service; __(a) of persons: Christ, Mat.10:40; the apostles, 10:16; servants, Mrk.12:2; angels, 13:27; __(b) of things: ὄνος, Mat.21:3; τὸ δρέπανον, Mrk.4:29; τ. λόγον, Act.10:36; τ. ἐπαγγελίαν (i.e. the promised Holy Spirit), Luk.24:49, Rec.; before εἰς, Mat.20:2, Luk.11:49, Jhn.3:17; ὀπίσω, Luk.19:14;…

G0650.d: ἀπο-στερέω, -ῶ (στερέω, to rob), to defraud, deprive of, despoil (in cl. chiefly of the misappropriation of trust funds, Field, Notes, 33; cf. MM, see word): absol., Mrk.10:19, 1Co.6:8; with accusative of person(s), 1Co.7:5. Mid., endure deprivation: 1Co.6:7 (WM, § 38, 3; but see Bl., § 54, 5; M, Pr., 162); pass., ἀπεστερημένοι, bereft of: 1Ti.6:5.† (AS)

G0651.d: ἀπο-στολή, -ῆς, ἡ (ἀποστέλλω), __1. In cl., a sending away (MM, see word), as, an expedition (Hdt.). __2. In LXX __(a) discharge, dis­missal (Ecc.8:8); __(b) a gift (3Ki.9:16, 1Ma.2:13). __3. In NT, the office of an Apostle of Christ, apostleship: Act.1:25, Rom.1:5, 1Co.9:2, Gal.2:8 (Cremer, 530).† (AS)

G0652.d: ἀπόστολος, -ου, ὁ (ἀοστέλλω), __1. a fleet, an expedition (Dem.). __2. a messenger, one sent on a mission (Hdt., LXX, l.with, and π.; see M, Pr., 37 f.; MM, see word; M, Th., i, 2:7 and reff.): Jhn.13:16, 2Co.8:23 Php.2:25. __3. In NT, an Apostle of Christ __(a) with special ref. to the Twelve: Mat.10:2, Mrk.3:14, Luk.11:49, Eph.3:5, Rev.18:20, al., equality with whom is claimed by St. Paul,…

G0653.d: ἀποστοματίζω (στόμα), __1. In cl., to speak from memory, to dic­tate to a pupil (Plat.). __2. In late Gk., to catechize, question: Luk.11:53 (MM, see word).† (AS)

G0654.d: ἀπο-στρέφω trans., with accusative, __(a) to turn away, remove: Rom.11:26, 2Ti.4:4; metaphorically, to turn away from allegiance, pervert: Luk.23:14; __(b) to turn back, return: μάχαιραν, Mat.26:52. Pass., reflex., to turn oneself away from: with accusative, Mat.5:42, 2Ti.1:15, Tit.1:14, Heb.12:25; so act., absol., Act.3:26 (cf. Sir.8:5; Bl., § 53, 1; Cremer, 880).† (AS)

G0655.d: ἀπο-στυγέω, -ῶ (στυγέω, to hate), to abhor: Rom.12:9.† (AS)

G0656.d: ἀποσυνάγωγος, -ον (συναγωγή), expelled from the congregation (Field, Notes, 96), excommunicated: Jhn.9:22 12:42 16:2 (Cremer, 64, 607).† (AS)

G0657.d: ἀπο-τάσσω to set apart. Mid., in late Gk. (El., § 37, 1; Swete, Mk., 136 f.; MM, e. dative, __(a) to take leave of: Mrk.6:46, Luk.9:61, Act.18:18, 21, 2Co.2:13; __(b) to forsake: Luk.14:33.† (AS)

G0658.d: ἀπο-τελέω, -ῶ to bring to an end, complete, accomplish (cf. MM, see word): Luk.13:32, Jas.1:15.† (AS)

G0659.d: ἀπο-τίθημι to put off or aside; in NT always mid., __(a) to put of from oneself as a garment: τ. ἱμάτια, Act.7:58; metaphorically, in ethical sense, to put of, lay aside: Rom.13:12, Eph.4:22, 25, Col.3:8, Heb.12:1, Jas.1:21, 1Pe.2:1; __(b) to stow away, put: ἐν τ. φυλακῇ (MM, see word), Mat.14:3.† (AS)

G0660.d: ἀπο-τινάσσω to shake of: Luk.9:5, Act.28:5.† (AS)

G0661.d: ἀπο-τίνω (or -τίω) to pay off, repay: Phm 19 (MM, see word).† (AS)

G0662.d: ἀπο-τολμάω, -ῶ to be quite bold, make a bold venture: Rom.10:20.† (AS)

G0663.d: ἀποτομία, -ας, ἡ (ἀποτέμνω, to cut of), [in Sm.: Jer.51:35, Nam.3:1 * ;] steepness, sharpness; metaphorically, severity (MM, see word): Rom.11:22.† (AS)

G0664.d: ἀποτόμως adv., abruptly, curtly, hence sharply, severely: 2Co.13:10, Tit.1:13 (MM, see word).† (AS)

G0665.d: ἀπο-τρέπω to turn away; mid., to turn oneself away from: with accusative, 2Ti.3:5.† (AS)

G0666.d: ἀπουσία, -ας, ἡ (ἄπειμι); __1. absence (Æsch., Thuc.): Php.2:12, __2. deficiency, waste (MM, s.v).† (AS)

G0667.d: ἀπο-φέρω to carry off, bear, or lead away: with accusative, Mrk.15:1, 1Co.16:3, Rev.17:3 21:10. Pass., Luk.16:22, Act.19:12.† (AS)

G0668.d: ἀπο-φεύγω to flee from, escape: with accusative, 2Pe.2:18 2:20; with genitive, 2Pe.1:4.† (AS)

G0669.d: ἀπο-φθέγγομαι to speak forth, give utterance: Act.2:4, 14 26:25 (MM, s. see).† (AS)

G0670.d: ἀπο-φορτίζομαι (φορτίζω, to load), to discharge a cargo (Field, Notes, 134), to unlade: with accusative, τ. γόμον, Act.21:3.† (AS)

G0671.d: ἀπό-χρησις, -εως, ἡ (ἀποχράομαι, to use to the full, abuse) abuse, misuse: Col.2:22 (MM, see word).† (AS)

G0672.d: ἀπο-χωρέω, -ῶ to go away, depart, withdraw: before ἀπό, Mat.7:23, Luk.9:39, Act.13:13 (absol., Luk.20:20, Tr., mg.).† (AS)

G0673.d: ἀπο-χωρίζω to separate, part asunder: pass., Rev.6:14; reflexively, to separate oneself: Act.15:39.† (AS)

G0674.d: ἀπο-ψύχω __1. to breathe out life, expire (Thue.; LXX, l.with). __2. to leave off breathing, faint (Hom., Od., xxiv, 348): before ἀπό, Luk.21:26.† (AS)

G0675.d: Ἀππιος, -ου, ὁ Appius; Ἀππίου Φόρον, Appii Forum (Market of Appius), a town in Italy: Act.28:15.† (AS)

G0676.d: ἀ-πρόσ-ιτος, -ον (πρόσειμι, to go to), unapproachable: φῶς, 1Ti.6:16.† (AS)

G0677.d: ἀπρόσκοπος, -ον (προσκόπτω), __1. act., not causing to stumble: metaphorically, of not leading others into sin, 1Co.10:32. __2. Pass., not stumbling, without offence, blameless: Act.24:16, Php.1:10 (for exx., see MM, see word).† (AS)

G0678.d: ἀπροσωπολήμπτως (Rec. -λήπτως, cl.), adv. (α- neg., προσωπολήμπτης), without respect of persons, impartially: 1Pe.1:17.† (AS)

G0679.d: ἄ-πταιστος, -ον (πταίω), without stumbling, sure-footed: metaphorically (MM, see word), Ju 24.† (AS)

G0681.d: ἅπτω prop., to fasten to; hence, of fire, to kindle, light: Luk.8:16 11:33 15:8, Act.28:2. Mid., with genitive, to fasten oneself to, cling to, lay hold of (so in π.; MM, see word): Mat.8:3, 15, Jhn.20:17, al.; of carnal intercourse, 1Co.7:1; with reference to levitical and ceremonial prohibitions, 2Co.6:17, Col.2:21; of hostile action, 1Jn.5:18 (cf. ἀν-, καθ-, περι- άπτω) SYN.: θιγγάνω, ψηλαφάω.…

G0682.d: Ἀπφία, -ας, ἡ Apphia: Phm 2 (MM, see word).† (AS)

G0683.d: ἀπ-ωθέω, -ῶ to thrust away. Mid., to thrust away from oneself, refuse, reject: with accusative of person(s) (MM, see word), Act.7:27, 39 13:46, Rom.11:1-2, 1Ti.1:19.† (AS)

G0684.d: ἀπώλεια, -ας, ἡ (ἀπόλλυμι), destruction, waste, loss, perishing (in π., of money, see MM, see word): Mat.26:8, Mrk.14:4, Act.8:20, Rom.9:22, 1Ti.6:9, 2Pe.2:1; in special sense of the loss of eternal life, perdition, the antithesis of σωτηρία: Mat.7:13, Jhn.17:12, Php.1:28 3:19, 2Th.2:3, Heb.10:39, 2Pe.2:3 3:7 3:16, Rev.17:8, 11 (DB, iii, 744).† (AS)

G0685.d: ἀρά, -ᾶς, ἡ ; __1. a prayer (MM, see word). __2. (as in Homer) a curse, malediction: Rom.3:14 (LXX),† (AS)

G0686.d: ἄρα, illative particle, expressing a more subjective or informal inference than οὖν, then: prop. (as in cl.), the second word in the sentence, Rom.7:21 8:1, Gal.3:7; ἐπεὶ ἄρα, 1Co.7:14 (with another word between) 5:10; as the first word, Luk.11:48, Act.11:18, Rom.10:17, 1Co.15:18, 2Co.5:15 7:12, Heb.4:9; so prop. in apodosis after protasis with εἰ, Mat.12:28, Luk.11:20, Gal.2:21 3:29 5:11,…

G0687.d: ἆρα, interrog. particle, implying anxiety or impatience, "quite rare and only in Luke and Paul, therefore a literary word" (Bl., §77, 2). __1. (num igitur) expecting a neg. reply, Luk.18:8; ἆρά γε, Act.8:30. __2. (ergone) in apodosis, expecting an affirm. reply, Gal.2:17 (Bl., l.with; Lft., Ga., in l.; MM, see word). † (AS)

G0688.d: Arabia , (Herdotus Historicus), poetry Ἀρραβία, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G0689.d: Ἀράμ indec. (Heb. רָם), Aram: Mat.1:3-4, Luk.3:33 (R, txt., WH, Ἀρνεί).† (AS)

G0691.d: ἀργέω, -ῶ (ἀργός), to be idle; τὸ κρίμα . . . ἀ., lingers (cf. MGr. ἀργά, late: MM, see word): 2Pe.2:3.† (AS)

G0692.d: ἀργός, -όν (in late Gk., incl. NT, -ή, -όν; ἀ- neg., ἔργον) inactive, idle: Mat.20:3, 6, 1Ti.5:13, Tit.1:12, 2Pe.1:8. Metaphorical, of things, inactive, ineffective, worthless: ῥῆμα, Mat.12:36; πίστις, Jas.2:20 (see Cremer, 259 f.).† SYN.: βραδύς, slow; νωθρός, sluggish (Tr., Syn., § civ) (AS)

G0693.d: ἀργύρεος (see MM, see word), -οῦς, -ᾶ, -οῦν (ἄργυρος), of silver: Act.19:24 (WH, br.), 2Ti.2:20, Rev.9:20.† (AS)

G0694.d: ἀργύριον, -ου, τό (ἄργυρος), prop., a piece of silver (Lft., Notes, 191); in NT, __(a) silver: Act.3:6 7:16 19:19 20:33, 1Co.3:12, 1Pe.1:18; __(b) money: Mat.25:18, 27, Mrk.14:11, Luk.9:3 19:15, 23 22:5, Act.8:20; __(with) a silver coin: p1., Mat.26:15 27:3-6, 9 28:12, 15, where the value is that of a shekel or tetradrachm; ἀργυρίου μυριάδες πέντε (prob. drachmas; MM, see word), Act.19:19.† (AS)

G0695.d: ἀργυροκόπος, -ου, ὁ (ἄργυρος, κόπτω, to beat) a silversmith: Act.19:24 (Plut.; 77., see MM, see word).† (AS)

G0696.d: ἄργυρος, -ου, ὁ (ἀργός, shining), silver (on its relation to ἀργύριον, see MM, see word): Mat.10:9, Act.17:29, Jas.5:5, Rev.18:12.† (AS)

G0697.d: Ἄρειος Πάυος (T, Ἄριος Π.), -ου, ὁ Hill of Pres or Mars, Areopagus; also, the Court of Areopagus, the highest tribunal of Athens: Act.17:19, 22.† (AS)

G0698.d: Ἀρεοπαγίτης (T, -είτης), -ου, ὁ (see supr.), a judge of the Court of Areopagus: Act.17:34.† (AS)

G0699.d: ἀρεσκία (Rec. -εία), -ας, ἡ (ἀρέσκω), pleasing, desire to please: Col.1:19 In Gk. writers (Arist., Polyb.), most frequently in bad sense, but in π., Inscr., and in Philo, as above (see Deiss., BS, 224; MM, see word; Cremer, 642).† (AS)

G0700.d: ἀρέσκω __1. to please (Hom., Hdt., al.): with dative of person(s), Mat.14:6, Mrk.6:22, Rom.8:8 15:2, 1Th.2:15 4:1, 1Co.7:32-34 Gal.1:10, 2Ti.2:4; before ἐνώπισν (= Heb. בּעֵנֵי, Bl., § 37, 1; 40, 7), Ac 65. __2. In late Gk., esp. in Inscr., to render service to (see M, Th., ICC, 1 Co., ll with; Cremer, 640 f.); Rom.15:1, 3, 1Co.10:33, 1Th.2:4.† (AS)

G0701.d: ἀρεστός, -ή, -όν (ἀρέσκω), pleasing, agreeable (Hdt., Xen., and later writers; see Cremer, 641 f; MM, see word): with dative of person(s), Jhn.8:29, Act.12:3; before ἐνώπιον, with genitive (Bl., § 37, 1; 40, 7), 1Jn.3:22; ἀρεστόν ἐστιν, with accusative and inf (El., § 69, 5; 72, 5), Act.6:2.† (AS)

G0702.d: Ἀρέτας (WH, Ἀρ.; Intr., 313), -α, ὁ, Aretas, an Arabian king: 2Co.11:32 (Deiss., BS, 183 f., thinks the proper spelling Ἀρέθας was changed, as Schürer suggests, "by desire to Hellenise a barbaric name by assimilation to ἀρετή").† (AS)

G0703.d: ἀρετή, -ῆς, ἡ prop., whatever procures pre-eminent estimation for a person or thing, in Hom. any kind of conspicuous advantage. Later confined by philos. writers to intrinsic eminence-moral goodness, virtue; __(a) of God: 2Pe.1:3; __(b) of men: Php.4:8, 2Pe.1:5; pl. (Isa, Es, ll. with), excellencies: 1Pe.2:9 (the usage appears to be a survival of an early comprehensive sense in which the original…

G0704.d: ἀρήν, ἀρνός, ὁ (nom, not in use, exc. in early times: see MM, see word), a lamb: Luk.10:3.† (AS)

G0705.d: ἀριθμέω, -ῶ to number (esp. for payment, MM, see word): Mat.10:30, Luk.12:7, Rev.7:9.† (AS)

G0706.d: ἀριθμός, -οῦ, ὁ number, a number: Luk.22:3, Jhn.6:10, Act.4:4 5:36 6:7 11:21 16:5, Rom.9:27, Rev.5:11 7:4 9:16 13:17-18 15:2 20:8 (for exx. of mystical use in π., see MM, see word).† (AS)

G0707.d: Ἁριμαθεία (WH, Ἁρ.), -ας, ἡ Arimathæa: Mat.27:57, Mrk.15:43, Luk.23:51, Jhn.19:38.† (AS)

G0708.d: Ἀρίσταρχος, -ου, ὁ (ἄριστος, ἀρχός; i.e. best-ruling) Aristarchus: Act.19:29 20:4 27:2, Col.4:10, Phm 24 (AS)

G0709.d: ἀριστάω, -ῶ (ἄριστον), __1. prop., to breakfast: Jhn.21:12, 15 __2. In late Gk., to take a meal, dine: Luk.11:37.† (AS)

G0710.d: ἀριστερός, -ά, -όν left, on the left: ὅπλα, 2Co.6:7; ἡ ἀ.. (sc. χείρ), Mat.6:3; ἐξ ἀριστερῶν, on the left (MM, see word ): Mrk.10:37, Luk.23:33.† (AS)

G0711.d: Ἀριστόβουλος, -ου, ὁ (ἄριστος, βουλή, i.e. best-counselling) Aristobulus, a Christian: Rom.16:10.† (AS)

G0712.d: ἄριστον, -ου, τό __1 1, prop., breakfast. __2. In late Gk. = cl. δεῖτνον, dinner: Mat.22:4, Luk.11:38 14:12.† (AS)

G0713.d: ἀρκετός, -ή, -όν (ἀρκέω), [in Aq.: Deu.25:2 * ;] sufficient: Mat.6:34 (on the neut., see B1., § 31, 2); before ἵνα (M, Pr., 210), Mat.10:25; with inf., 1Pe.4:3 (for exx., see Deiss., BS, 257; MM, see word).† (AS)

G0714.d: ἀρκέω, -ῶ __1. to keep off; with dative, to assist. __2. to suffice: with dative of person(s), Jo 67, 2Co.12:9; impers., Mat.25:9, Jhn.14:8 (MM, see word). Pass., to be satisfied: with dative of thing(s), Luk.3:14, 1Ti.6:8, Heb.13:5; before ἐπί, III Jn 10.† (AS)

G0715.d: ἅρκος (Rec. (cl.) ἅρκιος), -ου, ὁ, ἡ, a bear: Rev.13:2. (This form is also found in late Inscr.; MM, see word)† (AS)

G0716.d: ἅρμα, -τος, τό (ἀραρίσκω, to join), a chariot: Act.8:28-29, 38, Rev.9:9.† (AS)

G0717.d: Ἁρμαγεδών (WH, Ἃρ Μαγεδών; Rec. Ἀρμαγεδδών, prop. = הַר מְגִדּוֹן), cf. LXX, Μαγεδών, 2Ch.35:22, Μαγεδώ, Jdg.1:27; Har-Magedon (AV, Armageddon): Rev.16:16 (see Swete, in l, but also Thayer, see word).† Ἅρ, indecl., Rev.16:16, see, Ἁρμαγεδών Μαγεδών, Magedon: Rev.16:16 (WH, Ἅρ M. for Ἁρμαγεδών, which see).† (AS)

G0718.d: ἁρμόζω (ἁρμός), __1. to fit, join. __2. of marriage, to betroth. Mid., __(a) to join to oneself, marry, take to wife; (b) to give in marriage: 2Co.11:2 (for this there is no direct parallel. But see M, Pr., 160; MM, see word).† (AS)

G0719.d: ἁρμός, -ου, ὁ a joining, joint: Heb.4:12.† (AS)

G0720.d: ἀρνέομαι -οῦμαι, depon., __1. to deny, say no, opposite to είπεῖν: absol., Mat.26:70, Luk.8:45; before ἅτι, 1Jn.2:22; with inf., Heb.11:24 __2. In late Gk. (MM, see word), with accusative of person(s), to deny, refuse to acknowledge, disown: Act.3:14 7:35; Ἰησοῦν, Mat.10:33, 2Ti.2:12, 1Jn.2:22, Ju 4; ἑαυτόν, Luk.9:23, 2Ti.2:13 (prove false to) __3. C. accusative of thing(s) (in cl. to refuse), to…

G0721.d: ἀρνίον, -ου, τό (dimin. of ἀρήν; see MM, see word), a little lamb, a lamb: Jhn.21:15, Rev.2:7.† (AS)

G0722.d: ἀροτριάω, -ῶ (ἄροτρον), later form of ἀρόω, to plough (MM, see word): Luk.17:7, 1Co.9:10.† (AS)

G0723.d: ἄροτρον, -ου, τό (ἀρόω, to plough), a plough: Luk.9:62.† (AS)

G0724.d: ἁρπαγή, -ῆς, ἡ (ἁρπάζω), pillage, plundering, robbery: Mat.23:25, Luk.11:39, Heb.10:34.† (AS)

G0725.d: ἁρπαγμός, οῦ, ὁ (ἁρπάζω); __1. prop., accusative, to the rule of its formation (Bl., § 27, 2), actively, the act of seizing, robbery (Plut., Deu Puer. Educ., p. 12A), Php.2:6, AV (Waterland, Works, II, 108; Cremer, 649 f.; Meyer, in l; cf. also JThS, July, 1909, April, 1911; MM, see word). __2. Passively = ἅρπαγμα (Eze.22:25, of a lion's prey, ), a thing seized, hence, a prize: Phi, l.with, RV…

G0726.d: ἁρπάζω to seize, catch up, snatch away, carry off by force: with accusative of thing(s), Mat.12:29 13:19, Jhn.10:12, 28-29; τ. βασιλείαν τ. θεοῦ, Mat.11:12; with accusative of person(s), Jhn.6:15, Act.8:39 23:10, Ju 23; pass., before ἕως, 2Co.12:2; εἰς, 2Co.12:4, 1Th.4:17; πρός, Rev.12:5 (cf. δι-, συν-αρπάζω, and see MM, see word).† (AS)

G0727.d: ἅρπαξ, -αγος, ὁ, ἡ (ἁρπάζω), rapacious: Mat.7:15, Luk.18:11; as subst., a swindler, an extortioner (MM, see word), 1Co.5:10-11 6:10.† (AS)

G0728.d: ἀρραβών (T, ἀραβ-: 2Co, ll. with), -ώνος, ὁ, an earnest, part payment in advance for security, a first instalment: 2Co.1:22 5:5, Eph.1:14. (The word is found in cl. and was prob. brought to Greece by the Phænicians (AR, Eph., l.with). It is found in π. with both spellings (see Milligan, NTD, 73). In MGr. ἀρραβῶνα is an engagement ring; see MM, see word)† (AS)

G0729.d: ἄραφος, -ον (Rec. ἄρραφο), (ῥάπτω, to sew) without seam: Jhn.19:23.† (AS)

G0730.d: ἄρσην (ἄρρην, T, in Rom.1:27; Rec. in Rev.12:5, 13) -ενος, ὁ, ἡ, ἄρσεν, τό (old Attic for ἄρρην, see supr.; both forms are found in π.; MM, see word), male: Mat.19:4, Mrk.10:6, Luk.2:23, Rom.1:27, Gal.3:28, Rev.12:5, 13.† (AS)

G0731.d: ἄρρητος, -ον (ἀ- neg., ῥητός, ῥέω), [in Sm.: Lev.18:23 * ;] __1. unspoken (Hom., al.). __2. unspeakable (Hat., al.; frequently in Inscr.; MM, see word): 2Co.12:4.† (AS)

G0732.d: ἄρρωστος, -ον (ἀ- neg., ῥώννυμι), feeble, sickly: Mat.14:14, Mrk.6:5, 13 16:18, 1Co.11:30.† (AS)

G0735.d: Ἄρτεμις, -ιδος, ἡ Artemis, an Asiatic goddess, to be disting. from the Gk. goddess of the same name: Act.19:24, 27-28 (AS)

G0736.d: ἀρτέμων, -ωνος (Rec. -ονος), ὁ (ἀρτάω, to fasten to), a fore-sail or top-sail: Act.27:40 (see DB, ext., 366b, 399a; MM, see word).† (AS)

G0737.d: ἄρτι adv., adv., of coincidence, denoting strictly present time, as contrasted with past or future, just, just now, this moment: Mat.3:15 9:18 26:53, Jhn.13:7, Gal.4:20, 1Th.3:6 (see Lft., Notes, 44; Milligan, in l), Rev.12:10; opposite to past time, Jhn.9:19, 25 13:33, 1Co.16:7, Gal.1:9-10; to future, Jhn.13:37 16:12, 31, 1Co.13:12, 2Th.2:7, 1Pe.1:6 1:8; ἄχρι τῆς ἅ. ὥρας, 1Co.4:11; ἕως ἄ.,…

G0740.d: ἄρτος, -ου, ὁ, bread, a loaf: Mat.4:3, 4 Mrk.3:20, al.; ἄρτοι τ. προθέσεως, bread of the setting forth, i.e. the shewbread. Metaphorical, ὁ ἄ. τ. θεοῦ, τ. ζωῆς, ref. to Christ, Jhn.6:33, 35; in general, food: Mat.6:11, al.; ἄ. φαγεῖν (Heb. אֲכֹל לֶחֶם), to eat (MM, see word), Lu 14:1, al. (AS)

G0741.d: ἀρτύω [in Sm.: Sng.8:2 * ;] __1. to arrange, make ready (Hom.). __2. Of food (as in comic writers), to season (MM, see word): Mrk.9:50, Luk.14:34, Col.4:6.† (AS)

G0743.d: ἀρχ-άγγελος, -ου, ὁ (ἄρχι-, ἄγγελος), archangel, a chief angel: 1Th.4:16, Ju 9 (Cremer, 24; MM, see word).† (AS)

G0744.d: ἀρχαῖος, -αία, -αῖον (ἀρχή), original, ancient: Mat.5:21, 33, Luk.9:8, 19, Act.15:7, 21 21:16, 2Co.5:17, 2Pe.2:5, Rev.12:9 20:2.† SYN.: παλαιός, old, without the reference to beginning and origin contained in ἀ. The distinction is observed in π. (MM, see word). ἀ. is the antithesis to καινός: παλ. to vέος (see Westc., He., 223; Cremer, 116) (AS)

G0745.d: Ἀρχέλαος, -ου, ὁ Archelaus, son of Herod the Great, King of Judma, Samaria and Idumæa: Mat.2:22.† (AS)

G0746.d: ἀρχή, -ῆς, ἡ __1. beginning, origin; __(a) absol., of the beginning of all things: of God as the Eternal, the First Cause, Rev.21:6 (cf. 18); similarly, of Christ, Rev.22:13; of Christ as the uncreated principle, the active cause of creation, Rev.3:14; in his relation to the Church, Col.1:18; ἐν ἀ., Jhn.1:1-2; ἀπ᾽ ἀ. (and ἀπ᾽ ἀ. κτισεως), Mat.19:4, 8 24:21, Mrk.10:6 13:19, Jhn.8:44, 2Th.2:13,…

G0747.d: ἀρχηγός, -όν beginning, originating: more freq., as subst.; __1. founder, author (Lat. auchor; so some­times in π., see MM, see word; Milligan, NTD, 75): Act.3:15 (R, mg.), Heb.2:10 (R, txt.; but see Westc., in l, and Page, Ac., l.with). __2. prince, leader (so in MGr., see Kennedy, Sources, 153): Act.3:15 (R, txt.) Act.5:31, Heb.2:10 (cf. R, mg.) 122 (Cremer, 117).† (AS)

G0749.d: ἀρχιερεύς, -έως, ὁ, __1. high-priest: Mrk.2:26 14:47, al.; of Christ: Heb.2:17 3:1, al. __2. In pl., chief priests, including ex-high-priests and members of high-priestly families: Mat.2:4, Mrk.8:31, al. (Cremer, 294; DCG, i, 297f.; MM, see word). (AS)

G0750.d: ἀρχι-ποίμην, -ενος, ὁ [in Sm.: 4Ki.3:4 * ;] found on an Egyptian mummy label (Deiss., LAE, 97 ff.; cf. MM, see word); used by modem Greeks of tribal chiefs; chief shepherd. of Christ, 1Pe.5:4.† (AS)

G0752.d: ἀρχισυνάγωγος, -ου, ὁ (συναγωγή), ruler of a synagogue, an administrative officer, supervising the worship (הַכְּנֵםֶת רֹאשׁ): Mrk.5:22, 35-36 5:38 Luk.8:49 13:14, Act.13:15 18:8, 17 (Inscr., see MM, see word; cf. also DB, ext., 101).† (AS)

G0753.d: ἀρχι-τέκτων, -ονος, ὁ (τέκτων), a master-builder, architect: 1Co.3:10 (in π. of building contractors, MM, see word).† (AS)

G0754.d: ἀρχι-τελώνης, -ου, ὁ a chief tax-collector, chief publican: Luk.19:2.† (AS)

G0755.d: ἀρχι-τρίκλινος, -ου, ὁ (τρί-κλινος or -ον, a room with three couches) the superintendent of a banquet, whose duty it was to arrange the tables and food (DB, ii, 253): Jhn.2:8-9.† (AS)

G0757.d: ἄρχω __1. to begin. __2. to rule (see DCG, ii, 538b.): with genitive, Mrk.10:42, Rom.15:12. Mid., to begin: before ἀπό, Mat.16:21 20:8, Luk.14:18 23:5 24:27, 47, Jhn.8:9, Act.1:22 8:35 10:37, 1Pe.4:17; with inf., an Aramaic pleonasm, Mrk.1:45 2:23 5:17, Luk.3:8, al. (see M, Pro.14:1-35 f.; Dalman, Words, 27; MM, see word) (AS)

G0758.d: ἄρχων, -οντος, ὁ (present ptcp. of ἄρχω), a ruler, chief: Jesus, Rev.1:5; rulers of nations, Mat.20:25, Act.4:26 7:35; magistrates, Act.23:5, Rom.13:3; judges, Luk.12:58, Act.7:27, 35 16:19; members of the Sanhedrin, Luk.14:1 23:13, 35 24:20, Jhn.3:1 7:26, 48 12:42, Act.3:17 4:5, 8 13:27 14:5; rulers of synagogues, Mat.9:18, 23, Luk.8:41 18:18; οἱ ἄ. τ. αἰῶνος τούτου, 1Co.2:6-8; of the devil: ἄ.…

G0759.d: ἄρωμα, -τος, τό spice: Mrk.16:1, Luk.23:56 24:1, Jhn.19:40.† (AS)

G0760.d: Ἀσάφ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. אָסַף), [H609] Asaph, an obvious error for Ἀσά, found in the best texts, and adopted by LTTr. and WH, R, mg.: Mat.1:7-8.† (AS)

G0761.d: ἀ-σάλευτος, -ον (σαλεύω), unmoved, immovable: Act.27:41; metaphorically, Heb.12:28.† (AS)

G0762.d: ἄ-σβεστος, -ον (σβέννυμι), unquenched, unquenchable: πῦρ, Mat.3:12, Mrk.9:43, Luk.3:17.† (AS)

G0763.d: ἀσέβεια, -ας, ἡ (ἀσεβής), ungodliness, impiety: Rom.1:18 11:26, 2Ti.2:16, Tit.2:12; ἔργα ἀσεβείας, ungodly deeds, Ju 15; ἐπιθυηίαι τ. ἀσεβειῶν, desires for ungodly things or deeds, Ju 18 (DB, iv, 532; Cremer, 523; MM, see word).† (AS)

G0764.d: ἀσεβέω, -ῶ (ἀσεβής), to be ungodly, act profanely: 2Pe.2:6; with cogn. accusative (MM, see word), Ju 15.† (AS)

G0765.d: ἀσεβής, -ές (σέβω, to reverence), un­godly, impious: Rom.4:5 5:6, 1Ti.1:9, 1Pe.4:18, 2Pe.2:5-6 3:7, Ju 4 15.† (AS)

G0766.d: ἀσέλγεια, -ας, ἡ (ἀσελγής, licentious; see MM, see word), licentiousness, wantonness, excess: Mrk.7:22, Rom.13:13, 2Co.12:21, Gal.5:19 (Lft., in l), Eph.4:19, 1Pe.4:3, 2Pe.2:2 2:7 2:18, Ju 4.† SYN.: ἀσωτία, profligacy, prodigality (see Tr., Syn., § xvi; DB, iii, 46). (AS)

G0767.d: ἄσημος, -ον (σῆμα, a mark), without mark (in π. of an uncircumcised boy: Deiss., BS, 153; MM, see word). Metaphorical (MM, see word), unknown, obscure: litotes, οὐκ ἄ (Eur., al.), πόλις, Act.21:39.† (AS)

G0768.d: Ἀσήρ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. אָשֵׁר), Asher: Luk.2:36, Rev.7:6.† (AS)

G0769.d: ἀσθένεια, -ας, ἡ (ἀσθενής), weakness, frailty, sickness: Luk.13:11-12, Jhn.11:4, Act.28:9, Rom.6:19 8:26, 2Co.11:30 13:4, Gal.4:13 (MM, see word), Heb.5:2 7:28 11:34; ἐν ἀ., Jhn.5:5, 1Co.2:3 15:43, 2Co.12:9; pl., Mat.8:17, Luk.5:15 8:2, 2Co.12:5 12:9-10, 1Ti.5:23, Heb.4:15.† SYN.: μαλακία, νόσος (see DB, iii, 323a) (AS)

G0769G.d: ἀσθένεια, -ας, ἡ (ἀσθενής), weakness, frailty, sickness: Luk.13:11-12, Jhn.11:4, Act.28:9, Rom.6:19 8:26, 2Co.11:30 13:4, Gal.4:13 (MM, see word), Heb.5:2 7:28 11:34; ἐν ἀ., Jhn.5:5, 1Co.2:3 15:43, 2Co.12:9; pl., Mat.8:17, Luk.5:15 8:2, 2Co.12:5 12:9-10, 1Ti.5:23, Heb.4:15.† SYN.: μαλακία, νόσος (see DB, iii, 323a) (AS)

G0923H.d: Βαρσαββᾶς (Rec. -αβᾶς), -ᾶ (Aram., son of Sabba), Barsabbas: __1. the surname of one Joseph: Act.1:23. __2. The surname of one Judas: Act.15:22. † (AS)

G0924.d: Βαρτίμαιος, -ου, ὁ (-μαῖος, T; perh. Aram. בַּר־טִמְאַי, see DB, iv, p. 762), Bartimæus: Mrk.10:46.† (AS)

G0925.d: βαρύνω, to weigh down = βαρέω (which see): Luk.21:34, Rec.† (AS)

G0926.d: βαρύς, -εῖα, ύ, heavy: Mat.23:4. Metaphorical, burdensome: ἐντολή, 1Jn.5:3; severe (perh. impressive): ἐπιστολή, 2Co.10:10; weighty: τὰ βαρύτερα τ. νόμου, Mat.23:23; αἰτιώματα, Act.25:7; violent, cruel (EV, grievous): λύκος, Act.20:29.† (AS)

G0927.d: βαρύτιμος, -ον (βαρύς, τιμή), of great value, very costly: Mat.26:7 (T, πολυτίμου) .† (AS)

G0928.d: βασανίζω (βάσανος), __1. prop., to rub on the touchstone, put to the test. __2. to examine by torture, hence, generally, to torture, torment, distress: Mat.8:6, 29 14:24, Mrk.5:7 6:48, Luk.8:28, 2Pe.2:8, Rev.9:5 11:10 12:2 14:10 20:10. † (AS)

G0928G.d: βασανίζω (βάσανος), __1. prop., to rub on the touchstone, put to the test. __2. to examine by torture, hence, generally, to torture, torment, distress: Mat.8:6, 29 14:24, Mrk.5:7 6:48, Luk.8:28, 2Pe.2:8, Rev.9:5 11:10 12:2 14:10 20:10. † (AS)

G0928H.d: βασανίζω (βάσανος), __1. prop., to rub on the touchstone, put to the test. __2. to examine by torture, hence, generally, to torture, torment, distress: Mat.8:6, 29 14:24, Mrk.5:7 6:48, Luk.8:28, 2Pe.2:8, Rev.9:5 11:10 12:2 14:10 20:10. † (AS)

G0930.d: βασανιστής, -οῦ, ὁ (βασανίζω), prop., a torturer; used of a gaoler, Mat.18:34.† (AS)

G0931.d: βάσανος, -ου, ὁ (of Oriental origin), __1. prop., touchstone, a dark stone used in testing metals. __2. examination by torture. __3. torment, torture: Mat.4:24, Luk.15:23, 28. † (AS)

G0932.d: βασιλεία, -ας, ἡ (βασιλεύω), __1. prop. abstract, sovereignty, royal power, dominion: Luk.1:33 22:29, Jhn.18:36, Act.1:6, Heb.1:8, 1Co.15:24; λαβεῖν β., Luk.19:12, 15 Rev.17:12; δοῦναι τὴν, ib. 17; ἔχειν β., ib. 18; ἔρχεσθαι ἐν τ. (εἰς τὴν) β., Mat.16:28, Luk.23:42; β. τ. θεοῦ, Rev.12:10. __2. By meton., concrete (MM, Exp., x), __(a) a kingdom, the territory or people over whom the king rules…

G0933.d: βασίλειον, -ου, τό (βασίλειος, which see), __1. a capital city. __2. Freq. in pl., τὰ β., a palace: Luk.7:25. † (AS)

G0934.d: βασίλειος, -ον (also -α, -ον; βασιλεύς), royal: 1Pe.2:9 (LXX) (see Hort, in l.).† royal, regal, kingly;, metaphorically possessed of high prerogatives and distinction, 1Pet. 2:9; (AS)

G0935.d: βασιλεύς, -έως, ὁ, a king: Mat.1:6 2:1; used by courtesy of Herod the Tetrarch, Mat.14:9; of the Roman Emperor, as frequently in κοινή (Deiss., LAE, p. 367), 1Pe.2:13, 17; of the Christ, in the phrase ὁ β. τ. Ἰουδαίων, Mat.2:2, al.; τοῦ Ἰσραήλ, Mrk.15:32, Jhn.1:50 12:13; of God, Mat.5:35, 1Ti.1:17, Rev.15:3; β. βασιλέων, Rev.17:14 19:16; β. τ. βασιλευόντων, 1Ti.6:15 (on the associations of the…

G0936.d: βασιλεύω, (βασιλεύς), to be king, to reign, rule: 1Ti.6:15; with genitive (cl.), Mat.2:22; before ἐπί, with accusative (= Heb. מלךְ על; Bl., §36, 8), Luk.1:33 19:14, 27 Rom.5:14; ἐπὶ τ. γῆς, on earth, Rev.5:10; of God, Rev.11:15, 17 19:6; of Christ, Luk.1:33, 1Co.15:25, Rev.11:15; of Christians, Rev.5:10 20:4 (constative aor., M, Pr., 130), ib. 6 22:5. Metaphorical, Christians, Rom.5:17, 1Co.4:8;…

G0937.d: βασιλικός, -ή, -όν (βασιλεύς), royal, belonging to a king: χώρα, Act 12:20; ἐσθής, Act.12:21; νόμος β., a supreme law, "a law which governs other laws and so has a specially regal character" (Hort), or because made by a king (LAE, p. 3673), Jas.2:8; τις, one in the service of a king, a courtier, Jhn.4:46, 49 (WH, mg., βασιλίσκος).† (AS)

G0938G.d: βασίλισσα, -ης, ἡ (in Attic, βασιλεία, βασιλίς), a queen: Mat.12:42, Luk.11:31, Act.8:27, Rev.18:7.† (AS)

G0938H.d: βασίλισσα, -ης, ἡ (in Attic, βασιλεία, βασιλίς), a queen: Mat.12:42, Luk.11:31, Act.8:27, Rev.18:7.† (AS)

G0939.d: βάσις, ־εως, ἡ (βαίνω), __1. a step (Æsch., al.). __2. Hence, a foot (Plat.; Wis.13:18): Act.3:7. † (AS)

G0940.d: βασκαίνω, __1. to slander (Dem.). __2. to blight by the evil eye, to fascinate, bewitch: Gal.3:1. † (AS)

G0941.d: βαστάζω, __1. to take up with the hands, to lift: λίθους, Jhn.10:31. __2. to bear, to carry, as a burden, and metaphorically, to endure; Mat.3:11 20:12, Mrk.14:13, Luk.7:14 10:7 11:27 14:27 22:10, Jhn.16:12 19:17, Act.3:2 9:15 15:1 21:35, Rom.11:18 15:1, Gal.5:10 6:2, 5 17, Rev.2:2, 3 17:7. __3. In late writers (MM, Exp., ii, iii, x), __(a) to take away; Mat.8:17 (Isa.53:4, Heb.); __(b) to carry…

G0942.d: βάτος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ, a bramble-bush: Luk.6:44, Act.7:30, 35; ἐπὶ τοῦ (τῆς) β., in the place concerning the bush: Mrk.12:26, Luk.20:37.† (AS)

G0943.d: βάτος, -ου, ὁ (Heb. בַּת), bath, a Jewish liquid measure, = μετρητής (which see), or about 8 3/4 gals.: Luk.16:6.† (AS)

G0945.d: βατταλογέω, -ῶ (Rec. βαττολ-, D, βλαττ- = βατταρίζω, prob. onomatop.; see MM, see word; DCG, ii, 499b, 790a); to stammer, repeat idly: Mat.6:7 (Cremer, 765).† (AS)

G0946.d: βδέλυγμα, -τος, τό (βδελύσσω), an abomination, a detestable thing: Luk.16:15, Rev.17:4, 5 21:27; τὸ β. τ. ἐρημώσεως (Dan LXX 12:11, cf . 1Ma.1:54; DB, i, 12f.; DCG, i, 6f.), Mrk.13:14, Mat.24:15 (Cremer, 138).† (AS)

G0948.d: βδελύσσω, βδελύσσομαι (βδέω, to stink), in cl., mid. only (Attic, -ττομαι); to make foul; pass., Rev.21:8; mid., to turn away in disgust from, to detest: Rom.2:22 (Cremer, 137).† (AS)

G0949.d: βέβαιος, -ον (also -α, -ον; βαίνω), firm, secure: ἄγκυρα, Heb.6:19; metaphorically, sure (esp. "in the sense of legally guaranteed security," Deiss., BS, 109; cf . two foll. words): ἐπαγγελία, Rom.4:16; ἐλπίς, 2Co.1:6; λόγος, Heb.2:2; παρρησία, Heb.3:6; ἀρχή (τ. ὑποστάσεως), Heb.3:14; διαθήκη, Heb.9:17; κλῆσις κ. ἐκλογή, 2Pe.1:10; comp. (-ότερος), προφητικὸς λόγος, 2Pe.1:19.† (AS)

G0950.d: βεβαιόω, -ῶ (βέβαιος), to confirm, establish, secure, of things (cl.): λόγον, Mk 16:[20]; ἐπαγγελίας, Rom.15:8; of persons (DCG, ii, 605): 1Co.1:8, 2Co.1:21. Pass., 1Co.1:6, Col.2:7, Heb.2:3 13:9 (as an Attic legal term, to guarantee the validity of a purchase, establish or confirm a title; see next word, Cremer, 139; cf. δια-β.).† (AS)

G0951.d: βεβαίωσις, -εως, ἡ (βεβαιόω, which see), confirmation: τ. εὐαγγελίου, Php.1:7; εἰς β., Heb.6:16, a phrase frequently in π. of guarantee in a business transaction (Deiss., BS, 104ff.; Cremer, 140).† (AS)

G0952.d: βέβηλος, -ον (βαίνω, whence βηλός, a threshold), __1. permitted to be trodden, accessible (see DCG, ii, 422b); hence, __2. (opposite to ἱερός) unhallowed, profane: of things, 1Ti.4:7 6:20, 2Ti.2:16; of men, 1Ti.1:9, Heb.12:16 (cf. κοινός; Cremer, 140). † (AS)

G0953.d: βεβηλόω, -ῶ (βέβηλος), to profane: τ. σάββατον, Mat.12:5; τ. ἱερόν, Act.24:6 (Cremer, 141).† SYN.: κοινόω, which see (AS)

G0954.d: Βεελζεβούλ (WH, App., 159, Rec., βεελζεβούλ), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בַּעַל, lord, and the Talmudic זִבּוּל, from זֶבֶל, dung (Dalman, Gr., 137.n), or perh. זִבֻל, habitation, but, see DB, iv, 409f.; DCG, i, 181). The AV, RV, Beelzebub, comes through Vg. from 4Ki.1:2, בַּעַל זִבוּב, lord of flies (LXX, βάαλ μυῖα, Sm., βεελζεβούβ), Beelzebul, Beelzebub, a name of Satan: Mat.10:25 12:24, 27 Mrk.3:22,…

G0955.d: Βελίαλ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בְּלִיַּעַל, worthlessness, but see DB, i, 268), Belial, a name of Satan: 2Co.6:15, Rec. See next word.† Βελιάρ, ὁ, indecl. (another form of previous word, "due to harsh Syriac pronunciation," or else Heb. בֵּל יַעַר, lord of the forest), Beliar, a name of Satan: 2Co.6:15 (see DB, i, 269).† (AS)

G0956.d: βέλος, -εος, τό (βάλλω), a missile, a dart: Eph.6:16.† (AS)

G0957.d: βελτίων, -ον (genitive -ονος), comp. of ἀγαθός, neut. as adv., better, very well: 2Ti.1:18 (also Act.10:28 D). On elative use in these passages, see M, Pr., 78, 236.† (AS)

G0958.d: Βενιαμίν, (Rec. -μίν), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בֶּנְיָמִין), Benjamin: Act.13:21, Rom.11:1, Php.3:5, Rev.7:8.† (AS)

G0959.d: Βερνίκη (elsewhere Βερενίκη), Macedonian form of Φερενίκη, cf. Veronica, Victoria), -ης, ἡ, Bernice, Berenice, dau. of Herod Agrippa I: Act.25:13, 23 26:3o.† (AS)

G0960.d: Βέροια, -ας, ἡ, Berœa, a city of Macedonia: Act.17:10, 13.† (AS)

G0962.d: Βηθαβαρά, -ας (Rec. -ρᾶ, indecl.; Heb. בֵּית עֲבָרָה, place of crossing; -αραβᾷ, R, mg.), Bethabara: Jhn.1:28, Rec. (WH, R, βηθανία).† (AS)

G0963.d: Βηθανία, -ας (also -ιά, indecl., Luk.19:29 and in B*, Mrk.11:1), ἡ, (Heb. בֵּית עֲנִיָּה, house of affliction, accusative to Jerome, or perh., house of dates, cf. Bethphage), Bethany; __1. a village fifteen furlongs from Jerusalem, the modern El Azerîyeh: Mat.21:17 26:6, Mrk.8:22 (WH, mg.) 11:1, 11, 12 14:3 Luk.19:29 24:50, Jhn.11:1, 18 12:1. __2. A place on E. bank of Jordan: Jhn.1:28 (R, mg.,…

G0964.d: Βηθεσδά, ἡ, indecl. (deriv. uncertain, see Westc. on Jhn.5:2, and DB, i, 279), Bethesda, a pool in Jerusalem: Jhn.5:2, Rec. (Βηθζαθά, WH, Βηθσαϊδά, WH, mg.).† (AS)

G0965.d: Βηθλέεμ, ἡ, indecl. (Heb. בֵּית לֶחֶם, house of bread), Bethlehem, a town 6 m. S. of Jerusalem: Mat.2:1, 5 6, 8, 16, Luk.2:4, 15 Jhn.7:42.† (AS)

G0966.d: Βηθσαιδά (Rec. -σαϊδά), and -δάν (Mt, Mk, ll. with), ἡ, indecl. (Syr., house of fish), Bethsaida, a town on NE. shore of the Sea of Galilee: Luk.9:10. It is generally supposed that a second B. on the W. shore is referred to in Mat.11:21, Mrk.6:45 8:22, Luk.10:13, Jhn.1:45 12:21 (DB, i, 282f.; but see Swete on Mrk.6:45). __2. 2. Βηθζαθά, ἡ, indecl. (perh. Aram. בֵּית זַיְתָה, house of olives)…

G0967.d: Βηθφαγή (L, -γῆ), ἡ, indecl. (Aram. בֵּית־פַּגֵּי, house of unripe figs; Dalman, Gr., 191), Bethphage: Mat.21:1, Mrk.11:1, Luk.19:29.† (AS)

G0968.d: βῆμα, -τος, τό (βαίνω), __1. a step, stride, pace: Act.7:5. __2. a raised place, a platform reached by steps, originally that in the Pnyx at Athens from which orations were made; frequently of the tribune or tribunal of a Roman magistrate or ruler: Mat.27:19, Jhn.19:13, Act.12:21, 18:12, 16, 17 25:6, 10, 17; β. τοῦ θεοῦ, Rom.14:10; τ. Χριστοῦ, 2Co.5:10. † (AS)

G0969.d: βήρυλλος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ, ) beryl, a jewel of sea-green colour: Rev.21:20.† (AS)

G0970.d: βία, -ας, ἡ, strength, force, violence: Act.5:26 21:35 24:7 27:41.† (AS)

G0971.d: βιάζω (βία), and depon. -ομαι, to force, constrain, rare in active (poet, and late prose), but found in cl. in pass., and so perh. βιάζεται, suffereth violence, Mat.11:12, EV (but see infr.), whether __(a) in good sense, of disciples (Thayer, al.), or __(b) in bad sense, of the enemies of the kingdom (Meyer, in l.; Dalman, Words, 139ff.; Cremer, 141ff.). Mid., advanceth violently, Mt, l.with…

G0973.d: βιαστής, -οῦ, ὁ (βιάζω), late form of βιατάς; __1. strong, forceful. __2. violent (Philo): Mat.11:12 (see: βιάζω). † (AS)

G0974.d: βιβλαρίδιον, -ου, τό (diminutive of βιβλάριον, diminutive of βίβλος), a little book: Rev.10:2, 8 (WH, βιβλιόν, T2, 7 βιβλιδάριον) 9, 10. Not hitherto found elsewhere.† (AS)

G0975.d: βιβλίον, -ου, τό (diminutive of βίβλος, which see), __1. a paper, letter, written document: β. ἀποστασίου, bill of divorce, Mat.19:7, Mrk.10:4. __2. a book, a roll: Luk.4:17, 20 Jhn.20:30 21:25, Gal.3:10, 2Ti.4:13, Heb.9:19 10:7, Rev.1:11 5:1-9 6:14 10:8 20:12 22:7-19; β. τ. ζωῆς, Rev.13:8 17:8 20:12 21:27. † (AS)

G0976.d: βίβλος, -ου, ἡ (variant form of βύβλος, the Egyptian papyrus, paper made from its fibrous coat), a book, a roll, used much less frequently than βιβλίον, and with a "connotation of sacredness and veneration" (MM, Exp., x), Mat.1:1 Mrk.12:26, Luk.3:4 20:42 Act.1:20 7:42 19:19; β. τ. ζωῆς, Php.4:3, Rev.3:5 20:15.† (AS)

G0977.d: βιβρώσκω, poët, and late prose, to eat: Jhn.6:13.† (AS)

G0978.d: Βιθυνία, -ַας, Bithynia, a province in Asia Minor: Act.16:7, 1Pe.1:1.† (AS)

G0979.d: βίος, -ου, ὁ, __1. period or course of life, life: Luk.8:14, 1Ti.2:2, 2Ti.2:4, 1Jn.2:16. __2. living, livelihood, means (in Pro.31:14 for לֶחֶם; see DCG, ii, 39a): Mrk.12:44, Luk.8:43 15:12, 30 21:4, 1Jn.3:17.† SYN.: ζωή, is life intensive, "vita quâ, vivimus," the vital principle; βίος, life extensive, "vita quam vivimus," (1) the period of life, (2) the means by which it is sustained. Hence, in…

G0980.d: βιόω, -ῶ (βίος), to spend life, to live: τ. χρόνον βιῶσαι (cl., more frequently 2 aor., -ναι), 1Pe.4:2 (cf. Jb, l.with).† SYN.: ζάω (which see). (AS)

G0981.d: βίωσις, -εως, ἡ (βιόω), manner of life: Act.26:4.† (AS)

G0982.d: βιωτικός, -ή, -όν (βιός), pertaining to life, hence, worldly (Field, Notes, 171): Luk.21:34, 1Co.6:3, 4.† (AS)

G0984.d: βλάπτω, to hurt, injure: with accusative, Mrk.16:[18], Luk.4:35.† (AS)

G0985.d: βλαστάνω, __1. to sprout: Mat.13:26, Mrk.4:27, Heb.9:4. __2. In late Gk., causal, to make to grow, produce: with accusative, Jas.5:18. † (AS)

G0986.d: Βλάστος, -ου, ὁ, Blastus, chamberlain of Agrippa: Act.12:20.† (AS)

G0987.d: βλασφημέω, -ῶ (βλάσφημος), __1. to speak lightly or profanely of sacred things (in cl., opp. of εὐφημέω), esp. to speak impiously of God, to blaspheme, speak blasphemously: absol., Mat.9:3 26:65, Mrk.2:7, Jhn.10:36, Act.26:11, 1Ti.1:20, 2Pe.2:12; τ. θεόν, Act.19:37, Rev.16:11, 21; τὸ ὄνομα τ. θεοῦ, Rev.13:6 16:9; δόξας, Ju 3, 2Pe.2:10; εἰς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, Mrk.3:29, Luk.12:10. __2.…

G0988.d: βλασφημία, -ας, ἡ (βλάσφημος), __(a) railing slander: Mat.12:31 15:19, Mrk.3:28 7:22, Eph.4:31, Col.3:8, 1Ti.6:4, Ju 9, Rev.2:9 __(b) spec., impious speech against God, blasphemy: Mat.26:65, Mrk.14:64, Luk.5:21, Jhn.10:33, Rev.13:5; ὄνομα βλασφημίας, Rev.13:1 17:3; with genitive obj. Mat.12:31; πρὸς τ. θεόν, Rev.13:6 (Cremer, 570; DB, i, 305; DCG ii, 423).† (AS)

G0989.d: βλάσφημος, -ον (βλασ-, of uncertain deriv., see Thayer, Boisacq; + φήμη, speech), __(a) evil-speaking, slanderous, blasphemous: Act.6:11, 2Ti.3:2, 2Pe.2:11 (cf. Ju 9); __(b) as subst. a blasphemer: 1Ti.1:13 (Cremer, 570). † (AS)

G0990.d: βλέμμα, -τος, τό (βλέπω), a look, a glance: βλέμματι καὶ ἀκοῇ, 2Pe.2:8, sight and hearing, a sense not found for β. in Gk. lit., but perh. recognized in the vernacular (ICC, in l.)† (AS)

G0991.d: βλέπω, __1. of bodily sight; __(a) to see, have sight (opposite to τυφλὸς): Mat.12:22, Jhn.9:7, Act.9:9, Rom.11:8, Rev.3:18, al.; __(b) to perceive, look (at), see: absol., Act.1:9; with accusative, Mat.7:3, Mrk.5:31, Luk.6:41, Jhn.1:29, al.; ὅραμα, Act.12:9; γυναῖκα, Mat.5:28; βιβλίον, Rev.5:3, 4; τ. βλεπόμενα, 2Co.4:18. __2. Metaphorical, of mental vision; __(a) to see, perceive, discern:…

G0992.d: βλητέος, -α, -ον (gerundive of βάλλω), (that which) one must put: Luk.5:38.† (AS)

G0993.d: Βοανηργές, indecl. (on the derivation, see Dalman, Gr., 144; Words, 42; Swete, Mk., l.with; DCG, i, 216), Boanerges: Mrk.3:17.† (AS)

G0994.d: βοάω, -ῶ (βοή), __1. absol., to cry, call out: Mat.3:3, 27:46, Mrk.1:3 15:34, Luk.3:4 9:38 18:38, Jhn.1:23, Act.8:7 17:6 25:24, Gal.4:27. __2. C. dative, to call on for help (Heb. זעק על, Hos.7:14, al.), Luk.18:7.† SYN.: καλέω, to call, invite, summon; κράζω, to cry, harshly or inarticulately, as animals; κραυγάζω, intensive of κράζω. βοάω expresses emotion, whether joy, fear, etc. (AS)

G0996.d: βοήθεια, -ας, ἡ (see: βοηθέω), help: Heb.4:16; pl., helps, "frapping," a technical nautical term (MM, Exp., x; DB, ext., 367): Act.27:17.† (AS)

G0997.d: βοηθέω, -ῶ (βοή + θέω, to run), to come to aid, to help, succour: absol., Act.21:28; with dative, Mat.15:25, Mrk.9:22, 24 Act.16:9, 2Co.6:2" (LXX), Heb.2:18, Rev.12:16.† (AS)

G0998.d: βοηθός, -ον (see: βοηθέω), __1. (poët. -όος), hasting to the war-cry (Hom.). __2. helping, auxiliary; as subst. (Hdt.), a helper: Heb.13:6 (LXX). † (AS)

G0999.d: βόθυνος, -ου, ὁ (= βόθρος, more frequently in cl.), a pit: Mat.12:11 15:14, Luk.6:39 (cf. DB, iii, 885; DCG, ii, 367).† (AS)

G1000.d: βολή, -ῆς, ἡ (βάλλω), a throw; λίθου β. (Thuc., v, 65, 2), a stone's throw: Luk.22:41.† (AS)

G1001.d: βολίζω (βολίς, in sense of sounding-lead), to heave the lead, take soundings: Act.27:28.† (AS)

G1002.d: βολίς, -ίδος, ἡ (βάλλω), a dart, javelin: Heb.12:20, Rec. (LXX).† (AS)

G1003.d: Βοός and Βοές (RV, Βοάζ, Rec. Βοόζ), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בֹּעַז), Boaz (Rut.2:1): Mat.1:5, Luk.3:32.† (AS)

G1005.d: βορρᾶς, -ᾶ (Attic contr. of Βορέας, the North wind personified), __1. Boreas, the North wind. __2. the north: Luk.13:29, Rev.21:13. † (AS)

G1006.d: βόσκω, prop., of a herdsman, to feed: Mat.8:33, Mrk.5:14, Luk.8:34 15:15; metaphorically, of Christian pastoral care, Jhn.21:15, 17. Pass., of cattle, to feed, graze: Mat.8:30, Mrk.5:11, Luk.8:32.† SYN.: ποιμαίνειν, to tend, shepherd, a wider term, including oversight as well as feeding (see Tr., Syn., §xxv). (AS)

G1007.d: Βοσόρ see Βεώρ - ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בְּעוֹר), Beor, father of Balaam: 2Pe.2:15 (Rec. Βοσόρ).† (AS)

G1008.d: βοτάνη, -ῆς, ἡ (βόσκω), __1. grass, fodder. __2. green herb: Heb.6:7.† SYN.: λάχανον, a garden herb, a vegetable. (AS)

G1009.d: βότρυς, -οῦ, ὁ, a cluster of grapes: Rev.14:18 (cf. στραφυλή) .† (AS)

G1010.d: βουλευτής, -οῦ, ὁ (βουλεύω), a councillor, a senator; of a member of the Sanhedrin: Mrk.15:34, Luk.23:50.† (AS)

G1011.d: βουλεύω (βουλή), to take counsel, deliberate, resolve. In mid., __1. to take counsel with oneself, consider: before εἰ, Luk.14:31. __2. to determine with oneself, resolve: with inf., Act.5:33 27:39; with accusative, 2Co.1:17; before ἵνα, Jhn.11:53 12:10 (cf. παρα-, συμ-). † (AS)

G1012.d: βουλή, -ῆς, ἡ (βούλομαι), counsel, purpose (in cl., esp. of the gods): Luk.23:51, Act.4:28 5:38 19:1 27:12, 42; pl., 1Co.4:5; of the Divine purpose, Heb.6:17; τ. βουλὴν τ. θελήματος αὐτοῦ, Eph.1:11; β. τ. Θεοῦ, Luk.7:30, Act.2:23 13:36 20:27.† (AS)

G1013.d: βούλημα, -τος, τό (βούλομαι), purpose, will: Act.27:43, Rom.9:19, 1Pe.4:3.† SYN.: θέλημα. (AS)

G1014.d: βούλομαι, to will, wish, desire, purpose, be minded, implying more strongly than θέλω (which see), the deliberate exercise of volition (see Hort on Jas.1:18): with inf. (M, Pr., 205; Bl., §69, 4), Mrk.15:15, Act.5:28, 33 12:4 15:37 17:20 18:15, 27 19:30 22:30 23:28 27:43 28:18, 2Co.1:15, 1Ti.6:9, Heb.6:17, II Jhn.12, 3Jo.10, Ju 5; with accusative, 2Co.1:17; with accusative and inf., Php.1:12,…

G1015.d: βουνός, -οῦ, ὁ (a Cyrenaїc word, Hdt., iv, 199), a hill: Luk.3:5 (LXX) 23:30.† (AS)

G1016.d: βοῦς, βοός, ὁ, ἡ, an ox, a cow: Luk.13:15 14:5, 19 Jhn.2:14, 15 1Co.9:9" (LXX), 1Ti.5:18.† (AS)

G1017.d: βραβεῖον, -ου, τό (βραβεύς, an umpire), a prize in the games: 1Co.9:24; metaphorically, of the Christian's reward, Php.3:14.† (AS)

G1018.d: βραβεύω (βραβεύς, an umpire), __(a) prop., to act as umpire; hence, __(b) generally, to arbitrate, decide (Isocr., Dem.; Lft., Col., l.with; MM, see word): Col.3:15; __(with) in some late writers, to direct, rule, control (so in Col., l.with, accusative to Thayer, see word, Meyer, in l.), (cf. κατα-βραβεύω). † (AS)

G1019.d: βραδύνω (βραδύς), __1. trans., to retard (Soph., Is, l.with). __2. More frequently intrans., to be slow, to tarry: 1Ti.3:15, 2Pe.3:9. † (AS)

G1020.d: βραδυπλοέω, -ῶ (βραδύς, πλοῦς), to sail slowly: Act.27:7.† (AS)

G1021.d: βραδύς, -εῖα, -ύ, slow: εἰς τὸ λαλῆσαι, Jas.1:19; metaphorically, of the understanding: β. τ. καρδίᾳ, assoc. with ἀνόητος, Luk.24:25.† (AS)

G1022.d: 1. slowness , (Iliad by Homer), attic 2. of the mind, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G1023.d: βραχίων, -ὀνος, ὁ, the arm; as in OT, β. Κυρίου, metaphorically, for the Divine power: Luk.1:51, Jhn.12:38" (LXX), Act.13:17.† (AS)

G1024.d: βραχύς, -εῖα, -ύ, short; __(a) of time; short, little: βραχύ, Act.5:34; μετὰ β., Luk.22:58; β. τι, a short time, Heb.2:7, 9 RV, mg.; __(b) of distance: Act.27:28; __(with) of quantity or value, little, few: Jhn.6:7, Heb.2:7, 9 RV, txt.; pl., διὰ βραχέων, in few words, Heb.13:22. † (AS)

G1025.d: βρέφος, -ους, τό, __1. an unborn child: Luk.1:41, 44. __2. a newborn child, a babe: Luk.2:12, 16 18:15, Act.7:19, 1Pe.2:2; ἀπὸ βρέφους, from infancy, 2Ti.3:15. † (AS)

G1026.d: βρέχω, __1. to wet: Luk.7:38, 44. __2. In late Gk. writers and vernac. = ὕειν, to send rain, to rain (Kennedy, Sources, 39, 155): Mat.5:45; trop., β. πῦρ κ. θεῖον, Luk.17:29; impers., βρέχει, it rains: Jas.5:17; with ὐετός as subj., Rev.11:6. † (AS)

G1028.d: βροχή, -ῆς, ἡ (βρέχω), __1. = βροχετός, a wetting (in π., of irrigation in Egypt; Deiss., LAE, 77). __2. As in MGr. (Kennedy, Sources, 153), = ὑετός, rain: Mat.7:25, 27. † (AS)

G1029.d: βρόχος, -ου, ὁ, a noose, a slip-knot, a halter: metaphorically, a restraint (not, as AV, R, txt., a snare): 1Co.7:35.† (AS)

G1030.d: βρυγμός, -οῦ, ὁ (βρύχω), a biting, a gnashing of teeth: Mat.8:12 13:42, 50 22:13 24:51 25:30, Luk.13:28.† (AS)

G1031.d: βρύχω (Attic, βρύκω), __1. to bite or eat greedily. __2. to gnash, grind, with the teeth: Act.7:54. † (AS)

G1032.d: βρύω, poët., late prose and vernac., to be full to bursting; __1. of the earth producing vegetation. __2. Of plants putting forth buds. __3. Of springs, to gush with water: Jas.3:11. † (AS)

G1033.d: βρῶμα, -τος, τό (cf. βιβρώσκω), food: Rom.14:15, 20 1Co.8:8, 13 10:3; pl., Mat.14:15, Mrk.7:19, Luk.3:11 9:13, 1Co.6:13, 1Ti.4:3, Heb.9:10 13:9; trop., of spiritual food, Jhn.4:34, 1Co.3:2 (cf. βρῶσις).† (AS)

G1035.d: βρῶσις, -εως, ἡ (cf. βιβρώσκω), __1. eating: β. καὶ πόσις, Rom.14:17, Col.2:16 (see Lft., ICC, in l.); with genitive obj., 1Co.8:4; metaphorically, corrosion, rust: Mat.6:19, 20. __2. As also in cl. (Hom., al.) = βρῶμα, food: Jhn.6:27a, 2Co.9:10, Col.2:16 (EV, but see supr.). Heb.12:16; metaphorically, of spiritual nourishment, Jhn.4:32 6:27b, 55.† (AS)

G1036.d: βυθίζω (βυθός), trans., to cause to sink, to sink: metaphorically, εἰς ὄλεθρον, 1Ti.6:9; pass., to sink, intrans.: Luk.5:7.† (AS)

G1037.d: βυθός, -οῦ, ὁ, __1. the bottom. __2. the depth of the sea, the deep sea: 2Co.11:25. † (AS)

G1038.d: βυρσεύς, -έως, ὁ (βύρσα, a hide), late form for βυρσοδέψης, a tanner: Act.9:43 10:6, 32.† (AS)

G1039.d: βύσσινος, -η, -ον (βύσσος), made of βύσσος, fine linen: Rev.18:12, 16 19:8, 14.† (AS)

G1040.d: βύσσος, -οῦ, ἡ (cf. Heb. בּוּץ), byssus, a fine species of flax, also the linen made from it: Luk.16:19.† (AS)

G1041.d: βωμός, -οῦ, ὁ (βαίνω), __1. any raised place, a platform. __2. an altar: Act.17:23 (cf. θυσιαστήριον and see DB, i, 75). † (AS)

G1042.d: Γαββαθα (Rec. -θᾶ), ἡ, indecl., Gabbatha, the Greek transliteration of an uncertain Aramaic word (DB, see word; Dalman, Words, 7), used as the equivalent of λιθόστρωτον, stone pavement: Jhn.19:13.† (AS)

G1043.d: Γαβριήλ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. גַּבְרִיאֵל, hero of God), the archangel Gabriel: Luk.1:19, 26.† (AS)

G1044.d: γάγγραινα, -ης, ἡ, a gangrene, an eating sore, which leads to mortification: 2Ti.2:17.† (AS)

G1045.d: Γάδ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. גָּד), Gad (Gen.30:11 49:13, al.): Rev.7:5.† (AS)

G1046.d: Γαδαρηνός, -ή, -όν (Γαδαρά, Gadara, the capital of Peræa), Gadarene, of Gadara: Mat.8:28 (Rec. Γεργεσηνῶν), Mrk.5:1, Rec. (Edd., Γερασηνῶν), Luk.8:26, 37 Rec. (Edd., Γερασηνῶν).† (AS)

G1047.d: γάζα, -ης, ἡ (a Persian word), treasure: Act.8:27.† (AS)

G1048.d: Γάζα -ης, ἡ (Heb. עַזָּה), Gaza, in OT, one of the five chief cities of the Philistines: Act.8:26.† (AS)

G1049.d: γαζο-φυλάκιον, -ου, τό (γάζα, φυλακή), treasury: also, apparently, the trumpet-shaped chests into which the peoples' temple-offerings were thrown (DB, iv, 96; DCG, ii, 748): Mrk.12:41, 43 Luk.21:1, Jhn.8:20.† (AS)

G1050G.d: Γαῖος, -ου, ὁ (Γάϊος, Rec.), Gaius, the name of a Christian; __1. of Macedonia: Act.19:29. __2. Of Derbe: Act.20:4. __3. Of Corinth: Rom.16:23, 1Co.1:14. __4. The one to whom in Ep. Jo is addressed: III Jo 1. † (AS)

G1050H.d: Γαῖος, -ου, ὁ (Γάϊος, Rec.), Gaius, the name of a Christian; __1. of Macedonia: Act.19:29. __2. Of Derbe: Act.20:4. __3. Of Corinth: Rom.16:23, 1Co.1:14. __4. The one to whom in Ep. Jo is addressed: III Jo 1. † (AS)

G1050I.d: Γαῖος, -ου, ὁ (Γάϊος, Rec.), Gaius, the name of a Christian; __1. of Macedonia: Act.19:29. __2. Of Derbe: Act.20:4. __3. Of Corinth: Rom.16:23, 1Co.1:14. __4. The one to whom in Ep. Jo is addressed: III Jo 1. † (AS)

G1050J.d: Γαῖος, -ου, ὁ (Γάϊος, Rec.), Gaius, the name of a Christian; __1. of Macedonia: Act.19:29. __2. Of Derbe: Act.20:4. __3. Of Corinth: Rom.16:23, 1Co.1:14. __4. The one to whom in Ep. Jo is addressed: III Jo 1. † (AS)

G1051.d: γάλα, -ακτος, τό milk: 1Co.9:7. Metaphorical, of elementary Christian teaching: 1Co.3:2, Heb.5:12, 13; τὸ λογικὸν ἄδολον γ., the rational (spiritual) genuine milk (see Hort, in l.), 1Pe.2:2 (in support of AV, milk of the word, see ICC, in l.).† (AS)

G1052.d: Γαλάτης, -ου, ὁ (originally syn. with cl. Κέλτης; cf. 1Ma.8:2, and see next word), a Galatian: Gal.3:1.† (AS)

G1053.d: Γαλατία, -ας, ἡ, Galatia; __1. a gentilic region in Asia Minor, settled by Gauls (iii/B.C). __2. A Roman Province which included this region (DB, ii, 85ff.): 1Co.16:1, Gal.1:2, 2Ti.4:10 (T, Tr., mg., Γαλλίαν), 1Pe.1:1. † (AS)

G1054.d: Γαλατικός, -ή, -όν (see previous word), Galatian, belonging to Galatia: Act.16:6 18:23.† (AS)

G1055.d: γαλήνη, -ης, ἡ, a calm: Mat.8:26, Mrk.4:39, Luk.8:24.† (AS)

G1056.d: Γαλιλαία, -ας, ἡ (Heb. הַגָּלִיל, the circle, district), Galilee, the name of the northern region of Palestine in NT times: Γ. τῶν ἐθνῶν, Mat.4:15 (LXX); θάλασσα τῆς Γ., Mat.15:29 (cf. Jhn.6:1). (AS)

G1056G.d: Γαλιλαία, -ας, ἡ (Heb. הַגָּלִיל, the circle, district), Galilee, the name of the northern region of Palestine in NT times: Γ. τῶν ἐθνῶν, Mat.4:15 (LXX); θάλασσα τῆς Γ., Mat.15:29 (cf. Jhn.6:1). (AS)

G1056H.d: Γαλιλαία, -ας, ἡ (Heb. הַגָּלִיל, the circle, district), Galilee, the name of the northern region of Palestine in NT times: Γ. τῶν ἐθνῶν, Mat.4:15 (LXX); θάλασσα τῆς Γ., Mat.15:29 (cf. Jhn.6:1). (AS)

G1057.d: Γαλιλαῖος, -αία, -αῖον, Galilæan: Mat.26:69, Mrk.14:70, Luk.13:1, 2 22:59, 23:6, Jhn.4:45, Act.1:11 2:7 5:37.† (AS)

G1058.d: Γαλλίων, -ωνος, ὁ, Gallio, proconsul of Achaia: Act.18:12, 14 17.† (AS)

G1059.d: Γαμαλιήλ, ὁ (Heb. גַּמְלִיאֵל), Gamaliel the elder, a Pharisee and Doctor of the Law: Act.5:34 22:3.† (AS)

G1060.d: γαμέω, -ῶ, to marry; __1. of the man, to marry, take to wife (ducere): absol., Mat.19:10 22:25, 30 24:38, Mrk.12:25, Luk.17:27, 20:34, 35, 1Co.7:28, 33; with accusative: Mat.5:32 19:9, Mrk.6:17 10:11, Luk.14:20 16:18. __2. Of the woman, __(a) mid. (and in late writers, pass.), to give oneself in marriage, marry (nubere): 1Co.7:39; __(b) in Hellenistic (M, Pr., 159), act. (as of the man), to…

G1061.d: γαμίζω (γάμος), to give in marriage, a daughter: 1Co.7:38. Pass., Mat.22:30 24:38, Mrk.12:25, Luk.17:27 20:35 (WH, mg., γαμίσκονται; cf. γαμίζω).† (AS)

G1062.d: γάμος, -ου, ὁ, __1. a wedding, esp. a wedding-feast: Mat.22:8, 10 11, 12, Jhn.2:1-3, Rev.19:7, 9; pl. (Field, Notes, 16), Mat.22:2-4, 9 25:10, Luk.12:36 14:8. __2. marriage: Heb.13:4 (Cremer, 666). † (AS)

G1063.d: γάρ, co-ordinating particle, contr. of γε ἄρα, verily then, hence, in truth, indeed, yea, then, why, and when giving a reason or explanation, for, the usage in NT being in general accord with that of cl.; __1. explicative and epexegetic: Mat.4:18 19:12, Mrk.1:16 5:42 16:4, Luk.11:3o, Rom.7:1, 1Co.16:5, al. __2. Conclusive, in questions, answers and exclamations: Mat.9:5 27:23, Luk.9:25 22:27,…

G1064.d: γαστήρͅ, -τρός, ἡ, __1. the belly: metaphorically, a glutton, Tit.1:12. __2. the womb: ἐν γ. ἔχειν, to be with child, Mat.1:18, 23" (LXX) 24:19, Mrk.13:17, Luk.21:23, 1Th.5:3, Rev.12:2; εν γ. συλλαμβ., to conceive, Luk.1:31. † (AS)

G1065.d: γε, enclitic postpositive particle, rarer in κοινή than in cl., giving special prominence to the word to which it is attached, distinguishing it as the least or the most important (Thayer, see word), indeed, at least, even (but not always translatable into English); __1. used alone: Luk.11:8 18:5 Rom.8:32. __2. More frequently with other particles: αλλά γε, Luk.24:21, 1Co.9:2; ἄρα γε, Mat.7:20…

G1066.d: Γεδεών, ὁ, indecl. in LXX and NT, in FlJ, Ant., see 6, 3 and 4 -ῶνος (Heb. גִּדְעוֹן), Gideon (Jdg.6-8): Heb.11:32.† (AS)

G1067.d: γέεννα (γέενα, Mrk.9:45, Rec.), -ης, ἡ (perh. through Aram. גֵּיהִנָּם, from Heb. גֵּי הִנֹּם, Neh.11:30; גֵּי בֶּן־הִנֹּם, Jhn.18:16; גֵּי בּנֵי־הִנֹּם, 4Ki.23:10; valley of (the son, sons of) lamentation); Gehenna, a valley W. and S. of Jerusalem, which as the site of fire-worship from the time of Ahaz, was desecrated by Josiah and became a dumping-place for the offal of the city. Later, the…

G1068.d: Γεθσημασεί (Rec. -νῆ, LTr. -νεῖ) indecl. (Heb. גֵּת שְׁמָנִי, oil-press), Gethsemane: called in Jhn.18:1 a κῆπος, but named only in Mat.26:36, Mrk.14:32.† (AS)

G1069.d: γείτων, -ονος, ὁ, ἡ (γῆ), a neighbour: Luk.14:12 15:6, 9 Jhn.9:8.† (AS)

G1070.d: γελάω, -ῶ, to laugh: Luk.6:25; fut., γελάσω) (M, Pr., 154), ib. 21 (cf. κατα-γελάω).† (AS)

G1072.d: γεμίζω (γέμω), to fill; __1. properly, of a ship (Thuc, al.): Mrk.4:37 (pass.). __2. In late writers, generally (MGr., see Kennedy, Sources, 155), with accusative, before genitive, Mrk.15:36, Jhn.2:7 6:13, Rev.15:8; ἀπό, Luk.15:16, Rec. WH, mg.; ἐκ, Luk.15:16, WH, Rev.8:5. Pass., absol.: Luk.14:23. † (AS)

G1073.d: γέμω (used only in present and impf.), to be full; __1. properly, of a ship (Xen.). __2. Generally (Plat., al.), __(a) with genitive of thing(s): Mat.23:27, Luk.11:39, Rom.3:14" (LXX), Rev.4:6, 8 5:8 15:7 17:3 (Rec.) 4 21:9 __(b) before ἐκ: Mat.23:25; __(with) with accusative of thing(s) (called a solecism in WM, 251; Bl., §36, 4), as in later Gk. from Byz. to Mod. times (Jannaris, Gr., 1319):…

G1074.d: γενεά, -ᾶς, ἡ (γίγνομαι), __1. race, stock, family (in NT, γέννημα, which see). __2. generation; __(a) of the contemporary members of a family: pl., Mat.1:17 (cf. Gen.31:3, מוֹלֶדֶת); metaphorically, of those alike in character, in bad sense, Mat.17:17, Mrk.9:19, Luk.9:41 16:8, Act.2:40; __(b) of all the people of a given period: Mat.24:34, Mrk.13:30, Luk.21:32, Php.2:15; pl., Luk.1:48; esp. of…

G1075.d: γενεαλογέω, -ῶ (γενεά, λέγω), to trace ancestry, reckon genealogy; pass., before ἐκ: Heb.7:6.† (AS)

G1076.d: γενεαλογία, -ας, ἡ (see previous word); __1. the making of a pedigree. __2. a genealogy: pl., 1Ti.1:4, Tit.3:9 (see CGT, in l., and ib. Intr., xlix ff.; DB, ii, p. 141). † (AS)

G1077.d: γενέσια, -ων, τά, neut. pl. of adj. -ιος, -ον, relating to birth (γένεσις); __1. in Attic Gk., a commemoration of the dead. __2. In late Gk., a birthday feast (= cl. γενέθλια; so in π., see MM, Exp., x; cf. also Ῥutherford, NPhr., 184): Mat.14:6, Mrk.6:21. † (AS)

G1078.d: γένεσις, -εως, ἡ (γίγνομαι), __1. origin, lineage: βίβλος γενέσεως (as in Gen.2:4a 5:1), Mat.1:1. __2. birth: Mat.1:18, Luk.1:14 (Rec. γέννησις); πρόσωπον τῆς γ., face of his birth ("what God made him to be," Hort., in l.), Jas.1:23; ὁ τροχὸς τῆς γ., the wheel (course) of birth or creation ("the wheel of man's nature according to its original Divine purpose," Hort), Jas.3:6. † (AS)

G1079.d: γενετή, -ῆς, ἡ = γενεή, Ion. for γενεά, birth: ἐκ γ., Jhn.9:1.† (AS)

G1080.d: γεννάω, -ῶ (γέννα, poët. for γένος), __1. of the father, to beget: with accusative, Mat.1:1-16, Act.7:8, 29; before ἐκ, Mat.1:3, 5, 6. __2. Of the mother, to bring forth, bear: Luk.1:13, 57 23:29, Jhn.16:21; εἰς δουλείαν, Gal.4:24. Pass. __(1) to be begotten: Mat.1:20; __(2) to be born: Mat.2:1, 4 19:12 26:24, Mrk.14:21, Luk.1:35, Jhn.3:4, Act.7:20, Rom.9:11, Heb.11:23; before εἰς, Jhn.16:21…

G1081.d: γέννημα, -τος, τό (γεννάω), offspring of men or animals: ἐχιδνῶν, Mat.3:7 12:34 23:33, Luk.3:7 (and elsewhere in Rec. for γένημα, which see).† (AS)

G1081G.d: γέννημα, -τος, τό (γεννάω), offspring of men or animals: ἐχιδνῶν, Mat.3:7 12:34 23:33, Luk.3:7 (and elsewhere in Rec. for γένημα, which see).† (AS)

G1082.d: Γεννησαρέτ (Rec. Γενησ-, Mk, l.with; Targ. גְּנֵיסַר), Gennesaret, a fertile plain on W. shore of the Sea of Galilee; ἡ γῆ, Mat.14:34, Mrk.6:53; ἡ λίμνη (יָם כִּנֶּרֶת, Num.34:11, elsewhere ἡ θάλασσα τ. Γαλιλαίας, Mrk.1:16; ἡ θ. τ. Τιβεριάδος, Jhn.6:1), Luk.5:1.† (AS)

G1083.d: γέννησις, -εως, ἡ, __1. begetting. __2. birth: Mat.1:18, Luk.1:14, Rec. † (AS)

G1084.d: γεννητός, -ή -όν (γεννάω), begotten, born: pl., γ. γυναικῶν (cf. יְלוּד אִשָּׁה, Job.14:1), periphrasis for mankind, Mat.11:11, Luk.7:28 (Cremer, 147). (AS)

G1086.d: Γεργασηνός, -ή, -όν, Gerasene, of Gerasa, not the G. of Decapolis, 30 m. S.E. of the Lake, but a Gerasa or Gergesa (perh. the mod. Kersa) on E. shore; as subst., pl. οἱ Γ., Mrk.5:1, Luk.8:26, 37 (Γεργεσηνῶν, RV, mg. 1; Γαδαρηνῶν, RV, mg. 2).† (AS)

G1087.d: γερουσία, -ας, ἡ (γέρων), a council of elders, senate; in NT, of the Sanhedrin (Cl. Rev., i, 43f.; DB, ext., 99): Act.5:21.† (AS)

G1088.d: γέρων, -οντος, ὁ, an old man: Jhn.3:4.† (AS)

G1089.d: γεύω, γεύομαι, to make to taste. Mid., to taste eat: absol., Act.10:10 20:11, Col.2:21; with genitive, Mat.27:34, Luk.14:24, Act.23:14; with accusative (not cl., but see Westc, Heb., l.with; M, Pr., 66, 245), Jhn.2:9. Metaphorical, Heb.6:4; ῥῆμα θεοῦ, Heb.6:5 (on case, see supr., and cf. Milligan, NTD, 68) θανάτου (cf. Talmudic טַעַם מִיתָה), Mat.16:28, Mrk.9:1, Luk.9:27, Jhn.8:52, Heb.2:9;…

G1090.d: γεωργέω, -ῶ (γεωργός), to till the ground: pass., Heb.6:7. (AS)

G1091.d: γεώργιον, -ου, τό (γεωργός), __1. a field (Pro.24:5, 30, Strabo). __2. cultivation, husbandry, tillage (Pro.6:7 9:12, Jer.28:23, Sir.27:6): 1Co.3:9. † (AS)

G1092.d: γεωργός, -οῦ, ὁ (γῆ, ἔργω = ἔρδω, to do), __1. a husbandman: 2Ti.2:6, Jas.5:7. __2. a vine-dresser (cf. ἀμπελουργός, Luk.13:7): Mat.21:33-35, 38, 40, 41, Mrk.12:1, 2 7, 9, Luk.20:9, 10 14, 16, Jhn.15:1. † (AS)

G1093.d: γῆ, γῆς, ἡ, __1. the earth, world: Luk.21:35, Act.1:8, Heb.11:13, Rev.3:10, al.; opposite to οὐρανός, Mat.5:18 11:25, Mrk.13:27, al. __2. land; __(a) opposite to sea or water: Mrk.4:1, Luk.5:3, Jhn.6:21, al.; __(b) as subject to cultivation: Mat.13:5, Mrk.4:8, Luk.13:7, Heb.6:7, al.; __(with) the ground: Mat.10:29, Mrk.8:6, Luk.24:5, Jhn.8:6, al.; __(d) a region, country: Luk.4:25, Rom.9:28,…

G1093G.d: γῆ, γῆς, ἡ, __1. the earth, world: Luk.21:35, Act.1:8, Heb.11:13, Rev.3:10, al.; opposite to οὐρανός, Mat.5:18 11:25, Mrk.13:27, al. __2. land; __(a) opposite to sea or water: Mrk.4:1, Luk.5:3, Jhn.6:21, al.; __(b) as subject to cultivation: Mat.13:5, Mrk.4:8, Luk.13:7, Heb.6:7, al.; __(with) the ground: Mat.10:29, Mrk.8:6, Luk.24:5, Jhn.8:6, al.; __(d) a region, country: Luk.4:25, Rom.9:28,…

G1093H.d: γῆ, γῆς, ἡ, __1. the earth, world: Luk.21:35, Act.1:8, Heb.11:13, Rev.3:10, al.; opposite to οὐρανός, Mat.5:18 11:25, Mrk.13:27, al. __2. land; __(a) opposite to sea or water: Mrk.4:1, Luk.5:3, Jhn.6:21, al.; __(b) as subject to cultivation: Mat.13:5, Mrk.4:8, Luk.13:7, Heb.6:7, al.; __(with) the ground: Mat.10:29, Mrk.8:6, Luk.24:5, Jhn.8:6, al.; __(d) a region, country: Luk.4:25, Rom.9:28,…

G1093I.d: γῆ, γῆς, ἡ, __1. the earth, world: Luk.21:35, Act.1:8, Heb.11:13, Rev.3:10, al.; opposite to οὐρανός, Mat.5:18 11:25, Mrk.13:27, al. __2. land; __(a) opposite to sea or water: Mrk.4:1, Luk.5:3, Jhn.6:21, al.; __(b) as subject to cultivation: Mat.13:5, Mrk.4:8, Luk.13:7, Heb.6:7, al.; __(with) the ground: Mat.10:29, Mrk.8:6, Luk.24:5, Jhn.8:6, al.; __(d) a region, country: Luk.4:25, Rom.9:28,…

G1094.d: γῆρας, Attic, genitive (-αος) -ως, dative ᾳ; Ion. and κοινή, -εος (-ους), dative -ει, τό, old age: ἐν γήρει, Luk.1:36.† (AS)

G1095.d: γηράσκω (also γηράω; γῆρας), to grow old: Jhn.21:18, Heb.8:13.† SYN.: παλαιοῦμαι. (AS)

G1096.d: γίνομαι, Ion. and κοινή for Att. γίγν- (M. Pr., 47; Bl., §6, 8 Mayser, 166 f.), __1. of persons, things occurrences, to come into being, be born, arise, come on: Jhn.1:15 8:58, 1Co.15:37; a first appearance in public, Mrk.1:4, Jhn.1:6, al.; before ἐκ (of birth), Rom.1:3, Gal.4:4; διά, Jhn.1:3; βροντή, Jhn.12:29; σεισμός, Rev.6:12; γογγυσμός, Act.6:1; χαρά, Act.8:8, many other similar exx.; ἡμέρα,…

G1097.d: γινώσκω (= γιγν-: see previous word. So also vulgar Attic, in Inscr., see Thumb, MGV, 207), to be taking in knowledge, come to know, recognize, perceive, understand; in past tenses to know, realize; pass., to become known: with accusative, Mat.22:18, Mrk.5:43, Col.4:8, 1Th.3:5, al. Pass., Mat.10:26, Php.4:5, al.; before ὅτι, Mat.21:45, Jhn.4:1, al.; τί, Mat.6:3; ἀπό, Mrk.15:45; ὅ, Rom.7:15; τ.…

G1098.d: γλεῦκος (-εος), -ους, τό, must, sweet new wine (Arist.): Act.2:13.† (AS)

G1099.d: γλυκύς, -εῖα, -ύ, Jas.3:11, 12; opposite to πικρόν, ἁλυκόν, Rev.10:9, 10.† (AS)

G1100.d: γλῶσσα, -ης, ἡ, __1. the tongue, as the organ of speech: Mrk.7:33, 35 Luk.1:64 16:24, Act.2:26" (LXX), Rom.3:13 (LXX) 14:11 (LXX), 1Co.14:9, Php.2:11, Jas.1:26 3:5, 6 8, 1Pe.3:10" (LXX), 1Jo.3:18, Rev.16:10; of a tongue-like object, Act.2:3. __2. a tongue, language: Act.2:11; joined with φυλή, λαός, ἔθνος, frequently in pl., Rev.5:9 7:9 10:11 11:9 13:7 14:6 17:15; λαλεῖν ἑτέραις γ., Act.2:4; γ.…

G1101.d: γλωσσόκομον, -ου, τό, vernac. form of cl. γλωσσοκομεῖον (γλῶσσα, κομέω), __1. = cl. -εῖον (see supr.), a case for holding the reeds or tongues of musical instruments. __2. As in LXX, π. (MM, see word), a box, chest: Jhn.12:6 13:29. † (AS)

G1102.d: γναφεύς, -έως, ὁ, Ion. and κοινή form of Att. κναφεύς (κνάπτω, to card wool), a fuller, cloth-dresser: Mrk.9:3.† (AS)

G1103.d: γνήσιος, -α, -ον (γίγνομαι), __1. prop., lawfully begotten, born in wedlock (in π., γυνὴ γ., a lawful wife; MM, see word). __2. true, genuine, sincere: Php.4:3, 1Ti.1:2, Tit.1:4; as subst., τὸ γ. = ἡ γνησιότης, sincerity, 2Co.8:8. † (AS)

G1104.d: γνησίως, adv., sincerely, honourably: Phi 2:20 (for a parallel in π., see MM, see word).† (AS)

G1105.d: γνόφος (later form of δν-), darkness, gloom (including "an element of tempest," Tr., Syn., §with): Heb.12:18.† SYN.: ἀχλύς, ζόφος, σκότος (Tr., l.with; DB, i, 457a). (AS)

G1106.d: γνώμη, -ης, ἡ (γιγνώσκω), __1. a means of knowing, a token (Theogn.). __2. In Attic writers, the mind, its operations and results (see Edwards, Lex., App., A); __(a) mind, understanding; __(b) purpose, intention: Act.20:3; __(with) judgment, opinion: 1Co.1:10, Rev.17:13; __(d) counsel, advice: 1Co.7:25, 40 2Co.8:10, Phm 14; __(e) royal purpose, decree (as in Da, I and II Es): Rev.17:17 (Cremer,…

G1107.d: γνωρίζω (γιγνώσκω), __1. as most commonly in cl., to come to know, discover, know: Php.1:22 (but cf. R, mg.). __2. to make known: with accusative, Rom.9:22, 23; with accusative of thing(s) da.t. of person(s), Luk.2:15, Jhn.15:15 17:26, Act.2:28" (LXX), 1Co.15:1, 2Co.8:1, Gal.1:11, Eph.1:9 6:19, 21 Col.4:7, 9 2Pe.1:16; with dative, before ὅτι, 1Co.12:3; before τί, Col.1:27; περί, Luk.2:17. Pass.,…

G1108.d: γνῶσις, -εως, ἡ (γιγνώσκω), __1. a seeking to know, inquiry, investigation. __2. knowledge, in NT, specially of the kn. of spiritual truth: absol., Luk.11:52, Rom.2:20 15:14, 1Co.1:5 (Lft., Notes, 147) 8:1, 7, 10, 11, 13:2, 8 14:6, 2Co.6:6 8:7 11:6, Eph.3:19, Col.2:3, 1Pe.3:7, 2Pe.1:5, 6; with genitive obj., σωτηρίας, Luk.1:77; τ. δόξης τ. θεοῦ, 2Co.4:6; τ. θεοῦ, 2Co.2:14 10:5; Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ,…

G1109.d: γνώστης, -ου, ὁ (γιγνώσκω), one who knows, an expert: Act.26:3.† (AS)

G1110.d: γνωστός, -ή, -όν, later form of γνωστός (γιγνώσκω), known: Act.9:42; with dative, Jhn.18:15, 16 (Rec.), Act.1:19 2:14 4:10 13:38 15:18 19:17 28:22, 28; γ. σημεῖον, a notable (EV) sign, one that is matter of knowledge, Act.4:16; γνωστὸν, Act.15:17, 18; τὸ γνωστὸν θεοῦ, Rom.1:19; in pl., as subst., γνωστοί, acquaintances, Luk.2:44 23:49; so in sing., Jhn.18:16 (WH).† (AS)

G1111.d: γογγύζω, to mutter, murmur: 1Co.10:10; before κατά, Mat.20:11; πρός, Luk.5:30; περί, Jhn.6:41, 61; μετ᾽ ἀλλήλων, Jhn.6:43; with accusative, before περί, Jhn.7:32 (cf. δια-γογγύζω).† (AS)

G1112.d: γογγυσμός, -οῦ, ὁ, a murmuring, muttering: Jhn.7:12, Act.6:1; ἄνευ γ., 1Pe.4:9; pl., χωρὶς γ., Php.2:14.† (AS)

G1113.d: γογγυστής, -οῦ, ὁ (γογγύζω); [in Sm.: Pro.26:22, Isa.29:24; Th.: Pro.26:20 * ;] a murmurer: Ju 16.† (AS)

G1114.d: γόης, -ητος, ὁ (γοάω, to wail), __1. a wailer. __2. a wizard. __3. an impostor (cf. γοητεία, trickery, 2Ma.12:24): 2Ti.3:13. † (AS)

G1115.d: Γολγοθά (Rec. -θᾶ; WH, mg., Γολγόθ, Jo, l.with, Aram. גָּלְגָּלְתָּא = Heb. גֻּלְגֹּלֶת, LXX, κρανίον, Jdg.9:53, 2Ki.9:35); indecl. (exc. Mrk.15:22, -άν), Golgotha, the place of the crucifixion: Mat.27:33, Mrk.15:22, Jhn.19:17.† (AS)

G1116.d: Γόμορρα, -ας, ἡ, and -ων, τά (Heb. עֲמֹרָה), Gomorrah, one of the cities of the plain (Gen.19): Mat.10:15, Rom.9:29" (LXX), 2Pe.2:6, Ju 7.† (AS)

G1117.d: γόμος, -ου, ὁ (γέμω), a ship's freight, cargo: Act.21:3, Rev.18:11, 12.† (AS)

G1118.d: γονεύς, -έως, ὁ (γίγνομαι), a begetter, a father; mostly in pl., οἱ γ., parents: Luk.2:41, 43 8:56 21:16, Jhn.9:2, 3 20, 22, 23 Rom.1:30, 2Co.12:14, Eph.6:1, Col.3:20, 2Ti.3:2; accusative pl. (Hellenistic, see Thackeray, Gr., i, 148), γονεῖς, Mat.10:21, Mrk.13:22, Luk.2:27 18:29, Jhn.9:18.† (AS)

G1119.d: γόνυ, -ατος, τό, the knee: Heb.12:12; of a suppliant, προσπίπτειν τοῖς γ., Luk.5:8; so also τιθέναι τὰ γ., to kneel: Luk.22:41, Act.7:60 9:40 20:36 21:5; in mockery, Mrk.15:19; κάμπτειν τὰ γ., to bend the knee: Rom.11:4 (LXX) 14:11 (LXX), Eph.3:14, Php.2:10.† (AS)

G1120.d: γονυπετέω, -ῶ) (γόνυ, πίπτω); __1. to fall on the knees: before ἔμπροσθεν, Mat.27:29. __2. to fall down before one: with accusative, Mat.17:14, Mrk.1:40, R, txt., 10:17. † (AS)

G1121.d: γράμμα, -τος, τό (γράφω), __1. that which is traced or drawn, a picture. __2. that which is written; __(1) a character, letter: Gal.6:11; __(2) a writing, a written document; __(a) a bill or account: Luk.16:6, 7; __(b) a letter: Act.28:21; __(with) τὰ ἱερὰ γ., the sacred writings, i.e. the OT: 2Ti.3:15 (so in Philo, Vit. Mos., iii, 39) ; __(d) τὸ γ., the letter, the written word as an external…
