So Jdg.5:14, 4Ki.25:19 (ספר), al. __3. a scribe, a biblical scholar, teacher of the law (so first in I Est.8:3, II Est.7:6; in Luk.5:17, νομοδιδάσκαλος; in Luk.10:25, νομικός): Mat.7:29, Mrk.1:22, and frequently in…

G1124.d: γραφή, -ῆς, ἡ (γράφω), __1. a drawing, painting. __2. __(a) writing; __(b) that which is written, a writing: πᾶσα γ., 2Ti.3:16; γ. ἅγιαι, Rom.1:2; προφητικαί, Rom.16:26; al αἱ γ. τ. προφητῶν, Mat.26:56; ἡ γ., αἱ γ., the sacred writings, the Scriptures (i.e. the OT; see Milligan, NTD, 205); in pl., when the sacred writings as a whole are meant, e.g. Mat.21:42 26:54, Jhn.5:39, Rom.15:4; in sing.,…

G1125.d: γράφω, ; __1. to scrape, graze (Hom.), and later (Hdt.) to sketch, draw. __2. to write; __(a) of forming or tracing letters on writing material: Jhn.8:[6], Gal.6:11, 2Th.3:17; __(b) to express in writing, commit to writing, record: Luk.1:63, Jhn.19:21, 22 Rev.1:11, 19 al.; of scripture as a standing authority (Deiss., BS, 112ff.), γέγραπται, it stands written (Luther), Mat.4:4, Mrk.7:6, Luk.4:8,…

G1126.d: γραώδης, -ες (γραῦς, an old woman, εἶδος), anile, old-womanish: 1Ti.4:7.† (AS)

G1127.d: γρηγορέω, -ῶ, = Attic ἐργήγορα, pf. of ἐγείρω, which see, __1. to be awake; metaphorically, of being alive, 1Th.5:10. __2. to watch: Mat.24:43 26:38, 40 Mrk.13:34 14:34, 37 Luk.12:37, 39; metaphorically, Mat.24:42 25:13 26:41, Mrk.13:35, 37 14:38, Act.20:31, 1Co.16:13, 1Th.5:6, 1Pe.5:8, Rev.3:2, 3 16:15; before ἐν, Col.4:2. (Cf. δια-γρηγορέω).† SYN.: see: ἀγρθπνέω. (AS)

G1128.d: γυμνάζω (γυμνός), __1. properly, to exercise naked. __2. Generally, to exercise, train the body or mind: 1Ti.4:7, Heb.5:14 12:11, 2Pe.2:14. † (AS)

G1130.d: γυμνιτεύω (Rec. γυμνητ-, V. Tdf ., Pr., 81), to be naked or scantily clad: 1Co.4:11 (cf. ἐν ψύχει κ. γυμνότητι), 2Co.11:27; γυμνοί, Jas.2:15. In κοινή writers, γ. also means to go light-armed.† (AS)

G1131.d: γυμνός, -ή, -όν, naked, without clothing, and sometimes (as frequently in cl.) scantily or poorly clad (Isa.20:2ff., Tob.1:16, 2Ma.11:12): Mat.25:36, 38 43, 44, Mrk.14:52, Jhn.21:7, Act.19:16, Jas.2:15, Rev.3:17 16:15, 17:16; as subst., to γ., the naked body, Mrk.14:51. Metaphorical, of things exposed, Heb.4:13; of the soul without a body (Plat., Crat., with, 20, and cf. Deiss., LAE, 293),…

G1133.d: γυναικάριον, -ου, τό (diminutive of γυνή), a little woman; contemptuously, a silly woman (EV): 2Ti.3:6.† (AS)

G1135G.d: γυνή, -αικός, ἡ, __1. a woman, married or unmarried: Mat.11:11 14:21, al.; ὕπανδρος γ., Rom.7:2; γ. χήρα, Luk.4:26; in vocat., γύναι implies neither reproof nor severity, but is used frequently as a term of respect and endearment, Mat.15:28, Jhn.2:4, 4:21 19:26. __2. a wife: Mat.1:20, 1Co.7:3, 4 al.; γ. ἀπολύειν, Mrk.10:2, al.; γ. ἔχειν Mrk.6:18; γ. λαβεῖν, Mrk.12:19; γ. γαμεῖν, Luk.14:20. __3. a…

G1136.d: Γώγ, ὁ (Heb. גּוֹג), indecl., Gog, assoc. with Magog (q.v): Rev.20:8.† (AS)

G1137.d: γωνία, -ας, ἡ (γόνυ), an angle, a corner: Mat.6:5, Act.26:26; τ. τέσσαρας γ. τ. γῆς, Rev.7:1, 20:8; κεφαλὴ γνωνίας (רֹאשׁ פִּנָּה, Ps 117(118):22, LXX), Mat.21:42, Mrk.12:10, Luk.20:17, Act.4:11, 1Pe.2:7.† (AS)

G1138.d: Δαυείδ (Rec. Δαβίδ), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. דָּוִד), David, King of Israel: Mat.1:6; 12:3, and al.; σκηνὴ Δ., Act.15:16; κλεὶς Δ., Rev.3:7; θρόνος Δ., Luk.1:32; ῥίζα Δ., Rev.5:5; βασιλεία Δ., Mrk.11:10; υἱὸς Δ., the Messiah (Ps. Sol., 17:23; for other reff. in Jewish lit., see Dalman, Words, 317), Mat.1:1 9:27, and al.; ἐν Δ., i.e. the Psalter, Heb.4:7 (AS)

G1139.d: δαιμονίζομαι (in cl. also δαιμονάω; δαίμων), [in Aq.: Ps 90(91):6 * ;] to be under the power of a δαίμων (δαιμόνιον, which see), to be possessed: Mat.15:22; elsewhere always ptcp., -ιζόμενος, -ισθείς: Mat.4:24; 8:16, 28, 33 9:32 12:22, Mrk.1:32 15 16 18, Luk.8:36, Jhn.10:21 (Cremer, 171).† (AS)

G1140.d: δαιμόνιον, -ου, τό (neut. of δαιμόνιος, -α, -ον, divine), __1. as in cl.; __(a) the Divine power, Deity (Hdt., Plat., al.); __(b) an inferior divinity, deity or demon (as in magical π, Deiss., BS, 281; MM, Exp., x): ξένα δ., Act.17:18. __2. (a) in OT, heathen deities, false gods (e.g. Deu.32:17, Psa.95 (96):5); __(b) in NT, evil spirits, demons: θύουσιν δαιμονίοις, 1Co.10:20; διδασκαλίαι…

G1141.d: δαιμονιώδης, -ες (δαιμόνιον, εἶδος), [in Sm.: Ps 90(91):6 * ;] demon-like: Jas.3:15 (Cremer, 171).† (AS)

G1142.d: δαίμων, -ονος, ὁ, ἡ in cl. and NT = δαιμόνιον; a demon: Mat.8:31.† (AS)

G1144.d: δάκρυον (poët. form δάκρυ), -ου, τό, a tear: Mrk.9:24 (WH, txt., R, txt. omit), Act.20:19, 31, 2Co.2:4, 2Ti.1:4, Heb.5:7 12:17, Rev.7:17 21:4; metaphorically, dative pl., δάκρυσι (La 2:11, Thuc., vii, 75; Bl., § 9, 3), Luk.7:38, 44.† (AS)

G1145.d: δακρύω to weep, shed tears: Jhn.11:35.† SYN.: κλαίω, of audible weeping, to cry; ὀδύρομαι, of grief expressed verbally, to lament; θρηνέω, of formal lamentation, to sing a dirge; ἀλαλάζω, to wail in Oriental fashion; στενάζω, of grief expressed by inarticulate sounds, to groan. (AS)

G1309.d: δια-φεύγω to flee through, escape: Act.27:42.† (AS)

G1310.d: δια-φημίζω in late writers only, to spread abroad: τ. λόγον (= דָּבָר, the matter), Mrk.1:45, Mat.28:15; with accusative of person(s), to spread abroad one's fame: Mat.9:31.† (AS)

G1311.d: δια-φθείρω __1. to destroy utterly: Luk.12:33, Rev.11:18; pass., to be destroyed, disabled: Rev.8:9, 2Co.4:16. __2. In moral sense, to corrupt, deprave: τ. γῆν, Rev.11:18; pass., διεφθαρμένοι τ. νοῦν, 1Ti.6:5.† (AS)

G1312.d: δια-φθορὰ, -ᾶς, ἡ (διαφθείρω), __1. destruction. __2. corruption (physical or moral): of the grave, Act.2:27 (LXX), Act.2:31 13:34-37.† (AS)

G1313.d: διά-φορος, -ον (διαφέρω), __1. different: Rom.12:6, Heb.9:10. __2. excellent: compar., -ώτερος, Heb.1:4 8:6.† (AS)

G1314.d: δια-φυλάσσω to guard carefully (M, Pr., 116), defend: with accusative, Luk.4:10 (LXX).† (AS)

G1315.d: δια-χειρίζω (χείρ), to have in hand, conduct, manage. Mid. __(a) = act.; __(b) in late writers (Polyb., FlJ, al.), to lay hands on, kill: with accusative, Act.5:30 26:21.† (AS)

G1316.d: δια-χωρίζω to separate entirely. Mid., to separate oneself, depart: before ἀπό Luk.9:33.† (AS)

G1317.d: διδακτικός, -ή, -όν (= cl. διδασκαλικός) apt at teaching: 1Ti.3:2, 2Ti.2:24.† (AS)

G1318.d: διδακτός, -ή, -όν (διδάσκω), __1. that can be taught. __2. taught; with genitive, of source of teaching (in cl., poët. only); __(a) of persons: δ. θεοῦ, Jhn.6:45 (LXX); __(b) of things, λόγοις δ. πνεύματος, 1Co.2:13.† (AS)

G1319.d: διδασκαλία, -ας, ἡ (διδάσκω), teaching, instruction, in both active and objective senses, most frequently the latter: Rom.12:7 15:4, Eph.4:14, 1Ti.4:6, 13, 16 5:17 6:1, 3, 2Ti.3:10 3:16, Tit.2:7, 10; ὑγιαινοῦσα δ., 1Ti.1:10, 2Ti.4:3, Tit.1:9 2:1; pl., δ. τ. ἀνθρώπων, Col.2:22; δ. δαιμονίων, 1Ti.4:1, δ. διδάσκειν, Mat.15:9, Mrk.7:7" (LXX) (Cremer, 182).† SYN.: διδαχή (AS)

G1320.d: διδάσκαλος, -ου, ὁ (διδάσκω), given as rendering of Heb. רַבִּי ,רַבּוֺן (NT, Ῥαββεί, Ῥαββουνεί which see); a teacher: Jhn.1:39 20:16; of Jewish teachers, Luk.2:46, Jhn.3:10, cf. Rom.2:20-21; of John Baptist, Luk.3:12; of Jesus, Jhn.3:2, 10 8:4 11:28 13:13-14, and often in Syn., most frequently in voc., as title of address, as Mat.8:19, Mrk.4:38; of Jesus by himself, Mat.23:8; of an apostle,…

G1321.d: διδάσκω to teach (i.e. instruct) a person, teach a thing; __1. trans.: with accusative of person(s), Mat.5:2, Mrk.1:22, al.; before ὅτι, Mrk.8:31; περί, 1Jn.2:27; with inf., Luk.11:1; with accusative of thing(s), Mrk.6:30 12:14; with cogn. accusative, Mat.15:9 (LXX); with dupl. accusative, Mrk.4:2, Jhn.14:26; pass., Gal.1:12, 2Th.2:15; with dative of person(s) (like Heb., cf. Job.21:23, but prob.…

G1322.d: διδαχή, -ῆς, ἡ (διδάσκω), __1. objectively, teaching, doctrine, that which is taught: Mrk.1:27, Jhn.7:16, Act.17:19, Rom.6:7 16:17, 2Jn.10, Rev.2:24; with genitive poss., Mat.7:28 16:12 22:33, Mrk.1:22 11:18, Luk.4:32, Jhn.18:19, Act.5:28, Rev.2:14-15; ἡ δ., of Christ, Jhn.7:17, Act.13:12, 2Jn.9; of. τὴν δ., Tit.1:9; with genitive obj., βαπτισμῶν δ., Heb.6:2; pl., Heb.13:9. __2. Actively,…

G1323.d: δίδραχμος, -ον (δίς, δραχμή), worth two drachmae; τὸ δ. (sc. νόμισμα, coin), a double drachma, nearly equal to the Jewish half-shekel, the amount of the Temple tax: Mat.17:24 (DB, iii, 428).† (AS)

G1324.d: Δίδυμος, -ου, ὁ (prop. name from δίδυμος, -η, -ον, double, sc. παῖς, twin) Didymus, surname of the apostle Thomas: Jhn.11:16 20:24 21:2.† (AS)

G1325.d: δίδωμι, to give—in various senses, accusative to context—bestow, grant, supply, deliver, commit, yield: absol., Act.20:35; with accusative of thing(s) and dative of person(s), Mat.4:9 5:31, Jhn.1:12, al. mult.; with dative of person(s), before ἐκ, Mat.25:8; id. with genitive part.. Rev.2:17; with accusative of person(s), Jhn.3:16, Rev.20:13, al.; δεξιάς, Gal.2:9; φίλημα, Luk.7:45; γνῶσιν,…

G1326.d: δι-εγείρω to arouse completely, arouse as from rest or sleep: Luk.8:24; pass., Mrk.4:39, Luk.8:24; of the sea, Jhn.6:18. Metaphorical, of the mind: ἐν ὑπομνήσει, 2Pe.1:13 3:1.† (AS)

G1327.d: δι-έ-οδος, -ου, ἡ in π. of the conclusion of a trial (MM, Exp., xi); a way out through, an outlet; pl., δ. τῶν ὁδῶν, RV, the partings of the highways: Mat.22:9.† (AS)

G1329.d: δι-ερμηνεύω intensive of ἐρμηνεύω, to interpret; __(a) to explain, expound: with accusative, Luk.24:27; absol., 1Co.12:30 14:5 14:13 14:27; __(b) to translate: Act.9:36.† (AS)

G1330.d: δι-έρχομαι __1. to go through, pass through; __(a) of things: Mat.19:24, Mrk.10:25, Luk.2:35, al.; __(b) of persons: Luk.19:4; with accusative loc., Luk.19:1, Heb.4:14, Act.12:10; before διά, with genitive loc., Mat.12:43, 1Co.10:1; before εἰς, Mrk.4:35; ἕως, Luk.2:15. __2. to go about: Luk.9:6, Act.20:25; of a report, to spread, go abroad (Thuc.), Luk.5:15 (AS)

G1331.d: δι-ερωτάω, -ῶ to find by inquiry: with accusative, Act.10:17.† (AS)

G1332.d: διετής, -ές (δίς, ἔτος), __1. lasting two years. __2. two years old: ἀπὸ δ. (sc. παιδός, or neuter; cf. 1Ch.27:23, ἀπὸ εἰκοσαετοῦς), Mat.2:16.† (AS)

G1333.d: διετία, -ας, ἡ (διετής), the space of two years: Act.24:27 28:30.† (AS)

G1334.d: δι-ηγέομαι, -οῦμαι to set out in detail, recount, describe: absol., Heb.11:32; with accusative of thing(s), Act.8:33; with dative of person(s), before πῶς, Mrk.5:16, Act.9:27 12:17; ἅ εἶδον, Mrk.9:9; ὅσα ἐποίησε, -αν, Luk.8:39 9:10.† (AS)

G1335.d: δι-ήγησις, -εως, ἡ (διηγέομαι), a narrative: Luk.1:1 (cf. Milligan, NTD, 130).† (AS)

G1336.d: δι-ηνεκής, -ές (διήνεγκα, aorist of διαφέρω) [in Sm.: Psa.48:15, 89:30 ;] unbroken, continuous: adverbially, εἰς τὸ δ., continually (for exx., see Deiss., BS, 251), Heb.7:3 10:1, 12 10:14† (AS)

G1337.d: διθάλασσος, -ον (δις, θύλασσα); __1. divided into two seas (as the Euxine, Strab., ii, 522). __2. dividing the sea: τόπον δ., a tongue of land, or reef, running out into the sea: Act.27:41.† (AS)

G1338.d: δι-ικνέομαι (Rec. διϊκ-), -οῦμαι, to go through, penetrate: Heb.4:12.† (AS)

G1339.d: δι-ίσπημι (Rec. διΐσ), to set apart, separate; of time (or space), to make an interval, intervene: διαστάσης ὥρας μιᾶς, Luk.22:59; βραχὺ διαστήσαντες, Act.27:28. In pass., mid. and 2 aor., pf. and plpf. act., to part, withdraw: Luk.24:51.† (AS)

G1340.d: δι-ισχυρίζομαι (T, Rec. διϊσ-), depon.; __1. to lean upon. __2. to affirm confidently: with ptcp., Luk.22:59; with accusative and inf. (Bl., § 70, 3), Act.12:15.† (AS)

G1341.d: δικαιοκρισία, -ας, ἡ righteous judgment: Rom.2:5 (cf. τ. δικαίας κρίσεως, 2Th.1:5; τὴν δ. κ., Jhn.7:24. For use in π., see Deiss., LAE, 89 f.).† (AS)

G1342.d: δίκαιος, -α, -ον (δίκη), in early Gk. writers __(a) of persons, observant of δίκη, custom, rule, right, righteous in performing duties to gods and men ; __(b) of things, righteous, in accordance with right. In NT __1. righteous, chiefly in the broad sense, as above, of the person or thing corresponding to the Divine standard of right __(a) of persons: of God, Rom.3:26, 1Jn.2:29 Jn 3:7; of Christ,…

G1343.d: δικαιοσύνη, -ης, ἡ (δίκαιος), the character of ὁ δίκαιος (which see) __1. in broad sense, righteousness, conformity to the Divine will in purpose, thought and action: Mat.5:6, Jhn.16:8, Act.13:10, Rom.4:3; λόγος δικαιοσύνης, teaching of r., Heb.5:13; βασιλεὺς δ. (cf. FlJ, BJ, vi, 10, β. δίκαιος), Heb.7:2; ὅπλα δ., Rom.6:13; ὁδὸς δ., Mat.21:32; θώραξ τῆς δ., Eph.6:14; διὰκονοι δ., 2Co.11:15;…

G1344.d: δικαιόω, -ῶ (δίκαιος), __1. in cl., __(a) with accusative of thing(s), to deem right; __(b) with accusative of person(s), to do one justice; pass., δικαιοῦσθαι, to be treated rightly, opposite to ἀδικεῖσθαι. __2. In NT, as in LXX, and as usual with verbs in -όω from adjectives of moral meaning; __(1) to show to be righteous: Mat.11:19, Luk.7:35, Rom.3:4" (LXX), 1Ti.3:16; __(2) to declare,…

G1345.d: δικαίωμα, -τος, τ (δικαιόω), a concrete expression of righteousness, the expression and result of the act of δικαίωσις, "a declaration that a thing is δίκαιον, or that a person is δίκαιος," hence, __(a) an ordinance: δ. τ. θεοῦ, Rom.1:32; τ. κυρίου, Luk.1:6; τ. νόμου, Rom.2:26 8:4; λατρείας, Heb.9:1; σαρκός, Heb.9:10; __(b) a sentence: of acquittal, Rom.5:16 (also Rom.5:18; ICC, in l), or of…

G1346.d: δικαίως adv. (δίκαιος, which see), __1. righteously: 1Co.15:34, 1Th.2:10, Tit.2:12. __2. justly: Luk.23:41, 1Pe.2:23.† (AS)

G1347.d: δικαίωσις, -εως, ἡ (δικαιόω), the act of pronouncing righteous, justification, acquittal: Rom.4:25 5:18 (Cremer, 199).† (AS)

G1348.d: δικαστής, -οῦ, ὁ (δικάζω), a judge: Act.7:27, 35" (LXX) .† SYN.: κριτής, WH. "gives prominence to the mental process" (Thayer). δ. is the forensic term. In Attic law, the δικασταί were jurors, with a κριτής as presiding officer (LS, see word; Enc. Brit. 11, xii, 504 f.) (AS)

G1349.d: δίκη, -ης, ἡ __1. custom. __2. right. __3. a judicial hearing; hence its result, the execution of a sentence, punishment: δ. τίνειν, 2Th.1:9; δ. υπεχειν, Ju 7. __4. Personified (cf. Lat. Justitia), justice, vengeance: Act.28:4.† (AS)

G1350.d: δίκτυον, -ον, τό general term for a net: Mat.4:20-21, Mrk.1:18-19, Luk.5:2, 4-6, Jhn.21:6, 8 21:11 † SYN.: ἀμφίβληστρον (which see), σαγήνη. (AS)

G1351.d: διλογος, -ον (δίς, λέγω), __1. in sense of διλογεῖν, -ία (Xen.), given to repetition. __2. In NT, prob. (cf. δίγλωσσος, Pro.11:13, Sir.5:9) double-tongued: 1Ti.3:8.† (AS)

G1352.d: διό conjunct. for δι᾽ ὅ, wherefore, on which account: Mat.27:8, Luk.7:7, Act.15:19, Rom.1:24, al.; δ. καί, Luk.1:35, Act.10:29 24:26, Rom.4:22 15:22, 2Co.1:20 4:13 5:9, Php.2:9, Heb.11:12 13:12 (see Ellic. on Gal.4:31). (AS)

G1352 G2532.d: διό conjunct. for δι᾽ ὅ, wherefore, on which account: Mat.27:8, Luk.7:7, Act.15:19, Rom.1:24, al.; δ. καί, Luk.1:35, Act.10:29 24:26, Rom.4:22 15:22, 2Co.1:20 4:13 5:9, Php.2:9, Heb.11:12 13:12 (see Ellic. on Gal.4:31). (AS)

G1353.d: δι-οδεύω, __1. to travel through: with accusative, Act.17:1 __2. to travel along (Bar.4:2, 1Ma.12:32-33): Luk.8:1.† (AS)

G1354.d: Διονύσιος, -ου, ὁ Dionysius, an Athenian: Act.17:34.† (AS)

G1355.d: διό-περ conjunct. (διό, which see, strengthened by πέρ), for which very reason: 1Co.8:13 10:14.† (AS)

G1356.d: διοπετής (written also διϊπ-), -ές (δῖος, πίπτω, see Page on Ac, l.with; DB, i, 605, n., ext., 112a; Field, Notes, 130 f.), fallen from heaven (R, mg.): τὸ δ. (sc. ἄγαλμα, statue, image), Act.19:35.† (AS)

G1357.d: διόρθωσις, -εως, ἡ (see supr.), __1. a making straight. __2. a reforming, reformation (used in late writers of laws, etc.): Heb.9:10 (Cremer, 807).† διόρθωμα, -τος, τό (διορθόω, to make straight, set right), a correction, reform: Act.24:3.† διόρθωσις, -εως, ἡ (see supr.), __1. a making straight. __2. a reforming, reformation (used in late writers of laws, etc.): Heb.9:10 (Cremer, 807).† (AS)

G1358.d: δι-ορύσσω to dig through: with accusative, of house-breaking (as in π.; MM, Exp., xi), Mat.24:43, Luk.12:39; absol., Mat.6:19-20.† (AS)

G1359.d: Διόσ-κουροι, -ων, οἱ (Ion. and κοινή form of Att..., Διόσκοροι; Διός, genitive of Ζεύς + κόρος, a son), the Dioscuri (Castor and Pollux), twin sons of Zeus and Leda (RV, The Twin Brothers): Act.28:11.† (AS)

G1360.d: δι-ότι , conjunct., for διὰ τοῦτο, ὅτι (Lat. propterea quod), because: Luk.1:13 2:7 21:28, Act.13:35 18:10 20:26 22:18, Rom.1:19, 21 3:20 8:7, 21, 1Co.15:9, Php.2:26, 1Th.2:8, 18 (Lft., Notes, 37) 1Th.4:6, Heb.11:5, 23, Jas.4:3, 1Pe.1:16 1:24 2:6. It is usually stronger than ὅτι, but sometimes, as in Luk.1:13, Rom.1:19, 1Th.2:18, approximates to MGr. sense, for; cf. Milligan, Th., l.with† (AS)

G1361.d: Διοτρέφης (Rec. -τρεψής), -ες (Διός, genitive of Ζεύς + τρέφω: cherished by Zeus), as proper name, Diotrephes: III Jn 9.† (AS)

G1362.d: διπλόος (poët., διπλός, whence corp. -ότερον), -όη, -όον (-οῦ, -ῆ, -οῦν) twofold, double: 1Ti.5:17, Rev.18:6; διπλότιρον, in twofold measure: Mat.23:15.† (AS)

G1363.d: διπλόω, -ῶ (δυτλόος), to double: δ. τὰ διπλᾶ, Rev.18:6.† (AS)

G1364.d: δίς adv., twice: Mrk.14:30, 72; δ. τ. σαββάτου, Luk.18:12; καὶ ἅπαξ κ. δ., Php.4:16, 1Th.2:18; δ. ἀποθανόντα, Ju 12 (see Mayor, ICC, in l); δ. μυριάδες, Rev.9:16.† (AS)

G1365.d: διστάζω (δίς), to doubt, hesitate: Mat.14:31 28:17.† SYN.: ἀπορέω, διαπορέω, διακρίνομαι, μετεωρίζομαι (see DCG, i, 491) (AS)

G1366.d: δίστομος, -ον (δίς, στόμα), __1. of rivers and roads, double-mouthed, double branching. __2. Of swords (Eur.; LXX, ll with), two-edged: Heb.4:12, Rev.1:16 2:12.† (AS)

G1367.d: two thousand , (Herdotus Historicus):—;singular with collective nouns, δισχιλίη ἵππος 2000 horse, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G1368.d: δι-υλίζω (δια, ὑλίζω, to strain) __1. to strain thoroughly (Archytas; Am., l.with). __2. Later, to strain out: figuratively, Mat.23:24.† (AS)

G1369.d: διχάζω (δίχα, apart), [in Aq.: Lev.1:17, Deu.14:6 * ;] to cut apart, divide in two; metaphorically, to set at variance: Mat.10:35.† (AS)

G1370.d: διχοστασία, -ας, ἡ (διχοστατέω, to stand apart), standing apart, dissension: Rom.16:17, Gal.5:20.† (AS)

G1371.d: διχοτομέω, -ῶ (διχοτόμος, δίχα, τέμνω), to cut in two, cut asunder: perh. metaphorically of severe scourging (but see Meyer on Mt, l.with, and cf. 1Ki.15:33, 2Ki.12:31, Heb.11:37), Mat.24:51, Luk.12:46.† (AS)

G1372.d: διψάω,-ῶ (δίψα, thirst), to thirst: absol., Mat.25:35, 37 25:42, 44, Jhn.4:13, 15 19:28, Rom.12:20" (LXX), 1Co.4:11; figuratively, Jhn.4:14 6:35 7:37, Rev.7:16 21:6 22:17; with accusative (= cl. with genitive), τ. δικαιοσύνην, Mat.5:6.† (AS)

G1373.d: δίψος, -εος (-ους), τό (late form of δίψα), thirst: 2Co.11:27.† (AS)

G1374.d: δίψυχος, -ον (δίς, ψυχή), of two minds, wavering: Jas.1:8 4:8 (Cremer, 588; DB, iv, 528).† (AS)

G1375.d: διωγμός, -oῦ, ὁ (διώκω), persecution: Mat.13:21, Mrk.4:17 10:30 Act.8:1 13:50, Rom.8:35, 2Co.12:10, 2Th.1:4, 2Ti.3:11.† (AS)

G1377.d: διώκω __1. to put to flight, drive away: Mat.23:34. __2. to pursue; __(a) of persons; with accusative, without hostility, to follow after: Luk.17:23; with hostile purpose: Act.26:11, Rev.12:13. Hence, to persecute: Mat.5:10-12, 44 10:23, Luk.11:49 21:12, Jhn.5:16 15:20, Act.7:52 9:4-5 22:4, 7-8 26:14-15 Rom.12:14, 1Co.4:12 15:9, 2Co.4:9, Gal.1:13, 23 4:29 5:11 6:12, Php.3:6, 2Ti.3:12; __(b)…

G1378.d: δόγμα, -τος, τό (δοκέω), __1. an opinion. __2. A public decree, ordinance: of Roman rulers, Luk.2:1, Act.17:7; of the Jewish law, Eph.2:15, Col.2:14; of the Apostles, Act.16:4 (Cremer, 205).† (AS)

G1379.d: δογματίζω to decree. Mid., to subject oneself to an ordinance: Col.2:20.† (AS)

G1380.d: δοκέω, -ῶ (δόκος, opinion, δέκομαι, Ion, form of δέχ-), __1. to be of opinion, suppose: Mat.24:44, Luk.12:40, Heb.10:29; with inf., Mat.3:9, Luk.8:18 24:37, Jhn.5:39 16:2, Act.12:9 27:13, 1Co.3:18 7:40 8:2 10:12 14:37, Gal.6:3, Php.3:4, Jas.1:26; with accusative and inf., 1Co.12:23, 2Co.11:16; before ὅτι, Mat.6:7 26:53, Mrk.6:49, Luk.12:51 13:2, 4 19:11, Jhn.5:45 11:13, 31 13:29 20:15, 1Co.4:9,…

G1381.d: δοκιμάζω (δόκιμος), __1. primarily of metals (Pro.8:10 17:3, Sir.2:5, Wis.3:6), to test, try, prove (in the hope and expectation that the test will prove successful, see reff. s. Syn.): χρυσίον, 1Pe.1:7; other things, Luk.12:56 14:19, 2Co.8:8, Gal.6:4, 1Th.2:4 5:21; τὰ διαφέροντα, Rom.2:18, Php.1:10 (R, mg., but see infr.); πνεύματα, 1Jn.4:1; of men, 1Ti.3:10 (pass.); ἑαυτόν, 1Co.11:28, 2Co.13:5;…

G1382.d: δοκιμή, -ῆς, ἡ (δόκιμος), [in Sm.: Psa.68:31 * ;] __1. the process of trial, proving, test: 2Co.8:2 9:13 __2. The result of trial, approval, approvedness, proof: Rom.5:4, 2Co.2:9 13:3, Php.2:22 (Cremer, 212, 701).† (AS)

G1383.d: δοκίμιον, -ου, τό usually regarded as a variant form of δοκιμεῖον, a test, and so perh. Jas.1:3 (see Mayor, in l), but see next word (cf. Cremer, 212, 702).† (AS)

G1384.d: δοκίμιος, -α, -ον (δοκιμή), = δόκιμος, tested, approved: τὸ δ. ὑμῶν τ. πίστεως, that which is approved in your faith, 1Pe.1:7 (where Hort suggests the seel. δόκιμος, found in some cursives), Jas.1:3 (but see Mayor, in l For full discussion of this word, not hitherto found in a Gk. Lexicon, and for exx. of its use in π., see Deiss. (to whom is due the credit of its discovery), BS, 259 ff.; MM,…

G1385.d: δοκός, -οῦ, ἡ (δέχομαι) a beam of timber: Mat.7:3-5, Luk.6:41-42 (DCG, i, 176).† (AS)

G1387.d: δολιόω (δόλιος), to deceive: ἐδολιοῦσαν (-σαν, frequently in κοινή Gk. for imperfect 3rd of person(s) pl.), Rom.3:13 (LXX).† (AS)

G1388.d: δόλος, -ου, ὁ, __1. in Hom., a bait. __2. a snare. __3. In the abstract, craft, deceit: Mat.26:4, Mrk.7:22 14:1, Jhn.1:47, Act.13:10, Rom.1:29, 2Co.12:16, 1Th.2:3, 1Pe.2:1 2:22 3:10" (LXX) (λαλῆσαι δ.).† (AS)

G1389.d: δολόω, -ῶ (δόλος) __1. to ensnare. __2. As of wine, to adulterate, corrupt: τ. λόγον τ. θεοῦ, 2Co.4:2.† SYN.: καπηλεύω which see (AS)

G1390.d: δόμα, -τος, τό (δίδωμι), a gift: Mat.7:11, Luk.11:13, Eph.4:8" (LXX), Php.4:17.† SYN.: δόσις, δῶρον, δωρεά, δώρημα (AS)

G1790.d: ἔν-τρομος, -ον trembling with fear (Pint.): Act.7:32 16:29, Heb.12:21 (ἔκτρ-, WH, mg.).† (AS)

G1791.d: ἐν-τροπή, -ῆς, ἡ __1. with genitive of person(s), respect, reverence (Soph., Polyb., al.). __2. Absol., shame (Hipp.): 1Co.6:5 15:34.† (AS)

G1792.d: ἐν-τρυφάω, ῶ to revel in: ἐν-τ. ἀπάταις, 2Pe.2:13 (see Mayor, in l).† (AS)

G1793.d: ἐν-τυγχάνω __1. to fall in with. __2. to meet with in order to converse. __3. to petition, make petition: with dative of person(s), before ὑπέρ with genitive of person(s), Act.25:24 (cf. G1794.d: ἐν-τυλίσσω to wrap up (LS), roll or coil about (DCG, ii, 227, 507a): with accusative and dative, Mat.27:59 (iv, Tr. [WH], cf. similar sentence in π.; MM, Exp., xiii), Luk.23:53; pass., Jhn.20:7.† (AS)

G1795.d: ἐν-τυπόω, -ῶ (τύπος), to imprint, engrave: pass. ptcp., with dative, 2Co.3:7.† (AS)

G1796.d: ἐν-υβρίζω [in OT (Al.), Lev.24:11 * ;] to insult, mock at: Heb.10:29.† (AS)

G1797.d: ἐνυπνιάζω (ἐνύπνιον), to dream: ἐνυπνίοις ἐ., Act.2:17 (LXX); present ptcp., Ju 8.† (AS)

G1798.d: ἐνύπνιον, -ου, τό (ὕπνος), a dream: pl., Act.2:17.† (AS)

G1799.d: ἐνώπιος, -ον (ὤψ), face to face, in sight (Theocr.; ἄρτοι ἐ., Exo.25:29): neut., ἐνώπιον, in vernacular, with force of prep. with genitive , in NT, most frequently in Lk, Ac, Re, never in Mt, Mk, before, in the presence of: Luk.1:19 Luk.4:7, Act.4:10 Act.6:5, Rev.1:4 2:14, al.; esp. ἐ. Κυρίου (θεοῦ), in the sight of God, or with God as witness or as judge, Rom.14:22, 1Co.1:29, 1Ti.2:3, Jas.4:10,…

G1801.d: ἐνωτίζομαι (οὖς), depon. mid., to give ear to, hearken to: with accusative, Act.2:14.† Also used for יָחַל שָׁמַע (AS)

G1802.d: Ἐνώχ (Heb. חֲנוֹךְ), ὁ, Enoch (Gen.5:18): Luk.3:37, Heb.11:5, Ju 14.† (AS)

G1803.d: ἕξ, οἱ, αἱ, τά indecl., six: Mat.17:1, Luk.13:14, al. (AS)

G1804.d: ἐξ-αγγέλλω to tell out, proclaim: 1Pe.2:9 [Mrk.16:1-20, "shorter conclusion"] (Cremer, 29).† (AS)

G1805.d: ἐξ-αγοράζω __1. to redeem, ransom (esp. of slaves): metaphorically, Gal.3:13 4:5. __2. to buy up; mid., to buy up for oneself: τ. καιρόν, Eph.5:16, Col.4:5 (Cremer, 60).† (AS)

G1806.d: ἐξ-άγω to lead out: with accusative, Mrk.15:20, Jhn.10:3, Act.5:19 7:36 16:37-39; before ἔξω, Luk.24:50; ἐκ, Act.7:40 12:17 13:17, Heb.8:9; εἰς, Act.21:38.† (AS)

G1807.d: ἐξ-αιρέω -ῶ to take out: with accusative, ὀφθαλμόν, Mat.5:29 18:9; mid. __(a) to take out for oneself, choose: Act.26:17 (Thayer, see word; Page, Ac., l.with, but see infr.); __(b) to deliver: Act.7:10, 34" (LXX) Act.12:11 Act.23:27 Act.26:17 (EV, but see supr.), Gal.1:4.† (AS)

G1808.d: ἐξ-αίρω to lift up, lift off the earth, remove: 1Co.5:13 (LXX)† (AS)

G1809.d: ἐξ-αιτέω, -ῶ to ask from; mid., to ask for oneself, demand: aor., ἐξῃτήσατο, with accusative (obtained you by asking, R, mg.), Luk.22:31 (see Field, Notes, 76; Cremer, 73).† (AS)

G1810.d: ἐξ-αίφνης (WH, ἐξέφνης, exc. Act.22:6; see App., p. 151, and cf. M, Pr., 35), adv. (ἄφνω), suddenly Mrk.13:36, Luk.2:13 9:39, Act.9:3 22:6.† (AS)

G1811.d: ἐξ-ακολουθέω, -ῶ to follow, follow up (in various senses): metaphorically, 2Pe.1:16 2:2 2:15 † (AS)

G1813.d: ἐξ-αλείφω __1. to plaster, wash over (LXX). __2. to wipe off, wipe out: δάκρυον, Rev.7:17 21:4; metaphorically, χειρόγραφον, Col.2:14; τ. ὄνομα, before ἐκ, Rev.3:5 (MM, Exp., xiii); pass., ἀμαρτίαι (ἐξαλιφθῆναι, WH), Act.3:19 (cf. Psa.51:11 Psa.109:13, Isa.43:25, Sir.46:20 (ἁμ. ἀπαλ-), 3Ma.2:19).† (AS)

G1815.d: ἐξ-ανάστασις, -εως, ἡ (ἐξανίστημι), a rising again: ἐκ τ. νεκρῶν, Php.3:11 (Cremer, 308).† (AS)

G1816.d: ἐξ-ανα-τέλλω __1. trans., to cause to spring up (LXX). __2. Intrans. (as ἀνατέλλω, Gen.3:18), to spring up: Mat.13:5, Mrk.4:5.† (AS)

G1817.d: ἐξ-ανίσημι __1. trans., to raise up: σπέρμα (cf. Gen.38:8), Mrk.12:19, Luk.20:28. __2. In 2 aor. act., intrans., to rise: Act.15:5.† (AS)

G1818.d: ἐξ -απατάω, -ῶ strengthened form of ἀπατάω, to deceive: with accusative, Rom.7:11 Rom.16:18, 1Co.3:18, 2Co.11:3, 2Th.2:3; pass., 1Ti.2:14.† (AS)

G1819.d: ἐξάπινα = ἐξαπίνης, ἐξαίφνης (which see), suddenly: Mrk.9:8.† (AS)

G1820.d: ἐξ-απορέω, -ῶ so in NT, depon. pass., to be utterly at a loss, be in despair: absol. (as Ps, l.with), 2Co.4:8; τοῦ ζῆν, 2Co.1:8.† (AS)

G1821.d: ἐξ-απο-στέλλω __1. to send forth: with accusative of person(s), Act.7:12 12:11, Gal.4:4; τ. ἐπαγγελίαν, Luk.24:49; τ. πνεῦμα, Gal.4:6; [τ. κήρυγμα, Mrk.16:1-20, "shorter conclusion," WH ;] before εἰς, Act.22:21; pass., ὁ λόγος, Act.13:26. __2. to send away: with accusative of person(s), before εἰς, Act.9:30; before ἕως, Act.11:22; with inf., Act.17:14; κενόν, Luk.1:53 20:10-11.† (AS)

G1822.d: ἐξ-αρτίζω (ἄρτιος), __1. to com­plete, finish: τ. ἡμέρας, Act.21:5. __2. to furnish, supply: pass., 2Ti.3:17 (for exx., see MM, Exp., xiii; Cremer, 651).† (AS)

G1823.d: ἐξ-αστράπτω to flash like lightning, gleam, be radiant: ἱματισμός, Luk.9:29.† (AS)

G1824.d: ἐξ-αυτῆς (a κοινή word, = ἐξ αὐτῆς τ. ὥρας) at once, forthwith: Mrk.6:25, Act.10:33 Act.11:11 Act.21:32 Act.23:30, Php.2:23.† (AS)

G1825.d: ἐξ-εγείρω to raise up: Rom.9:17 (cf. ICC, in l); from the dead, 1Co.6:14.† (AS)

G1826.d: ἔξ-ειμι (εἶμι), to go forth: Act.13:42 Act.17:15 Act.20:7; before ἐπί, with accusative, Act.27:43.† (AS)

G1827.d: ἐξ-ελίγχω to convict: Ju 15, Rec. (for ἐλέγχω, WH, which see).† (AS)

G1828.d: ἐξ-έλκω to draw out or away: metaphorically, ὑπὸ τ. ἐπιθυμίας, Jas.1:14 (see Mayor, in l).† (AS)

G1829.d: ἐξέραμα, -τος, τό (ἐξεράω, to evacuate, disgorge) a vomit: 2Pe.2:22 (LXX).† (AS)

G1830.d: ἐξ-εραυνάω (Rec. ἐξερευνάω), -ῶ, to search out, search carefully: before περί, 1Pe.1:10.† (AS)

G1831.d: ἐξέρχομαι, depon., to go, or come out of: Mat.10:11, Mrk.1:35, Jhn.13:30, al.; with inf., Mat.11:8, Mrk.3:21, Luk.7:25, 26 Act.20:8; id. before ἐπί, Mat.26:55, al.; εἰς, Mrk.1:38; ἵνα, Rev.6:2; ἐ. before ἐκ (cl. with genitive loc.), Mrk.5:2, Jhn.4:30, al.; ἔξω, with genitive, Mat.21:17, Mrk.14:68, Act.16:13, Heb.13:13; ἀπό, Mrk.11:12, Luk.9:5, Php.4:15; ἐκεῖθεν, Mat.15:21, Mrk.6:1, Luk.9:4, al.;…

G1832.d: ἔξ-εστι (εἰμί), impers. verb., it is permitted, lawful: Mrk.2:24, Act.8:37 (R, mg.), 1Co.10:23; with inf., Mat.12:2, 10 12 14:4 15:26 19:3 22:17 27:6, Mrk.3:4 12:14, Luk.6:2, 9 14:3, Jhn.5:10; before accusative, Mrk.2:26, Luk.6:4 20:22; with dative of person(s) and inf., Mat.20:15, Mrk.6:18 10:2, Jhn.18:31, Act.16:21 21:37 22:25 (inf. understood), 1Co.6:12; ἐξόν (sc. ἐστί), Act.2:29, 2Co.12:4;…

G1833.d: ἐξ-ετάζω (ἐτάζω (rare), to examine), to examine closely, inquire carefully (of ): before περί (with ἀκριβῶς), Mat.2:8; before τίς, Mat.10:11; with accusative of person(s), Jhn.21:12.† SYN.: ἀνακρίνω, ἐραυνάω (see DCG, ii, 594b) (AS)

G1834.d: ἐξ-ηγέομαι, -οῦμαι to lead, show the way; metaphorically, to unfold, narrate, declare: with accusative of thing(s), Luk.24:35 Act.21:19; with dative of person(s), Act.10:8; θεόν (understood), Jhn.1:18; before ὅσα, Act.15:12; καθώς, Act.15:14.† (AS)

G1835.d: ἑξήκοντα, οἱ, αἱ, τά indecl., sixty: Mat.13:8, 23, Mrk.4:8, 20, Luk.24:13, 1Ti.5:9, Rev.11:3 Rev.12:6 Rev.13:18.† (AS)

G1836.d: ἑξῆς adv. (ἔχω), in order, successively, next: τῇ ἑ. ἡμέρᾳ, Luk.9:37; ἐν τῷ ἑ. (sc. χρόνῳ), soon after, Luk.7:11; τῇ ἑ. (sc. ἡμέρα), Act.21:1 Act.25:17 Act.27:18.† (AS)

G1837.d: ἐξ-ηχέω, -ῶ to sound forth (as a trumpet, or thunder; see M, Th., l.with): pass., 1Th.1:8.† (AS)

G1838.d: ἐξις, -εως, ἡ (ἔχω), habit, use, experience: Heb.5:14.† (AS)

Intr. in pass. and mid., also in 2 aor., pf., plpf. act., before ἐκ or with genitive, to stand aside from, retire…

G1840.d: ἐξ-ισχύω to have strength enough, to be quite able: with inf., Eph.3:18.† (AS)

G1841.d: ἔξ-οδος, -ου, ὁ (ὁδός), a going out, departure: Heb.11:22; of death, Luk.9:31, 2Pe.1:15.† (AS)

G1844.d: ἐξ-ορκίζω (later form of ἐξορκόω ), __1. to administer an oath to (Dem., Polyb., al.). __2. to adjure: with accusative of person(s), before κατά, with genitive (as frequently in magic π.; MM, Exp., xiv), Mat.26:63.† (AS)

G1845.d: ἐξ-ορκιστής, -οῦ, ὁ (ἐξορκίζω), __1. one who administers an oath. __2. an exorcist: Act.19:13.† (AS)

G1846.d: ἐξ-ορύσσω to dig out, dig up: στέγην, Mrk.2:4; metaphorically, ὀφοαλμούς (cf. LXX, ll with; Herod., viii, 116), Gal.4:15.† (AS)

G1847.d: ἐξ-ουδενέω (Rec. -όω; T, -θανόω), -ῶ, to despise, set at nought: Mrk.9:12 (cf. ἐξουθενέω).† (AS)

G1849.d: ἐξουσία, -ας, ἡ (ἔξεστι), __1. prop., liberty or power to act, freedom to exercise the inward force or faculty expressed by δύναμις (which see): 1Co.9:12; ἐ. ἔχειν, 2Th.3:9; id. before inf., Jhn.10:18, 1Co.9:4, 5; with genitive obj., Rom.9:21; before ἐπί, with accusative, Rev.22:14; περί, 1Co.7:37. __2. Later (cf. Milligan, Th., 114; MM, Exp., xiv), of the power of right, authority: Mat.21:33,…

G1851.d: ἐξοχή, -ῆς, ἡ (ἐξέχω, to stand out), __1. a projection (ἐ. πέτρας, Job.39:28). __2. Metaphorical, eminence, excellence: οἱ κατ᾽ ἐ., the chief men, Act.25:23.† (AS)

G1852.d: ἐξ-υπνίζω to awaken out of sleep (= ἀφυπνίζω): with accusative of person(s), Jhn.11:11.† (AS)

G1853.d: ἔξ-υπνος, -ον (ὕπνος), roused out of sleep: Act.16:27.† (AS)

G1854.d: ἔξω adv. (ἐξ), __1. outside, without; __(a) adverbially: Mat.12:46, Mrk.3:31 11:4, Luk.8:20, Jhn.18:16, al.; with art., ὁ ἔ., he who is without; metaphorically, in pl., οἱ ἔ., of those outside the Church, 1Co.5:12-13, Col.4:5 (Lft., in l), 1Th.4:12; ὁ ἔ. ἄνθρωπος, 2Co.4:16; αἱ ἔ. πόλεις, Act.26:11; __(b) as prep. with genitive: Luk.13:33, Act.21:5, Heb.13:11-12 __2. G1857.d: ἐξώτερος, -α, -ον (compar., from ἔξω; opposite to ἐσώτερος) outer: σκότος, Mat.8:12 Mat.22:13 Mat.25:30.† (AS)

G1859.d: ἑορτή, -ῆς, ἡ a feast, festival: Luk.2:42, Jhn.5:1, Jhn.6:4 Jhn.7:37, Col.2:10; ἡ ἑ. τοῦ πάσχα, Luk.2:41, Jhn.13:1; τ. ἀζύμων, Luk.22:1; ἡ σκηνοπηγία, Jhn.7:2 (Deiss., LAE, 116); ἐν τ. ἑ., Mat.26:5, Mrk.14:2, Jhn.4:45 7:11 12:20 (εἶναι ἐν ἑ.), Jhn.2:23; εἰς τ. ἑ. (for the feast), Jhn.13:29; ἀναβαίνειν, ἔρχεσθαι εἰς τ. ἑ., Jhn.4:45 7:8-10 11:56 12:12; τῆς ἐ μεσούσης, Jhn.7:14; κατὰ ἑ. (at each…

G1860.d: ἐπ-αγγελία, -ας, ἡ (ἐπαγγέλλω), __1. a summons (as Attic law-term, Dem., al.). __2. a promise (Dem., Arist., al.): Act.23:21; esp. in NT of the divine promises, Act.7:17, Rom.4:14, 16 Rom.9:4, Gal.3:17-18, 21 4:23, Heb.8:6 11:9, 17, 2Pe.3:9; with inf., Heb.4:1; γίνεται, etc., with dative of person(s), Act.2:39, Rom.4:13, Gal.3:16; before πρός, Act.13:32 26:6; έπαγγέλεσθαι τὴν ἐ., 1Jn.2:25; ἔχειν…

G1861.d: ἐπ-αγγέλλω __1. to announce, proclaim. __2. (a) to promise; __(b) to profess. Mid., also frequently in both these senses; __(with) to promise: with dab. of person(s), Heb.6:13; with accusative of thing(s), Rom.4:21, Tit.1:2; with dative of person(s) and accusative of thing(s), Jas.1:12 2:5, 2Pe.2:19; ἐπαγγελίαν, 1Jn.2:25; with inf., Mrk.14:11, Act.7:5; before λέγων, Heb.12:26; ptcp., Heb.10:23…

G1863.d: ἐπ-άγω to bring upon: with dative and accusative, 2Pe.2:5; ἑαυτοῖς ἐ. (for cl. mid., see Mayor, in l), 2Pe.2:1; ἐ. τὸ αἷμα (cf. Ge 209), Act.5:28.† (AS)

G1864.d: ἐπ-αγωνίζομαι depon.; __1. to contend with (Plut.). __2. to contend for (C.I., 2335, 19): with dative of thing(s), Ju 3.† (AS)

G1866.d: Ἐπαίνετος (Rec. -τός), -ου, ὁ Epænetus, a Christian of Borne: Rom.16:5.† (AS)

G1869.d: ἐπ-αίρω to lift up, raise: τ. ἀρτέμονα, Act.27:40; χεῖρας, Luk.24:50, 1Ti.2:8; κεφαλάς, Luk.21:28; ὀφθαλμούς, Mat.17:8, Luk.6:20 16:23 18:13, Jhn.4:35 6:5 17:1; φωνήν, Luk.11:27, Act.2:14 14:11 22:22; τ. πτέρναν (figuratively), Jhn.13:18. G1870.d: ἐπ-αισχύνομαι to be ashamed (of): absol., 2Ti.1:12; with accusative of person(s), Mrk.8:38, Luk.9:26; with accusative of thing(s), Rom.1:16, 2Ti.1:8 1:16; ἐπί, with dative of thing(s), Rom.6:21; with inf., Heb.2:11; with, accusative of person(s), and inf., Heb.11:16,† (AS)

G1873.d: ἐπ-ακούω __1. to listen to. __2. to hearken to, hear with favour (one's prayer): with genitive of person(s), 2Co.6:2 (LXX).† (AS)

G2616.d: κατα-δυναστεύω to exercise power over, oppress: with accusative of person(s) (Xen.; LXX, Mic.2:2, Wis.2:10, al.); with genitive of person(s), Jas.2:6 (ὑμᾶς, T); pass., Act.10:38 (cf. MM, Exp., xv).† (AS)

G2617.d: κατ-αισχύνω to disgrace, dishonour, put to shame: with accusative of thing(s), 1Co.11:4-5; with accusative of person(s), 1Co.1:27 11:22; pass., to be ashamed: Luk.13:17, 2Co.7:14 9:4, 1Pe.3:16; as in LXX (Psa.22:6 25:2-3, al.), of unfulfilled hopes: Rom.5:5; pass., Rom.9:33 10:11, 1Pe.2:6" (LXX) .† (AS)

G2618.d: κατα-καίω to burn up, burn completely: with accusative of thing(s), Mat.13:30 Act.19:19; pass., 1Co.3:15, Heb.13:11, 2Pe.3:10, Rev.8:7; before πυρί Mat.3:12 13:40, Luk.3:17 (cf. Exo.29:14, al.); ἐν πυρί (Deu.9:21, al.): Rev.17:16 18:8.† (AS)

G2619.d: κατα-καλύπτω to cover up; mid., to cover or veil oneself: 1Co.11:6; τ. κεφαλήν, 1Co.11:7.† (AS)

G2620.d: κατα-καυχάομαι, -ῶμαι __1. to boast against, exult over: with genitive, Rom.11:18, Jas.2:13; before κατά, with genitive, Jas.3:14 (T, om. κατά). __2. before ἐν, to glory in (Za., l.with, Jer.27:38).† (AS)

G2621.d: κατά-κειμαι __1. to lie down. __2. to lie sick: Mrk.1:30 2:4, Jhn.5:6, Act.28:8; before ἐπί with genitive, Act.9:33; id. with accusative, Luk.5:25; ἐν, Jhn.5:3. __3. to recline at meals (cf. ἀνάιειμαι): Mrk.14:3, Luk.5:29; before ἐν, Mrk.2:15, Luk.7:37, 1Co.8:10.† (AS)

G2622.d: κατα-κλάω, -ῶ to break up, break in pieces: Mrk.6:41, Luk.9:16.† (AS)

G2623.d: κατα-κλείω to shut up:. with accusative of person(s), before ἐν φυλακῇ (-αῖς), Luk.3:20, Act.26:10.† (AS)

G2624.d: κατα-κληρονομέω, -ῶ __1. to distribute by lot or as an inheritance (Num.34:18, Jos.14:1, al.): Act.13:19. __2. to receive by inheritance (Deu.1:38, al.).† κατα-κληροδοτέω, ῶ, Act.13:19, Rec., = -νομέω, which see† (AS)

G2625.d: κατα-κλίνω to lay down, make to lie down, esp. for meals: with accusative of person(s), Luk.9:14-15; mid., to recline at meals: Luk.7:36 24:30; before εἰς, Luk.14:8 (cf. Jth, Lc.).† (AS)

G2627.d: κατα-κλυσμός, -οῦ, ὁ (κατακλύζω), a flood, deluge: Mat.24:38-39 Luk.17:27, 2Pe.2:5.† (AS)

G2628.d: κατ-ακολουθέω, -ῶ to follow after: Luk.23:55; with dative of person(s), Act.16:17.† (AS)

G2629.d: κατα-κόπτω to cut up, cut in pieces (cf. Isa.27:9, Jer.21:7, 2Ch.34:7): ἑαυτὸν λίθοις, Mrk.5:5.† (AS)

G2630.d: κατα-κρημνίζω (κρημνός), to throw over a precipice, cast down head­long: Luk.4:29.† (AS)

G2631.d: κατά-κριμα, -τος, τό (κατακρίνω), penalty (RV, condemnation; but cf. Deiss., BS, 264 f.; MM, Exp., xv): Rom.5:16, 18 8:1.† (AS)

G2632.d: κατα-κρίνω to give judgment against, condemn: Rom.8:34; with accusative of person(s), Mrk.14:64, Jhn.8:10-11; disting. fr. κρίνειν, Rom.2:1, 1Co.11:32; before θανάτῳ (cl. -ου or -ον), Mat.20:18, Mrk.10:33; pass., Mat.27:3, Mrk.16:16, Rom.14:23, 1Co.11:32, 2Pe.2:6. Metaphorical, of condemning through a good example: Mat.12:41-42, Luk.11:31-32, Rom.8:3, Heb.11:7 † (AS)

G2633.d: κατά-κρισις, -εως, ἡ (κατακρίνω), condemnation: 2Co.3:9 7:3 (cf. Deiss., LAE, 91 f.).† (AS)

G2634.d: κατα-κυριεύω to gain or exercise dominion (over); __(a) absol. (Arist.); __(b) with genitive (Arist., al.): Mat.20:25, Mrk.10:42, Act.19:16, 1Pe.5:3.† SYN.: (κατεξουσιάζω) (see Swete, Mk., l.with) (AS)

G2635.d: κατα-λαλέω, -ῶ to speak evil of, rail at: in cl., with accusative; in LXX, __(a) with genitive, __(b) before κατά, with genitive; in NT, with genitive (M, Pr., 65): Jas.4:11, 1Pe.2:12; pass., 1Pe.3:16,† (AS)

G2637.d: κατά-λαλος, -ου, ὁ a railer, defamer: Rom.1:30.† SYN.: (ψιθυριστής), a whisperer (see Tr., Syn., § cvii, 15; Lft., Notes, 256) (AS)

G2638.d: κατα-λαμβάνω __1. to lap hold of, seize, appropriate: Mrk.9:18; with accusative of thing(s), 1Co.9:24, Php.3:12-13 __2. to overtake: as carrel, of διώκω (Field, Notes, 158 f.), Rom.9:30; ἡ ἡμέρα, 1Th.5:4; of evils, Jhn.1:5 12:35 (cf. 617 T); hence, to surprise, discover: Jhn.8:3-4], __3. Of mental action, to apprehend, comprehend; so mid., in NT (M, Pr., 158): Eph.3:18; before ὅτι, Act.4:13…

G2639.d: κατα-λέγω __1. to lay down; mid. (in Hom.), to lie down. __2. to narrate (LXX, ll. with). __3. to choose out, hence, to enrol (as of soldiers, Hdt., Thuc., a1., see LS, see word): of widows, pass., 1Ti.5:9 (cf. Ellic.; CGT, in l).† (AS)

G2640.d: κατά-λειμμα, -τος, τό (καταλείπω), a remnant: Rom.9:27, Rec. (for ὑπόλειμμα, which see).† (AS)

G2641.d: κατα-λείπω __1 1, to leave behind, leave: with accusative of person(s) (of thing(s)), Mat.4:13, Mrk.12:19, 21, Luk.20:31, Act.24:27 25:14, Heb.11:27; of sailing by a place, Act.21:3; ptcp., καταλιπών, redundant (Dalman, Words, 21 f.), Mat.16:4 21:17; pass., Jhn.8:9, 1Th.3:1; metaphorically, εὐθεῖαν ὁδόν, 2Pe.2:15. __2. to forsake, abandon: Mat.19:5, Mrk.10:7" (LXX) Mrk.14:52, Luk.5:28 15:4,…

G2642.d: κατα-λιθάζω (= cl. -θόω; cf. -θοβολέω, Exo.17:4, Num_14:10) to cast stones at, to stone: Luk.20:6.† (AS)

G2643.d: κατ-αλλαγή, -ῆς, ἡ (καταλλάσσω), __1. exchange. __2. reconciliation: Rom.5:11; κ. κόσμου, Rom.11:15; διακονία τῆς κ., 2Co.5:18; λόγος τῆς κ., 2Co.5:19.† (AS)

G2644.d: κατ-αλλάσσω (Att.. -ττω; cf. ἀλλάσσω) prop., to change, exchange (esp. of money); hence, of persons, to change from emnity to friendship, to reconcile (for exx. in cl., see Thayer„ LS): of the reconciliation of man to God (Lft., Notes, 288; ICC on Ro, l.with; DCG, ii, 474, 797), 2Co.5:18-19; pass Rom.5:10, 2Co.5:20; of a woman returning to her husband, 1Co.7:11 (cf. ἀπο-καταλλάσσω).† (AS)

G2645.d: κατά-λοιπος, -ον left remaining: ἱο κ. τ. ἀνθρώπων, Act.15:17 (LXX).† (AS)

G2646.d: κατά-λυμα, -τος, τό (καταλύω), __1. = cl. καταγώγιον (cf. πανδοχεῖον), an inn, lodgingplace: Luk.2:7 (so Ex, l.with, and MGr.). __2. a guest-room (1Sam,l.with): Mrk.14:14, Luk.22:11.† (AS)

G2647.d: κατα-λύω __1. to destroy, cast down: Mat.24:2, Mrk.13:2, Luk.21:6; τ. ναόν, Mat.26:61 27:40, Mrk.14:58 15:29, Act.6:14; οἰκίαν, 2Co.5:1; opposite to οἰκοδομεῖν, Gal.2:18. Metaphorical, to overthrow, annul, abrogate: Act.5:38-39; τ. ἔργον τ. θεοῦ, Rom.14:20; τ. νόμον, Mat.5:17 (2Ma.2:22). __2. to unloose, unyoke (e.g. horses), hence intrans., of travellers (cf. κατάλυμα), to take up one's…

G2648.d: κατα-μανθάνω to learn thoroughly, observe well, consider carefully (on distinction bet. κ. and μανθάνω, cf. M, Pr., 117): Mat.6:28.† (AS)

G2649.d: κατα-μαρτυρέω, -ῶ to bear witness againt: with accusative of thing(s) and genitive of person(s), Mat.26:62 27:13, Mrk.14:60.† (AS)

G2650.d: κατα-μένω to remain permanently, abide: Act.1:13, 1Co.16:6, WH (παραμ-, T, EV).† (AS)

G2653.d: κατα-θεματίζω to curse vehemently: Mat.26:74 (cf. ἀναθεμ-).† (AS)

G2654.d: κατ-αν-αλίσκω __1. to use up, spend. __2. to consume: of fire, ptcp., Heb.12:29 (LXX).† (AS)

G2655.d: κατα-ναρκάω, -ῶ (ναρκάω, to grow numb, in LXX, in causal sense, for יָקַע, Gen.32:25 (26); without Heb. equiv., Gen.32:32 (33) Job.33:19, Dan LXX 11:6*); __1. to cause to grow numb. __2. Intrans., to grow numb; hence metaphorically, to be inactive, be burdensome to with genitive, 2Co.11:9 12:13-14; pass., to be quite numb (Hippocr.).† (AS)

G2656.d: κατα-νεύω __1. to nod assent, __2. to make a sign by nodding the head: with dative of person(s), Luk.5:7.† (AS)

G2657.d: κατα-νοέω, -ῶ to take note of, perceive, consider carefully: Act.7:31-32; with accusative of thing(s), Mat.7:3, Luk.6:41 12:24, 27 20:23, Act.11:6 27:39, Rom.4:19; with accusative of person(s), Heb.3:1 10:24, Jas.1:23-24 (on the distinction bet. κ. and νοέω simplex, see M, Pr., 117).† (AS)

G2658.d: κατ-αντάω, -ῶ to come to, arrive at: before εἰς, with accusative loc., Act.16:1 18:19, 24 21:7 25:13 (see M, Pr., 132) Act.27:12 28:13; before ἀντικρύ, with genitive, Act.20:15. Metaphorical, before εἰς, with accusative of person(s), 1Co.10:11 14:36; id. with accusative of thing(s), to attain to: Act.26:7, Eph.4:13, Php.3:11.† (AS)

G2659.d: κατά-νυξις, -εως, ἡ (κατανύσσω, which see), __1. a pricking. __2. (Perhaps through resembl. of κατανύσσω to -νυστάζω), torpor of mind, stupefaction: Rom.11:8 (LXX) (see ICC, in l; Field, Notes, 157).† (AS)

G2660.d: κατα-νύσσω __1. to strike or prick violently. __2. to stun. __3. Of strong emotion, pass., to be smitten: τὴν καρδίαν, Act.2:37 (see: κατάνυξις).† (AS)

G2661.d: κατ-αξιόω, -ῶ to deem worthy: with accusative of person(s) and genitive of thing(s), 2Th.1:5; pass. before inf., Luk.20:35, Act.5:41.† (AS)

G2662.d: κατα-πατέω, -ῶ to tread down, trample under foot: Mat.7:6, Luk.12:1; pass., Mat.5:13, Luk.8:5. Metaphorical, τ. υἱὸν τ. θεοῦ, Heb.10:29.† (AS)

G2663.d: κατά-παυσις, -εως, ἡ (καταπαύω), __1. in cl., a putting to rest, causing to cease. __2. In LXX and NT, rest, repose: Act.7:49 (LXX), Heb.3:11, 18 4:1, 3 4:5, 10-11† (AS)

G2664.d: κατα-παύω __1. trans., __(a) to cause to cease, restrain: Act.14:18; __(b) to cause to rest: Heb.4:8. __2. Intrans., to rest: before ἀτό, Heb.4:4 (LXX), Heb.4:10.† (AS)

G2665.d: κατα-πέτασμα, -τος, τό (= cl. παραπέτασμα) in NT always the inner veil or curtain of the Temple (or Tabernacle): Mat.27:51, Mrk.15:38, Luk.23:45, Heb.6:19 9:3; figuratively, ἡ σὰρξ αὐτοῦ Heb.10:20.† (AS)

G2666.d: κατα-πίνω __1. to drink down, swallow: Mat.23:24, Rev.12:16. __2. to devour: 1Pe.5:8. Metaphorical, to swallow up, consume: pass., 1Co.15:54 (LXX), 2Co.2:7 5:4, Heb.11:29.† (AS)

G2667.d: κατα-πίπτω to fall down: Act.28:6; before εἰς, Act.26:14; ἐπί with accusative, Luk.8:6.† (AS)

G2668.d: κατα-πλέω, -ῶ to sail down, sail to land, put in: εἰς τ. χώραν, Luk.8:26.† (AS)

G2669.d: κατα-πονέω, -ῶ to wear down, oppress, treat hardly: pass., Act.7:24, 2Pe.2:7.† (AS)

G2670.d: κατα-πονίζω to throw into the sea, sink or drown therein: Mat.14:30; pass., Mat.18:6.† (AS)

G2671.d: κατ-άρα, -ας, -ἡ a curse: Gal.3:10, 13 Heb.6:8, 2Pe.2:14; opposite to εὐλογία, Jas.3:10; concrete, of Christ, Gal.3:13 (see Lft. in l).† (AS)

G2672.d: κατ-αράομαι, -ώμαι depon. (κατάρα), to curse: with accusative, Mrk.11:21; opposite to εὐλογέω, Luk.6:26, Rom.12:14, Jas.3:9; pass. pf. ptcp., accursed, under a curse (see M, Pr., 221): Mat.25:41.† (AS)

G2673.d: κατ-αργέω, -ῶ (κατά, causative, ἀργός = ἀ-εργός), to make idle or inactive (χέρας, Eur., Phœn., 753): of soil occupied by an unfruitful tree, Luk.13:7. Metaphorical (Inscr.), to render inoperative or invalid, to abrogate, abolish: Rom.3:3, 31, 1Co.1:28 6:13 13:11 15:24, Gal.3:17, Eph.2:15, 2Th.2:8, 2Ti.1:10, Heb.2:14; pass., Rom.4:14 6:6, 1Co.2:6 13:8 13:10 15:26, 2Co.3:7 3:11-14 Gal.5:11; before…

G2674.d: κατ-αριθμέω, -ῶ to number or count among: before ἐν, Act.1:1.† (AS)

G2675.d: κατ-αρτίζω to render ἄρτιος, i.e. fit, complete; __(a) to mend, repair: Mat.4:21, Mrk.1:19; __(b) to furnish completely, complete, equip, prepare: pass., Luk.6:40, Rom.9:22, Heb.11:3; mid., Mat.21:16 (LXX), Heb.10:5 (LXX); __(with) in ethical sense, to prepare, complete, perfect: Gal.6:1 (EV, restore), 1Pe.5:10; pass., 1Co.1:10 (Field, Notes, 167), 2Co.13:11, Heb.13:21 (cf. προ-καταρτίζω).† (AS)

G2676.d: κατ-άρτισις, -εως, ἡ (καταρτίζω), a strengthening, making fit: in ethical sense, 2Co.13:9.† (AS)

G2677.d: καταρτισμός, -οῦ, ὁ [in Sm.: Isa.38:12 * ;] = κατάρτισις (but see ICC, Eph. l.with): Eph.4:12.† (AS)

G2678.d: κατα-σείω __1. to shake down. __2. Of the hand, to shake or wave as a signal: τ. χεῖρα, Act.19:33; τ. χειρί, Act.13:16; id. with dative of person(s), Act.21:40; before inf., Act.12:17.† (AS)

G2680.d: κατα-σκευάζω to prepare, make ready: τ. ὁδόν, Mat.11:10, Mrk.1:2, Luk.7:27; οἶκον, Heb.3:3-4; σκηνήν, Heb.9:2, 6; κιβωτόν, Heb.11:7, 1Pe.3:20; pass. pf. ptcp., λαον κ., Luk.1:17.† (AS)

G2681.d: κατα-σκηνόω, -ῶ to pitch one's tent, lodge, dwell: before ἐν, Mat.13:32, Luk.13:19; ὑπό, with accusative, Mrk.4:32; ἐπ᾽ ἐλπιδι, Act.2:26 (LXX).† (AS)

G2682.d: κατα-σκήνωσις, εως, ἡ __1. prop., an encamping, taking up one's quarters (Polyb., al., see LS; and cf. LXX, ll. with). __2. a lodging, abode: of birds, Mat.8:20, Luk.9:58.† (AS)

G2683.d: κατα-σκιάζω to overshadow: with accusative, Heb.9:5.† (AS)

G2684.d: κατα-σκοπέω, -ῶ to view closely, inspect, spy out: with accusative, Gal.2:4.† (AS)

G2686.d: κατα-σοφίζομαι to deal craftily with, outwit: Act.7:19 (LXX) † (AS)

G2687.d: κατα-στέλλω __1. to let down, lower. __2. to keep down, restrain: with accusative, Act.19:35-36 † (AS)

G2688.d: κατά-στημα, -τος, τό (καθίστημι), in LXX: 3Ma.5:45 (-εμα, A) * ;] __1. condition, of health, etc. __2. demeanour: Tit.2:3 (for exx. see Field, Notes, 220).† (AS)

G2689.d: κατα-στολή, -ῆς, ἡ (καταστέλλω), __1. a letting down, checking. __2. steadiness, quietness in demeanour. __3. LXX and NT (cf. Plut., ii, 65 D; -ίζω = vestire), a garment, dress, attire: 1Ti.2:9 (but see Ellic., in l).† (AS)

G2690.d: κατα-στρέφω __1. to turn down, turn over; as, the soil. __2. to overturn, overthrow: Mat.21:12, Mrk.11:15; pass. pf. ptcp., Act.15:16 (LXX).† (AS)

G2691.d: κατα-στρηνιάω, -ῶ to wax wanton against: with genitive, 1Ti.5:11 (AS)

G2692.d: κατα-στροφή, -ῆς, ἡ (καταστρέφω), __1. overthrow: 2Pe.2:6 (WH, om.). __2. Metaphorical, subversion, upsetting (cf. καθαίρεσις, 2Co.13:10): 2Ti.2:14.† (AS)

G2693.d: κατα-στρώννυμι __1. to strew or spread over. __2. to lay low, overthrow: 1Co.10:5.† (AS)

G2694.d: κατα-σύρω __1. to pull down. __2. to drag away: with accusative of person(s), Luk.12:58.† (AS)

G2695.d: κατα-σφάζω to kill off, slay: with accusative, Luk.19:27.† (AS)

G2696.d: κατα-σφραγίζω to seal up, secure with a seal: Rev.5:1.† (AS)

G2697.d: κατά-σχεσις, -εως, ἡ (κατέχω), __1. a holding back. __2. LXX and NT, a holding fast, possession: Act.7:5, 45.† (AS)

G2698.d: κατα-τίθημι to lay down, deposit, lay by: Mrk.15:46, T; mid., to lay up for oneself: χάριν (Hdt., al., see LS, see word), with dative of person(s), Act.24:27 25:9.† (AS)

G2699.d: κατα-τομή, -ῆς, ἡ [in Sm.: Jer.31:37 (κατατέμνω is used in LXX of forbidden mutilations: Lev.21:5, al.) ;] __1. incision. __2. excision, concision, mutilation: in sarcasm, by paronomasia, in contrast to (true) περιτομή (v3), of Judaizing Christians, Php.3:2 (see Lft., in l; Cremer, 883).† (AS)

G2700.d: κατα-τοξεύω to strike down with an arrow, shoot dead: Heb.12:20 (LXX) (Rec.; WH, R, om.).† (AS)

G2701.d: κατα-τρέχω to run down: before ἐπί, with accusative of person(s), Act.21:32.† (AS)

G2702.d: κατα-φέρω to bring down: αἰτιώματα, Act.25:7; ψῆφον, to cast a ballot, Act.26:10; pass., to be borne down: ὕπνῳ, ἀπὸ τ. ὕ., Act.20:9.† (AS)

G2703.d: κατα-φεύγω to flee for refuge: before εἰς, Act.14:6; metaphorically, with inf., Heb.6:18.† (AS)

G2704.d: κατα-φθείρω __1 1 to destroy entirely. __2. In moral sense (as LXX), to deprave, corrupt: pass. pf. ptcp., before τ. νο ν, 2Ti.3:8.† (AS)

G2705.d: κατα-φιλέω, -ῶ to kiss fervently, kiss affectionately: Mat.26:49, Mrk.14:45, Luk.7:38, 45 15:20, Act.20:37.† (AS)

G2706.d: κατα-φρονέω, -ῶ to think little of, despise: with genitive, Mat.6:24 18:10, Luk.16:13, Rom.2:4, 1Co.11:22, 1Ti.4:12 6:2, Heb.12:2, 2Pe.2:10.† (AS)

G2708.d: κατα-χέω to pour down upon: with genitive (cl.), Mrk.14:3; before ἐπί, with genitive, Mat.26:7.† (AS)

G2709.d: κατα-χθόνιος, -ον (χθών, the earth), subterranean, under the earth (in cl., of the infernal gods): of the departed in Hades, opposite to ἐπουράνιος, ἐπίγειος, Php.2:10.† (AS)

G2710.d: κατα-χράομαι, -ῶμαι to make full use of, use to the uttermost, use up: 1Co.7:31; with dative, 1Co.9:18 (for other senses, see LS, see word)..† (AS)

G2711.d: κατα-ψύχω to cool: with accusative, Luk.16:24.† (AS)

G2713.d: κατέναντι adv., over against, opposite, before: ἡ, κ. κώμη, Luk.19:30; as prep., with genitive, Mat.21:2 27:24 (ἀπ-, WH, mg.), Mrk.11:2 12:41 (ἀπ-, WH, mg.) Mrk.13:3; metaphorically, before, before θεοῦ, Rom.4:17, 2Co.2:17 12:19.† (AS)

G2714.d: κατενώπιον adv. (= Hom., κατένωπα), over against, before: with genitive, τ. δόξης, Ju 24; metaphorically (cf. κατέναντι, and see Lft., Col., l.with), τ. θεοῦ, Eph.1:4, Col.1:22.† (AS)

G2715.d: κατ-εξουσιάζω to exercise authority over: with genitive of person(s), Mat.20:25, Mrk.10:42.† SYN: (κατακυριεύω) (see Swete, Mk., l.with) (AS)

G2716.d: κατ-εργάζομαι (emphatic form of ἐργάζομαι), to effect by labour, achieve, work out, bring about: with accusative, Rom.4:15 5:3 7:8, 15-20, 2Co.7:10, Eph.6:13, Jas.1:3; pass., 2Co.12:12; with accusative of thing(s) and dative of person(s), Rom.7:13, 2Co.4:17 7:11 9:11; id. before διά, with genitive of person(s), Rom.15:18; τ. σωτηρίαν, Php.2:12; with accusative of person(s) before εἰς, 2Co.5:5…

G2718.d: κατ-έρχομαι to come down, go down: before εἰς, Luk.4:31, Act.8:5 13:4 15:30 19:1, Τ; ἀπό, Luk.9:37, Act.15:1 18:5 21:10; ἀπό and εἰς, Act.11:27 12:10; of coming to port by ship, Act.18:22 21:3 27:5; before πρός, with accusative of person(s), Act.9:32; metaphorically, of gifts from God, Jas.3:15.† (AS)

G2719.d: κατ-εσθίω ("perfective" comp. of ἐσθίω, which see, and cf. G2798.d: κλάδος, -ου, ὁ (κλάω), a young tender shoot broken off for grafting; then, a branch: Mat.13:32 21:8 24:32, Mrk.4:32 13:28, Luk.13:19; metaphorically, of descendants (cf. Sir.40:15), Rom.11:16-19, 21.† (AS)

G2800.d: κλάσις, -εως, ἡ (κλάω), a breaking: Luk.24:35, Act.2:42.† (AS)

G2801.d: κλάσμα, -τος, τό (κλάω), a broken piece, fragment: Mat.14:20 15:37, Mrk.6:43 8:8, 19-20, Luk.9:17, Jhn.6:12-13 † (AS)

G2802.d: Καῦδα (TR, mg., Κλαῦδα; Rec. Κλαύδή), ἡ, Cauda, Clauda, an island near Crete: Act.27:16.† (AS)

G2804G.d: Κλαύδιος, -ου, ὁ Claudius; __1. the Emperor: Act.11:28 18:2. __2. A military tribune, C. Lysias: Act.23:26.† (AS)

G2804H.d: Κλαύδιος, -ου, ὁ Claudius; __1. the Emperor: Act.11:28 18:2. __2. A military tribune, C. Lysias: Act.23:26.† (AS)

G2805.d: κλαυθμός, -οῦ, ὁ (κλαίω), crying, weeping, Act.20:37; κ. καὶ ὀδυρμός, Mat.2:18 (LXX); ὁ κ. καὶ ὁ βρυγμός, Mat.8:12 13:42, 50 22:13 24:51 25:30, Luk.13:28.† (AS)

G2806.d: κλάω to break, break in pieces: of bread, Mat.14:19 15:36 26:26, Mrk.8:6 14:22, Luk.22:19 24:30, Act.2:46 20:7, 11 27:35, 1Co.10:16 11:24; before εἰς, with accusative of person(s), Mrk.8:19 (cf. ἐκ-, κατα-κλάω).† (AS)

G2807.d: κλείς, -δός Att.. accusative, κλεῖν, later -εῖδα, pl., κλεῖδες, -ας, contr., -εῖς, ἡ, a key. Fig., τ. βασιλείας τ. οὐρανῶν, Mat.16:19; τ. γνώσεως, Luk.11:52; of David (cf. LXX, l.with), Rev.3:7; τ. θανάτου κ. τ. ᾅδου, Rev.1:18; τ. ἀβύσσαυ, Rev.20:1; τ. φρέατος τῆς ἀ., Rev.9:1.† (AS)

G2808.d: κλείω to shut: θύραν, Mat.6:6; τ. ἄβυσσον, Rev.20:3; pass., θύρα, Mat.25:10, Luk.11:7 (pl.), Jhn.20:19, 26, Act.21:30; δεσμωτήριον, Act.5:23; πυλῶνες, Rev.21:25. Metaphorical, τ. οὐρανόν, Luk.4:25, Rom.11:6; τ. σπλάγχνα, 1Jn.3:17; τ. βασιλείαν, Mat.23:14; id. absol., Rev.3:7; τ. θύραν, Rev.3:8. (cf. ἀπο-, ἐκ-, κατα-, συν-κλείω.) † (AS)

G2809.d: κλέμμα, -τος, τό (κλέπτω), __1. a thing stolen (Arist., LXX) __2. = κλοπή, theft (Plato, al.): pl., Rev.9:21.† (AS)

G2811.d: κλέος, -ους, τό __1. a rumour, report. __2. good report, fame, glory: 1Pe.2:20.† (AS)

G2812.d: κλέπτης, -ου, ὁ a thief: Mat.6:19-20 24:43, Luk.12:33, 39, Jhn.10:1, 10 12:6, 1Co.6:10, 1Pe.4:15. Fig., ὡς κ. ἐν νυκτί, 1Th.5:2 5:4 (κλέπτας, WH, txt., R, mg.; see Lft., Notes, 73; but cf. also M, Th., l.with), 2Pe.3:10, Rev.3:3 16:15. Metaphorical, of false teachers, Jhn.10:8.† SYN.: λῃστής, a robber, a brigand who plunders, openly, with violence; κ. is a thief who steals in secret, by fraud and…

G2813.d: κλέπτω to steal: absol., Mat.6:19-20 19:18, Mrk.10:19, Luk.18:20, Jhn.10:10, Rom.2:21 13:9, Eph.4:28; with accusative, Mat.27:64 28:13.† (AS)

G2814.d: κλῆμα, -τος, τό (κλάω), a vine-twig, vine-branch: Jhn.15:2, 4-6.† (AS)

G2816.d: κληρονομέω, -ῶ (κληρονόμος) __1. to receive by lot. __2. to inherit (in cl., usually with genitive of thing(s)): absol., Gal.4:30 (LXX); in general, to possess oneself of, receive as one's own, obtain (as Deu.4:5, al., cf. Psa.25:3, Isa.61:7): with accusative of thing(s) (as generally in late Gk., see M, Pr., 65), of the Messianic Kingdom (cf. Psa.37:11, Sir.4:13 37:26, and see Dalman, Words, 125…

G2817.d: κληρονομία, -ας, ἡ (κληρονόμος) prop., an inherited property, an inheritance: Mat.21:38, Mrk.12:7, Luk.12:13 20:14; in general, a possession, inheritance: Act.7:5, Heb.11:8; of the Messianic Kingdom and its blessings, Act.20:32, Gal.3:18, Col.3:24, Eph.1:14, 18 5:5, Heb.9:15, 1Pe.1:4.† (AS)

G2818.d: κληρο-νόμος, -ου, ὁ (κλῆρος, νέμομαι, to possess) __1. (as in cl.) an heir: Mat.21:38, Mrk.12:7, Luk.20:14, Gal.4:1; of those who as sons of God inherit the privileges of the Messianic Kingdom; of Christ himself, Heb.1:2; of Abraham, Rom.4:13-14; of Christians, Rom.8:17, Gal.3:29, Tit.3:7, Jas.2:5. __2. (As in LXX: Jg, Mi, Je, ll. with) a possessor: Heb.6:17 11:7 (Cremer, 359 f.).† (AS)

G2819.d: κλῆρος, -ου, ὁ a lot; __(a) that which is cast or drawn: Mat.27:35, Mrk.15:24, Luk.23:34, Jhn.19:24" (LXX), Act.1:26; __(b) that which is obtained by casting: Act.1:17 8:21; of a part in the Kingdom of God (cf. Wis 55), Act.26:18, Col.1:12; pl. of the "cure" of a presbyter, 1Pe.5:3 (see ICC, in l).† (AS)

G2820.d: κληρόω, -ῶ __1. to cast lots. __2. to choose by lot. __3. to assign by lot, assign a portion: pass., ἐν ᾧ καὶ ἐκληρώθημεν, Eph.1:11 (on the various interpretations, see ICC; AR; Ellic., in l).† (AS)

G2821.d: κλῆσις, -εως, ἡ (καλέω) a calling, call; in NT, always of the Divine call to salvation: Rom.11:29, 1Co.1:26 7:20, Eph.1:18 4:1, 4, Php.3:14, 2Th.1:11, 2Ti.1:9, Heb.3:1, 2Pe.1:10 (Cremer, 332).† (AS)

G2822.d: κλητός, -ή, -όν (καλέω), called, invited (as to a banquet, Æsch., 1Sa 1:41, 3Ma.5:14); in NT, always of the Divine call; __(a) to some office: κ. ἀπόστολος, Rom.1:1, 1Co.1:1; __(b) to salvation: Rom.8:28, 1Co.1:24, Ju 1; κ. καὶ ἐκλεκτοὶ κ. πιστοί, Rev.17:14; in gosp. (not in pl., see: καλέω) disting. fr.ἐκλεκτός, Mat.20:16 (WH, txt., R, omit), Mat.22:14; κ. Ἰησοῦ Χρ., Rom.1:6; κ. ἅγιοι, saints by…

G2823.d: κλίβανος, -ον, ό (Att.., κρίβ-, but κλ- in Ion., Hdt., ii, 92), __1. in cl., a clibanus, cribanus, an earthen vessel for baking bread. __2. In LXX and NT, a furnace (cf. MM, Exp., xv), an oven: Mat.6:30, Luk.12:28.† (AS)

G2824.d: κλίμα, -τος, τό (κλίνω) __1. an inclination, slope, esp. the slope from the equator to the pole (Arist). __2. a region (Polyb., al.): pl., Rom.15:23, 2Co.11:10, Gal.1:21.† (AS)

G2825.d: κλίνη, -ης, ἡ (κλίνω), a bed, couch: Mat.9:2, 6, Mrk.4:21 7:4, 30, Luk.5:18 8:16 17:34, Rev.2:22 (cf. MM, Exp., xv).† (AS)

G2826.d: κλινίδιον, -ου, τό dimin. of κλίνη, a conch: Luk.5:19, 24 (cf. κλενάριον).† (AS)

G2827.d: κλίνω __1. to make to bend, to bow: τ. κεφαλήν (of one dying), Jhn.19:30; τ. πρόσωτον (of terrified persons), Luk.24:5. __2. to make to lean, to rest: τ. κεφαλήν (in sleep), Mat.8:20, Luk.9:58. __3. As in Hom., of soldiers, to turn (to flight), παρεμβολάς, Heb.11:34. __4. In late Gk. (as mid, in cl.), to decline: intrans., ἡ ἡμέρα, Luk.9:12 24:29.† (AS)

G2828.d: κλισία, -ας, ή (κλίνω), __1. a place for reclining; hence, __(a) a hut; __(b) an easy chair; __(with) a couch. __2. a company reclining: pl., Luk.9:14 (cf. FlJ, Ant., xii, 2, 12) (AS)

G2829.d: κλοπή, -ῆν, ἡ (κλέπτω), theft: pl., Mat.15:19, Mrk.7:22.† (AS)

G2830.d: κλύδων, -ωνος, ὁ (κλύζω, of the sea, to wash over), a billow, surge: Luk.8:24, Jas.1:6.† SYN.: κῦμα, a wave (AS)

G2831.d: κλυδωνίζομαι (κλύδων), to be tossed by waves; metaphorically, to be tossed like waves (cf. FlJ, Ant., ix, 11, 3): Eph.4:14.† (AS)

G2832.d: Κλωπᾶς, -ᾶ, ὁ (Aram.; on the original, see Lft., Gal., 267 f.), Clopas: Jhn.19:25.† (AS)

G2833.d: κνήθω (late form of κνάω), __1. to scratch. __2. to tickle; pass., to itch: 2Ti.4:3.† (AS)

G2834.d: Κνίδος, -ου, ἡ Cnidus, a city (and peninsula) on S.W. coast of Asia Minor: Act.27:7.† (AS)

G2835.d: κοδράντης, -ου, ὁ (Lat. quadrans, the fourth part of an as), a quadrans (AV, farthing): Mat.5:26, Mrk.12:42.† (AS)

G2836.d: κοιλία, -ας, ἡ (κοῖλος, hollow), __1. the belly (stomach or intestines or both): Mat.12:40 15:17, Mrk.7:19, Luk.15:16, Rom.16:18, 1Co.6:13, Php.3:19, Rev.10:9-10. __2. (As often in LXX) the womb: Luk.1:41-42, 44 2:21 11:27 23:29, Jhn.3:4; ἐκ κ. μητρός (cf. Psa.22:11, Job.1:21, al.), Mat.19:12, Luk.1:15, Act.3:2 14:8, Gal.1:15. __3. Metaphorical (as Heb. בֶּטֶן, cf. Job.15:35, Pro.20:27,…

G2837.d: κοιμάω, -ῶ to lull to sleep, put to sleep. Mid and pass., to fall asleep (M, Pr., 162; M, Th., 1, 4, 13): Mat.28:13, Luk.22:45, Jhn.11:12, Act.12:6. Metaph, of death: Mat.27:52, Jhn.11:11 Act.7:60 13:36, 1Co.7:39 11:30 15:6 15:18 15:20 15:51, 1Th.4:13-15, 2Pe.3:4 (cf. Isa.14:8 43:17, 2Ma.12:45).† SYN.: καθεύδω (AS)

G2838.d: κοίμησις, -εως, ἡ a reclining, resting: Jhn.11:13.† (AS)

G2839G.d: κοινός, -ή, -όν __1. common (general; = Lat. communis): Act.2:44 4:32; κ. πίστις, Tit.1:4; σωτηρία, Ju 3 __2. common (ordinary; = vulgaris); hence in LXX (1Ma.1:47, al.) and NT, unhallowed, unclean (cl., βέβηλος, which see): Mrk.7:2, 5, Act.10:14, 28 11:8, Rom.14:14, Heb.10:29, Rev.21:27.† (AS)

G2839H.d: κοινός, -ή, -όν __1. common (general; = Lat. communis): Act.2:44 4:32; κ. πίστις, Tit.1:4; σωτηρία, Ju 3 __2. common (ordinary; = vulgaris); hence in LXX (1Ma.1:47, al.) and NT, unhallowed, unclean (cl., βέβηλος, which see): Mrk.7:2, 5, Act.10:14, 28 11:8, Rom.14:14, Heb.10:29, Rev.21:27.† (AS)

G2840.d: κοινόω, -ῶ __1. in cl., to make common. __2. In LXX, l.with, and NT (as κοινός, 2), to make ceremonially unclean, to profane (= cl., βεληλόω): Mat.15:11, 18 15:20, Mrk.7:15, 18 7:20, 23, Act.21:28; pass., Heb.9:13. __3. to count unclean (cf. δικαιόω): Act.10:15 11:9.† SYN.: βεβηλόω. Thayer (see word κ.) mentions that Winer Notes the accuracy whereby the Jews are said to use κ. in addressing Jews,…

G2841.d: κοινωνέω, -ῶ to have a share of, go shares in (something) with (some one), take part in: with genitive of thing(s) (as usually in cl., so Pr, l.with), Heb.2:14; with dative of thing(s), Rom.12:13 15:27, 1Ti.5:22, 1Pe.4:13, 2Jn.11; with dative of person(s), before εἰς, Php.4:15; ἐν, Gal.6:6 (cf. συν-κοινωνέω).† (AS)

G2842.d: κοινωνία, -ας, ἡ (κοινωνός), __1. fellowship, communion: Act.2:42, 2Co.6:14, Php.1:5; τ. υἱοῦ, 1Co.1:9; τ. αἵματος, σώματος Χρ., 1Co.10:10 : παθημάτων αὐτσῦ, Php.3:10; τ. πνεύματος, 2Co.13:13, Php.2:1; δεξιὰς κοινωνίας, Gal.2:9; τ. πίστεώς σου, Phm 6; before μετὰ: τ. πατρός, 1Jn.1:3 Jn 1:6; ἡμῶν, ἀλλήλων, 1Jn.1:3 Jn 1:7. __2. contribution (as outcome of fellowship): Rom.15:26, 2Co.8:4 9:13,…

G2843.d: κοινωνικός, -ή, -όν (κοινωνία), __1. sociable. __2. ready to com­municate or impart (R, mg., ready to sympathize, see Field, Notes, 213 f.): 1Ti.6:18.† (AS)

G2844.d: κοινωνός, -ή, -όν (κοινός), __1. as adj., = κοινός. __2. As subst., ὁ, ἡ κ., __(a) a partner, associate, companion: 2Co.8:23, Phm 17; with dative of person(s), Luk.5:10; with genitive of person(s), Heb.10:33; id. before ἐν, Mat.23:30; __(b) a partaker, sharer: with genitive of thing(s), 1Co.10:18 10:20, 2Co.1:7, 1Pe.5:1, 2Pe.1:4 (see Deiss., BS, 368 n2).† (AS)

G2845.d: κοίτη, -ης, ἡ (in Hom., κοῖτος) a bed: Luk.11:7; esp. the marriage-bed: κ. ἀμίαντος, Heb.13:4; κ. ἔχειν, of a woman conceiving, Rom.9:10 (cf. peculiar phrases in LXX, Lev.15:18, al.); of illicit intercourse, pl., Rom.13:13.† (AS)

G2846.d: κοιτών, -ῶνος, ὁ (κοίτη = Att.., δωμότιον, see Kennedy, Sources, 40), a bed-chamber; ὁ ἐπὶ τοῦ κ., a chamberlain: Act.12:20.† (AS)

G2847.d: κόκκινος, -η, -ον (κόκκος, as used of the "berry" of the ilex coccifera, see DB, iv, 416), scarlet: Mat.27:28, Heb.9:19, Rev.17:3; neut., without substantive, of clothing, Rev.17:4 18:12, 16,† (AS)

G2849.d: κολάζω (κόλος, docked), __1. to curtail, dock, prune. __2. to check, restrain. __3. to chastise, correct, punish: pass., 2Pe.2:9; mid., cause to be punished (3Ma.7:3): Act.4:21.† (AS)

G2850.d: κολακία (Rec. -εία), -ας, ἡ (κολακεύω, to flatter), flattery: 1Th.2:5 (see Lft., Notes, 23).† (AS)

G2851.d: κόλασις, -εως, ἡ (κολάζω), correction, penalty, punishment: Mat.25:46, 1Jn.4:18.† SYN.: τιμωρία, requital. Arist. distinguishes between κ . as that which, being disciplinary, has reference to the sufferer, and τ. as that which, being penal, has reference to the satisfaction of him who inflicts (see Thayer, see word κ., and cf. Tr., Syn., § vii). But in late Gk. especially, the distinction is not…

G2852.d: κολαφίζω (κόλαφος = Att.., κόνδυλοι, the knuckles, the closed fist) to strike with the fist, to buffet: Mat.26:67, Mrk.14:65, 2Co.12:7; pass., 1Co.4:11, 1Pe.2:20.† (AS)

G2853.d: κολλάω, -ῶ (κόλλα, glue), __1. to glue or cement together. __2. Generally, to unite, to join firmly. Pass., to cleave to, join (oneself to): with dative of person(s), Mat.19:5(LXX), Luk.10:11 15:15, Act.5:13 (but see Field, Notes, 118) Act.9:26 10:28 (see Field, l.with) Act.17:34; τ. πόρνῃ, 1Co.6:16; τ. Κυρίῳ, 1Co.6:17; with dative of thing(s), ἅρματι, Act.8:29; τ. ἀγαθῴ, Rom.12:9; of sins…

G2854.d: κολλούριον (TTr., κολλύ-, the more usual form), -ου, τό (dimin. of κολλύρα = κόλλιξ, a coarse bread roll), __1. a small bread roll (LXX, ll. with). __2. (Usually in pl., LS, see word) an eye salve shaped like a roll: Rev.3:18.† (AS)

G2855.d: κολλυβιστής, -οῦ, ὁ (κόλλυβος, a small coin, a rate of exchange), a money-changer: Mat.21:12, Mrk.11:15, Jhn.2:15 (of. κερματιοτής).† (AS)

G2856.d: κολοβόω, -ῶ (κολοβός, docked), to cut off, amputate (LXX), hence, to curtail, shorten: Mat.24:22, Mrk.13:20.† (AS)

G2857G.d: Κολοσσαί (so in cl.; -ασσαί, Rec., LTr.), -ῶν, αἰ Colossæ, a city on the Lycus in Phrygia: Col.1:2.† (AS)

G2858.d: Κολασσαεύς (Rec. Κολοσ-), -έως, ὁ a Colossian: pl., Col., tit. (and subscr., Rec., Tr.).† (AS)

G2859.d: κόλπος, -ου, ὁ __1. prop., the bosom: Jhn.13:23; fig., of close association, ἐν (εἰς τὸν) τοῖς κ. Ἀβραάμ, Luk.16:22-23 (cf. 4Ma.13:16); ὁ ὢν εἰς τὸν κ. τ. πατρός, Jhn.1:18 __2. The bosom or fold of a loose garment falling over a girdle, used as a pocket, hence figuratively, εἰς τὸν κ. Isa.65:6, Jer.32:18 : Luk.6:38 __3. A bosom-like hollow, as a bay or gulf: Act.27:39.† (AS)

G2860.d: κολυμβάω, -ῶ [in AI.: Isa.25:11 * ;] to dive, plunge into the sea: Act.27:43 (cf. ἐκ-κολνμβάω).† (AS)

G2861.d: κολυμβήθρα, -ας, ἡ (κολνμβάω), a swimming pool, pool: Jhn.5:2, 4 5:7 9:7.† (AS)

G2862.d: κολωνία (Rec. -ώνια), -ας, ἡ (Lat. colonic), a colony: Act.16:12 (see Lft., Phi., 50 f.).† (AS)

G2865.d: κομίζω __1. to take care of. __2. to carry off safe. __3. to carry off as booty. __4. to bear or carry: Luk.7:37. Mid., to bear for oneself, hence, __(a) to receive: Heb.10:36 11:13, 39, 1Pe.1:9 5:4, 2Pe.2:13; __(b) to receive back, recover (in cl. so also act.): Mat.25:27, Heb.11:19; metaphorically, of requital, 2Co.5:10, Col.3:25; παρὰ Κυρίου, Eph.6:8 (cf. ἐκ-, συν-κομίζω).† (AS)

G2866.d: κομψός, -ή, -όν (κομέω, to take care of), well-dressed, elegant, fine; compar. neut., κομψότερον ἔχειν (cf. κόμψως ἔχειν, Epict., and colloq. Eng., "to be doing finely"): Jhn.4:52.† (AS)

G2867.d: κονιάω, -ῶ (κονία, dust, lime), to plaster or whiten over: of tombs, Mat.23:27; figuratively, of a hypocrite, Act.23:3.† (AS)

G2868.d: κονιορτός, -οῦ, ὁ (κόνις or κονία, dust, ὄρνυμι, to stir up), in cl., dust stirred up (Exo.9:9, Isa.5:24); in NT, simply dust: Mat.10:14, Luk.9:5 10:11, Act.13:51 22:23.† (AS)

G2869.d: κοπάζω (κόπος), to grow weary; of the wind (Hdt., Jh., l.with), to abate, cease raging: Mat.14:32, Mrk.4:39 6:51.† (AS)

G2870.d: κοπετός, -οῦ, ὁ (κόπτω, mid.), = cl. κομμός, a beating of the head and breast, lamentation: before ἐπί with dative of person(s), Act.8:2.† (AS)

G2871.d: κοπή, -ῆς, ἡ (κόπτω), __1. in cl., a stroke, a pounding (as in a mortar). __2. In LXX, a smiting in battle: Heb.7:1 (LXX).† (AS)

G2872.d: κοπιάω, -ῶ (κόπος), __1. (as in cl.) to grow weary: Mat.11:28, Jhn.4:6, Rev.2:3 (cf. Isa.40:31). __2. Hence, in LXX and NT, to work with effort, to toil: absol., Mat.6:23, Luk.5:5 12:27, Jhn.4:38, Act.20:35, 1Co.4:12, Eph.4:28, 2Ti.2:5; with accusative of thing(s), Jhn.4:38; frequently in Paul. Epp., of ministerial labour: 1Co.15:10 16:16; before ἐν, Rom.16:12, 1Th.5:12 (see M, Th., in l),…

G2873.d: κόπος, -ου, ὁ (κόπτω) __1. a striking, beating (in Jer.45:3 = κοπετός) __2. laborious toil, trouble: Jhn.4:38, 1Co.3:8 15:58, 1Th.3:5; κ. τ. ἀγάπης, 1Th.1:3; ἔργα καὶ κ., Rev.2:2; κ. καὶ μόχθος, 2Co.11:27, 1Th.2:9, 2Th.3:8; pl., ἐν κ., 2Co.6:5 10:15 11:23; ἐκ τ. κ., Rev.14:13; κόπονς (-ον) παρέχειν (in cl. more frequently π. πράγματα, πονον), with dative of person(s), Mat.26:10, Mrk.14:6,…

G2874.d: κοπρία, -ας, ἡ a dung hill (1Ki.2:8, Psa.113:7 al.): Luk.14:35.† κόπριον, -ου, τό, = κόπρος, dung: pl., Luk.13:8 (WH, mg., κόφινον κοπρίων).† (AS)

G2875.d: κόπτω __1. to strike, smite. __2. to cut off: with accusative of thing(s), before ἀπό, Mat.21:8; ἐκ, Mrk.11:8. (ML)
