G3454.d: μῦθος, -ου, ὁ __1. speech, con­versation. __2. (a) a story, narrative (Hom.); __(b) later, opposite to λόγος (a true narrative) = Lat. fabula, a myth, fable, fiction: 1Ti.1:4 4:7, 2Ti.4:4, Tit.1:14, 2Pe.1:16.† SYN.. λόγος, q.v (AS)

G3455.d: μυκάσμαι, -ῶμαι in cl. chiefly poët., [in Sm.: Job.6:5 * ;] prop., of oxen (onomatop.), to low, bellow; of a lion, to roar: Rev.10:3.† (AS)

G3456.d: μυκτηρίζω (μυκτήρ, the nose), to turn up the nose or sneer at, mock: pass., Gal.6:7 (cf. ἐκ-μυκτηρίζω).† (AS)

G3457.d: μυλικός, -ή, -όν (μύλη, a mill), of a mill: λίθος μ., Luk.17:2.† (AS)

G3458.d: μύλος, -ου, ὁ __1. = μύλη, a mill (Strab., Plut., LXX) : Mat.24:41, Rev.18:22. __2. a mill-stone (Anth.) : Rev.18:21 (T); μ. ὀνικός, Mat.18:6, Mrk.9:42 (see Swete, in l).† (AS)

G3459.d: μυλών, -ῶος, ὁ a mill-house: Mat.24:41 (Rec.; μύλος, WH, R).† (AS)

G3460.d: Μύρα, Μύρρα (LT, Tr., WH), -ων, τά, Myra, a city of Lycia : Act.27:5.† (AS)

G3461.d: μυριάς, -άδος, ἡ (μυρίος), ten thousand, a myriad: pl., Act.19:19, Rev.5:11 9:16; hyperb., of vast numbers, Luk.12:1, Act.21:20, Heb.12:12, Ju 14.† (AS)

G3462.d: μυρίζω (μύρον), Ionic and poët. (comic), to anoint: Mrk.14:8.† SYN.: see: ἀλείφω, and cf. μύρον (AS)

G3463.d: μυρίος, -α, -ον __1. numberless, countless, infinite: 1Co.4:15 14:19. __2. As a definite numeral, in pl., μύριοι, -αι, -α, ten thousand: Mat.18:24.† (AS)

G3464.d: μύρον, -ου, τό ointment: Mat.26:7, 12, Mrk.14:3-5, Luk.7:37-38, 46 23:56, Jhn.11:2 12:3, 5, Rev.18:13.† SYN.: ἔλαιον, q.v (AS)

G3465.d: Μυσία, -ας, ἡ Mysia, a province of Asia Minor: Act.16:7-8.† (AS)

G3466.d: μυστήρισν, -ου, τό (μυέω), __1. that which is known to the μύστης (initiated), a mystery or secret doctrine, mostly in pl., τὰ μ. (Æsch., Hdt., al.). __2. In later writers (Menand., Incert., 168), that which may not be revealed (not, however, as in the modern sense, intrinsically difficult to understand), a secret or mystery of any kind (To, Jth, 2Mac, ll, with). __3. In NT, of the counsels of…

G3467.d: μυ-ωπάζω (μύωψ, closing the eyes, short-sighted; μύω, ὤψ) to be short-sighted: 2Pe.1:9 (R, mg., closing his eyes; see ICC, in l).† (AS)

G3468.d: μώλωψ, -ωπος, ὁ a bruise, wound from a stripe: 1Pe.2:24 (LXX) (Arist., Plut., al.).† (AS)

G3469.d: μωμάομαι, -ῶμαι (μῶμος), poët. and late prose, to find fault with, blame: 2Co.8:20; pass., 2Co.6:3.† (AS)

G3470.d: μῶμος, -ου, ὁ __1. in cl. poets and late prose, blame, disgrace. __2. In LXX, perb. because of resemblance to a physical blemish (cf. ἄμωμος, 1Pe.1:19, and see Hort., in l); metaphorically, of licentious persons, 2Pe.2:13.† (AS)

G3471.d: μωραίνω (μωρός), __1. cl., to be foolish, play the fool. __2. LXX and NT, causal, to make foolish: 1Co.1:20; pass., to become foolish: Rom.1:22; of salt that has lost its flavour, become tasteless: Mat.5:13, Luk.14:34.† (AS)

G3474.d: μωρός, -ά, -όν __1. prop., of the nerves, dull, sluggish (Hipp., Arist.). __2. Of the mind, dull, stupid, foolish: Mat.5:22 (see Field, Notes, 3 ff.) Mat.7:26 23:17, 19 (T, WH, txt., R, om.) Mat.25:2-3, 8, 1Co.3:18 4:10; of things, παράδοσις, Mrk.7:13 (T, WH, txt., R, om.) : ζητήσεις, 2Ti.2:23, Tit.3:9; τὸ μ. τ. θεοῦ, 1Co.1:25; τὰ μ. τ. κόσμου, 1Co.1:27.† (AS)

G3475.d: Μωυσῆς (Μωϋσῆς, T; Μωσῆς, Rec.), -έως, dative - (as LXX: Exo.5:20, al.), and -εῖ, accusative -ῆν (ac LXX) and -έα (Luk.16:29 only) (Heb. מֹשֶׁה), Moses: Mat.8:4 17:3-4, al.; νόμος Μωυσέως, Luk.2:22 24:44, Jhn.7:23, Act.13:39 15:5 28:23, 1Co.9:9, Heb.10:28; by meton., of the books of Moses, Luk.16:29 24:27, Act.15:21, 2Co.3:15 (AS)

G3476.d: Ναασσών, ὁ indecl. (Heb. נַחְשׁוֹן), Naasson: Mat.1:4, Luk.3:32.† (AS)

G3478.d: Ναζαρά (Mat.4:13­ L, -άθ­Luk.4:16) Ναζαρέθ (Mat.21:11, Act.10:38), Ναζαρέτ (so always Rec.; WH, in foll, instances, where -έθ, T), ἡ, indecl. (Semitic form uncertain), Nazareth: Mat.2:23, Mrk.1:9, Luk.1:26 2:4, 39 2:51, Jhn.1:45-46.† (AS)

G3479.d: Ναζαρηνός, -οῦ, ὁ (on the Semitic form, see Dalman, Gr., 141 n.) a Nazarene: Mrk.1:24 10:47 14:67 16:6, Luk.4:34 24:19.† (AS)

G3480.d: Ναζωραῖος, -ου, ὁ (= -ρηνός, which see), a Nazarene: Mat.2:23 (LXX) Mat.26:71, Luk.18:37, Jhn.18:5, 7 19:19, Act.2:22 3:6 4:10 6:14 22:8 24:5 26:9.† (AS)

G3481.d: Ναθάμ (Rec. Ναθάν), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. נָתַן), Nathan: Luk.3:31.† (AS)

G3482.d: Ναθαναήλ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. נְתַנְאֵל), Nathaniel, prob. to be identified with Bartholomew (which see): Jhn.1:45-49 21:2.† (AS)

G3483.d: ναί particle of affirmation, yea, verily, even so; in answer to a question: Mat.9:28 13:51 17:25 21:16, Jhn.11:27 21:15-16, Act.5:8 22:27, Rom.3:29; before λέγω ὑμῖν, Mat.11:9, Luk.7:26; repeated for emphasis, ναὶ ναί (opposite to oὒ oὔ): Mat.5:37; ἤτω ὑμῶν τὸ ναὶ ναί, Jas.5:12; ν. καὶ οὔ, 2Co.1:18-19; ἵνα ᾖ . . . τὸ ναὶ ναί, 2Co.1:17; τὸ ν., 2Co.1:20; in assent to an assertion: Mat.15:27,…

G3484.d: Ναίν (Rec. Ναΐν), ἡ, indecl. (Heb. נָאָה), Nain, a village of Galilee: Luk.7:11.† (AS)

G3485.d: ναός, -οῦ, ὁ (Att.. νεώς; ναίω, to inhabit), __1. a temple (Hom., Find., al.). __2. The inmost part of a temple, the shrine (Hat., Xen., al.); in NT, __(a) generally: pl., Act.17:24; of silver models of a heathen shrine, Act.19:24; __(b) of the temple building proper, or sanctuary, at Jerusalem, as distinct from τ. ἱερόν (which see), the whole temple enclosure: Mat.23:16-17, 35 27:5, 40,…

G3486.d: Ναούμ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. נַחוּם;), Nahum: Luk.3:25.† (AS)

G3487.d: νάρδος, -ου, ἡ (Heb. נֵרְדְּ, both from Sanscrit narda, see Boisacq, see word), nard; __(a) an Indian plant, the Nardostachys nardus jatamansi, used for the preparation of a fragrant ointment; __(b) ointment of nard: Mrk.14:3, Jhn.12:3.† (AS)

G3488.d: the narcissus , (Homeric Hymns), etc. From ναρκάω, because of its narcotic properties. (ML)

G3489.d: ναυαγέω, -ῶ (ναῦς, + ἄγνυμι, to break) to suffer shipwreck: 2Co.11:25; metaphorically, before περὶ τ. πίστιν, 1Ti.1:19.† (AS)

G3490.d: ναύ-κληρος, -ου, ὁ (ναῦς, κλῆρος), a shipowner, shipmaster: Act.27:11.† (AS)

G3491.d: ναῦς, νεώς accusative ναῦν, ἡ, a ship: Act.27:41 (elsewhere in NT always τ. πλοῖον; see M, Pro.25:1-28 f.; Bl., Gosp., 186 f.).† (AS)

G3492.d: ναύτης, -ου, ὁ (ναῦς), [in Aq.: Eze.27:9; Sm.: Eze.27:29 * ;] a seaman, sailor: Act.27:27, 30, Rev.18:17.† (AS)

G3493.d: Ναχώρ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. נָחוֹר), Nahor: Luk.3:34.† (AS)

G3494.d: νεανίας, -ου, ὁ (νεάν = νέος) a young man: Act.7:58 20:9 23:17-18.† (AS)

G3495.d: νεανίσκος, -ου, ὁ (dimin. of νεανίας) a young man, youth: Mat.19:20, 22, Mrk.14:51 16:5, Luk.7:14, Act.2:17" (LXX) Act.23:18, 22, 1Jn.2:13-14; of an attendant (cf. Gen.14:24, al.) : Act.5:10.† (AS)

G3497.d: Ναιμάν (Rec. Νεεμάν), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. נַעֲמָן), Naaman: Luk.4:27.† (AS)

G3498.d: νεκρός, -α, -ον, dead, __I. as adj., __1. prop.: Act.5:10 20:9, Jas.2:26, Rev.1:18, al.; ὡσεὶ ν., Mat.28:4, Mrk.9:26, Rev.1:17; of that which is subject to death, Rom.8:10. __2. Metaphorical, __(a) of persons: Luk.15:24, 32; of those immersed in worldly cares, Mat.8:22, Luk.9:60; of spiritual death, Jhn.5:25, Rom.6:13, Eph.5:14, Rev.3:1; τ. παραπτώμασιν, Eph.2:1, 5 Col.2:13; of the opposite…

G3499.d: νεκρόω, ῶ (νεκρός), to make dead, put to death; pass., to be dead: hyperbolically, of impotent age, Heb.11:12; σῶμα, Rom.4:19. Trop., of carnal impulses, τὰ μέλη, Col.3:5.† (AS)

G3500.d: νέκρωσις, -εως, ἡ (νεκρόω), __1. a putting to death. __2. a state of death, death: Rom.4:19, 2Co.4:10 (see Deiss., LAE, 94).† (AS)

G3501.d: νέος, -α, -ον __1. young, youthful: Tit.2:4. __2. new (prop., in respect of time; see: καινός): οἶνος (cf. οἶ. καινός, Mat.26:20), Mat.9:17, Mrk.2:22, Luk.5:37-39; φύραμα (figuratively), 1Co.5:7; διαθήκη (cf. καινὴ δ., Heb.9:15), Heb.12:24; metaphorically, ἄνθρωπος (cf. καινὸς ἀ, Eph.2:15), Col.3:10. __3. Compar., -ώτερος, -α, -ον, younger: Luk.15:12-13 22:26, Jhn.21:18; pl., οἱ ν., Act.5:6…

G3502.d: νοσσός (νεοσσός, Rec., as in cl. Att.. -ττός; Phryn. rejects the dissyl. form), -οῦ, ὁ (νόος), a young bird: Luk.2:24 (LXX).† (AS)

G3503.d: νεότης, -ητος, ἡ (νέος), youth: Mrk.10:20, Luk.18:21, Act.26:4, 1Ti.4:12.† (AS)

G3504.d: νεό-φυτος, -ον (νέος, φύω) newly planted (LXX). Metaphorical, as subst., ὁ ν., a new convert, neophyte, novice: 1Ti.3:6† (AS)

G3506.d: νεύω to nod or beckon, as a sign : with dative of person(s) and inf., Jhn.13:24, Act.24:10 (cf. δια-, ἐκ-, ἐν-, ἐπι-, κατα-νεύω).† (AS)

G3507.d: νεφέλη, -ης, ἡ (νέφος), a cloud (single and specific as opposite to νεφος, a great indefinite mass of vapour): Mat.17:5 24:30 26:64, Mrk.9:7 13:26 14:62, Luk.9:34-35 12:54 21:37, Act.1:9, 1Th.4:17, Ju 12, Rev.1:7 10:1 11:12 14:14-16; of the pillar of cloud in the wilderness (Exo.14:19-20, Psa.105:39, al.): 1Co.10:1-2.† (AS)

G3508.d: Νεφθαλείμ (-λίμ, WH in Re, l.with), ὁ indecl. (Heb. נַפְתָּלִי) Naphtali: Mat.4:13, 15" (LXX) Rev.7:6.† (AS)

G3509.d: νέφος, -ους, τό a mass of clouds, a cloud (cf. νεφέλη); metaphorically as in Hom., Hdt., al.), of a dense throng: Heb.12:1.† (AS)

G3510.d: νεφρός, -οῦ, ὁ a kidney; pl., the kidneys, reins; metaphorically, of the will and affections: ν. καί καρδίαι (thoughts), Rev.2:23.† (AS)

G3511.d: νεω-κόρος, -ου a temple-keeper; as honorary title given to a city (see DB, i, 722 b) : Act.19:35.† (AS)

G3512.d: νεωτερικός, -ή, -όν (νεώτερος), = νεανικός, youthful, esp. of qualities: ἐπιθυμίαι, 2Ti.2:22 (Polyb.).† (AS)

G3513.d: νή particle of affirmation employed in oaths, by: with accusative, 1Co.15:31.† (AS)

G3515.d: νηπιάζω (νήπιος), (Hippocr., = νηπιαχεύω, Hom.) to be a babe: 1Co.14:20.† (AS)

G3516.d: νήπιος, -α, -ον infant; of children and minors: Mat.21:16 (LXX), 1Co.13:11, Gal.4:1 (see Lft., in l). Metaphorical, childish, unskilled, simple (Psa.19:8, Pro.1:32 al.): Mat.11:25, Luk.10:21, Rom.2:20, Gal.4:3, Eph.4:14, 1Th.2:7 (WH, fox ἤπιοι); opposite to τέλειος, Heb.5:13; ν. ἐν Χριστῷ, 1Co.3:1.† (AS)

G3517.d: Nereus , a sea-god, son of Πόντος (the sea) , father of the Nereids, (Hesiod) (ML)

G3518.d: Νηρεί (Rec. -ρί), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. נֵרִיָּה), Neri: Luk.3:27.† (AS)

G3519.d: νησίον, -ου, τό (dimin. of νῆσος), = νησίς (Hdt., Thuc., al.) a small island: Act.27:16.† (AS)

G3521.d: νηστεία, -ας, ἡ (νηστεύω), fasting, a fast; __(a) of voluntary abstinence from food: Mat.17:21 (WH, R, txt., om.), Mrk.9:29 (WH, txt., R, txt., om.), Luk.2:37, Act.14:23; of the Day of Atonement, Act.27:9; __(b) of involuntary abstinence: 2Co.6:5 11:27.† SYN.: ἀσιτία, q.v (AS)

G3522.d: νηστεύω (νῆστις), to fast (Arist., Aristoph., al.): Mat.4:2 6:16-18 9:14-15 Mrk.2:18-20, Luk.5:33-35 18:12, Act.13:2-3.† (AS)

G3523.d: νῆστις, -ιος, ὁ, ἡ (νη-, neg. prefix, + ἐσθίω), in cl., chiefly poët., not eating, fasting: Mat.15:32, Mrk.8:3.† (AS)

G3524.d: νηφάλιος (-λεος, Rec., in 1Ti, ll. with), -ον (in cl., -α, -ον), (νήφω), __1. in cl., of drink, not mixed with wine. __2. In later writers (Plut., al.), of persons, sober, temperate: 1Ti.3:2 3:11, Tit.2:2.† (AS)

G3525.d: νήφω to be sober, abstain from wine; metaphorically, of moral alertness, to be sober, calm, circumspect: 1Th.5:6 5:8, 2Ti.4:5 (see Ellic., in l), 1Pe.1:13 4:7 5:8 (cf. ἐκ-, ἐκ-νήφω, and see MM, xvii).† SYN.: ἀγρυπνέω, γρηγορέω (AS)

G3528.d: νικἀω, -ῶ (νίκη), to conquer, prevail: absol., of Christ, Rev.3:21 6:2; C. inf., Rev.5:5; of Christians, Rev.2:7, 11 2:17, 26 3:5, 12 3:21 21:7; before ἐκ (RV, come victorious from), Rev.15:2; as law-term (cl.), Rom.3:4 (LXX); with accusative of person(s), Luk.11:22, Rev.11:7 13:7 ([WH], R, mg., om.); of Christ, Jhn.16:33 (τ. κόσμον), Rev.17:14; of Christians, 1Jn.4:4; τ. πονηρόν, 1Jn.2:13-14;…

G3531.d: Νικολαΐτης, -αυ, ὁ a Nicolaitan: pl., Rev.2:6, 15.† (AS)

G3533.d: Νικόπολις, -εως, ἡ Nicopolis, prob. the city of that name in Epirus (CGT, in l): Tit.3:12† (AS)

G3534.d: νῖκος, -ους, τό late form of νίκη, victory: Mat.12:20 (Isa.42:3, LXX ἀλήθεια), 1Co.15:54 (Isa.25:8, Aq., Th.), 1Co.15:55 (Hos.13:14, LXX δίκη), 1Co.15:57.† (AS)

G3535.d: Νινευΐ, η (Heb. נִינְוֵה), Nineveh: Luk.11:32, Rec.† (AS)

G3536.d: Νινευείτης (Rec. -ενίτης, L, -ΐτης), -ου, ὁ a Ninevite: Mat.12:41, Luk.11:30, 32.† (AS)

G3538.d: νίπτω late form of νίζω, to wash, usually of a part of the body: with accusative of person(s), Jhn.13:8; τ. πόδας, Jhn.13:5-6, 8 13:12, 14, 1Ti.5:10; mid., reflexive, to wash oneself: Jhn.9:7, 11 9:15; τ. χεῖρας, Mat.15:2, Mrk.7:3; τ. πόδας, Jhn.13:10; τ. πρόσωπον, Mat.6:17 (in cl. Att.. prose, used only in compounds; cf. ἀπο-νίπτω).† νίζω, see: νίπτω SYN.: λούω (which see), πλύνω (AS)

G3539.d: νοιεω νοέω, -ῶ (νοῦς), __1. to perceive with the mind, understand (for the phrase νοῶν κ. φρονῶν, in wills, see MM, xvii): absol., Mat.16:9, Mrk.8:17; with accusative, Eph.3:4, 1Ti.1:7; with dative instr., τ. καρδίᾳ, Jhn.12:40; pass., Rom.1:20; before ὅτι, Mat.15:17 16:11, Mrk.7:18; with accusative and inf., Heb.11:8. __2. to think, consider: absol., Mat.24:15, Mrk.13:14, Eph.3:20; with…

G3540.d: νόημα, -τος, τό (νοέω) a thought, purpose, design: 2Co.2:11 10:5 11:3, Php.4:7. Meton., of the mind, 2Co.3:14 4:4.† (AS)

G3541.d: νόθος, -η, -ον a bastard, base born, i.e. born of a slave or concubine: Heb.12:8.† (AS)

G3542.d: νομή, -ῆς, ἡ (νέμω, to pasture), __1. a pasture, pasturage: figuratively, Jhn.10:9 __2. a grazing, feeding; metaphorically, of a spreading sore, 2Ti.2:17 (Polyb.).† (AS)

G3543.d: νομίζω (νόμος), __1. to practise, hold by custom: Act.16:13 (Rec., but see infr.). __2. to deem, consider, suppose: Mat.5:17 10:34 20:10, Luk.2:44 3:23, Act.7:25 8:20 14:19 16:13, 27 17:29 21:29, 1Co.7:26 7:36, 1Ti.6:5.† SYN.: ἡγέομαι, q.v (AS)

G3544.d: νομικός, -ή, -όν (νόμος), __1. relating to law: μάχαι, Tit.3:9. __2. learned in the law; as subst., ὁ ν. (EV, lawyer): Mat.22:35, Luk.10:25, Tit.3:13; pl., Luk.7:30 11:45-46, 52 14:3 (cf. MM, xvii).† SYN.: γραμματεύς, q.v (AS)

G3545.d: νομίμως adv. (νόμιμος, conformable to law), rightly, lawfully: 1Ti.1:8, 2Ti.2:5.† (AS)

G3546.d: νόμισμα, -τος, τό (νομίζω), __1. that which is established by usage, a custom. __2. The current coin of a state: Mat.22:19.† (AS)

G3547.d: νομο-διδάσκαλος, -ου, ὁ a teacher of the law: Luk.5:17, Act.5:34, 1Ti.1:7 (NT and eccl. only; cf. νομοδείκτης, -διδάκτης, Plut.).† SYN.: γραμματεύς, q.v (AS)

G3548.d: νομοθεσία, -ας, ἡ (νόμος, τίθημι), legislation, lawgiving: Rom.9:4.† (AS)

G3549.d: νομοθετέω, -ῶ __1. intrans., to make laws; pass., to be furnished with laws: Heb.7:11. __2. Trans., to ordain by law, enact: pass., Heb.8:6.† (AS)

G3550.d: νομο-θέτης, -ου, ὁ (νόμος, τίθημι), a law­giver: Jas.4:12.† (AS)

G3551.d: νόμος, -ου, ὁ (νέμω, to deal out, distribute), that which is assigned, hence, usage, custom, then law; in NT (only in Mt, Jo, Ja, and the Lucan and Pauline bks.); __1. of law in general: Rom.3:27 5:13b; pl., of divine laws, Heb.8:10 10:16; ὁ ν. τ. Χριστοῦ, Gal.6:2; (τ.) ἐλευθερίας, Jas.1:25 2:12; βασιλικιός (Hort., in l.; Deiss., LAE, 267:3), Jas.2:8. __2. Of a force or influence impelling to…

G3552.d: νοσέω, -ῶ (νόσος), to be sick: metaphorically, of mental ailment, before περί, 1Ti.6:4 (cf. Plat., Mor., 546 d).† (AS)

G3554.d: νόσος, -ου, ὁ disease, sickness: Mat.4:23-24 8:17 (Aq.) Mat.9:35 10:1, Mrk.1:34, Luk.4:40 6:17 7:21 9:1, Act.19:12.† SYN.: see: ἀσθένεια (AS)

G3555.d: νοσσιά, -ᾶς, ἡ (νοσσός), late form of cl., νεοσσιά, __1. a nest of birds. __2. a brood of young birds: Luk.13:34.† (AS)

G3556.d: νοσσίον, -ου, τό dimin. of νοσσός, which see, a young bird: Mat.23:37.† (AS)

G3557.d: νοσφίζω (νόσφι, apart, aside), __1. in Hom., as depon., to turn away (from), abandon. __2. After Hom., in act., to set apart, remove. Mid., to set apart for oneself, peculate, purloin: absol., Tit.2:10 (for ex. in π., see MM, xvii); before ἀπό, Act.5:2-3.† (AS)

G3558G.d: νότος, -ου, ὁ __1. prop., the south wind: Luk.12:55, Act.27:13 28:13 __2. South: Luk.13:29, Rev.21:13 __3. the South, as a region (cf. נֶגֶב): Mat.12:42, Luk.11:31.† (AS)

G3558H.d: νότος, -ου, ὁ __1. prop., the south wind: Luk.12:55, Act.27:13 28:13 __2. South: Luk.13:29, Rev.21:13 __3. the South, as a region (cf. נֶגֶב): Mat.12:42, Luk.11:31.† (AS)

G3559.d: νουθεσία, -ας ἡ (νουθετέω), = cl. νουθέτησις admonition: 1Co.10:11, Eph.6:4, Tit.3:10 (Aristoph., Diod., al.).† (AS)

G3560.d: νουθετέω, -ῶ (νοῦς, τίθημι, hence, put in mind), to admonish, exhort: with accusative of person(s), Act.20:31, Rom.15:14, 1Co.4:14, Col.1:28 3:16, 1Th.5:12 5:14, 2Th.3:15.† (AS)

G3561.d: νεομηνία (Att.. contr., νουμ-, Rec.), -ας, ἡ (νέος, μήν), new moon: of the Jewish festival, Col.2:16.† (AS)

G3562.d: νουνεχῶς adv. (νοῦς, ἔχω) sensibly, discreetly: Mrk.12:34.† (AS)

G3563.d: νοῦς (contr. from νόος), ὁ, genitive, dative, νοός, νοΐ (late forms, = cl., νοῦ, νῷ; Bl., § 9, 3), accusative, νοῦν, __1. prop., of the ruling faculty, mind, understanding, reason (see Lft., Notes, 88 f.; Vaughan on Rom.7:23): Luk.24:45, Rom.1:28 7:23 12:2 14:5, Eph.4:17, 23 Php.4:7, 2Th.2:2, 1Ti.6:5, 2Ti.3:8, Tit.1:15, Rev.13:18 17:9; ν. τ. σαρκός (ICC, in l), Col.2:18; opposite to σάρξ,…

G3564.d: Νυμφᾶς, -ᾶ, ὁ (WH, R, mg., Νύμφα, which see), Nymphas: Col.4:15, R, txt. (cf. ICC, Lft., in l).† Νύμφα (Rec., R, txt., Νυμφᾶς, which see), -ης, ἡ, Nympha (see M, Pr., 48): Col.4:15, WH, R, mg.† (AS)

G3565.d: νύμφη, -ης, ἡ __1. cl., a bride, young wife, young woman: Mat.25:1, WH, mg., Jhn.3:29, Rev.18:23 21:2, 9 22:17. __2. As frequently in LXX (Gen.38:11, al., for כַּלָּה; __(a) bride; __(b) daughter-in-law) and in MGr. (νύφφη, νύφη), a daughter-in-law: Mat.10:35, Luk.12:53.† (AS)

G3566.d: νυμφίος, -ου, ὁ (νύμφη), a bridegroom: Mat.9:15 25:1, 5-6 25:10, Mrk.2:19-20, Luk.5:34-35, Jhn.2:9 3:29, Rev.18:23.† (AS)

G3567.d: νυμφών, -ῶνος, ὁ (νύμφη), the bride-chamber (Heb. חֻפָּה, LXX, παστός, Psa.19:5, Jol.2:16): Mat.22:10 (WE; γάμος, RV); οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ ν. (cf. cl. νυμφαγωγός, νυμφευτής), the bridegroom's friends who have charge of the nuptial arrangements: Mat.9:15, Mrk.2:19, Luk.5:34.† (AS)

G3568.d: νῦν, adv., __1. prop., of time, now, i.e. at the present time: as opposite to past, Jhn.4:18, Act.7:52, Rom.13:11, 2Co.7:9, Col.1:24, al.; opposite to fut., Jhn.12:27, Rom.11:31, al.; with art., ὁ (ἡ, τὸ) and subst., the present: Rom.3:26, Gal.4:25, 1Ti.6:17, Tit.2:12, al.; απὸ τοῦ ν. (LXX for מֵעַתָּה), Luk.1:48, Act.18:6, al.; ἄχρι τοῦ ν., Rom.8:22, Php.1:5; ἕως τοῦ ν. (LXX for עַד עַתָּה),…

G3570.d: νῦνί an Attic strengthened form of νῦν (in cl. always of time, and most often strictly of the pres.), now; __1. of time: with praes., Act.24:13, Rom.15:23, 25, 1Co.13:13, 2Co.8:11 8:22, Phm 9 11; with pf., Rom.3:21; with pret., Rom.6:22 11:30 (WH, mg.) Rom.7:6, Eph.2:13, Col.1:21 3:8; ἡ ν. ἀπολογία, Act.22:1. __2. Of logical sequence (not so in cl.): Rom.7:17, 1Co.5:11 (νῦν, WH) 1Co.12:18 (νῦν,…

(of the time within which something happens; M, Pr., 73; B1., § 36, 13), νυκτός, by night, Mat.2:14, Jhn.3:2, 1Th.5:7, al.; ν. κ. ἡμέρας, Mrk.5:5, 1Th.2:9, al.; ἡμέρας κ. ν., Luk.18:7, Rev.4:8, al.; μέσης ν., Mat.25:6; dative, νυκτί, in ans. to the question, "when?" (rare in cl.; Hdt., Soph.), ταύτῃ τ. ν.,…

G3572.d: νύσσω (Att.. -ττω), to pierce: τ. πλευρὰν λόγχῃ, Jhn.19:34, [Mat.27:49], WH.† (AS)

G3573.d: νυστάζω (cf. νεύω), to nod in sleep, fall asleep: Mat.25:5. Metaphorical, of negligence or delay, ἡ ἀπώλεια αὐτῶν οὐ νυστάζει (cf. Psa.121:4, Isa.5:27) : 2Pe.2:3.† (AS)

G3574.d: νυχθήμερος, -α, -ον (νύξ, ἡμέρα, see B1., § 28, 4), lasting a night and a day; as subst., (τὸ) ν., a night and a day: 2Co.11:25 (pl., Or. Sib., 8, 203).† (AS)

G3575.d: Νῶε (as LXX, FlJ, who also gives Νώεος, Νῶχος), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. נֹחַ) Noah: Mat.24:37-38, Luk.3:36 17:26-27 Heb.11:7, 1Pe.3:20, 2Pe.2:5.† (AS)

G3576.d: νωθρός, -ά, -όν sluggish, slothful: Heb.5:11 6:12 (for similar usage in π., see MM, xvii). SYN.: ἀργός (which see), βραδύς (AS)

G3577.d: νῶτος, -ου, ὁ in Att.. most frequently τὸ νῶτον, and in pl. always τὰ νῶτα, /the back: Rom.11:10 (LXX).† (AS)

G3578.d: ξενία, -ας, ἡ (ξένος), hospitality, enter­tainment: Phm 22 (cf. ICC, in l, but see infr.). By meton., a place of entertainment, a lodging-place: Act.28:23, and so perh. Phm 22 (Lft., in l, Phi., p. 9; but see supr., and cf. MM, xvii).† (AS)

G3579.d: ξενίζω (ξένος), __1. to receive as a guest, entertain: with accusative of person(s), Act.10:23 28:7, Heb.13:2; pass., Act.10:6, 18 10:32 21:16. __2. In late writers (Polyb., al.; 2Mac, l.with), to surprise, astonish by strangeness: Act.17:20; pass., 1Pe.4:4 4:12.† (AS)

G3580.d: ξενοδοχέω late Gk. for -κέω (ξένος, δέχομαι), to entertain strangers: 1Ti.5:10.† (AS)

G3581.d: ξένος, -η, -ον __(a) foreign, alien: δαιμόνια, Act.17:18; διδαχαί Heb.13:9; __(b) with genitive of thing(s), strange to, estranged from, ignorant of: Eph.2:12; __(with) strange, unusual: 1Pe.4:12. As subst., ὁ ξ., __(a) a foreigner, stranger: Mat.25:35, 38 25:43-44 27:7, Act.17:21, 3Jn.5; ξέίνοι κ. τάροικοι (opposite to συμπολῖται, οίκεῖοι), Eph.2:19; ξ. καὶ παρεπίδημοι, Heb.11:13; __(b) one of…

G3582.d: ξέστης, -ου, ὁ (a Sicilian corruption of Lat. sextarius), [in Al. : Lev.14:10 (לֹג, LXX κοτύλη)* ;] __1. a sextarius (about a pint). __2. In NT, a pitcher of wood or stone : Mrk.7:4.† (AS)

G3583.d: ξηραίνω (ξηρός), to dry up, parch, wither. with accusative, τ. χόρτον, Jas.1:11; pass., to become or be dry or withered. of plants, Mat.13:6 21:19-20, Mrk.4:6 11:20-21, Luk.8:6, Jhn.15:6, 1Pe.1:24; of ripened crops, Rev.14:15; of liquids, Mrk.5:20, Rev.16:12; of members of the body, to waste away, Mrk.3:1 (cf. 3Ki.13:4) Mrk.9:18.† (AS)

G3584.d: ξηρός, -ά, -όν dry: metaphorically (of a sinner), ξύλον ξ., Luk.23:31; of members of the body shrunken by disease, withered: Jhn.5:3; of the hand, Mat.12:10 Mrk.3:3, Luk.6:6, 8; of the dry land, ἡ ξηρά (sc. γῆ, cf. Gen.1:9-10; Jon.1:19, al.): Mat.23:15; γῆ, Heb.11:29.† (AS)

G3585.d: ξύλινος, -η, -ον (ξύλον) wooden: 2Ti.2:20, Heb.9:20 (cf. Ep. Jer.4:1-31 ff).† (AS)

G3586.d: ξύλον, -ου, τό __1. wood: 1Co.3:12, Rev.18:12. __2. a piece of wood, hence, anything made of wood, as, __(a) a cudgel, staff: pl., Mat.26:47, 55, Mrk.14:43, 48, Luk.22:52; __(b) stocks, for confining the feet (Job.33:11, סַד) : Act.16:24; __(with) a beam to which malefactors were bound (late Gk.), in LXX, of a gibbet (Deu.21:22-23), in NT, of the Cross: Act.5:30 10:39 13:29, Gal.3:13, 1Pe.2:24.…

G3587.d: ξυράω, -ῶ late form of ξυρέω (which see) : 1Co.11:6 (ξυρᾶσθαι, Rec. and Edd., but see: ξύρω).† ξύρω, rare form of ξυρέω (Veitch, see word), aor. mid., ξύρασθαιι (Bl., § 24, see word; Zorell, see word, etc.) for -ᾶσθαι (Rec., Edd.) : 1Co.11:6.† (AS)

G3595.d: ὁδηγός, -οῦ, ὁ (ὁδός, ἡγέομαι) a leader on the way, a guide: Act.1:16. Fig., ὁ. τυφλῶν, Rom.2:19; pl., Mat.15:14 23:16, 24.† (AS)

G3596.d: ὁδοιπορέω, -ῶ (ὁδοιπόρος, a traveller, Gen.37:25, al.), to travel, journey: Act.10:9.† (AS)

G3597.d: ὁδοιπορία, -ας, ἡ (see supr.), a journey. Jhn.4:6, 2Co.11:26.† (AS)

G3600.d: ὀδυνάω, -ῶ (ὀδύνη), to cause pain or suffering; pass. and mid., to suffer pain, be tormented or greatly distressed: Luk.2:48 16:24-25 (ὀδυνᾶσαι, see M, Pr., 53 f.); before ἐπί, Act.20:38.† (AS)

G3601.d: ὀδύνη, -ης, ἡ pain, distress, of body or mind : Rom.9:2, 1Ti.6:10.† (AS)

G3602.d: ὀδυρμός, -οῦ, ὁ (ὀδύρομαι, to lament), lamentation, mourning: Mat.2:18 (LXX), 2Co.7:7.† (AS)

G3604.d: Ὀζείας (Rec. Ὀζίας), -ου, ὁ (Heb. עֻזִּיָּה), Uzziah: Mat.18:1-35 9:1-38.† (AS)

G3605.d: ὄζω to smell (i.e. emit a smell): Jhn.11:39.† (AS)

G3606.d: ὅθεν adv., whence; __(a) of direction or source: Mat.12:44, Luk.11:24, Act.14:26 28:13; = ἐκεῖθεν ὅπου, Mat.25:24, 26 (cf. Thuc., i, 89, 3); ὅ. γινώσκομεν, 1Jn.2:18; __(b) of cause, whence, wherefore: Mat.14:7, Act.26:19, Heb.2:17 3:1 7:25 8:3 9:18 11:19.† (AS)

G3607.d: ὀθόνη, -ης, ἡ (of Semitic origin, cf. Heb. אֵטוּן, yarn) __1. fine linen (Hom., al.). __2. Later, a sheet or sail: Act.10:11 11:5.† (AS)

G3608.d: ὀθόνιον, -ου, τό (dimin. of ὀθόνη, which see), a piece of fine linen, a linen cloth; Luk.24:12 (WH, R, mg., om.), Jhn.19:40 20:5-7.† (AS)

G3609.d: οἰκεῖος, -α, -ον (οἶκος), in or of the house (opposite to ξένος, ἀλλότριος); __(a) of things; τὰ οἰ., household affairs or goods; __(b) of persons, of the same family or kin; as subst., οἱ οἰ., kinsmen: 1Ti.5:8; with genitive of person(s), of the family of: metaphorically, τ. θεον, Eph.2:19; τ. πίστεως (Lft., in l), Gal.6:10.† SYN,: συγγενής, ἴδιος (see Cremer, 446; Deiss., BS, 123) (AS)

G3610.d: οἰκέτης, -ου, ὁ (οἰκέω), a house-servant: Luk.16:13, Rom.14:4; pl., Act.10:7, 1Pe.2:18 (In Plat., Hdt., Sir.4:30 6:11, the pl. includes all the inmates of the house, the familia, οἰκετεία.)† SYN.. see: διάκονος (AS)

G3611.d: οἰκέω, -ῶ (οἶκος), __(a) trans., to inhabit: with accusative, 1Ti.6:16; __(b) intrans., to dwell: before μετά (of married life), 1Co.7:12-13; metaphorically, before ἐν: ἀγαθόν, Rom.7:18; ἁμαρτία, Rom.7:20; πνεῦμα θεοῦ, Rom.8:9, 11, 1Co.3:16 (cf. ἐν-, κατ-, ἐν-κατ-, παρ-, περι-, συν-οικέω).† (AS)

G3612.d: οἴκημα, -τος, τό (οἰκέω), a dwelling. As a euphemism for other definite terms (e.g. brothel. Hdt., ii, 121; cf. Ez, l.with), a prison (Thus., iv, 47 f.); Act.12:7.† (AS)

G3613.d: οἰκητήριον, -ου, τό (οἰκητήρ = οἰκήτωρ, an inhabitant), a habitation: Ju 6; trop., 2Co.5:2.† (AS)

G3615.d: οἰκιακός (in Plut., al., -ειακός), ή, όν (οἰκία), = οἰκεῖος belonging to the household, one's own: Mat.10:36; opposite to οἰκοδεσπότης, Mat.10:25.† (AS)

G3617.d: οἰκο-δεσπότης, -ου, ὁ (οἶκος, δεσπότης), the master of a house, a householder: Mat.10:25 13:27 20:11 24:43, Mrk.14:14, Luk.12:39 13:25 14:21; ἄνθρωπος οἰ., Mat.13:52 20:1 21:33; pleonast., oἰ. τ. οἰκίας, Luk.22:11 (see Bl., § 81, 4).† (AS)

G3619.d: οἰκοδομή, -ῆς, ἡ (οἶκος, + δέμω, to build), = cl. οἰκοδομία (which see), -δόμησις (Thuc., Plat.), __1. the act of building; in NT always metaphorically, building up, edifying: Rom.14:19 15:2, 1Co.14:26, 2Co.10:8 13:10, Eph.4:29; with genitive obj., 1Co.14:12, 2Co.12:19, Eph.4:12, 16; λαλεῖν, λαβεῖν, οἰ., 1Co.14:3. __2. = οἰκοδόμημα, a building: Mat.24:1, Mrk.13:1-2; metaphorically, 1Co.3:9,…

G3621.d: οἰκονομέω, -ῶ (οἰκονόμος), to manage as house-steward, be a steward: absol., Luk.16:2; hence, generally (see: οἰκονομία), to manage, regulate, arrange (cl., 2Mac, Lc., 3Ma.3:2 R).† (AS)

G3622.d: οἰκονομία, -ας, ἡ (οἰκονομέω), __1. prop. (Plat., Arist.), the office of οἰκονόμος, stewardship: Luk.16:2-4. __2. In later writers (Plut., al.; see AR on Eph.1:10; MM, xviii), generally, administration, dispensation: 1Co.9:17, Eph.1:10 3:2, 9, Col.1:25, 1Ti.1:4.† (AS)

G3623.d: οἰκονόμος, -ου, ὁ (οἶκος + νέμω, to manage) __1. prop., the manager of a household or estate, a house- or land-steward (usually a slave or freedman): Luk.12:42 16:1, 3 16:8, 1Co.4:2, Gal.4:2; ὀ οἰ. τ. πόλεως (RV, treasurer; cf. I Est.4:49), Rom.16:23. __2. Metaphorical (in wider sense; cf. οἰκονομία), an administrator, a steward: of Christian ministers, 1Co.4:1, Tit.1:7; of Christians generally,…

G3624.d: οἶκος, -οῦ, ὁ, __1. prop., a house, dwelling: Act.2:2 19:16; with genitive poss., Mat.9:6, 7 Mrk.2:11, Luk.1:23, al.; with genitive attrib., ἐμπορίου, Jhn.2:16; προσευχῆς, Mat.21:13, al.; of a sanctuary (Hdt., Eur.): οἶ. τ. θεοῦ, of the tabernacle, Mat.12:4, al.; the temple, Mat.21:13, al.; metaphorically of a city: Mat.23:38, Luk.13:35; of the body, Mat.12:44, Luk.11:24; of Christians, 1Pe.2:5;…

G3624G.d: οἶκος, -οῦ, ὁ, __1. prop., a house, dwelling: Act.2:2 19:16; with genitive poss., Mat.9:6, 7 Mrk.2:11, Luk.1:23, al.; with genitive attrib., ἐμπορίου, Jhn.2:16; προσευχῆς, Mat.21:13, al.; of a sanctuary (Hdt., Eur.): οἶ. τ. θεοῦ, of the tabernacle, Mat.12:4, al.; the temple, Mat.21:13, al.; metaphorically of a city: Mat.23:38, Luk.13:35; of the body, Mat.12:44, Luk.11:24; of Christians, 1Pe.2:5;…

G3624H.d: οἶκος, -οῦ, ὁ, __1. prop., a house, dwelling: Act.2:2 19:16; with genitive poss., Mat.9:6, 7 Mrk.2:11, Luk.1:23, al.; with genitive attrib., ἐμπορίου, Jhn.2:16; προσευχῆς, Mat.21:13, al.; of a sanctuary (Hdt., Eur.): οἶ. τ. θεοῦ, of the tabernacle, Mat.12:4, al.; the temple, Mat.21:13, al.; metaphorically of a city: Mat.23:38, Luk.13:35; of the body, Mat.12:44, Luk.11:24; of Christians, 1Pe.2:5;…

G3625.d: οἰκουμένη, -ης, ἡ (fern. Pres. pass. ptcp. of οἰκέω; sc. γῆ) the inhabited earth; __(a) in cl., the countries occupied by Greeks, as disting. from barbarian lands (Hdt., Dem., al.); __(b) in later writers, the Roman world: Luk.2:1, Act.11:28 24:5; by meton., of its inhabitants : Act.17:6 19:27; __(with) in LXX (Psa.23:1 71:8, al.) and NT, also of the whole inhabited world: Mat.24:14, Luk.4:5…

G3626.d: οἰκ-ουρός, -ον (οἶκος + οὖρος, a keeper) __1. watching or keeping the house; as subst., ἡ οἰ., a housekeeper (Soph., Eur.; see LS, see word). __2. keeping at home: Tit.2:5, Rec. (see Field, Notes, 220 ff.; CGT, in l, and cf. οίκουργός).† (AS)

G3627.d: οἰκτείρω (οἶκτος, pity), to pity, have compassion on. with accusative of person(s), Rom.9:15 (LXX).† SYN.: ἐλεέω, q.v (AS)

G3628.d: οἰκτιρμός, -οῦ, ὁ (οἰκτείρω), compassion, pity. σπλάγχνα οἰκτιρμοῦ, a heart of compassion, Col.3:12; in pl. (as LXX for Heb. רַחַם), οἰ. τ. θεοῦ, Rom.12:1, Heb.10:28; ό πατὴρ τῶν οἰ, 2Co.1:3; σπλάγχνα κ. οἰ., Php.2:1.† SYN.: ἔλεος, q.v (AS)

G3629.d: οἰκτίρμων, -ον (οἰκτείρω), in cl. poët, for ἐλεήμων (which see), merciful: Luk.6:36, Jas.5:1.† (AS)

G3630.d: οἰνο-πότης, -ου, ὁ (οίνος + πότης, a drinker), poët. and late prose, a wine-drinker, wine-bibber: Mat.11:19, Luk.7:34.† (AS)

G3631.d: οἶνος, -ου, ὁ wine; Mat.9:17, Luk.1:15, Jhn.2:3, al.; οἴνῳ προσέχειν, 1Ti.3:8; δουλοῦσθαι, Tit.2:3. Metaphorical, Rev.14:8, 10 16:19 17:2 18:3 19:15. By meton. for ἄμπελος, Rev.6:6 (AS)

G3632.d: οἰνοφλυγία, -ας, ἡ (φλύω, to bubble up, overflow), cf. -γέω, Deu.21:20 drunkenness, debauchery: 1Pe.4:3.† SYN.: see: κραιπάλη (AS)

G3633.d: οἴομαι, οἶμαι to suppose, expect, imagine; with accusative and inf., Jhn.21:25; with inf., Php.1:17; before ὅτι, Jas.1:7.† οἶμαι, see: οἴομαι SYN.. see: ἡγέομαι (AS)

G3634.d: οἷος, -α, -ον relat. pron., qualitative (related to ὅς as qualis to qui), what sort or manner of, such as, in NT usually without its correl. τοιοῦτος : Mat.24:21, Mrk.9:3, 2Co.12:20, 1Th.1:5, 2Ti.3:11, Rev.16:18; before τοιοῦτος, 1Co.15:48 15:2 2Co.10:11; id. redundant, Mrk.13:19; τ. αὑτὸν . . . σἷον, Php.1:30; οὐχ οἷον δὲ ὅτι, elliptically, but it is not as though (RV), Rom.9:6.† (AS)

G3635.d: ὀκνέω, -ῶ (ὄκνος, shrinking, hesitation), to shrink from doing, hesitate to do (Hom., Thuc., al.); hence, to delay with inf., Act.9:38 (cf. Nu, l.with, and see MM, xviii).† (AS)

G3636.d: ὀκνηρός, -ά, -όν (ὀκνέω), shrinking, hesitating, timid: with dative (Bl., § 38, 2), Rom.12:11; hence, slothful: Mat.25:26. Of things, that which causes shrinking, irksome: Php.3:1.† (AS)

G3637.d: ὀκταήμερος, -ον (ὀκτώ, ἡμέρα), of the eighth day, eight days old: with dative ref., περιτομῇ., Php.3:5 (words of this class denote duration, cf. τεταρταῖος).† (AS)

G3638.d: ὀκτώ, οἱ, αἱ, τά indecl., eight: Luk.2:21, Jhn.5:5, al (AS)

G3639.d: ὄλεθρος, -ον (ὄλλυμι, to destroy), ruin, destruction, death: 1Th.5:3, 1Ti.6:9; αἰώνιος, 2Th.1:9 (L, txt., ὀλέθριος, which see); εἰς ὄ. τῆς σαρκός, for physical discipline, to destroy carnal lusts, 1Co.5:5.† (AS)

G3640.d: ὀλιγό-πιστος, -ον of little faith or trust: Mat.6:30 8:26 14:31 16:8, Luk.12:28.† (AS)

G3641.d: ὀλίγος, -η, -ον (on οὐχ ὁλ., see infr.), of number, quantity, size, few, little, small, slight: Mat.9:37 15:34, Mrk.6:5 8:7, Luk.10:2 12:48 (sc. πληγάς, opposite to πολλάς), 1Ti.5:23, Heb.12:10, Rev.3:4 12:12; οὐκ ὀ. (in the best uncials written οὐκ ὁ.; see WH, App., 143; M, Pr., 44; Thackeray, Gr., 126 f.), Act.12:18 14:28 15:2 (with genitive part.) Act.17:4, 12 19:23-24 27:20; pl., absol.,…

G3643.d: ὀλιγωρέω, -ῶ (ὀλίγος + ὤρα, care), to esteem lightly, think little of: with genitive, Heb.12:5 (LXX),† (AS)

G3644.d: ὀλοθρευτής (Rec. όλ-), -οῦ, ὁ (ὀλοθρεύω), a destroyer: 1Co.10:10 (not elsewhere).† (AS)

G3645.d: ὀλοθρεύω (ὄλεθρος), late (Alex.) form of ὄλεθρεύω ω (cf. MGr., ξολοθρεύω) to destroy: Heb.11:28 (cf. ἐξ-ολοθρεύω).† ὀλεθρεύω, see: ὀλοθρεύω ὀλοθρεύω (ὄλεθρος), late (Alex.) form of ὄλεθρεύω ω (cf. MGr., ξολοθρεύω) to destroy: Heb.11:28 (cf. ἐξ-ολοθρεύω).† ὀλεθρεύω, see: ὀλοθρεύω (AS)

G3646.d: ὁλοκαύτωμα, -τος, τό (ὅλος, καίω), a whole burnt offering: Mrk.12:33, Heb.10:6, 8" (LXX) (of. Kennedy, Sources, 113 f.).† SYN.: see: θυσία (AS)

G3648.d: ὁλό-κληρος, -ον (ὅλος, κλῆρος, i.e. with all that has fallen by lot), complete, entire; in NT in ethical sense (as Wis, 4Mac, ll. with), 1Th.5:23; ὁ. καὶ τέλειοι, Jas.1:4.† SYN.: ὁλοτελής (which see), τελειος (Tr., Syn., § xxii) (AS)

G3649.d: ὀλολύζω (onomatop.), (in Hom., of women crying to the gods in prayer or thanksgiving), to cry aloud: Jas.5:1.† (AS)

G3650.d: ὅλος, -η, -ον, of persons and things, whole, entire, complete; __1. of indefinite ideas, with subst. anarth.: Luk.5:5, Act.11:26 28:30, Tit.1:11; ὅλον ἄνθρωπον (an entire man; see Field, Notes, 93), Jhn.7:23; ὅλη Ἰερουσαλήμ (= πᾶσα Ἰ, Mat.2:3; see Bl., §47, 9), Act.21:31. __2. Definite, with art.; __(a) preceding subst.: Mat.4:23, 24 Luk.8:39, 1Co.12:17, al.; __(b) following subst.: Mrk.1:33,…

G3651.d: ὁλοτελής, -ές (ὅλος, τίλος), complete, perfect.. 1Th.5:23.† SYN.: ὁλόκληρος (which see), τέλειος. "As regards meaning, ὁλόκληρος can hardly be distinguished from ὁλοτελής though, in accordance with its derivation, it draws more special attention to the several parts to which the wholeness spoken of extends, no part being wanting or lacking in completeness" (M, Th., 78) (AS)

G3652.d: Ὀλυμπᾶς (perh. contr. fr. Ὀλνμπιόδωρος, Bl., § 29), -ᾶ, Olympas: Rom.16:15.† (AS)

G3653.d: ὄλυνθος, -ου, ὁ an unripe fig, which grows in winter and usually falls off in the spring : Rev.6:13.† (AS)

G3654.d: ὅλως adv. (ὅλος), altogether, assuredly, actually (with neg., at all) : Mat.5:34, 1Co.5:1 6:7 15:29.† (AS)

G3655.d: ὄμβρος, -ου, ὁ a storm of rain, a shower: Luk.12:54.† (AS)

G3656.d: ὁμιλέω, -ῶ (ὅμιλος), to be in company with, consort with; hence, to converse with: Act.20:11; with dative, Act.24:26; before πρός, Luk.24:14-15.† (AS)

G3658.d: ὅμιλος, -ου, ὁ [in Aq. : 1Ki.19:20 * ;] a crowd, throng: Rev.18:17, Rec.† (AS)

G3659.d: ὄμμα, -τος, τό in cl. chiefly poët.; an eye: p1., Mat.20:34 Mrk.8:23.† (AS)

G3660.d: ὀμνύω (so Hdt. and some Att.. writers) and ὄμνυμι (so generally in Att.. prose and always in Trag.; Mrk.14:71, -ύναι), to swear, affirm by oath: Mat.26:74, Mrk.14:71, Heb.7:21; before εἰ (q.v), Heb.3:11 4:3; with dative of person(s), Mrk.6:23; id. with inf., Heb.3:18; before ὅρκῳ, Act.2:30; ὀ. ὅρκον, πρός, with accusative of person(s) (cl.), Luk.1:73; with accusative (of that by which one swears;…

G3661.d: ὁμοθυμαδόν (ὁμός, θυμός), with one mind, with one accord: Act.1:14 2:46 4:24 5:12 7:57 8:6 12:20 15:25 18:12 19:29, Rom.15:6 (Hatch, Essays, 63 f., argues that the un-cl. sense together, which is found in Job.3:18 38:33, Num.24:24, Wis.18:5, 12 (but not Wis.10:20), al., should be attached to the NT instances, but see Abbott, Essays, 96; MM, xviii).† (AS)

G3662.d: ὁμοιάζω (ὅμοιος), to be like: Mat.23:27 (L, Tr., txt., WH, mg.) Mat.26:73 (WH, mg.) (not found elsewhere. cf. παρ-ομοιάζω.) † (AS)

G3663.d: ὁμοιοπαθής, -ές (ὅμοιος, πάσχω), of like feelings or affections: with dative, Act.14:15, Jas.5:17.† (AS)

G3664.d: ὅμοιος, -οία, -οιον like, resembling, such as, the same as: with dative, of form or appearance, Jhn.9:9, Rev.1:13 (WH, mg., R, but see infr.) Rev.1:15 2:18 4:6-7 9:7, 10 (B1., § 37, 62) Rev_9:19; Rev_11:1; Rev_13:2; Rev_13:11; ὁράσει, Rev_4:3; of nature, condition, ability, etc., Mat_22:39, Act_17:29, Gal_5:21, 1Jn_3:2, Rev_13:4; Rev_18:18; Rev_21:11; Rev_21:18; of comparison in parables,…

G3665.d: ὁμοιότης, -ητος, ἡ (ὅμοιος), likeness: καθ᾽ ὁμοιότητα, in like manner, Heb.4:15; id. with genitive (MM, xviii), after the likeness (of), Heb.7:15.† (AS)

G3666.d: ὁμοιόω, -ῶ (ὅμοιος), __1. to make like, with genitive and dative; pass., to be made or become like: Mat.6:8 13:24 18:23 22:2 25:1, Act.14:11, Heb.2:17; before ὡς (cf. Eze.32:2, Heb.), Rom.9:29. __2. to liken, compare: with dative, accusative, Mat.11:16, Luk.7:31 13:18, 20; πῶς όμοιώσωμεν, Mrk.4:30; pass., Mat.7:24, 26 (cf. ἀφ-ομοιόω).† (AS)

G3667.d: ὁμοίωμα, -τος, τό (ὁμοιόω), that which is made like something; __(a) concrete, an image, like­ness (Psa.106:20, Eze.1:5, 1Ma.3:48, al.) : Rev.9:7; __(b) abstract, like­ness, resemblance: Rom.5:14 6:5 8:3, Php.2:7; ἐν ὁ. εἰκόνος, Rom.1:23.† SYN.: εἰκών (which see), ὁμοίωσις (AS)

G3668.d: ὁμοίως (ὅμοιος), adv., likewise, in like manner, equally: Mat.22:26, Mrk.4:16, Luk.10:37, al.; with dative, Mat.22:39, Luk.6:31; ὁ. καί, Mat.22:26, Mrk.15:31, al.; ὁ. καθώς, Luk.17:28; καθὼς . . . ὁ., Luk.6:31; ὁ. μέντοι καί, Ju 8 (AS)

G3669.d: ὁμοίωσις, -εως, ἡ (ὁμοιόω) __1. a making like, becoming like (Plat.). __2. likeness: Jas.3:9 (LXX).† SYN.: see: ὁμοίωμα, and cf. Tr., Syn., § xv (AS)

G3670.d: ὁμολογέω, -ῶ (ὁμόλογος, of one mind: Dan LXX Su 1:60 *), __1. to speak the same language (Hdt.). __2. to agree with (Hdt., Plat., al.). __3. to agree, confess, acknowledge (Plat., al.) : absol., Jhn.1:20 12:42; pass., Rom.10:10; before ὅτι, ib., Heb.11:13; with accusative of thing(s), Act.23:8, 1Jn.1:9, Rev.3:5; id. with dative of person(s), Act.24:14; with accusative cogn., 1Ti.6:12; with…

G3671.d: ὁμολογία, -ας, ἡ (όμολογέω), __1. in cl., an agreement assent, compact (in π., of a contract; Deiss., BS, 249). __2. confession (prob. always in an objective sense): 2Co.9:13, 1Ti.6:12-13 Heb.3:1 4:14 10:13.† (AS)

G3672.d: ὁμολογουμένως adv. (ὁμ oλογέω), __1. as agreed, conformably with. __2. confessedly, by common consent: 1Ti.3:16.† (AS)

G3673.d: ὁμότεχνος, -ον (ὁμός, τέχνη), practising the same craft, of the same trade: Act.18:3.† (AS)

G3674.d: ὁμοῦ adv. (ὁμός), together; __(a) prop., of place: Jhn.21:2, Act.2:1; __(b) without idea of place: Jhn.4:36 20:4.† (AS)

G3675.d: ὁμόφρων, -ον (ὁμός, φρήν), = ὁμόνοος, agreeing, of one mind: 1Pe.3:8.† (AS)

G3676.d: ὅμως adv. (ὁμίς), yet: ὅ. μέντοι, but yet, nevertheless, Jhn.12:42; by hyperbaton, out of its proper position, 1Co.14:7, Gal.3:15 (but see Bl., § 77, 14).† (AS)

G3677.d: ὄναρ, τό indecl., used only in nom, and accusative sing. (the other cases are supplied by ὄνειρος), a dream: κατ᾽ ὄ. (in later writers only), in a dream, Mat.1:20 2:12-13, 19 2:22 27:19.† (AS)

G3678.d: ὀνάριον, -ου, τό (dimin. of ὄνος), a young ass: Jhn.12:14.† (AS)

G3679.d: ὀνειδίζω (ὄνειδος), to reproach, upbraid: absol., Jas.1:5; with accusative of person(s) (in cl. more frequently with dative of person(s); Bl., § 34, 2; WM, 278), Mat.5:11, Mrk.15:32, 34, WH, mg., Luk.6:22, Rom.15:3" (LXX) ; τ. πόλεις, Mat.11:20; pass., 1Ti.4:10, WH, mg., 1Pe.4:14; with accusative of thing(s), Mrk.16:14; with dupl. accusative, Mat.27:44.† (AS)

G3680.d: ὀνειδισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (ὀνειδίζω) a reproach: Rom.15:3, Heb.10:33; εἰς ὀ. ἐμπεαεῖν, 1Ti.3:7; ὁ ὀ. τοῦ Χριστοῦ Heb.11:26 13:13.† (AS)

G3681.d: ὄνειδος, -ους, τό __1. reproach, censure, blame. __2. matter of reproach, disgrace: Luk.1:25.† (AS)

G3682.d: Ὀνήσιμος, -ου, ὁ (i.e. profitable, ὄνησις, profit), Onesimus: Col.4:9, Phm 10 (a common name among slaves; see MM, iii, xviii).† (AS)

G3684.d: ὀνικός, -ή, -όν (ὄνος), of or for an ass. μύλος ὀ., Mat.18:6, Mrk.9:42 (elsewhere only in π.; see MM, xviii).† (AS)

G3685.d: ὀνίνημι to profit, benefit, help; mid., to have profit, derive benefit: optative (M, Pr., 195), with genitive, Phm 20.† (AS)

G3686.d: ὄνομα, -τος, τό, __1. in general, the name by which a person or thing is called: Mat.10:2, Mrk.3:16, Luk.1:63, Jhn.18:10, al.; ἄνθρωπος (etc.), ᾧ (οὗ) ὄ. (τ. ὄ), sc. ἦν or ἐστίν (BL, §30, 3), Mrk.14:32, Luk.1:26, 27; with same ellipsis, καὶ τ. ὄ. αὐτοῦ, Luk.1:5, Jhn.1:6, al.; ὀνόματι, before nom. prop., Mat.27:32, Mrk.5:22, Luk.1:5, Act.5:1, al.; accusative absol. (Bl., §34, 7), τοὔνομα (= τ.…

G3687.d: ὀνομάζω (ὄνομα), __1. to name, mention, or address by name: Act.19:13; pass., Rom.15:20, Eph.1:21 5:3; of the use of the Divine name in praise and worship, 2Ti.2:19 (LXX, Num.16:26; cf. Isa.52:11, Amo.6:10). __2. to name, call, give a name to: Mrk.3:14 (T, R, txt. om.), Luk.6:13-14; pass., 1Co.5:11; before ἐξ (cl.), Eph.3:15 (cf. ἐπ-ονομάζω).† (AS)

G3688.d: ὄνος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ an ass: Mat.21:2, 5" (LXX), Luk.14:5, Jhn.12:15" (LXX) ; ὁ, Luk.13:15; ἡ, Mat.21:7 .† (AS)

G3689.d: ὄντως adv. (ὤν, ptcp. of εἰμί, sum) really, actually, truly: Mrk.11:32, Luk.23:47 24:34, Jhn.8:36, 1Co.14:25, Gal.3:21 4:1-31 ἡ ὄ. ζωή, 1Ti.6:19; ἡ ὄ. χήρα, 1Ti.5:3 5:5 5:16 † (AS)

G3690.d: ὄξος, -εος (-ους), τό (ὄξύς), sour wine (posca, vin-Deu pays), the ordinary drink of labourers and common soldiers: Mat.27:48, Mrk.15:36, Luk.23:36, Jhn.19:29-30.† (AS)

G3691.d: ὄξύς, -εῖα, -ύ __1. sharp: Rev.1:16 2:12 14:14, 17-18 19:15. __2. Of motion, swift: Rom.3:15 (LXX ταχινός).† (AS)

G3692.d: ὀπή, -ῆς, ἡ an opening, a hole: Jas.3:11 (cf. Exo.33:22), Heb.11:33 (cf. Ob 3).† (AS)

G3693.d: ὄπισθεν adv. of place, behind, after: Mat.9:20, Mrk.5:27, Luk.8:44, Rev.4:6 5:1. As prep. with genitive: Mat.15:23, Luk.23:26, Rev.1:10 (WH, mg.).† (AS)

G3694.d: ὀπίσω adv. of place and time, __1. prop., as in cl., adv., __(a) of time (not in NT); __(b) of place, back, behind, after: Mat.24:18, Luk.7:38; τὰ ὀ., Php.3:13; εἰς τὰ ὀ., Mrk.13:16, Luk.9:62 17:31, Jhn.6:66 18:6 20:14. __2. By a usage not found in cl., and in LXX representing the Heb. prep. אַחַר (Bl., § 40, 8; Thackeray, Gr., 46 f.), but also prob. general in vernacular (M, Pr., 99), as prep.…

G3695.d: ὁπλίζω (ὅπλον), [in Sm.: Jer.52:25 * ;] to make ready, equip; of soldiers, to arm. Mid., to arm oneself; figuratively, ἔννοιαν: 1Pe.4:1 (cf. θράσος ὁ., Soph., Elec., 995), (cf. καθ-ὁπλίζω).† (AS)

G3696.d: ὅπλον, -ου, τό __1. a tool, implement, instrument: ὅπλα ἀδικίας (Opp. to ὅ. δικαιοσύνης), Rom.6:13. __2. Freq., in pl., arms, weapons: Jhn.18:3, 2Co.10:4; metaphorically, τ. φωτός, Rom.13:12; τ. δικαιοσύνης, 2Co.6:7.† (AS)

G3697.d: ὁποῖος, -οία, -οῖον of what sort: 1Co.3:13, Gal.2:6, 1Th.1:9, Jas.1:24; τοιοῦτος ὁ., such as, Act.26:29.† (AS)

G3699.d: ὅπου adv. of place, correlat. of ποῦ (which see), where. __I. Prop., of place, __1. where; __(a) in relative sentences, with indic: Mat.25:24, 26, Mrk.2:4 4:5, 15 5:40 13:14, Jhn.3:8 6:62 7:34, 36 11:32 14:3 17:24 20:19, Rom.15:20, Rev.2:13; after nouns of place, for relat. prepositional phrase (ἐν ᾧ., etc.), Mat.6:19-20 13:5 26:57 28:6, Mrk.6:55 9:48 Luk.12:33, Jhn.1:28 4:20, 46 6:23 7:42 10:40…

G3700.d: ὀπτάνω late present as from ὤφθην (= ὁράω); mid., ὀπτάνομαι, to allow oneself to be seen, to appear. with dative, Act.1:3. (For exx. from π., see Deiss., LAE, 79, 2526; MM, ii, xviii.) † (AS)

G3700G.d: ὀπτάνω late present as from ὤφθην (= ὁράω); mid., ὀπτάνομαι, to allow oneself to be seen, to appear. with dative, Act.1:3. (For exx. from π., see Deiss., LAE, 79, 2526; MM, ii, xviii.) † (AS)

G3700H.d: ὀπτάνω late present as from ὤφθην (= ὁράω); mid., ὀπτάνομαι, to allow oneself to be seen, to appear. with dative, Act.1:3. (For exx. from π., see Deiss., LAE, 79, 2526; MM, ii, xviii.) † (AS)

G3701.d: ὀπτασία, -ας, ἡ (ὀπτάζομαι, Num.14:14* = ὀπτάνομαι), later form of ὄψις, __1. an appearing, coming into view (Ma, Es, Sir, ll. with). __2. a vision: Luk.1:22 24:23, Act.26:19, 2Co.12:1 (Da, ll. with, also in MGr.).† (AS)

G3703.d: ὀπώρα, -ας, ἡ __1. late summer, early autumn (the time between the risings of Sirius and Arcturus, i.e. late July, all August and early September). __2. By meton. (as being fruit-time), ripe fruits Rev.18:14 (cf. φθινοπωρινά, Ju 12).† (AS)

G3704.d: ὅπως __I. Relat. adv. of manner, as, how: with indic., Luk.24:20. __II. Conj., with subjc. (in cl. also with opt., indic.: so in Mat.26:59, LT, Tr.), in order that, to the end that, that; __1. final, denoting purpose or design (in which the original idea of modality has been merged): after pres., Mat.6:2, al.; pf., Act.9:17, al.; impf., Act.9:24; aor., Act.9:2, al.; plpf., Jhn.11:57; fut.,…

G3705.d: ὅραμα, -τος, τό (ὁράω), that which is seen; __(a) a sight, spectacle: Mat.17:9, Act.7:31; __(b) an appearance, vision: Act.9:10, 12 (Rec.) Act.10:3, 17 10:19 11:5 12:9 16:9-10 18:9 (cf. ὀπτασία).† (AS)

G3706.d: ὅρασις, -εως, ἡ (ὁράω) __1. in Arist. and later writers, the act of seeing, the sense of sight, and by meton., pl., the eyes. __2. appearance (Num.24:4, Eze.1:5, Sir.41:20, al.): Rev.4:3. __3. = ὅραμα, a vision: Act.2:17 (LXX), Rev.9:17.† (AS)

G3708.d: ὁράω, -ῶ, in "durative" sense (hence aor. act., εἶδον, pass., ὤφθην, fut., ὄψομαι, from different roots; see M, Pr., 110f.), to see (in colloq. even the present is rare, its place being generally taken by θεωρέω, see BL, §24). __1. Of bodily vision, to see, perceive, behold: absol., Mrk.6:38, al.; ἔρχου καὶ ἴδε, Jhn.1:46, al.; before ὅτι, Mrk.2:16, al.; with accusative, Mat.2:2, Mrk.1:10 16:7,…

G3709.d: ὀργή, -ῆς, ἡ __1 1, impulse, propensity, disposition. __2. anger, wrath; __(a) of men: Mrk.3:5, Eph.4:31, Col.3:8, 1Ti.2:8, Jas.1:19-20; __(b) of God; __α that reaction of the divine nature against sin which in anthropomorphic language is called anger: Rom.1:18 9:22 12:19, (ICC, in l), 1Th.1:10 2:16, Heb.3:11 4:3" (LXX) Rev.14:10 16:19 19:15; __β of the effect of God's anger: Mat.3:7, Luk.3:7…

G3710.d: ὀργίζω (ὀργή), to make angry, provoke to anger; in cl. most frequently in pass., and so always in NT, to be provoked to anger, be angry: absol., Mat.18:34 22:7, Luk.14:21 15:28, Eph.4:26" (LXX), Rev.11:18; with dative, Mat.5:22; before ἐπί, with dative (3Ki.11:9, al.), Rev.12:17 (cf. παρ-ὀργίζω).† (AS)

G3711.d: ὀργίλος, -η, -ον (ὀργή), inclined to anger, passionate: Tit.1:7.† (AS)

G3712.d: ὀργυιά, -ᾶς, ἡ (ὀρέγω), the length of the outstretched arms, a fathom: Act.27:28.† (AS)

G3713.d: ὀρέγω [in Sm.: Job.8:20, Eze.16:49 * ;] to reach, stretch out; pass. and mid., to stretch oneself out, reach forth; metaphorically, to reach after, grasp at, aspire to: with genitive of thing(s), 1Ti.3:1, Heb.11:16; φιλαργυρίας (see Ellic. and CGT, in l), 1Ti.6:10.† SYN.: ἐπιθυμέω, to desire (which see) (AS)

G3714.d: ὀρεινός (WH, ὀριν-; see MM, xviii,) -ή, -όν (ὄρος), mountainous, hilly; ἡ ὀ. (sc. χώρα), the hill-country (LXX for הַר): Luk.1:39, 65 † (AS)

G3715.d: ὄρεξις, -εως, ἡ (ὀρέγομαι), the most general ward for all kinds of desire, longing, appetite: of lust, Rom.1:27 SYN.: see: πάθος (AS)

G3716.d: ὀρθοποδέω, -ῶ (ὀρθό-πους, going straight), = cl. εὐθυπορέω, to walk straight: metaphorically, Gal.2:14 (not elsewhere).† (AS)

G3717.d: ὀρθός, -ή, -όν straight; __(a) in height, straight, upright: Act.14:10; __(b) in line, straight, direct: figuratively, Heb.12:13 (LXX).† (AS)

G3718.d: ὀρθοτομέω, -ῶ (- ὀρθός, τέμνω), to cut straight, as a road (τ. ὁδούς, figuratively, Pr, ll with). Metaphorical, τ. λόγον τ. ἀληθείας, 2Ti.2:15 (V. Ellic. and CGT, in l; not found elsewhere).† (AS)

G3719.d: ὀρθρίζω (ὄρθρος), = cl. poët., ὀρθρεύω, to rise early: before πρός, with accusative of person(s) (as Ps, l.with, al.), Luk.21:38 (see Thumb, Hellen., 123).† (AS)

G3720.d: ὀρθρινός, -ή, -όν (ὄρθρος), late form of ὄρθριος (which see), early: Luk.24:22.† (AS)

G3721.d: ὄρθριος, -α, -ον (ὄρθρος), early, in the early morning: Luk.24:22, Rec. (see: ὀρθρινός).† (AS)

G3722.d: ὄρθρος, -ου, ὁ daybreak, dawn: ὄρθρου βαθέως (M, Pr., 73), at early dawn, Luk.24:1; ὄρθρου, Jhn.8:2; ὑπὸ τὸν ὄ., Act.5:21 (cf. MM, xviii).† (AS)

G3724.d: ὁρίζω (ὅρος, a boundary), __1. to separate, mark off by boundaries (so Num.34:6, Jhn.13:27). __2. to determine, appoint, designate: of time, with accusative, Act.17:26, Heb.4:7; with accusative of person(s), Act.17:31; with inf., Act.11:29; pass., Luk.22:22, Act.2:23 10:42, Rom.1:4 (cf. ὀφ-, ἀπο- δι-, τρο-ορίζω),† (AS)

G3725.d: ὅριον, -ου, τό (ὅρος, a boundary), a boundary, bound; chiefly in pl., and so always in NT: Mat.2:16 4:13 8:34 15:22, 39 19:1, Mrk.5:17 7:24, 31 10:1, Act.13:50.† (AS)

G3726.d: ὁρκίζω (ὅρκος), __1. to make one swear (Xen., Polyb., a1.). __2. to adjure: with dupl. accusative, Mrk.5:7, Act.19:13 (cf. ἐν-, ἐξ-ορκίζω).† (AS)

G3728.d: ὁρκωμοσία, -ας, ἡ (ὅρκος, ὄμνυμι; by metapl. for τὰ ὁρκωμόσια, asseverations on oath; see MM, xviii), affirmation on oath, an oath: Heb.7:20-21, 28.† (AS)

G3729.d: ὁρμάω, -ῶ (ὁρμή), __1. causal, to set in motion, urge on. __2. Intrans., to hasten on, rush: before εἰς, Mat.8:32, Mrk.5:13, Luk.8:33, Act.19:29; ἐπί, with accusative, Act.7:57.† (AS)

G3730.d: ὁρμή, -ῆς, ἡ __1. a violent movement, impulse: Jas.3:4; __2. a hostile movement, onset, assault. Act.14:5.† (AS)

G3732.d: ὄρνεον, -ου, τό = ὄρνις, a bird: Rev.18:2 19:17, 21 (Hom., al.).† (AS)

G3733.d: ὄρνις, -ιθος, ὁ, ἡ a bird; specif., a cock, a hen: Mat.23:3, Luk.13:34 (WH).† (AS)

G3734.d: ὁροθεσία, -ας, ἡ (ὅρος, a boundary, + τίθημι) a setting of boundaries; in pl., bounds; Act.17:26.† (AS)

G3735.d: ὄρος, -ους, τό a mountain: Mat.4:8 17:1, Mrk.9:2, Jhn.4:20, 2Pe.1:18, al.; opposite to βουνός, Luk.3:5 (LXX); ὄ. τ. ἐλαιῶν, Mat.21:1 24:3, al. (see: ἐ.); ὄ. Σιών (Σ., prob. in gem appos.), Heb.12:22, Rev.14:1; ὄ. Σινά, Act.7:30, 38 Gal.4:24-25; τὸ ὄ., of the hill district as distinct from the lowlands, esp. the hills above the Sea of Galilee, Mat.5:1 8:1, Mrk.3:13 6:46, al.; τὰ ὄ., Mat.18:12,…

G3736.d: ὀρύσσω to dig: with accusative, ληνόν, Mat.21:33; ὁπολήνιον, Mrk.12:1; γῆν, Mat.25:18 (cf. δι-, ἐξ-ορύσσω).† (AS)

G3737.d: ὀρφανός, -ή, -όν __1. prop., orphan, fatherless: Mrk.12:40, WH, mg, Jas.1:27. __2. In a general sense (as also in cl.; see LS, see word; and cf. MM, xviii), bereft, friendless, desolate: Jhn.14:18.† (AS)

G3738.d: ὀρχέομαι, -οῦμαι to dance; Mat.11:17 14:6, Mrk.6:22, Luk.7:32.† (AS)

G3739.d: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ, the postpositive article (ἄρθρον ὑποτακτικόν). __I. As demonstr. pron. = οὗτος, ὅδε, this, that, also for αὐτός, chiefly in nom.: ὅς δέ, but he (cf. ἦ δὲ ὅς, frequently in Plat.), Mrk.15:23, Jhn.5:11; ὃς μὲν . . . ὃς δέ, the one . . . the other, Mat.21:35, 22:5, 25:15, Luk.23:33, Act.27:14, Rom.14:5, 1Co.11:21, 2Co.2:18, Ju 22; neut., ὃ μὲν . . . ὃ δέ, the one . . . the other, some . .…

G3739 G3404.d: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ, the postpositive article (ἄρθρον ὑποτακτικόν). __I. As demonstr. pron. = οὗτος, ὅδε, this, that, also for αὐτός, chiefly in nom.: ὅς δέ, but he (cf. ἦ δὲ ὅς, frequently in Plat.), Mrk.15:23, Jhn.5:11; ὃς μὲν . . . ὃς δέ, the one . . . the other, Mat.21:35, 22:5, 25:15, Luk.23:33, Act.27:14, Rom.14:5, 1Co.11:21, 2Co.2:18, Ju 22; neut., ὃ μὲν . . . ὃ δέ, the one . . . the other, some . .…

G3739 G5100.d: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ, the postpositive article (ἄρθρον ὑποτακτικόν). __I. As demonstr. pron. = οὗτος, ὅδε, this, that, also for αὐτός, chiefly in nom.: ὅς δέ, but he (cf. ἦ δὲ ὅς, frequently in Plat.), Mrk.15:23, Jhn.5:11; ὃς μὲν . . . ὃς δέ, the one . . . the other, Mat.21:35, 22:5, 25:15, Luk.23:33, Act.27:14, Rom.14:5, 1Co.11:21, 2Co.2:18, Ju 22; neut., ὃ μὲν . . . ὃ δέ, the one . . . the other, some . .…

G3740.d: ὁσάκις (ὅσος), relat. adv., as often as: before ἐάν (which see), 1Co.11:25-26, Rev.11:6,† (AS)

G3741.d: ὅσιος, -ον (so sometimes in cl., but most frequently -α, -ον), religiously right, right­eous, pious, Holy: of men, Tit.1:8. Heb.7:26; by meton., ὁ. χεῖρας, 1Ti.2:8 (cf. Deu.32:4); of God, Rev.15:4 16:5; as subst., ὁ ὅ., of the Messiah, Act.2:27 13:35" (LXX) ; τὰ ὅ. Δανεὶδ τ. πιστά (Field, Notes, 121), Act.13:34 (LXX).† SYN.: see: ἅγιος (cf. also DB, ii, 399.b; iv, 352.b, and ref. see word -ίως)…

G3742.d: ὁσιότης, -ητος, ἡ (ὅσιος), piety, holiness: assoc. with δικαιοσύνη, Luk.1:75, Eph.4:24.† SYN.: see: ἅγιος (AS)

G3743.d: ὁσίως (ὅσιος), adv., piously, holily: ὁ. καὶ δικαίως κ. ἀμέμπτως (on the distinction here between these synonyms, see M, Th., 24 f.), 1Th.2:10.† (AS)

G3744.d: ὀσμή, -ῆς, ἡ (ὄζω), a smell, odour: Jhn.12:3; metaphorically (EV, savour), 2Co.2:14 2:16; of the effect of sacrifice (cf. נִיחוֹחַ רֵיחַ, Gen.8:21, al., see: εὐωδία), ὀ. εὐωδίας, Eph.5:2, Php.4:18.† (AS)

G3745.d: ὅσος, -η, -ον, correlat. of τοσοῦτος, how much, how many, how great, how far, how long, as much as, etc. (= Lat. quantus); __(a) of number and quantity: m. pl., Mat.14:36, Mrk.3:10, Rom.2:12, al.; n. pl., Mat.17:12, Mrk.10:21, Luk.11:8, al.; πάτνες (πάντα) ὅ., Mat.13:46, Luk.4:40, al.; before οὗτοι (ταῦτα), Rom.8:14, Php.4:8; with indic., Mrk.6:56, Rev.3:19; with subjc. Mrk.3:28, al.; ὅ. ἄν,…

G3746.d: ὅσπερ, see: ὅς. ὅς, ἥ, ὅ, the postpositive article (ἄρθρον ὑποτακτικόν). __I. As demonstr. pron. = οὗτος, ὅδε, this, that, also for αὐτός, chiefly in nom.: ὅς δέ, but he (cf. ἦ δὲ ὅς, frequently in Plat.), Mrk.15:23, Jhn.5:11; ὃς μὲν . . . ὃς δέ, the one . . . the other, Mat.21:35, 22:5, 25:15, Luk.23:33, Act.27:14, Rom.14:5, 1Co.11:21, 2Co.2:18, Ju 22; neut., ὃ μὲν . . . ὃ δέ, the one . . . the…

G3747.d: ὀστέον (Att.. contr. ὀστοῦν, -οῦ, and so Jo, l.with), -ου, τό a bone: contr., ὀστοῦν (see supr.), Jhn.19:36 (LXX); uncontr. (as in Hom., Hdt.), ὀστέα, Luk.24:39; ὀστέων, Mat.23:27, Heb.11:22.† (AS)

G3748.d: ὅστις, ἥτις, ὅ τι (also written ὅ, τι and ὅτι; see LS, see word; WH, §411; Tdf., Pr., 111), in NT scarcely ever except in nom. (M, Pr., 91), the only instance of the oblique cases being found in ἕως ὅτου (see: ἕως), relative of indef. reference (related to simple ὅς as Lat. quisquis to qui), whoever, anyone who; __(a) of an indef. person or thing: in general statements, Mat.5:39, 41 13:12, and…

G3749.d: ὀστράκινος -η, -ον (ὄστρακον, an earthen vessel or potsherd), made of clay, earthen: 2Co.4:7, 2Ti.2:20.† (AS)

G3750.d: ὄσφρησις, -εως, ἡ (ὀσφραίνομαι, to smell), the sense of smell, smell­ing: 1Co.12:17.† (AS)

G3751.d: ὀσφύς, -ύος, ἡ the loin: Mat.3:4, Mrk.1:6; metaphorically, περιζώννυσθαι (ἀναζ-) τ. ὀσφύας, Luk.12:35, Eph.6:14, 1Pe.1:13; regarded, as by the Hebrews, as the seat of generative power, Heb.7:5, 10; metaphorically, καρπὸς τ. ὀσφύος, Act.2:30 (AS)

G3752.d: ὅταν (for ὅτ᾽ ἄν = ὅτε ἄν), temporal particle, with a conditional sense, usually of things expected to occur in an indefinite future; __1. prop., whenever; __(a) (a) with subjc. praes.: Mat.6:2, 5 Mrk.14:7, Luk.11:36, Jhn.7:27, Act.23:35, 1Co.3:4, al.; ἕως τ. ἡμέρας ἐκείνης, ὅ., Mat.26:29, Mrk.14:25; before τότε, 1Th.5:3; __(b) with subjc. aor. (M, Pr., 185): Mat.5:11, Mrk.4:15, Luk.6:22,…

G3753.d: ὅτε, temporal particle (correlat. of πότε, τότε), when; with indic., (so generally in cl., but also with optative, subjc.; LS, see word), most frequently with aor., Mat.9:25, Mrk.1:32, Luk.4:25, Jhn.1:19, Act.1:13, Rom.13:11, Gal.1:15, Rev.1:17, al.; with impf., Mrk.14:12, Jhn.21:18, Rom.6:20, 1Th.3:4, al.; with pf., since, now that, 1Co.13:11 (B, ἐγένομην); with praes., Mrk.11:1, Jhn.9:4,…

G3754.d: ὅτι, conjc. (prop. neut. of ὅστις). __I. As conjc, introducing an objective clause, that; __1. after verbs of seeing, knowing, thinking, saying, feeling: Mat.3:9 6:32 11:25, Mrk.3:28, Luk.2:49, Jhn.2:22, Act.4:13, Rom.1:13 8:38 10:9, Php.4:15, Jas.2:24, al.; elliptically, Jhn.6:46, Php.3:12, al. __2. After εἶναι (γίνεσθαι): defining a demonstr. or of person(s) pron., Jhn.3:19 16:19, Rom.9:6,…

G3754G.d: ὅτι, conjc. (prop. neut. of ὅστις). __I. As conjc, introducing an objective clause, that; __1. after verbs of seeing, knowing, thinking, saying, feeling: Mat.3:9 6:32 11:25, Mrk.3:28, Luk.2:49, Jhn.2:22, Act.4:13, Rom.1:13 8:38 10:9, Php.4:15, Jas.2:24, al.; elliptically, Jhn.6:46, Php.3:12, al. __2. After εἶναι (γίνεσθαι): defining a demonstr. or of person(s) pron., Jhn.3:19 16:19, Rom.9:6,…

G3754H.d: ὅτι, conjc. (prop. neut. of ὅστις). __I. As conjc, introducing an objective clause, that; __1. after verbs of seeing, knowing, thinking, saying, feeling: Mat.3:9 6:32 11:25, Mrk.3:28, Luk.2:49, Jhn.2:22, Act.4:13, Rom.1:13 8:38 10:9, Php.4:15, Jas.2:24, al.; elliptically, Jhn.6:46, Php.3:12, al. __2. After εἶναι (γίνεσθαι): defining a demonstr. or of person(s) pron., Jhn.3:19 16:19, Rom.9:6,…

G3756.d: οὐ, before a vowel with smooth breathing οὐκ, before one with rough breathing οὐχ (but improperly οὐχ ἰδού, Act.2:7, WH, mg.; cf. WH, Intr., §409; M, Pr., 44, 244), neg. particle, not, no, used generally with indic, and for a denial of fact (cf . μή); __1. absol. (accented), οὔ, no: Mat.13:29 Jhn.1:21 21:5; οὒ οὕ, Mat.5:37 Jas.5:12. __2. Most frequently negativing a verb or other word, Mat.1:25…

G3756 G0272.d: οὐ, before a vowel with smooth breathing οὐκ, before one with rough breathing οὐχ (but improperly οὐχ ἰδού, Act.2:7, WH, mg.; cf. WH, Intr., §409; M, Pr., 44, 244), neg. particle, not, no, used generally with indic, and for a denial of fact (cf . μή); __1. absol. (accented), οὔ, no: Mat.13:29 Jhn.1:21 21:5; οὒ οὕ, Mat.5:37 Jas.5:12. __2. Most frequently negativing a verb or other word, Mat.1:25…

G3756/G2089.d: οὐ, before a vowel with smooth breathing οὐκ, before one with rough breathing οὐχ (but improperly οὐχ ἰδού, Act.2:7, WH, mg.; cf. WH, Intr., §409; M, Pr., 44, 244), neg. particle, not, no, used generally with indic, and for a denial of fact (cf . μή); __1. absol. (accented), οὔ, no: Mat.13:29 Jhn.1:21 21:5; οὒ οὕ, Mat.5:37 Jas.5:12. __2. Most frequently negativing a verb or other word, Mat.1:25…

G3757.d: oὗ (prop. genitive of ὅς), adv. of place, where, whither; __(a) in answer to the question "where?" (= ubi): Mat.2:9 18:20, Luk.4:16-17 23:53, Act.1:13 2:2 7:29 12:12 16:13 20:6, 8 25:10 28:14, Rom.9:26" (LXX), Col.3:1, Heb.3:9" (LXX), Rev.17:15; of condition, Rom.4:15 5:20, 2Co.3:17; __(b) in answer to the question "whither?" (= quo): Mat.28:16, Luk.10:1 24:28; before ἐάν, with subjc., 1Co.16:6.†…

G3758.d: οὐά, interj. of wonder or irony, ah! ha!: Mrk.15:29.† (AS)

G3759.d: οὐαί interj. of grief or denunciation, alas! woe! most frequently with dative of person(s) Mat.11:21 23:14, Mrk.13:17 14:21, Luk.6:24-26 Ju 11, al.; with vocat. (nom.), Rev.18:10, 16 18:19 (cf. Isa.1:24, al.); with accusative, Rev.12:12, before ἐκ, Rev.8:13; with dative before ἀπό (see M, Pr., 246), Mat.18:7. As subst., 1Co.9:16 (cf. Jer.6:4); ἡ οὐ., Rev.9:12 11:14; pl., Rev.9:12; οὐ., οὐ., οὐ.,…

G3760.d: οὐδαμῶς (οὐδαμός, not even one), adv., in no wise, by no means: Mat.2:6 (OT).† (AS)

G3761.d: οὐδέ, negative particle, related to μηδέ as οὐ to μή. __I. As conjc., and not, also not, neither, nor: Mat.6:15, Luk.16:31, Rom.4:15, al.; οὐ . . . οὐδέ, Mat.5:15 10:24, Mrk.4:22, Luk.6:43, 44, Jhn.6:24, Act.2:27, Rom.2:28, al. (see Bl., §77, 10). __II. G3833.d: πανοπλία, -ας, ἡ (πᾶς, ὅπλον) full armour: Luk.11:22; metaphorically (cf. Wis, l.with), τ. θεοῦ, Eph.6:11, 13 † (AS)

G3834.d: πανουργία, -ας, ἡ (πανοῦργος), cleverness, in cl. nearly always in bad sense, craftiness, cunning, knavery: Luk.20:23, 1Co.3:19 (LXX, φρόνησις, for עׇרְמָה) 2Co.4:2 11:3, Eph.4:14.† (AS)

G3835.d: πανοῦργος, -ον ready to do anything; __(a) in cl., chiefly in bad sense, knavish, crafty: 2Co.12:16; __(b) in good sense, skilful, clever (Pro.13:1 28:2).† (AS)

G3836.d: πανταχόθεν adv., from all sides: Mrk.1:45, Rec.† (AS)

G3837.d: πανταχοῦ adv., everywhere: Mrk.1:28 16:20, Luk.9:6, Act.17:30 24:3 28:22, 1Co.4:17.† (AS)

G3838.d: παντελής, -ές (πᾶς, τέλος), all-complete, entire, perfect; εἰς τ. παντελές, completely, utterly: Luk.13:11, Heb.7:25 (where perhaps in temp. sense, finally; see MM, xviii).† (AS)

G3839.d: πάντῃ (Rec. -τη), adv. (πᾶς), every way, entirely: Act.24:3.† (AS)

G3840.d: πάντοθεν adv. (πᾶς), from all sides: Mrk.1:45, Luk.19:43, Heb.9:4.† (AS)

G3842.d: πάντοτε adv. of time (πᾶς), in late writers (once in Arist.) for διαπαντός, ἑκάστοτε, at all times, always: Mat.26:11, Mrk.14:7, Luk.15:31, Jhn.6:34, Rom.1:10, and frequently in Paul. Epp (AS)

G3843.d: πάντως adv. (πάς), altogether, by all means; __(a) without neg. (from Hdt. on) : 1Co.16:12; esp. in strong affirmations, surely, at all events: Luk.4:23, Act.21:22 28:4, 1Co.9:10; __(b) with neg. (so always in mom.), in a complete negation: Rom.3:9; in a partial negation (Bl., § 75, 7), 1Co.5:10.† (AS)

G3844.d: παρά, prep. with genitive, dative, accusative, with radical sense, beside. __I. C. genitive of person(s), from the side of, from beside, from, indicating source or origin, after verbs of motion, Mrk.14:43, Luk.8:49, Jhn.15:26, al.; after verbs of seeking, receiving, hearing, etc., Mrk.8:11 12:2, Jhn.4:9, 52 10:18, Php.4:18, 2Ti.1:18, Jas.1:7, al.; after passive verbs, of the agent (like ὑπό),…

G3845.d: παρα-βαίνω __1. in Hom. (twice), to go by the side of, stand beside. __2. In Æsch., Herod., Thuc., al., to go past or pass over, chiefly metaphorically, to overstep, violate, transgress (Jos.7:11, Eze.16:59, Sir.40:14, al.) : τ. παράδοσιν, Mat.15:2; τ. ἐντολήν, Mat.15:3; before ἀπό (as מִן סוּר, Deu.17:20, al.), to turn aside, fall away (cf. π. τῆς ἀληθείας, Arist., Cael., i, 5, 2): Act.1:25.†…

G3846.d: παρα-βάλλω __1. to throw to or beside, as fodder to horses (Hom., al.). __2. to lay beside, compare (Hdt., Plat., al.): Mrk.4:30, Rec. __3. Reflexive, to betake oneself, come near; of seamen, to cross over: εἰς Σάμον, Act.20:15. __4. In mid. = παραβολεύομαι, which see† (AS)

G3847.d: παρά-βασις, -εως, ἡ (παραβαίνω), __1. a going aside, a deviation (Arist.). __2. In later writers, an overstepping; metaphorically, transgression (Plut., al.) : Rom.4:15 5:14, Heb.2:2 9:15; τ. νόμου, Rom.2:23; ἐν π., 1Ti.2:14; τ. παραβάσεων χάριν, Gal.3:19 SYN.: see: ἁμαρτία (AS)

G3848.d: παρα-βάτης, -ου, ὁ (παραβαίνω), [in Sm.: Psa.17:4 139:19, Jer.6:28 * ;] __1. one who stands beside, the warrior who stands by the charioteer (of. παραβαίνω, 1). __2. a transgressor (Æsch., παρβάτης): Gal.2:18, Jas.2:9; π. νόμου, Rom.2:25, 27, Jas.2:11.† (AS)

G3849.d: παρα-βιάζομαι __1. prop., to force against nature or law. __2. to compel by force (Polyb.). __3. to constrain by entreaty (Ge, 1Sam, ll. with): Luk.24:29, Act.16:15.† (AS)

G3850.d: παραβολή, -ῆς, ἡ (παραβάλλω), __1. a placing beside, juxtaposition (Polyb., al.). __2. a comparing, comparison (Plat., Arist., al.). __3. a comparison, illustration, analogy, figure (Arist., al.) : Mat.24:32, Mrk.3:23, Heb.9:9 11:19; specif. of the pictures and narratives drawn from nature and human life which are characteristic of the synoptic teaching of our Lord, a parable: Mat.13:3, 10…

G3851.d: παρα-βολεύομαι = cl. παραβάλλομαι (2Ma.14:38), to expose oneself to danger, hazard one's life: with dative ref., τ. ψυχῇ (see M, Pr., 64), Php.2:30 (Rec. παραβουλ-). Cited by Deiss., LAE, 84, 120.† παρα-βουλεύομαι, to consult amiss, or perh. (see LS, see word), a vulg. form of παρα-βολ- (which see) : Php.2:30, Rec.† (AS)

G3852.d: παρ-αγγελία, -ας, ἡ (παραγγέλλω), an instruction, charge, com­mand: Act.5:28 16:24, 1Th.4:2, 1Ti.1:5 1:18. (In Xen., Polyb., of a military order.)† (AS)

G3853.d: παρ-αγγέλλω (παρά, ἀγγὲλλω), __1. to transmit a message (Æsch., Eur.). __2. to order, command (Hdt., Xen., al.) : with inf., Act.15:5; with accusative of thing(s), 1Co.11:17, 2Th.3:4, 1Ti.4:11 5:7; before ἵνα (M, Pr., 207; Bl., § 69, 4), Mrk.6:8, 2Th.3:12; with dative of person(s), Act.17:30 R, txt., 1Th.4:11; before λέγων, Mat.10:5; with inf. aor., Mat.15:35, Mrk.8:6, Luk.8:29, Act.10:42 16:18…

G3854.d: παρα-γίνομαι (Ion. and late for -γίγν-), __1. to be beside or at hand (Hom., Hdt., al.), hence, to stand by, sup­port (Æsch., Thuc., al.) : with dative of person(s), 2Ti.4:16. __2. to come, come up, arrive (Hdt., Xen., al., and frequently in later writers; see MM, xviii; Thackeray, Gr., 267.2): absol., Luk.14:21 19:16, Jhn.3:23, Act.5:21-22, 25 9:39 10:32-33 11:23 14:27 17:10 18:27 21:18 23:16,…

G3855.d: παρ-άγω __1. trans., to lead by, lead aside, lead into, lead forward, etc. __2. Intrans., __(a) to pass by: Mat.9:9, 27 20:30, Mrk.2:14 15:21, Jhn.8:59 R, txt., Jhn.9:1; before παρό, with accusative, Mrk.1:16; __(b) to go away, depart; metaphorically, to pass away: 1Co.7:31; mid., 1Jn.2:8 Jn 2:17.† (AS)

G3856.d: παρα-δειγματίζω (δείκνυμι), to set forth as an example; in bad sense, to put to open shame: Heb.6:6 (Polyb., Plut., al.).† (AS)

G3857.d: παράδεισος, -ου, ὁ (an Oriental word, first used by Xen. of the parks of Persian kings and nobles) __1. a park, pleasure-ground, garden (LXX), an orchard (in π., see MM, ii, xviii; Deiss., BS, 148). __2. Paradise, the abode of the blessed dead: Luk.23:43, 2Co.12:4, Rev.2:7.† (AS)

G3858.d: παρα-δέχομαι to receive, admit; __(a) of things: Mrk.4:20, Act.15:4 16:21 22:18, 1Ti.5:19; __(b) of persons: Heb.12:6 (LXX).† (AS)

G3859.d: παρα-δια-τριβή, -ῆς, ἡ useless wrangling: seel. in Rec. for διαπαρατριβή (which see), 1Ti.6:5.† δια-παρα-τριβή, -ῆς, ἡ (παρατριβή, friction, irritation) mutual irritation (Field, Notes, 211), wrangling: 1Ti.6:5 (Rec. παραδιατριβή).† (AS)

G3860.d: παρα-δίδωμι, correl. to παρδέχομαι, __1. to give or hand over to another: with accusative and dative, Mat.11:27 25:14, Luk.4:6, al.; of being delivered up to a course of teaching, pass. before εἰς, Rom.6:17. __2. to commit, commend: Act.14:26 15:40, 1Pe.2:23. __3. to give or deliver up to prison or judgment: with accusative of person(s), Mat.4:12, Mrk.1:14, Rom.4:25, 2Pe.2:4; id. before ὑπέρ,…

G3861.d: παράδοξος, -ον (παρά, δόξα), contrary to received opinion, incredible, marvellous: pl., Luk.5:26.† SYN.: see: δύναμις (AS)

G3862.d: παρά-δοσις, -εως, ἡ (παραδίδωμι), __1. a handing down or over, transfer, transmission (Arist., Polyb., al., LXX). __2. tradition of doctrine (Plat., Epict., al.); by meton., of the doctrine itself : Mat.15:2-3, 6, Mrk.7:3, 1Co.11:2, Gal.1:14, Col.2:8, 2Th.2:15 3:9.† (AS)

G3863.d: παρα-ζηλόω, -ῶ to provoke to jealousy: Rom.10:19 (LXX) Rom.11:11, 14, 1Co.10:22.† (AS)

G3864.d: παρα-θαλάσσιος, -α, -ον (παρά, θάλασσα) by the sea: Mat.4:13.† (AS)

G3865.d: παρα-θεωρέω, -ῶ __1. to examine side by side, compare. __2. to over­look, neglect: pass., Act.6:1.† (AS)

G3866.d: παρα-θήκη, -ης, ἡ (παρατίθημι), a deposit or trust: 1Ti.6:20, 2Ti.1:12 1:14 (for exx. of this form, see MM, Exp., iii, xviii).† (AS)

G3867.d: παρ-αινέω, -ω to exhort, advise: with accusative of person(s) and inf. (see Bl., § 72, 5; M, Pr., 205), Act.27:22; absol., before λέγων, Act.27:9.† (AS)

G3868.d: παρ-αιτέομαι, -οῦμαι __1. to beg of or from another: Mrk.15:6 (Rec. ὅνπερ ᾐτοῦντο, see Field, Notes, 43). __2. to deprecate; __(a) prop., with neg., to entreat that not (Thuc., al.): Heb.12:19; __(b) to refuse, decline, avoid: o. accusative, 1Ti.4:7 5:11, 2Ti.2:23, Tit.3:10, Heb.12:25 (EV; but see Field, Notes, 234). __3. to beg off, ask to be excused, excuse (Polyb., al.) : Luk.14:18-19…

G3869.d: παρα-καθίζω to set beside; act. for mid., to sit down beside: Luk.10:39, Rec. (for -έζομαι, which see).† (AS)

G3870.d: παρακαλέω, -ῶ, __1. to call to one, call for, summon: Act.28:20 (R, mg.; R, txt., entreat); hence (of the gods: Dem., Xen., al.), to invoke, call on, beseech, entreat: τ. πατέρα μου, Mat.26:53; τ. κύριον, 2Co.12:8; in late writers (Polyb., Diod., al.; rarely in LXX; in π., see Deiss., LAE, 176.14), also of men: absol., Phm 9; with accusative, Mat.8:5, Mrk.1:40, Act.16:9, al.; with inf., Mrk.5:17,…

G3871.d: παρα-καλύπτω to cover by hanging something beside, to hide: metaphorically (as Plat., al.), Luk.9:45.† (AS)

G3872.d: παρα-κατα-θήκη, -ης, ἡ (παρακατατίθημι) more usual than its variant in Gk. writers for a trust or deposit: 1Ti.6:20, 2Ti.1:14, Rec.† (AS)

G3873.d: παρά-κειμαι to lie beside, be near, be present: Rom.7:18, 21.† (AS)

G3874.d: παρά-κλησις, -εως, ἡ (παρακαλέω), __1. a calling to one's aid, summons (Thus.), hence, appeal, entreaty (Strab., Plut., al., 1Ma.10:24; of. Lft., Notes, 20) : 2Co.8:4. __2. exhortation, encouragement: Act.15:31, Rom.12:8, 1Co.14:3, 2Co.8:17, Php.2:1, 1Th.2:3, 1Ti.4:13, Heb.12:5; λόγος (τῆς) π., Act.13:15, Heb.13:22; υἱὸς π., Act.4:36. __3. consolation, comfort (Phalar., LXX) : Luk.6:24, Act.9:31,…

G3875.d: παρά-κλητος, -ον (παρακαλεω), [in Aq., Th.: Job.16:2 * ;] called to one's aid in a judicial cause (Dion. Cass.); hence, most frequently as subst., ὁ π., an advocate, pleader, intercessor (Dem., al.; so in Rabbinic lit., פְּרַקְלִיטָא), "a friend of the accused person, called to speak to his character, or otherwise enlist sympathy in his favour" (Field, Notes, 102). In NT, specif., ὁ π., __(a) of…

G3876.d: παρ-ακοή, -ῆς, ἡ __1. a hearing amiss (Flat.) __2. Later, as following inattention, disobedience: Rom.5:19, 2Co.10:6, Heb.2:2 (cf. παρακούω, and see Tr., Syn., § lxvi).† (AS)

G3877.d: παρ-ακολουθέω, -ῶ with dative, to follow closely, accompany. Metaphorical, in various senses, __(a) to result: Mrk.16:17; __(b) to follow up, trace, investigate: Luk.1:3 (so frequently in cl.); __(with) to follow as a standard of conduct: 1Ti.4:6, 2Ti.3:10. (For exx. from π., see MM, xviii.)† (AS)

G3878.d: παρ-ακούω __1. to overhear. __2. to hear amiss or imperfectly. __3. Later (as in LXX, Polyb., Plut.; also in π., see MM, xviii), to hear without heeding, take no heed: Mrk.5:36; with genitive, Mat.18:17.† (AS)

G3879.d: παρα-κύπτω __1. to stoop sideways. __2. to stoop to look: Luk.24:12 (R, txt.), Jhn.20:5, 11, Metaphorical (see Hort, Ja., in l), to look into: before εἰς, Jas.1:25, 1Pe.1:12.† (AS)

G3880.d: παρα-λαμβάνω __1. with accusative of thing(s), like παραδέχομαι, correl. to παραδίδωμι, to receive from another: Col.4:17, Heb.12:28; of the mind, 1Co.11:23 15:1 15:3, Gal.1:9, Php.4:9; with inf., Mrk.7:4; before παρά, with gem, Gal.1:12, 1Th.2:13 4:1, 2Th.3:6; τ. Χριστόν (Lft., in l), Col.2:6. __2. C. accusative of person(s), to take to or with oneself: Mat.2:13-14, 20-21 17:1 26:37, Mrk.4:36…

G3881.d: παρα-λέγω to lay beside; mid., __(a) to lie beside (Hom.); __(b) later, of sailors, to sail past: with accusative, Act.27:8, 13.† (AS)

G3882.d: παρ-άλιος, -ον (in cl., chiefly -α, -ον), by the sea; ἡ π. (sc. χώρα, in LXX ἡ παραλία, Deu.1:7, Jos.9:1, Jdth.1:7, al.), the sea coast: Luk.6:17.† (AS)

G3883.d: παρ-αλλαγή, -ῆς, ἡ (παραλλάσσω), in various senses (LS, see word), change: Jas.1:17.† (AS)

G3884.d: παρα-λογίζομαι __1. to miscalculate. __2. to reason falsely, hence, to mislead: Col.2:4, Jas.1:22.† (AS)

G3885.d: παρα-λυτικός, -ή, -όν (παραλύω), paralytic: Mat.4:24 8:6 9:2, 6, Mrk.2:3-5, 9-10 Luk.5:24 (Rec., WH, mg.).† (AS)

G3886.d: παρα-λύω __1. to loose from the side, set free. __2. to weaken, enfeeble; pass., to be en­feebled, esp. by a paralytic stroke: Luk.5:18, 24, Act.8:7 9:33, Heb.12:12" (LXX) .† (AS)

G3887.d: παρα-μένω to remain beside or near: Heb.7:23, Jas.1:25; of remaining alive, 1Co.16:6 (WH, κατα-), Php.1:25 (cf. συμ-παραμένω).† (AS)

G3888.d: παρα-μυθέομαι, -οῦμαι __1. to en­courage, exhort. __2. to comfort, console: with accusative of person(s), Jhn.11:31, 1Th.2:11 5:14; id. before περί, Jhn.11:19.† SYN.: παρακαλέω (AS)

G3889.d: παραμυθία, -ας, ἡ (παραμυθέομαι) __1. encouragement, exhortation. __2. comfort, consolation: 1Co.14:3 .† SYN.: παράκλησις (AS)

G3890.d: παραμύθιον, -ου, τό (παραμυθέομαι) __1. an exhortation, persuasion, encouragement: Php.2:1 (cf. Plat., Legg., vi, 773 E, al.; see Lft. and ICC, Phi., l.with). __2. assuagement, abatement, hence, consolation (Wis, l.with, and frequently in cl.).† (AS)

G3891.d: παρα-νομέω, ῶ to be a παράνομος, to transgress the law: Act.23:3.† (AS)

G3893.d: παρα-πικραίνω to embitter, provoke: absol. (yet sc. τ. θεόν, cf. Psa.106:7, Eze.2:5-8, al., and with τὸν θ. added, Psa.5:4, Eze.20:21, al.), Heb.3:16 (cf. παραπικρασμός).† (AS)

G3894.d: παρα-πικρασμός, -οῦ, ἁ (παραπικραίνω) provocation: ἐν τῷ π. (Heb. at Meribah), Heb.3:8, 15" (LXX) .† (AS)

G3895.d: παρα-πίπτω __1. most frequently (Hdt., Thuc., al.), to fall in one's way, befall. __2. to fall into or in (before εἰς, Polyb.; with dative, 2Mac, l.with). __3. to fall away (En, Wis, ll. with; in Polyb., with genitive) : absol., Heb.6:6. __4. to fail (λόγος, Es, l.with; cf. 1Ki.3:19).† (AS)

G3896.d: παρα-πλέω to sail by or past: with accusative, Act.20:16.† (AS)

G3897.d: παρα-πλήσιος, -α, -ον (Hdt., Plat., al.; also -ος, -ον, Thuc., Polyb.), coming near, nearly resembling. Neut. -ον, adverbially, = ίως, in a way nearly resembling: with dative, Php.2:27.† (AS)

G3898.d: παρα-πλησίως adv. (παραπλήσιος) [in Quint.: Hos.8:6 * ;] in like manner: Heb.2:14.† (AS)

G3899.d: παρα-πορεύομαι __1. to go beside, accom­pany. __2. to go past, pass by: Mat.27:39, Mrk.11:20 15:29; before διά, with genitive, Mrk.2:23 9:30 (WH, mg.).† (AS)

G3900.d: παρά-πτωρμα, -τος, τό (παραπίπτω), __1. a false step, a blunder (Polyb.). __2. Ethically, a misdeed, trespass (LXX): Mat.6:14-15, Mrk.11:25-26, Rom.4:25 5:15 ff Rom.11:11-12, 2Co.5:19, Gal.6:1, Eph.1:7 2:1, 5, Col.2:13.† SYN.: see: ἁμαρτία (AS)

G3901.d: παρα-ρρέω to flow by, drift away, slip away: Heb.2:1.† (AS)

G3902.d: παράσημος, -ον (σῆμα, a mark) __1. in cl., marked amiss, spurious, counterfeit. Later, __2. marked at the side, annotated (Plut.). __3. marked with a sign (LXX); as subst., a figure­head : Act.28:11 (see MM, xix).† (AS)

G3903.d: παρα-σκευάζω to prepare, make ready: absol. (sc. τ. δεῖπνον, etc.; of. Hdt., ix, 82, 2Ma.2:27), Act.10:10; mid., to prepare, make preparations: 1Co.14:8 (cf. Je, l.with); pass., 2Co.9:2-3.† (AS)

G3904.d: παρα-σκευή, -ῆς, ἡ __1. preparation. __2. equipment (Jth, ll with). __3. In Jewish usage, the day of preparation for a Sabbath or a feast (= προσάββατον, which see) : Mat.27:62, Mrk.15:42, Luk.23:54, Jhn.19:31; with genitive, τοῦ πάσχα, Jhn.19:14; τ. Ἰoυδαίων, Jhn.19:42 (it is the name for Friday in MGr.).† (AS)

G3905.d: παρα-τείνω to extend, pro­long: τ. λόγον, Act.20:7.† (AS)

G3906.d: παρα-τηρέω, -ῶ __1. to watch closely, observe narrowly: so mid., τ. πύλας, Act.9:24; with evil intent, Mrk.3:2, Luk.20:20 (absol., see Field, Notes, 74); so mid., Luk.6:7 14:1. __2. to observe scrupulously (of days and seasons; cf. Exo.12:42, Sm.): mid., Gal.4:10.† (AS)

G3907.d: παρα-τήρησις, -εως, ἡ [in Aq.: Exo.12:42 (see: παρατηρέω) * ;] obser­vation: Luk.17:20 (Polyb., Plut., al.).† (AS)

G3908.d: παρα-τίθημι __I. Act., to place beside, set before, with accusative and dative: of food, Mrk.6:41 8:6-7, Luk.9:16 11:6; τράπεζαν, Act.16:34; pass. ptcp., Luk.10:8, 1Co.10:27; metaphorically, of teaching, παραβολήν, Mat.13:24, 31. __II. Mid., __1. to have set before one (Hom., Thuc., Xen., al.). __2. to deposit with another, give in charge or commit to (Hdt., Xen., Polyb., al.) : with accusative…

G3909.d: παρα-τυγχάνω to happen to be near or present: Act.17:17.† (AS)

G3910.d: παρ-αυτίκα adv. (πάραυτα = παρ ̓ αὐτά, sc. τὰ πράγματα) __1. immediately. __2. C. subst., to express brief duration (cf. ἡ π. λαμπρότης, Thuc., ii, 64), momentary, for a moment: 2Co.4:17.† (AS)

G3911.d: παρα-φέρω __1. to bring to, set before, esp. of food (Hdt., al.). __2. to take or carry away: with accusative of thing(s), before ἀπό, Mrk.14:36, Luk.22:42; pass., before ὑπό, Ju 12; metaphorically, pass., with dative, Heb.13:9.† (AS)

G3912.d: παρα-φρονέω (ιαρά, φρήν), to be beside oneself, be deranged: 2Co.11:23.† (AS)

G3914.d: παρα-χειμάζω to winter at a place: before εἰς, Act.27:12; ἐν, Act.28:11; πρὸς ὑμᾶς, 1Co.16:6; ἐκεῖ, Tit.3:12.† (AS)

G3915.d: παρα-χειμασία, -ας, ἡ (παρα-χειμάζω) a wintering: Act.27:12 (Polyb., al.).† (AS)

G3916.d: παραχρῆμα adv. (= παρὰ τὸ χρῆμα), on the spot, forthwith, instantly: Mat.21:19-20, Luk.1:64 4:39 5:25 8:44, 47 8:55 13:13 18:43 19:11 22:60, Act.3:7 5:10 12:23 13:11 16:26, 33 (on the usage in Mt, Lk, see Dalman, Words, 28 f.).† (AS)

G3917.d: πάρδαλις, -εως, ἡ a panther, leopard: Rev.13:2.† (AS)

G3918.d: πάρ-ειμι __1. to be by, at hand or present; __(a) of persons: Rev.17:8; παρών (opposite to ἀπών), 1Co.5:3, 2Co.10:2 10:11 13:2 13:10; before ἐπί with genitive, Act.24:19; ἐνώπιον, Act.10:33; ἐνθάδε, Act.17:6; πρός, with accusative of person(s), Act.12:20, 2Co.11:8, Gal.4:18, 20; __(b) of things : of time, ὁ καιρός, Jhn.7:6; τ. παρόν, Heb.12:11; ἡ ἀλήθεια, 2Pe.1:12; ταῦτα, 2Pe.1:9; τ. παρόντα,…

G3919.d: παρ-εισ-άγω __1. to lead in by one's side, bring forward, introduce. __2. In late writers, to introduce or bring in secretly: 2Pe.2:1.† (AS)
