G4637.d: σκηνόω, -ῶ (σκηνή), to have one's tabernacle, to dwell (in π. of temporary dwelling, see MM, Exp., xxii): before ἐπί, with accusative of person(s), Rev.7:15; before ἐν, with dative of person(s), Jhn.1:14; id. with dative loc., Rev.12:12 13:6; before μετά, with genitive of person(s), Rev.21:3 (cf. ἐπι-, κατα-σκηνόω).† (AS)

G4638.d: σκήνωμα, -τος, τό (σκηνόω), a tent, tabernacle (cf. σκηνή, σκῆνος): of the temple as God's dwelling (Psa.132:5, al.), Act.7:46. Metaphorical, of the body: 2Pe.1:13-14.† (AS)

G4639.d: σκιά, -ᾶς, ἡ __1. shadow, shade, caused by interception of light: Mrk.4:32, Act.5:15; metaphorically, σ. θανάτου, of ignorance and error, Mat.4:16, Luk.1:79" (LXX) . __2. a shadow, the image or outline cast by an object: figuratively, ὑπόδειγμα καὶ σ., Heb.8:5; opposite to σῶμα, Col.2:17; opposite to εἰκών, Heb.10:1.† (AS)

G4641.d: σκληρο-καρδία, -ας, ἡ (σκληρός, καρδία), hardness of heart: Mat.19:8, Mrk.10:5 16:14.† (AS)

G4642.d: σκληρός, -ά, -όν (σκέλλω, to dry), hard to the touch, rough, harsh, (opposite to μαλακός); metaphorically, in various uses; __(a) of men, hard, stern, severe: Mat.25:24; __(b) of things, hard, rough, violent: σκληρόν σοι (ἐστι), Act.26:14; λόγος, Jhn.6:60; ἄνεμος, Jas.3:4; σκληρὰ λαλεῖν, Ju 15.† SYN.: αὐστηρός, q.v (AS)

G4643.d: σκληρότης, -ητος, ἡ (σκληρός), hardness; metaphorically, of stubbornness: Rom.2:5.† (AS)

G4645.d: σκληρύνω (σκληρός), to harden. Metaphorical, to harden, make stubborn: with accusative of person(s), Rom.9:18; T. καρδίας (Psa.95:8), Heb.3:8, 15 4:7. Pass., to become hardened: Act.19:9, Heb.3:13.† (AS)

G4646.d: σκολιός, -ά, -όν curved, bent, winding (opposite to ὀρθός, εὐθύς): Luk.3:5 (LXX). Metaphorical, crooked, perverse, unjust: Act.2:40, Php.2:15, 1Pe.2:18.† (AS)

G4647.d: σκόλοψ, -οπος, ὁ anything pointed, esp. __1. in cl., a stake __2. In Hellenistic vernacular, a thorn (cf. LXX, ll. with): σ. τῇ σαρκί, 2Co.12:7 (cf. MM, i., xxiii; DB, iii, 700 f.; Deiss., St. Paul, 62 f.; Field, Notes, 187).† (AS)

G4648.d: ακοπέω, -ῶ (σκοπός), to look at, behold, watch, contemplate. Metaphorical, to look to, consider: with accusative of thing(s), 2Co.4:13, Php.2:4; with accusative of person(s), Rom.16:17, Php.3:17; before μή, Luk.11:35; σεαυτόν, before μή (see M, Pr., 192), Gal.6:1 (cf. ἐπι-, κατα-σκοπέω).† SYN.: βλέπω, θεωρέω, ὁράω (AS)

G4649.d: σκοπός, -οῦ, ὁ __1. a watcher, watchman (Eze.3:17, al.). __2. a mark on which to fix the eye (Wis.5:12, 21, al.). Metaphorical, of an aim or object: Php.3:14.† (AS)

G4650.d: σκορπίζω in vernac. and in Ion, and late writers for σκεδάννυμι (see MM, xxiii; Rutherford, NPhr., 295), to scatter: ὁ λύκος, Jhn.10:12; ὁ μὴ συνάγων μετ᾽ ἐμοῦ σκορπίζει, Mat.12:30, Luk.11:23; pass., before εἰς, with accusative loc., Jhn.16:32; of one who dispenses blessings, 2Co.9:9 (LXX) (of. δια-σκορπίζομαι).† (AS)

G4651.d: σκορπίος, -ου, ὁ a scorpion: Luk.10:19 11:12, Rev.9:3, 5 9:10 † (AS)

G4652.d: σκοτεινός (WH. -τινός), -ή, -όν (σκότος), dark: opposite to φωτεινός, Mat.6:23, Luk.11:34, 36.† (AS)

G4653.d: σκοτία, -ας, ἡ in late writers = σκότος, darkness: Jhn.6:17 20:1. Metaphorical, __(a) of secrecy (opposite to ἐν τ. φωτί): Mat.10:27, Luk.12:3; __(b) of spiritual darkness: Mat.4:16, Jhn.1:5 8:12 12:35, 40, 1Jn.1:5 Jn 2:8-9 Jn 2:11.† (AS)

G4654.d: σκοτίζω (σκότος), to darken; in NT always pass., -ομαι, to be darkened: of the heavenly bodies, Mat.24:29, Mrk.13:24, Luk.23:45 (Rec., WH, mg.), Rev.8:12. Metaphorical, of the mind, Rom.1:21 11:10" (LXX) (cf. σκοτόω).† (AS)

G4655.d: σκότος, -ου, ὁ the more usual cl. form (cf.σ., τό), darkness: Heb.12:18, Rec.† (AS)

G4656.d: σκοτόω, -ῶ (σκότος), to darken: Rev.9:2 16:10. Metaphorical, of the mind! pass., Eph.4:18 (cf. σκοτίζω).† (AS)

G4657.d: σκύβαλον, -ου, τό refuse, esp. dung (see MM, ii, iii, xxiii): Php.3:8.† (AS)

G4658.d: Σκύθης, -ου, ὁ Scythian, an inhabitant of Scythia, i.e. Russia and Siberia, a synonym with the Greeks for the wildest of barbarians: Col.3:11.† (AS)

G4659.d: σκυθρωπός, -όν (also -ή, -όν) (σκυθρός, sullen, + ὤψ), of a gloomy countenance: Mat.6:16, Luk.24:17.† (AS)

G4660.d: σκύλλω __1. in cl., to skin, flay, rend (Æsch., Anthol.). __2. In Hellenistic writers, to vex, trouble, annoy: with accusative of person(s), Mrk.5:35, Luk.8:49; pass., ἐσκυλμένοι, distressed, Mat.9:36; mid., to trouble oneself, μὴ σκύλλου, Luk.7:6 (frequently in π.; see MM, i, ii, and cf. M, Pr., 89; Abbott, Essays, 87; Kennedy, Sources, 82).† (AS)

G4661.d: σκῦλον (Rec. σκύλον), -ου, τό mostly in pl., σκίλα, arms stripped from a foe, spoils: Luk.11:22.† (AS)

G4662.d: σκωληκό-βρωτος, -ον (σκώληξ, βιβρώσκω), eaten of worms: Act.12:23 (cf. 2Ma.9:9, and see MM, xxiii) † (AS)

G4663.d: σκώληξ, -ηκος, ὁ a worm: of the kind which preys upon dead bodies, metaphorically, of fut. punishment, Mrk.9:48 (LXX, Isa.66:24; cf. Sir.7:17, Jdth.16:17).† (AS)

G4664.d: σμαράγδινος (σμάραγδος, which see), __1. of emerald (Luc., V.H., ii, 11). __2. As in π. (Deiss., BS, 267), emerald-green: Rev.4:3 (for the construction, see Swete, in l; Zorell, see word).† (AS)

G4665.d: σμάραγδος, -ου, ἡ (and in late writers also ὁ), emerald or other trans parent green stone (LS, see word; DB, iv, 620; Swete, Ap., 67, 288): Rev.21:19.† (AS)

G4666.d: σμύρνα (in some MSS, ζμ-; see Bl., § 3, 9), -ης, ἡ, myrrh, a resinous gum used as an unguent and for em­balming: Mat.2:11, Jhn.19:39.† (AS)

G4667.d: Σμύρνα (T, Ζμ-; B1., § 3, 9), -ας, ἡ Smyrna, an Ionian city on the Ægean: Rev.1:11 2:8.† Ζμύρνα, -ης, ἡ, Rev.1:11 2:8 T, for Σμ-, which see (cf. B1., § 3, 9; Mayser, 204).† (AS)

G4668.d: Σμύρνα (T, Ζμ-; B1., § 3, 9), -ας, ἡ Smyrna, an Ionian city on the Ægean: Rev.1:11 2:8.† Ζμύρνα, -ης, ἡ, Rev.1:11 2:8 T, for Σμ-, which see (cf. B1., § 3, 9; Mayser, 204).† (AS)

G4669.d: σμυρνίζω (σιύρνα), __1. intrans., to be like myrrh (Diosc., i, 79). __2. Trans., to mingle or drug with myrrh: pass., Mrk.15:23.† (AS)

G4671.d: αὐτός, -ή, -ό, determinative pron., in late Gk. much more frequently than in cl. (WM, 178f.; Jannaris, HGG, §1399). __1. Emphatic (so always in nom. exc. when preceded by the art., see infr., iii); __(1) self (ipse), expressing opposition, distinction, exclusion, etc., αὐ. ἐκχυθήσεται, Luk.5:37; αὐ. ἐγινώσκεν, Jhn.2:25; αὐ.ὑμεῖς, Jhn.3:28; καὶ αὐ. ἐγώ, Rom.15:14; αὐ. Ἰησοῦς, Jhn.2:24; αὐ. καὶ οἱ…

G4672G.d: Σολομών, -ῶνος (so prop., but Rec. has frequently -ῶν, -ῶντος, as also WH in Act.3:11 5:12; in Act.7:47 T has Σαλωμών, as LXX freq., indecl.; see B1., § 10, 1; Tdf., Prol., 104, 119; WH, App., 158), ὁ (Heb. שְׁלֹמֹה), Solomon: Mat.1:6-7 6:29 12:42, Luk.11:31 12:27, Jhn.10:23, Act.3:11 5:12 7:47.† (AS)

G4672H.d: Σολομών, -ῶνος (so prop., but Rec. has frequently -ῶν, -ῶντος, as also WH in Act.3:11 5:12; in Act.7:47 T has Σαλωμών, as LXX freq., indecl.; see B1., § 10, 1; Tdf., Prol., 104, 119; WH, App., 158), ὁ (Heb. שְׁלֹמֹה), Solomon: Mat.1:6-7 6:29 12:42, Luk.11:31 12:27, Jhn.10:23, Act.3:11 5:12 7:47.† (AS)

G4673.d: σορός, -οῦ, ἡ __(a) a cinerary urn (Hom.); __(b) a coffin (Hdt., i, 68, 3, a1.): Luk.7:14.† (AS)

G4675.d: αὐτός, -ή, -ό, determinative pron., in late Gk. much more frequently than in cl. (WM, 178f.; Jannaris, HGG, §1399). __1. Emphatic (so always in nom. exc. when preceded by the art., see infr., iii); __(1) self (ipse), expressing opposition, distinction, exclusion, etc., αὐ. ἐκχυθήσεται, Luk.5:37; αὐ. ἐγινώσκεν, Jhn.2:25; αὐ.ὑμεῖς, Jhn.3:28; καὶ αὐ. ἐγώ, Rom.15:14; αὐ. Ἰησοῦς, Jhn.2:24; αὐ. καὶ οἱ…

G4676.d: σουδάριον, -ου, τό(Lat.), handkerchief, kerchief: Luk.19:20, Act.19:12; used as a head covering for the dead, Jhn.11:44 20:7 (cf. Deiss., BS, 223).† (AS)

G4677.d: Σουσάννα, -ης (cf. Dan LXX TH Su, inscr., 2, 7, al.) Susanna: Luk.8:3.† (AS)

G4678.d: σοφία, -ας, ἡ skill, intelligence, wisdom, ranging from knowledge of the arts and matters of daily life to mental excellence in its highest and fullest sense; __(a) of human wisdom: 1Co.2:1 2:4-5, Jas.3:15, Rev.13:18 17:9; σ. Σολομῶνος, Mat.12:42, Luk.11:31; Αἰγυπτίων, Act.7:22; Ἕλληνες σ. ζητοῦσιν, 1Co.1:22; σ. λόγου, 1Co.1:17; τ. σοφῶν, 1Co.1:19 (LXX); τ. κόσμου, 1Co.1:20-21 3:19; ἀνθρωπίνη,…

G4679.d: σοφίζω (σοφός), to make wise, instruct: with accusative of person(s), 2Ti.3:15 (cf. Psa.19:8 (Psa.119:98). As depon., -ομαι; __(a) intrans., to become wise (I2Ki.4:27 (3Ki.5:11), Ecc.2:15, and frequently in Sir.7:5, al.); __(b) trans., to invent, devise cleverly: pass., 2Pe.1:16 (cf. κατα-σοφίζομαι).† (AS)

G4680.d: σοφός, -ή, -όν skilled, clever, wise, whether in handicraft, the affairs of life, the sciences or learning: Rom.16:19, 1Co.3:10; of the learned, Rom.1:14, 22, 1Co.1:19-20 1:26-27 3:18-20; of Jewish teachers, Mat.11:25, Luk.10:21; Christian, Mat.23:34; of those en­dowed with practical wisdom, 1Co.6:5, Eph.5:15, Jas.3:13; of God, Rom.16:27; compar., τ. μωρὸν τ. θεοῦ σοφώτερον, 1Co.1:25.† SYN.:…

G4681.d: Σπανία, -ας, ἡ (= cl. Ἑσπερία or Ἰβηρία; late writers adopted the Roman name, Ἱσπανία (1Ma.8:3) or Σ. as here), Spain: Rom.15:24, 28.† (AS)

G4682.d: σπαράσσω __1. to tear, rend, mangle. __2. to convulse: Mrk.1:26 (see Swete, in l) Mrk.9:26, Luk.9:39 (cf. συν-σπαράσσω).† (AS)

G4683.d: σπαργανόω, -ῶ (σπάργανον, a swathing-band) to swathe, wrap in swaddling-clothes: Luk.2:7, 12 (Hipp., Arist., Plut.).† (AS)

G4684.d: σπαταλάω, -ῶ (σπατάλη, wantonness, luxury, Sir.27:13 *), to live riotously: 1Ti.5:6, Jas.5:5 (Polyb.).† SYN.: στρηνιάω, τρυφάω (see Tr., Syn., § liv) (AS)

G4685.d: σπάω in cl. poët. for ἕλκω; mostly used in mid. (cf. M, Pr., 157), to draw: μάχαιραν, Mrk.14:47, Act.16:27,† (AS)

G4686.d: σπείρα, -ης (on this form of genitive, see M, Pr., 38, 48; Bl., § 7, 1; Mayser, 12; Deiss., BS, 186), __1. (= Lat. spira) anything wound or rolled up, a coil. __2. As a military term used (by Polyb. and later writers) of a body of soldiers, a maniple (third part of a cohort) or cohort (see Swete, Mk., 375; Westc., Jo., 251 f.): Mat.27:27, Mrk.15:16, Jhn.18:3, 12, Act.10:1 21:31 27:1.† (AS)

G4687.d: σπείρω to sow (seed): absol., Mat.6:26 13:3-4, 18 25:24, 26, Mrk.4:3-4, Luk.8:5 12:24, Jhn.4:36, 2Co.9:10; with accusative of thing(s), Mat.13:24, 27 13:37, 39, Mrk.4:32, Luk.8:5, 1Co.15:36-37; before εἰς, Mat.13:22, Mrk.4:18; ἐν, Mat.13:24, 31; ἐπί, with genitive, Mrk.4:31; ἐπί, with accusative, Mat.13:20, 23, Mrk.4:16, 20; παρά, with accusative, Mat.13:19. Metaphorical: 1Co.9:11 15:42-44,…

G4688.d: σπεκουλάτωρ, -ορος (Rec. -ωρος), ὁ (Lat. speculator), __1. prop., a spy or scout. __2. An executioner: Mrk.6:27 (see Swete, in l).† (AS)

G4689.d: σπένδω to pour out as a drink-offering, make a libation; pass., figuratively, σπένδομαι, I am poured out or offered as a libation (in the shedding of my life-blood): Php.2:17 (see Lft., in l), 2Ti.4:6 (for exx. from π., see Milligan, Selections, 114 f.; MM, xxiii).† (AS)

G4690.d: σπέρμα, -τος, τό (σπείρω) seed; __(a) of plants: Mat.13:24, 27 13:37-38, 2Co.9:10; pl., Mat.13:32, Mrk.4:31, 1Co.15:33; metaphorically, of an escaping remnant (שָׂרִיד, Isa.1:9; cf. Wis.14:6; Plat., Tim., 23c; FlJ, Ant., xi, 5, 3), Rom.9:29; __(b) of men (as γονή; Lat. semen genitale; so in cl.; cf. in LXX, Lev.15:16, al.): Heb.11:11; metaphorically, of the divine influence, 1Jn.3:9; by meton.…

G4690G.d: σπέρμα, -τος, τό (σπείρω) seed; __(a) of plants: Mat.13:24, 27 13:37-38, 2Co.9:10; pl., Mat.13:32, Mrk.4:31, 1Co.15:33; metaphorically, of an escaping remnant (שָׂרִיד, Isa.1:9; cf. Wis.14:6; Plat., Tim., 23c; FlJ, Ant., xi, 5, 3), Rom.9:29; __(b) of men (as γονή; Lat. semen genitale; so in cl.; cf. in LXX, Lev.15:16, al.): Heb.11:11; metaphorically, of the divine influence, 1Jn.3:9; by meton.…

G4690H.d: σπέρμα, -τος, τό (σπείρω) seed; __(a) of plants: Mat.13:24, 27 13:37-38, 2Co.9:10; pl., Mat.13:32, Mrk.4:31, 1Co.15:33; metaphorically, of an escaping remnant (שָׂרִיד, Isa.1:9; cf. Wis.14:6; Plat., Tim., 23c; FlJ, Ant., xi, 5, 3), Rom.9:29; __(b) of men (as γονή; Lat. semen genitale; so in cl.; cf. in LXX, Lev.15:16, al.): Heb.11:11; metaphorically, of the divine influence, 1Jn.3:9; by meton.…

G4691.d: σπερμολόγος, -ον (σπέρμα, λέγω) a seed picker; __(a) prop., of birds (Arist., Aristoph, al.); __(b) in Attic slang, of an idler who lives on scraps picked up in the agora; hence, as subst., ὁ σ., an idle babbler: Act.17:18.† (AS)

G4692.d: σπεύδω __1. most frequently intrans., to hasten: with inf. (as frequently in cl.), Act.20:16; ptcp. with indic., Luk.2:16; with imperat., Luk.19:5-6; σπεῦσον κ. ἔξελθε, Act.22:18 __2. Trans., with accusative; __(a) to hasten, urge on, accelerate (as Hom., Od., xix, 137; Eur., Med., 152; Sir.33:8 (Sir.36:8): 2Pe.3:12, R, mg. (cf. Mayor and ICC, in l, but see infr.); __(b) to desire eagerly (find.,…

G4693.d: σπήλαιον, -ου, τό a cave, cavern: Jhn.11:38, Heb.11:38, Heb.6:15; σ. (EV, den) λῃστῶν (Jhn.7:11), Mat.21:13, Mrk.11:17, Luk.19:46.† (AS)

G4694.d: σπιλάς, -άδος, ἡ (on the gender in Ju, l.with, see Mayor, Ju., 41), __1. poët. in cl., a rock or reef over which the sea dashes (Polyb., FlJ, al.). Metaphorical, of men whose conduct causes danger to others, Ju 12, R, txt. (but see infr.). __2. In late writers = σπίλος (which see), a spot, stain; metaphorically, Ju, l.with, R, mg. (cf. Mayor, 41, but see supr.).† (AS)

G4695.d: σπιλόω to stain, spot, defile: with accusative, Jas.3:6, Ju 23.† (AS)

G4696.d: σπίλος (Rec. σπῖλος), -ου, ὁ __1. a rock, cliff (Arist., al.). __2. In late writers = Att.. κηλίς (see Rutherford, NPhr., 87 f.), a spot, stain; metaphorically, __(a) of moral blemish: Eph.5:27 __(b) of riotous and lascivious persons (cf. Dion. Hal., quoted by Mayor, in l): 2Pe.2:13.† (AS)

G4697.d: σπλαγχνίζομαι (σπλάγχνον), to be moved as to the σπλάγχνα (which see), hence, to feel pity or compassion: absol., Luk.10:33 15:20; ptcp., σπλαγχνισθείς, with indic., Mat.18:27 20:34, Mrk.1:41; before ἐπί, with dative of person(s), Mat.14:14, Luk.7:13; ἐπί, with accusative, Mat.15:32, Mrk.6:34 8:2 9:22; ωερί, Mat.9:36. (The word is elsewhere found only in Sm: 1Ki.23:21, Eze.24:21, Test. Zeb.,…

G4698.d: σπλάγχνον, -ου, τό mostly (in NT always) in pl., σπλάγχνα, -ων, τά, the inward parts (heart, liver, lungs, etc.; Lat. viscera): Act.1:18. Metaphorical, of the seat of the feelings and of the feelings themselves (in Gk. poets, of anger, anxiety, etc.), the heart, affections (the characteristic LXX and NT reference of the word to feelings of kindness, benevolence and pity, is found in π.; see MM,…

G4699.d: σπόγγος, -ου, ὁ a sponge: Mat.27:48, Mrk.15:36, Jhn.19:29.† (AS)

G4700.d: σποδός, -oῦ, ὁ ashes: Heb.9:13; ἐν σάκκῳ καὶ σ. (Isa.58:5, Jhn.3:6, Dan LXX 9:3, al.), Mat.11:21, Luk.10:13.† (AS)

G4701.d: σπορά, -ᾶς, ἡ (σπείρω), __1. a sowing. __2. seedtime. __3. seed sown (of human offspring, Soph., Tr., 316, 420): 1Pe.1:23 (cf. σπέρμα, and see Milligan, NTD, 105 f.).† (AS)

G4702.d: σπόριμος, -ον (σπείρω) fit for sowing, sown; as subst., τὰ σ., corn-fields: Mat.12:1, Mrk.2:23, Luk.6:1.† (AS)

G4703.d: σπόρος, -ου, ὁ (σπείρω), = σπορά, __1. sowing or seedtime. __2. seed sown (so usually in late Gk.): Mrk.4:26-27, Luk.8:5, 11, 2Co.9:10 a (LTr.); metaphorically, of almsgiving, 2Co.9:10 b.† (AS)

G4704.d: σπουδάζω (σπουδή), to make haste; hence, to be zealous or eager, to give diligence: with inf. (see M, Pr., 205 f.), Gal.2:10, Eph.4:3, 1Th.2:17, 2Ti.2:15 4:9 4:21, Tit.3:12, Heb.4:11, 2Pe.1:10 3:14; with accusative and inf. (on this construction see Mayor in l; MM, xxiii), 2Pe.1:15 (for other constructions see LS, see word).† (AS)

G4705.d: σπουδαῖος, -α, -ον (σπουδή), in haste; hence, zealous, eager, diligent, earnest: before ἐν, 2Co.8:22; compar., -οτεροσς 2Co.8:17 (here in superl. sense, see Bl., § 44, 3) 2Co.8:22.† (AS)

G4708.d: earnestly, zealously, with vigor; (compar.) all the more eager, with special urgency eagerly earnestly, eagerly, diligently, Lk. 7:4; 2Tim. 1:17; Tit. 3:13; comparative σπουδαιοτέρως, more earnestly, with special urgency, Phil. 2:28

G4709.d: σπουδαίως adv. (σπουδαῖος), __1. with haste or zeal, i.e. earnestly, zealously, diligently: Luk.7:4, 2Ti.1:17, Tit.3:13; compar., -οτέρως, Php.2:28 (RV, Lft., Weymouth, al., but see infr.) __2. hastily, speedily: compar., -οτέρως, Php.2:28 (Thayer, Zorell, see word; ICC, in l, al., but see supr.).† (AS)

G4710.d: σπουδή, -ῆς, ἡ (σπεύδω), __1. haste, speed: μετὰ σ. (Wis.19:2), Mrk.6:25, Luk.1:39. __2. zeal, diligence, earnestness: Rom.12:11, 2Co.7:11-12 8:7-8; ἐν σ., Rom.12:8 (see M, Pr, 104); before ὑπέρ, 2Co.8:16; σπουδὴν ἐνδείκνυσθαι, Heb.6:11; σ. παρεισφέρειν, 2Pe.1:5; πᾶσαν σ. ποιεῖσθαι, Ju 3 (see MM, xxiii; M, Pr., 214; Deiss., BS, 361, 364).† (AS)

G4711.d: σφυρίς (T, Rec. σπυρίς, see WH, App., 148; 131., § 6, 7), -ίδος, ἡ, a flexible mat-basket for carrying provisions: Mat.15:37 16:10, Mrk.8:8, 20 Act.9:25 (see: κόφινος).† (AS)

G4712.d: στάδιον, -ου, τό pl., στάδια (Jhn.6:19, T), and metapl., στάδιοι (see B1., 9, 1), a stadium, i.e. __1. a measure of length = 600 Greek feet or 1⁄8 of a Roman mile Mat.14:24 (Rec., WH, txt., R, mg.), Luk.24:13, Jhn.6:19 11:18, Rev.14:20 21:16, and, this being the length of the Olympic course, __2. a race-course: 1Co.9:24.† (AS)

G4713.d: στάρνος, -ου (ὁ and), ἡ prop., an earthen jar for racking off wine, hence, generally, a jar: Heb.9:4.† (AS)

G4714.d: στάσις, -εως, ἡ (ἵστημι), __1. a standing, place, status: σ. ἔχειν (Polyb., v, 5, 3; and cf. Lat. locum habere), Heb.9:8. __2. insurrection, sedition: Mrk.15:7, Luk.23:19, 25, Act.19:40 24:5. __3. In poets and late prose, strife, dissension (cf. MM, xxiii) Act.15:2 23:7, 10.† (AS)

G4715.d: στατήρ, -ῆρος, ὁ [in Aq., Sm., for מִשְׁקָל ;] a stater; __(a) a weight; __(b) a coin (used by late writers of the Greek τετράδραχμον): Mat.17:27 26:16, WH, mg.† (AS)

G4716.d: σταυρός, -oῦ, ὁ __1. an upright pale or stake (Hom., Hdt., Thuc., al.) __2. In late writers (Diod., Plut., al.) of the Roman instrument of crucifixion, the Cross: of the Cross on which Christ suffered, Mat.27:32, 40 27:42, Mrk.15:21, 30 15:32, Luk.23:26, Jhn.19:17, 19 19:25, 31, Col.2:14, Heb.12:2; θάνατος σταυροῦ, Php.2:8; τ. αἷμα τοῦ σ., Col.1:20. Metaphorical, in proverbial sayings: αἴρειν…

G4717.d: σταυρόω, -ῶ (σταυρός), __1. to fence with pales, impalisade (Thuc.). __2. In late writers (Polyb., FlJ; but ἀνασταυρόω is more common) to crucify: with accusative of person(s), Mat.20:19 23:34 26:2 27:22 ff. Mat.28:5, Mrk.15:16 ff. Mrk.16:6, Luk.23:21, 23 23:33 24:7, 20, Jhn.19:6 ff., Act.2:36 4:10, 1Co.1:13 1:23 2:2 2:8, 2Co.13:4, Gal.3:1, Rev.11:8; metaphorically, Gal.5:24 6:14.† (AS)

G4718.d: σταφυλή, -ῆς, ἡ a bunch of grapes: Mat.7:16, Luk.6:44, Rev.14:18. "σ. is properly the ripe grape-cluster as opposite to ὄμφαξ, cf. Gen.40:10, Job.15:33; as contrasted with βότρυς, it describes the grapes rather than the cluster on which they grow" (Swete, Apoc., 187 f.).† (AS)

G4719.d: στάχυς, -υος, ὁ an ear of corn: Mat.12:1, Mrk.2:23 4:28, Luk.6:1.† (AS)

G4720.d: Στάχυς, -υος, ὁ Stachys: Rom.16:9 (see Lft., Phi., 174; MM, xxiii).† (AS)

G4721.d: στέγη, -ης, ἡ (στέγω) a roof: Mrk.2:4; of entering a house, εἰσέρχεσθαι ὑπὸ τὴν σ., Mat.8:8, Luk.7:6 (cf. MM, xxiii).† (AS)

G4722.d: στέγω (cf. Lat. tego), __1. prop., to cover closely, to protect by covering, esp. to keep water in or out (Soph., Plat., al.). __2. to cover, keep secret, conceal (Sir, l.with, Polyb., al.): 1Co.13:7, R, mg. __3. By covering to ward of, bear up under, endure (for exx., see, Lft., Notes, 40; M, Th., 36): 1Co.9:12 13:7, 1Th.3:1 3:5.† (AS)

G4723.d: στεῖρος, -ον also -α, -ον, barren: of a woman, Luk.1:7, 36 23:29, Gal.4:27" (LXX) .† (AS)

G4724.d: στέλλω __1. prop., to set, place, arrange, fit out; hence, mid., to set oneself for, prepare (Wis, xi Mac, ll. with). __2. to bring together, gather up (in Hom. of furling sails), hence to restrain, check; mid., to restrain or withdraw oneself, hold aloof, avoid: 2Co.8:20; before ἀπό, 2Th.3:6 (cf. ἀπο-, ἐξ-απο-, συν-απο-, δια-, ἐπι-, κατα-, συ(ν)-, ὑπο-στέλλω).† (AS)

G4725.d: στέμμα, -τος, τό (στέφω, to put around, enwreath) a wreath, garland: as used in sacrifices, Act.14:13.† (AS)

G4726.d: στεναγμός, -οῦ, ὁ (στενάζω), a groaning: Act.7:34 (LXX κραυγή), Rom.8:26.† (AS)

G4727.d: στενάζω to groan ("the word denotes feeling which is internal and unexpressed," Mayor, Ja., 162): Mrk.7:34, 2Co.5:2 5:4, Heb.13:17, Jas.5:9 (EV, murmur); ἐν ἑαυτοῖς, Rom.8:23 (cf. ἀνα-, συ(ν)-στενάζω).† SYN.: see: κλαίω (AS)

G4728.d: στενός, -ή, -όν narrow: fig (v MM, xxiii), Mat.7:13-14, Luk.13:24.† (AS)

G4729.d: στενο-χωρέω, -ῶ (στενός + χῶρος, space) __1. to be straitened (cf. Isa.49:19); metaphorically, to be anxious (Hipp., al.). __2. In late writers, trans., to straiten, compress (LXX, Diod., al.; π. ap. MM, xxiii): pass., trop., 2Co.4:8 6:12.† (AS)

G4730.d: στενοχωρία, -ας, ἡ (see supr.) narrowness of space, want of room (Thuc., al.). Metaphorical (Ken., Polyb., Deu.28:53, Wis.5:3, al.), difficulty, distress: θλίψις καὶ (ἢ) σ., Rom.2:9 8:35 (EV, anguish); pl. (cf. Bl., § 32, 6; WM, 220), 2Co.6:4 12:10.† SYN.: θλίψις, q.v (AS)

G4731.d: στερεός, -ά, -όν hard, firm, solid: τροψή, Heb.5:12, 14; θεμέλιος, figuratively, 2Ti.2:19. Metaphorical, __(a) in bad sense, hard, cruel (Hom., al.); __(b) in good sense, steadfast, firm: τ. πίστει, 1Pe.5:9.† (AS)

G4732.d: στερεόω, -ῶ (στερεός), __(a) to make firm or solid; __(b) to strengthen, make strong; with accusative of person(s), Act.3:16; τ. βάσεις, pass., Act.3:7. Metaphorical (cf. Je, l.with): τ. πίστει, pass., Act.16:5.† (AS)

G4733.d: στερέωμα, -τος, τό (στερεόω), a solid body; __(a) a support, foundation (Arist., al.); metaphorically, strength (Psa.17:1-15 70:1-5, 1Mac, ll. with); steadfastness, firmness: τ. πίστεως, Col.2:5; __(b) the dome of heaven (believed to be a solid canopy), the firmament (LXX).† (AS)

G4735.d: στέφανος, -ου, ὁ (στέφω, to encircle), __1. that which surrounds or encompasses (as a wall, a crowd: Hom., al.). __2. a crown, i.e. the wreath, garland or chaplet given as a prize for victory, as a festal ornament, or as a public honour for disting­uished service or personal worth (so to sovereigns, especially on the occasion of a παρουσία, which see; cf. Deiss., LAE, 372 ff.; on its use in LXX…

G4737.d: στεφανόω, -ῶ (στέφανος), with accusative of person(s), to crown: of a victor, 2Ti.2:5. Metaphorical, δόξῃ κ. τιμῇ, Heb.2:7, 9" (LXX) .† (AS)

G4738.d: στῆθος, -ους, τό the breast: Jhn.13:25 21:10, Rev.15:6; as a sign of penitence, τύπτειν (εἰς) τὸ σ., Luk.18:13 23:48,† (AS)

G4739.d: στήκω late Pres., formed from perf., ἕστηκα (see B1., § 17; WH, App., 169; Kennedy, Sources, 158; M, Pr., 238; MM, xxiii), = ἵστημι, to stand: Mrk.3:31 11:25, Jhn.1:26, Rev.12:4 (ἕστηκεν T). Metaphorical, to stand firm, stand fast: absol., Gal.5:1 (but see Field, Notes, 189 f.), 2Th.2:15; before ἐν, Jhn.8:44 (ἕστηκεν, T, R, mg.), 1Co.16:13, Php.1:27 4:1; with dative, Rom.14:4.† (AS)

G4740.d: στηριγμός, -οῦ, ὁ (στηρίζω), [in Sm.: Isa.3:1 * ;] __1. a setting firmly, supporting. __2. fixedness, firmness, steadfastness: 2Pe.3:17.† (AS)

G4741.d: στηρίζω to fix, set fast, make fast: Luk.16:26; τ. πρόσωτον (Eze.6:2 13:17, al.; see Dalman, Words, 30 f.), Luk.9:51. Metaphorical, to confirm, establish: with, accusative, Luk.22:32, Act.18:23, Rom.1:11 16:25, 1Th.3:2 3:13, 2Th.3:3, Jas.5:8, 1Pe.5:10, Rev.3:2; id. before ἐν, 2Th.2:17, 2Pe.1:12.† (AS)

G4742.d: στίγμα -τος, τό (στίζω, to prick), a tattoed mark or brand: τὰ σ. τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, Gal.6:17 (see Lft., in l; Deiss., BS, 349; LAE, 303; MM, xxiii).† (AS)

G4743.d: στιγμή, -ῆς, ἡ (στίζω, to prick), a prick, a point; metaphorically, σ. χρόνου, a moment: Luk.4:5.† (AS)

G4745.d: στοά, -ᾶς, ἡ a portico: Jhn.5:2; used of the covered colonnade in the Temple (EV, porch), Jhn.10:23 Act.3:11 5:12 † (AS)

G4746.d: στοιβάς, see: στιβάς. στιβάς, -άδος, ἡ, [in Aq.: Eze.46:23 (טִירוֺת) * ;] a litter of leaves or rushes: pl., Mrk.11:8 (Rec. στοιβ-).† (AS)

G4747.d: στοιχεῖον, -ου, τό prop., one of a row (στοῖχος) or series, hence, __1. the shadow-line of a dial (Aristoph.). __2. an elementary sound or letter of the alphabet (Anth., Plut., π.). __3. the elements or rudiments of knowledge (Arist., al.) Heb.5:12; πτωχὰ σ., Gal.4:9; σ. τοῦ κόσμου, Gal.4:3, Col.2:8, 20 (but see infr.). __4. The material elements of the universe (Plat.; LXX, ll. with): 2Pe.3:10…

G4748.d: στοιχέω, -ῶ (στοῖχος, a row), to be in rows (of waves, plants, etc., as well as of men), to walk in line (esp. of marching in file to battle; Xen., Cyr., vi, 3, 34, al.). Metaphorical, in late writers, to walk by rule: Act.21:24; with dative, to walk by or in (as a rule of life), Rom.4:12 (cf. MM, xxiii), Gal.5:25 6:16, Php.3:16 (cf. συν-στοιχέω).† (AS)

G4749.d: στολή, -ῆς, ἡ (στέλλω), __1 1, an equipment, an armament (Æsch.). __2. Equipment in clothes, apparel, esp. flowing raiment, a festal robe: (cf. Jon.3:6, Est.8:15, 1Ma.6:15): Mrk.12:38 16:5, Luk.15:22 20:46, Rev.6:11 7:9, 13-14 22:14.† (AS)

G4750.d: στόμα, -τος, τό the mouth: of man, Mat.15:11, Jhn.19:29, Act.11:8, al.; of animals, Mat.17:27, 2Ti.4:17 (fig.), Heb.11:33, Jas.3:3, al.; figuratively, of inanimate things (ποταμοῦ, Hom.), ἤνοιξεν ἡ γῆ τὸ σ., Rev.12:16; σ. μαχαίρας (Heb. חֶרֶב ־פֶּה, Gen.34:26 al.), the edge of the sword, Luk.21:24, Heb.11:34; esp. of the mouth as the organ of speech: opposite to καρδία, Mat.12:34, Rom.10:8, 10;…

G4751.d: στόμαχος, -ου, ὁ (στόμα), prop., a mouth, an opening; __(a) in early Gk. writers, the throat; __(b) of the opening of the stomach (Arist.); __(with) in later writers (Plut., al.), the stomach: 1Ti.5:23.† (AS)

G4752.d: στρατεία (on the orthogr., see Deiss., BS, 181 f.), -ας, ἡ (οτρατεύω), an expedition, a campaign, warfare: metaphorically, 2Co.10:4 (-τιά, T), 1Ti.1:18.† (AS)

G4753.d: στράτευμα, -τος, τό (στρατεύω), __1. = στρατεία (Hdt., al.). __2. an army, a host: pl., Mat.22:7, Rev.9:16 19:14, 19; = soldiers, company of soldiers, Act.23:10, 27; pl., Luk.23:11.† (AS)

G4754.d: στρατεύω and depon., -ομαι, so always in NT (στρατός, an encamped army), used of the general, to make war, do battle, and (chiefly) of the soldiers serving under him, to serve as a soldier: Luk.3:14, 1Co.9:7, 2Ti.2:4. Metaphorical (cf. MM, ii, xxiii), of spiritual conflict, to war, make war: 2Co.10:3, 1Ti.1:18, Jas.4:1, 1Pe.2:11.† (AS)

G4755.d: στρατηγός, -οῦ, ὁ (στραός, ἄγω), __1. a military commander, a general (Hdt., al.). __2. A civic commander, a governor, magistrate (Hdt., Xen., al.): Act.16:20, 22 16:35-36, 38. __3. The commander of the Levitical guard of the Temple, ὁ σ. τ. ἱεροῦ (EV, captain of the Temple): Act.4:1 5:24, 26; pl., Luk.22:4, 52.† SYN.: ἄρχων (cf. EGT on Act.16:20; Ramsay, St. Paul, 217). (AS)

G4756.d: στρατιά, -ᾶς, ἡ __1. = στρατός, an army, a host: of angels (3Ki.22:19, al.), Luk.2:13; of the stars of heaven (Jer.8:2, 2Ch.33:3), Act.7:42. __2. As sometimes in cl. (poët.), = στρατεία: 2Co.10:4, T (WH, RV, στρατεία).† (AS)

G4757.d: στρατιώτης, -ου, ὁ a soldier: Mat.8:9, Mrk.15:16, Jhn.19:2, Act.10:7, al.; metaphorically, σ. Χριστοῦ Ἰησ., 2Ti.2:3.† (AS)

G4758.d: στρατολογέω, -ῶ (στρατός, λέγω), to levy a troop, enlist soldiers: 2Ti.2:4 (Diod., Plut., al.).† (AS)

G4759.d: στρατοπέδ-αρχος (Rec. -ης), -ου, ὁ (στρατόπεδον, ἄρχω), a military commander, esp. the Pretorian prefect: Act.28:16 (WH, om.).† στρατοπεδάρχης, see: στρατοπέδαρχος (AS)

G4760.d: στρατό-πεδον, -ου, τό (στρατός + πέδον, a plain), __(a) a military camp; __(b) an army: Luk.21:20.† (AS)

G4761.d: στρεβλόω, -ῶ (στρέφω), to twist, torture. Metaphorical (cf. 2Ki, l.with), to twist or pervert language: 2Pe.3:16.† (AS)

G4762.d: στρέφω to turn: with accusative of thing(s) dative of person(s), Mat.5:39; = ἀποσ-, to bring back, Mat.27:3 (cf. Isa.38:8); reflexively (WM, § 38, 1), to turn oneself, Act.7:42; with accusative before εἰς, = μετασ-, to change, Rev.11:6. Pass., reflexive, to turn oneself: before εἰς, Jhn.20:14, Act.7:39 13:46; ptcp., στραφείς, with indic., Mat.7:6 9:22 16:23, Luk.7:9 9:55 14:25 22:61, Jhn.1:38…

G4763.d: στρηνιάω, ῶ (στρῆνος, which see), [in Sm.: Isa.61:6 (אָכַל) * ;] a word which first appears in the middle comedy (Rutherford, NPhr., 475 f.), to run riot, wax wanton: Rev.18:7-9 (cf. κατα-στρηνιάω).† SYN.: σπαταλάω (which see), τρυφάω (AS)

G4764.d: στρῆνος, -ους, τό (cf. Lat. strenuus), insolent luxury, wantonness: Rev.18:3 (a late word, first found in a Comic poet, B.C. 300, see Kennedy, Sources, 41, cf. στρηνιάω).† (AS)

G4765.d: στρουθίον, -ου, τό dimin. of στρουθός a sparrow: Mat.10:29, 31, Luk.12:6-7.† (AS)

G4766.d: στρωννύω or στρώννυμι (seeBl., § 23, 1; Veitch, see word), to spread: ἱμάτια ἐν τ. ὁδῷ (εἰς τ. ὁδόν), Mat.21:8, Mrk.11:8; of making a bed, στρῶσον (sc. τ. κλίνην) σεαυτῷ, Act.9:34; of furnishing a room, ἐστρωμένον, spread with carpets or carpeted couches (cf. Eze.23:41), Mrk.14:15, Luk.22:12.† (AS)

G4767.d: στυγητός, -όν (στυγέω, to hate), hated, hateful: Tit.3:3.† (AS)

G4768.d: στυγνάζω (στυγνός, sombre, gloomy, sullen, Isa.5:17, Wis.17:5, Dan LXX 2:12*), to have a sombre, gloomy appearance: of the human countenance (RV, his countenance fell), Mrk.10:22; of the sky (so στυγνότης, Polyb., iv, 21, 1), Mat.16:3 ([WH], R, mg., om.).† (AS)

G4769.d: στύλος (T, στῦλος, as in cl.), -ου, ὁ a pillar, regarded especially as a support: σ. πυρός, Rev.10:1; σ. ἐν τ. ναῷ, figuratively, Rev.3:12, Metaphorical, Gal.2:9; τ. ἀληθείας, 1Ti.3:15.† (AS)

G4771.d: σύ, pron. of 2nd of person(s), thou, you, genitive, σοῦ, dative, σοί, accusative, σέ, pl., ὑμεῖς, -ῶν, -ῖν, -ᾶς (enclitic in oblique cases sing., except after prep. (BL, §48, 3), though πρὸς σέ occurs in Mat.25:39). Nom. for emphasis or contrast: Jhn.1:30, 4:10, 5:33, 39, 44, Act.4:7, Eph.5:32; so also perhaps σὺ εἶπας, Mat.26:64, al. (M, Pr., 86); before voc., Mat.2:6, Luk.1:76, Jhn.17:5, al.;…

G4772.d: συγγένεια, -ας, ἡ (συγγενής), __1. kinship. __2. By meton., kinsfolk, kindred: Luk.1:61, Act.7:3, 14 † (AS)

G4773.d: σνγγενής, -ές (dative pl., -εῦσιν, Mrk.6:4, Luk.2:44, as though from -εύς, see Swete, Mk., l.with; Bl., § 8, 6; cf. 1Ma.10:89 A א2 *;) (σύν, γένος), __1. congenital, natural, innate. __2. akin to; as subst., a kinsman: Mrk.6:4, Luk.1:58 2:44 14:12 21:16, Jhn.18:26, Act.10:24; of tribal kinship, Rom.9:3 16:7, 11 16:21.† SYN.: ἴδιος, οἰκεῖος (which see) (AS)

G4774.d: συν-γνώμη (Rec. συγγ-), -ης, ἡ (συγγιγνώσκω, (a) to agree with; (b) to pardon), __1. confession. __2. fellow feeling; hence, concession, allowance: 1Co.7:6 (see ICC, in l). __3. pardon.† (AS)

G4775.d: συν-κάθημαι (Rec. συγκ-), to sit together or with: with dative, Act.26:30; before μετά, with genitive, Mrk.14:54.† (AS)

G4776.d: περι-καθ-ίζω __1. to invest, besiege (Diod., 4Ki.6:24, 1Ma.11:61, al.). __2. to sit around: Luk.22:55, L, txt. † (AS)

G4777.d: συν-κακοπαθέω (Rec. συγκ-), -ῶ, to bear evil treatment along with, take one's share of ill-treatment: 2Ti.2:3; with dative commod., τ. εὐαγγελίῳ, 2Ti.2:18.† (AS)

G4778.d: συν-κακουχέομαι (Rec. συγκ-), -οῦμαι, pass. to endure adversity with: with dative of person(s), Heb.11:25. Not elsewhere.† (AS)

G4779.d: συν-καλέω (Rec. συγκ-), -ῶ, to call together: with accusative, Mrk.15:16, Luk.15:6, 9 (seel. -εῖται, see B1., § 55, 1), Act.5:21. Mid., to call together to oneself: Luk.9:1 (and seel. in Luk.15:6, 9 see supr.) Luk.23:13, Act.10:24 28:17.† (AS)

G4780.d: συν-καλύπτω (Rec. συγκ-), to veil or cover completely: with accusative, pass., Luk.12:2.† (AS)

G4781.d: συν-κάμπτω (Rec. συγκ-), to bend completely, bend together: τ. νῶτον, figuratively, Rom.11:10 (LXX).† (AS)

G4782.d: συν-κατα-βαίνω (Rec. συγκ-), to go down with: Act.25:5. In late writers also metaphorically (Wis, l.with), to condescend, on WH. see Rutherford, NPhr., 485 f.† (AS)

G4783.d: συν-κατά-θεσις (Rec συγκ-), -εως, ἡ (συνκατατίθημι) concord, agreement: 2Co.6:16 (Polyb., Plut., al.).† (AS)

G4784.d: συν-κατα-τίθημι (Rec. συγκ-), to deposit together. Mid., to deposit one's vote with, hence, to agree with, assent to: with dative, Luk.23:51.† (AS)

G4785.d: συν-κατα-ψηφίζω (Rec. συγκ-), __1. to condemn with or together (Plut., Themist., 21). __2. to vote one a place among: pass., Act.1:26. Not elsewhere .† (AS)

G4786.d: συν-κεράννυμι (Rec. συγκ-), to mix or blend together, compound: with accusative, 1Co.12:24; ptcp. pf. pass., Heb.4:2, T, WH, mg., R, mg.; id., of persons, with dative instr., to be united with, agree with, ib., WH, txt., R, txt. (see Westc., in l).† (AS)

G4787.d: συν-κινέω (Rec. συγκ-), -ῶ, to move together. Metaphorical, to excite, stir up: τ. λαόν, Act.6:12 (Arist., Polyb., al.).† (AS)

G4788.d: συν-κλείω (Rec. συγκ-), to shut together, enclose, shut in on all sides: of a catch of fish, Luk.5:6; metaphorically (Psa.31:9, al.), Rom.11:32, Gal.3:22-23.† (AS)

G4789.d: συν-κληρο-νόμος (Rec. συγκ-), -ου, ὁ a co-inheritor, fellow-heir: Rom.8:17, Eph.3:6; with genitive of thing(s), Heb.11:9, 1Pe.3:7 (for exx., see Deiss., LAE, 88 f.).† (AS)

G4790.d: συν-κοινωνέω (Rec. συγκ-), -ῶ, to have fellowship with or in (in cl., with genitive of thing(s), dative of person(s)): with dative of thing(s), Eph.5:11, Rev.18:4; id. with genitive of person(s), Php.4:14.† (AS)

G4791.d: συν-κοινωνός (Rec. συγκ-), όν, partaking jointly of: with genitive of thing(s), Rom.11:17, 1Co.9:23; id. with genitive of person(s), Php.1:7; before ἐν, Rev.1:9.† (AS)

G4792.d: συν-κομίζω (Rec. συγκ-), __1. to bring together, collect (Hdt., Xen., al.). __2. to take up a body for burial (Soph., Aj., 1048): Act.8:2 (see Field, Notes, 116).† (AS)

G4793.d: συν-κρίνω (Rec. συγκ-) __1. to compound, combine: 1Co.2:13, R, mg.1 (Lft., Notes, 180 f.). __2. In Arist. and later writers (Wis.7:29, a1.) = παραβάλλω, to compare: 1Co, l.with, R, txt. (Field, Notes, 168), 2Co.10:12 __3. In LXX, of dreams, to interpret (Gen.40:8, 1Co, l.with, R, mg. 2 (but see reff. supr.).† (AS)

G4794.d: συν-κύπτω (Rec. συγκ-), __1. to bend forwards (Arist., al.). __2. to be bowed down: Luk.13:11.† (AS)

G4795.d: συγκυρία, -ας, ἡ (συγκυρέω, to happen), [in Sm.: 1Ki.6:9 (מִקְרֶה) * ;] (more frequently in late writers, συγκύρησις, -ημα), chance, coincidence: κατὰ σ. (see MM, xxiii), Luk.10:31 (Hippocr., Eccl.).† (AS)

G4796.d: συν-χαίρω (Rec. συγ-), __1. to rejoice with: with dative of person(s), Luk.1:58 15:6, 9, Php.2:17-18, EV; with dative of thing(s), 1Co.12:26 13:6. __2. to congratulate (Æschin., Polyb., al.): Phi, l.with (Lft., in I.; cf. MM, xxiv).† (AS)

G4797.d: συν-χέω (Rec. συγ-), to pour together, commingle, confuse; metaphorically, confound, throw into confusion, stir up trouble: Act.21:27 (cf. συν-χύννω).† (AS)

G4798.d: συν-χράομαι (Rec. συγ-), -ῶμαι, [in Al.: 1Ki.30:19 * ;] to use together with. Metaphorical, with dative of person(s), to associate with: Jhn.4:9 (Polyb., a1.).† (AS)

G4799.d: σύγχυσις, -εως, ἡ (συγχέω), confusion: of a popular uproar, Act.19:29.† (AS)

G4800.d: συν-ζάω (Rec. συζ-), to live with: opposite to συναποθανεῖν, 2Co.7:3; of life in union with Christ, here and hereafter, Rom.6:8, 2Ti.2:11.† (AS)

G4801.d: συν-ζεύγνυμι (Rec. συζ-), to yoke to­gether: metaphorically, of union in wedlock, Mat.19:6, Mrk.10:9.† (AS)

G4802.d: συν-ζητέω (Rec. συζ-), -ῶ, __1. to search or examine together (Plat.). __2. In NT (and π., see MM, xxiii; also in MGr., see Kennedy, Sources, 155), to discuss, dispute: Mrk.1:27 12:28, Luk.24:15; before quæst. indir., Mrk.9:10; with dative of person(s), Mrk.8:11 Act.6:9; before πρός, with accusative of person(s), Mrk.9:14, 16, Act.9:29; id. before quæst. indir., Luk.22:23.† (AS)

G4803.d: συν-ζήτηαις (Rec. συζ-), -εως, ἡ disputation: Act.28:29 (WH, R, txt., om.).† (AS)

G4804.d: συν-ζητητής (Rec. συζ-), -οῦ, ἁ (συνζητέω), a disputer, disputant: 1Co.1:20.† (AS)

G4805.d: σύν-ζυγος (Rec. ουζ-), or as WH, mg., Σύνζυγος, -ον (συνζεύγνυμι), [in Aq., Eze.23:21 * ;] a yoke fellow. Prob., as proper name, Σ. γνήσιε, genuinely Synzygus, S. properly so-called, Php.4:3 (see ICC, Lft., in l; MM, xxiii).† (AS)

G4806.d: συν-ζωο-ποιέω (Rec. συζ-), ῶ-, to make alive or quicken together with; metaphorically, of the spiritual life: τ. Χριστῷ, Eph.2:5; σὺν τ. Χ., Col.2:13.† (AS)

G4807.d: συκάμινος, -ου, ἡ the mulberry tree (Lat. morus; cf. μόρον, 1Ma.6:34 *), the sycamine: Luk.17:6. (In LXX, σ. appears to represent the συκόμορος (see: συκομορέα), but St. Luke distinguishes between the two; see ICC, in l; DB, iv, 634.) † (AS)

G4809.d: συκο-μορέα (Rec. -μωραία, L, -μωρέα), -ας, ἡ, more commonly (so Aq., Sm., Psa.78:47, Isa.9:10) συκόμορος (σῦκον + μόρον, the black mulberry), a fig-mulberry, a sycamore: Luk.19:4 (cf. συκάμινος).† (AS)

G4810.d: σῦκον, -ου, τό a fig: Mat.7:16, Mrk.11:13, Luk.6:44 Jas.3:12.† (AS)

G4811.d: συκοφαντέω, -ῶ (σῦκον, φαίνω), to act the συκοφάντης (on conjectures as to the origin of the term, see LS, see word), to accuse falsely (Aristoph., Xen., al.): Luk.3:14 (R, mg.) Luk.19:8 (RV, exact wrongfully; but cf. Hatch, Essays, 89 ff., see also Field, Notes, 56 f.; MM, xxiv).† (AS)

G4812.d: συλαγωγέω, -ῶ (σύλη, booty + ἄγω), to carry off as spoil, lead captive (θυγατέρα, Heliod., Aeth., 10, 35): metaphorically, Col.2:8.† (AS)

G4813.d: συλάω, -ῶ with accusative of person(s), to strip, plunder, spoil: 2Co.11:8.† (AS)

G4814.d: to talk or converse with another, (New Testament) (ML)

G4817.d: συλ-λογίζομαι __1. to compute. __2. to reason: Luk.20:5.† (AS)

G4818.d: συν-λυπέω (Rec. συλλ-), -ῶ, to make to grieve with (Arist.). Pass., to be moved to grief by sympathy: before ἐπί, with dative, Mrk.3:5.† (AS)

G4819.d: συμ-βαίνω __1. to stand with the feet together. __2. to come together, come to terms. __3. Of events, to come to pass, happen: with dative of person(s), Mrk.10:32, Act.3:10 20:19, 1Co.10:11, 1Pe.4:12, 2Pe.2:22; absol., τὰ σνμβεβηκότα, Luk.24:14 (cf. 1Ma.4:26); with accusative and nf., Act.21:35.† (AS)

G4820.d: συν-βάλλω (Rec. συμ-), to throw together, hence, __(a) of speech (before λόγους, Eur., al.), to discuss, confer (sc. λόγους): with dative of person(s), Luk.11:53, WH, mg., Act.17:18; before πρὸς ἀλλήλους, Act.4:15; __(b) to reflect, consider, ponder: ἐν τ. καρδίᾳ, Luk.2:19; __(with) to meet with, fall in with: Act.20:14; in hostile sense, εἰς πόλεμον, with dative (εἰς μάχην, Polyb.), Luk.14:31;…

G4821.d: συμ-βουλεύω __1. to advise, counsel: with dative of person(s), Jhn.18:14; id. before inf., Rev.3:18. __2. Mid., to take counsel, consult: before ἵνα, Mat.26:4 ("reciprocal middle," see M, Pr., 157); with inf., Act.9:23.† (AS)

G4822.d: συν-βιβάζω (Rec. συμ-), __1. to join or knit together, unite: Eph.4:16, Col.2:2 (but see infr.), Col.2:19. __2. to compare, consider, conclude (Plat.): Act.16:10. __3. to deduce, prove, demonstrate (Arist.): Act.9:22. __4. As in LXX ("translation Greek," = ἐμβιβάζω, metaphorically), to teach, instruct: 1Co.2:16 Act.19:33, R, mg. (also in Vg., Col.2:2, instructi, but see supr.).† (AS)

G4825.d: σύμβουλος, -ου, ὁ (σύν, βουλή), a counsellor, adviser: Rom.11:34 (LXX).† (AS)

G4827.d: συν-μαθητής (Rec. συμμ-), -οῦ, ὁ a fellow-disciple: Jhn.11:16 (on the use of συν- in such compounds as this, see Rutherford, NPhr., 255 f.).† (AS)

G4828.d: συν-μαρτυρέω (Rec. συμμ-), -ῶ, to bear witness with: Rom.2:15; with dative, Rom.8:16; before ὅτι, Rom.9:1.† (AS)

G4829.d: συν-μερίζω (Rec. συμμ-), to distri­bute in shares. Mid., to have a share in: 1Co.9:13 (Diod., al.).† (AS)

G4830.d: συν-μέτοχος (Rec. συμμ-), -ον, partaking together with; as subst., ὁ σ., a joint partaker (with dative of person(s) and genitive of thing(s), FlJ, BJ, i, 24, 6): with genitive of thing(s), Eph.3:6; with genitive of person(s), Eph.5:7 (Arist.).† (AS)

G4831.d: συν-μιμητής (Rec. συμμ-), -οῦ, ὁ a fellow-imitator: with genitive obj., Php.3:17 (see ICC, in l). Not elsewhere.† (AS)

G4832.d: σύμ-μορφος, -ον (σύν, μορφή), __1. absol., similar (Luc.). __2. con­formed to: with dative, Php.3:21; with genitive, Rom.8:29 (see B1., § 36, 11; 37, 6).† (AS)

G4833.d: Pass. to be conformed to , τινι (New Testament) (ML)

G4834.d: συν-παθέω (Rec. συμπ-), -ῶ, to have a fellow feeling for or with, sympathize with or in: with dative of thing(s), Heb.4:15; dative of person(s), Heb.10:34 (Arist., Plut., al.).† (AS)

G4835.d: συμπαθής, -ές (σύν, πάσχω) __1. affected by like feelings, sympathetic: 1Pe.3:8. __2. exciting sympathy (Jb, l.with; Dion. H.).† (AS)

G4836.d: συν-παρα-γίνομαι (Rec. συμπ-), __1. to come up or be present together: before ἐπί, Luk.23:48. __2. to come up to assist (Thuc., al.; 2Ti.4:16, Rec.).† (AS)

G4837.d: συν-παρα-καλέω (Rec. συμπ-), -ῶ, to call upon or exhort together (Plat.). Pass., to be strengthened or comforted with and among: Rom.1:12.† (AS)

G4838.d: συν-παρα-λαμβάνω (Rec. συμπ-), to take along with: as a companion, with accusative, Act.12:25 15:37-38 (on the tenses, see M, Pr., 130), Gal.2:1.† (AS)

G4839.d: συμ-παρα-μένω Rec, for παρα-μένω (which see), Php.1:25.† (AS)

G4840.d: συν-πάρειμι (Rec. σνμπ-), to be present together or with: with dative of person(s), Act.25:24.† (AS)

G4841.d: συν-πάσχω (Rec. συμπ-), [in Al.: 1Ki.22:8 * ;] __1. to suffer together or with: Rom.8:17, 1Co.12:28. __2. to sympathize with (Plat., Arist.).† (AS)

G4842.d: συν-πέμπω (Rec. συμπ-) to send together with: with accusative and dative, 2Co.8:22; id. before μετά, with genitive, 2Co.8:18.† (AS)

G4843.d: συν-περι-λαμβάνω (Rec. συμπ-), __1. to enclose (Eze.5:3 (צוּר) *). __2. to embrace: with accusative of person(s), Act.20:10.† (AS)

G4844.d: συμπόσιον, -ου, τό (συμπίνω), __1. a drinking party __2. By meton., of the party itself, the guests (Plut); pl., σ. σ. (colloq.; see M, Pr., 97), in parties or companies: Mrk.6:39.† (AS)

G4845.d: συν-πληρόω (Rec. συμπ-), -ῶ, __1. to fill up completely (Thuc., of manning ships): of a ship filling with water, and by meton., of those on board, Luk.8:23. __2. to complete, fulfil: of time (Je, l.with, and see MM, xxiv), Luk.9:51, Act.2:1 (on the "durative inf.," see M, Pr., 233).† (AS)

G4846.d: συν-πνίγω (Rec. συμπ-), to choke: of thronging by a crowd, Luk.8:42. Fig., of seed, τ. λόγον, Mat.13:22, Mrk.4:7, 19, Luk.8:14.† (AS)

G4847.d: συν-πολίτης (Rec. σνμπ-), -ου, ὁ a fellow-citizen: pl., σ. τ. ἁγίων, opposite to ξένοι κ. πάροικοι, Eph.2:19 (Eur.; C.I., 6446; condemned by Atticists; see Rutherford, NPhr., 255 f.).† (AS)

G4848.d: συν-πορεύομαι (Rec. σνμπ-), __1. to journey together (Plat., al.): with dative of person(s), Luk.7:11 14:25 24:15. __2. to come together: Mrk.10:1 (Plut., al.).† (AS)

G4849.d: 1. a drinking-party, symposium , (Theognis Elegiacus), etc. 2. the room in which such parties were given, drinking-room , (Lucian) (ML)

G4852.d: σύν φημι (Rec. συμ-), to consent, confess: with dative, before ὅτι, Rom.7:16.† (AS)

G4854.d: σύμ-φυτος, -ον (συμφύω, to make to grow together) __1. congenital, innate (Plat., al.; 3Mac, l.with). __2. grown along with, united with: τ. ὁμοιώματι τ. θανάτου αὐτσῦ (see Field, Notes, 155 f.), Rom.6:5.† (AS)

G4855.d: συν-φύω (Rec. συμ-), to cause to grow together. Pass., to grow together or with (Plat. al.): Luk.8:7.† (AS)

G4856.d: συμ-φωνέω, -ῶ, prop., to agree in sound, be in harmony (Plat., Arist.). Metaphorical, __(a) to agree with, agree together: Luk.5:36; with dative of thing(s), Act.15:15; before περί, Mat.18:19; pass., with dative of person(s), συνεφωνήθη ὑμῖν, Act.5:9; __(b) to agree as to a price (Polyb., Diod.): with dative of person(s), genitive pret., Mat.20:13; before μετά . . . ἐκ, Mat.20:2.† (AS)

G4857.d: συμ-φώνησις, -εως, ἡ (συμφωνέω), concord, agreement: before πρός, with accusative of person(s), 2Co.6:15.† (AS)

G4858.d: συμφωνία, -ας, ἡ (σύμφωνος), __1. symphony, music: Luk.15:25 __2. a musical instrument (Polyb., al.; Da, ll. with; v MM, xxiv).† (AS)

G4860.d: συμ-ψηφίζω to reckon together, count up: Act.19:19.† (AS)

G4861.d: σύν-ψυχος (Rec. συμ-), -ον (ψυχή), of one mind: Php.2:2.† (AS)

G4865.d: συν-αγωνίζομαι to strive together with, to help (prop., of sharing in a contest): with dative of person(s) and of thing(s), Rom.15:30.† (AS)

G4866.d: συν-αθλέω, -ῶ = συναγωνίζομαι: with dative commod., Php.1:27; with dative of person(s), before ἐν, Php.4:3.† (AS)

G4868.d: συν-αίρω to take up together: σ. λόγον (of which there are several exx. in π.; see Deiss., LAE, 118 f.; MM, i, xxiv; M, Pr., 160), to settle accounts, Mat.18:23-24; before μετά, C. genitive of person(s), Mat.25:19.† (AS)

G4869.d: συν-αιχμάλωτος, -ου, ὁ a fellow prisoner (prop., of a captive in war, see Lft., Col., 234): Rom.16:7, Col.4:10, Phm 23.† (AS)

G4874.d: συν-ανα-μίγνυμι (accusative to Bl., 8, -μείγνυμι), to mix up together; pass., reflex, and metaphorically, to associate with (Plut., Ath., al.): 1Co.5:9 5:11, 2Th.3:14 (see M, Th., 117).† (AS)

G4875.d: συν-ανα-παύομαι with dative of person(s), to lie down to rest with, sleep with. Metaphorical, to be refreshed in spirit with: Rom.15:32 (L, om.).† (AS)

G4876.d: συν-αντάω, -ῶ to meet with: with dative of person(s), Luk.9:18, 37 22:10, Act.10:25, Heb.7:1, 10. Metaphorical, of events, to happen, befall (Ding. L., Plut., al.): Act.20:22.† (AS)

G4877.d: συν-άντησις, -εως, ἡ Rec. for ὑπάντησις (which see), Mat.8:34.† (AS)

G4878.d: συν-αντι-λαμβάνομαι to take hold with at the side for assistance; hence, to take a share in, help in bearing, and generally, help (with various constructions, see LXX, ll. with, Deiss., LAE, 83 f.): with dative, Luk.10:40, Rom.8:26.† (AS)

G4879.d: συν-απ-άγω to lead away with or together (Ex, l.with). Pass., metaphorically (as συμπεριφέρομαι, see LS, see word), to be carried away with: with dative, Gal.2:13, 2Pe.3:17; of accommodating one­self to (EV, condescend to) things or persons (on the meaning, see ICC, in I.; Field, Notes, 163), Rom.12:16.† (AS)

G4880.d: συν-απο-θνήσκω to die with or together: Mrk.14:31, 2Co.7:3 (see Meyer, in l), 2Ti.2:11.† (AS)

G4881.d: συν-απ-όλλυμι to destroy with or together. Pass., to perish together (with): with dative of person(s), Heb.11:31.† (AS)

G4882.d: συν-απο-στέλλω to send along with: with accusative, 2Co.12:18 (cf. MM, xxiv).† (AS)

G4883.d: συν-αρμολογέω, -ῶ (ἁρμός, λέγω), = cl. συναρμόζω, to fit or frame together: of the parts of a building, Eph.2:21; of the members of the body, Eph.4:16 (Eccl.).† (AS)

G4884.d: συν-αρπάζω "perfective " of ἁοπάζω (see M, Pr., 113), __(a) to seize and carry away (so most commonly) : Act.27:15; __(b) to seize and hold: Luk.8:29, Act.6:12 19:29.† (AS)

G4885.d: συν-αυξάνω to cause to increase or grow together. Pass., to grow together: Mat.13:30 (Xen., al.).† (AS)

G4886.d: σύν-δεσμος, -ου, ὁ (συνδέω), that which binds together, a bond: of the ligaments of the body, Col.2:19. Metaphorical, σ. ἀδικίας, Act.8:23; τ. τελειότητος, Col.3:14; τ. εἰρήνης, Eph.4:3 (see Lft., Col., ll. with).† (AS)

G4887.d: συν-δέω __(a) to bind together; __(b) to bind together with: pass., Heb.13:3.† (AS)

G4888.d: συν-δοξάζω __1. to join in approving (Arist.). __2. In NT only, to glorify together: pass., Rom.8:17.† (AS)

G4889.d: σύν-δουλος, -ου, ὁ a fellow-servant: Mat.18:28-33 24:49; of servants of the same divine Lord, Col.1:7 4:7, Rev.6:11; so of angels, Rev.19:10 22:9.† (AS)

G4890.d: συνδρομή, -ῆς, ἡ (συντρέχω), concourse, esp. of a riotous gathering: Act.21:30 (Arist., Polyb., al.).† (AS)

G4891.d: συν-εγείρω to raise together: metaphorically, of the Christian's mystical resur­rection with Christ, Eph.2:6; pass., Col.2:12 3:1.† (AS)

G4892.d: συνέδριον, -ου, τό (σύν + ἕδρα, a seat) __1. a council (Plat., Xen., al.; LXX; in π., σ. τ. πρεσβυτέρων, Deiss., BS, 156): of a local Jewish tribunal, Mat.10:17, Mrk.13:9. __2. The supreme ecclesiastical court of the Jews, the Sanhedrin (i.e. Talmudic סַנְהֵדְרִין = συνέδριον): Mat.5:22 26:59, Mrk.14:55 15:1, Luk.22:66, Act.5:21, 27 5:34, 41 6:12, 15 22:30 23:1, 6 23:15, 20 23:28 (WH, R, mg.,…

G4893.d: συν-είδησις, -εως, ἡ (συνεῖδον), __1. consciousness: with genitive obj., Heb.10:2, 1Pe.2:19. __2. In ethical sense, innate discernment, self-judging consciousness, conscience (Stoics and late writers): Rom.2:15 9:1, 1Co.10:29, 2Co.1:12 4:2 5:11, 1Ti.4:2, Heb.9:14; σ. ἀγαθή, Act.23:1, 1Ti.1:5 1:19, 1Pe.3:16 3:21; ἀσθενής, 1Co.8:7 8:10; ἀσθενοῦσα, 1Co.8:12; ἀπρόσκοπος, Act.24:16; καθαρά, 1Ti.3:9,…

G4894.d: συν-εῖδον irreg. aorist of συνοράω (see: εἶδον), __1. to see together or at the same time (Arist., Xen.). __2. to see in one view, hence, of mental vision, to comprehend, understand (LXX, Polyb., Plut., al.) : Act.12:12 14:6 (on the related σύνοιδα, see see word).† (AS)

G4895.d: σύν-ειμι (εἰμί to be), to be with: Luk.9:18 (WH, mg., συνήντησαν), Act.22:11.† (AS)

G4896.d: σύν-ειμι (εἶμι, to go), to come together: Luk.8:4.† (AS)

G4897.d: συν-εισ-έρχομαι to enter together: with dative of person(s), before εἰς, with accusative loc., Jhn.6:22 18:15.† (AS)

G4898.d: συν-έκδημος, -ου, ὁ (ἔκδημος, abroad), a fellow-traveller: Act.19:29, 2Co.8:1.† (AS)

G4899.d: συν-εκ-λεκτός, -ή, -όν chosen together with, co-elect: ἡ ἐν Βαβυλῶνι συνεκλεκτή (on the meaning, see ICC, in l), 1Pe.5:13.† (AS)

G4900.d: συν-ελαύνω to drive together, force together: εἰς εἰρήνην, Act.7:26, Rec. (WH, RV, συνήλλασσεν).† (AS)

G4901.d: συν-επι-μαρτυρέω, -ῶ to join in attesting, bear witness together with: Heb.2:4 (Arist., Polyb., a1.).† (AS)

G4902.d: συν-έπομαι to follow with, accompany: with dative of person(s), Act.20:4.† (AS)

G4903.d: συνεργέω, -ῶ __1. prop., to work together (with): absol., Mrk.16:20, 1Co.16:16, 2Co.6:1; with dative, Jas.2:22; dative commod., Rom.8:28, T, R, txt. (but see infr.). __2. In Hellenistic writers (M, Pr., 65), trans., to cause to work together (cf. ICC, in l): with accusative of thing(s), Rom.8:28 [WH] R, mg. (but see supr.).† (AS)

G4904.d: συνεργός, -όν a fellow-worker: with genitive of person(s), Rom.16:3, 9 16:21, Php.2:25 4:3, 1Th.3:2, Rec., Phm 1 24; θεοῦ (cf. Lft., Notes, 41, 188), 1Co.3:9 (pl.), 1Th.3:2 [WH] R, mg. (R, txt., διάκονον τοῦ θ.; on the original reading, see ICC, in l); τ. χαρᾶς ὑηῶν, 2Co.1:24; τ. ἀληθείᾳ, III Jn 8; before εἰς, 2Co.8:23, Col.4:11.† (AS)

G4905.d: συν-έρχομαι __1. (cl.) to come together, assemble: Mrk.3:20 14:53, T, WH, txt., Act.1:6 2:6 10:27 16:13 19:32 21:22 22:30 28:17, 1Co.14:26; before εἰς, with accusative loc., Act.5:16; ἐπὶ τ. αὐτό, 1Co.11:20 14:23; with dative of person(s), Mrk.14:53, WH, mg., R (πρὸς αὐτόν, see Field, Notes, 40), Jhn.11:33; ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ, 1Co.11:18; ἐνθάδε, Act.25:17; Mrk.6:33, WH, mg. (cf. WH, Intr., 95 ff.);…

G4906.d: συν-εσθίω to eat with one: with dative of person(s), Luk.15:2, Act.10:41 11:3, 1Co.5:11; before μετά, with genitive of person(s), Gal.2:12.† (AS)

G4907.d: σύνεσις, -εως, ἡ (συνίημι), __1. a running or flowing together (Hom.). __2. (a) understanding: Luk.2:47, 1Co.1:19" (LXX), Eph.3:4, Col.1:9 2:2, 2Ti.2:7 __(b) the understanding, the mind or intelligence: Mrk.12:33.† SYN.: see: σοφία (AS)

G4908.d: συνετός, ή, -όν (συνίημι), intelligent, sagacious, understanding: Mat.11:25, Luk.10:21, Act.13:7, 1Co.1:19" (LXX) .† (AS)

G4909.d: συν-ευ-δοκέω, -ῶ to join in approving, consent, agree to or with: absol., Act.22:20; with dative of person(s), Rom.1:32; with dative of thing(s), Luk.11:48, Act.8:1; with inf., 1Co.7:12-13 (chiefly in late writers).† (AS)

G4910.d: συν-ευωχέω, -ῶ to entertain together. Pass., to fare sumptuously or feast together or with: Ju 12; with dative of person(s), 2Pe.2:13 (Arist., Luc., al.).† (AS)

G4911.d: συν-εφ-ίστημι to place over. Pass., __1. to stand over (Thuc.). __2. to rise together: before κατά, with genitive of person(s) (against), Act.16:22.† (AS)

G4912.d: συν-έχω __1. to hold together (τ. συνέχον τ. πάντα, Wis.1:7): of closing the ears, Act.7:57 (τ. στόμα, Isa.52:15); to hem in, press on every side: Luk.8:45 19:43. __2. to hold fast; __(a) of a prisoner, to hold in charge (Luc.; cf. exx. in Deiss., BS, 160; MM, xxiv): Luk.22:63; __(b) to constrain: 2Co.5:14; pass., Luk.12:50, Act.18:5 (τ. λόγῳ; cf. Field, Notes, 128), Php.1:23; in pass., of ills,…

G4913.d: συν-ήδομαι to rejoice together; with dative, to rejoice with or in: τ. νόμῳ τ. θεοῦ, Rom.7:22 (see Lft., Notes, 304).† (AS)

G4914.d: συνήθεια, -ας, ἡ (ἦθος), __1 1 intimacy. __2. habit, custom: Jhn.18:39, 1Co.11:16; with genitive obj. (cf. Æschin., 23, 37, and see MM, xxiv), habitual use, force of habit with respect to, 1Co.8:7.† (AS)

G4915.d: συν-ηλικιώτης (ἡλικία), = συνῆλιζ (Æsch.), one of the same age, an equal in age: Gal.1:14.† (AS)

G4916.d: συν-θάπτω to bury together with: in symbolical sense, of baptism, σὐτῷ (with Christ), Rom.6:4, Col.2:12.† (AS)

G4917.d: συν-θλάω, -ῶ to crush together, crush: Mat.21:44 ([WH], R, mg., om.), Luk.20:18.† (AS)

G4918.d: συν-θλίβω to press together, press on all sides: Mrk.5:24, 31.† (AS)

G4919.d: συν-θρύπτω to break in pieces, crush: metaphorically, τ. καρδίαν, Act.21:13.† (AS)

G4920.d: συν-ίημι and συνίω (see Bl., § 23, 7), __1. to bring or set together. __2. Metaphorical, to perceive, understand: Mat.13:13-15 (LXX), Mat.13:19 15:10, Mrk.4:9 (WH, mg.), Mrk.4:12 7:14 8:17, 21 Luk.8:10, Act.7:25 28:26-27, Rom.15:21" (LXX), 2Co.10:12; with accusative of thing(s), Mat.13:23, 51, Luk.2:50 18:34 24:45; before ὅτι, Mat.16:12 17:13; before quæst. indir., Eph.5:17; ἐπὶ τ. ἄρτοις,…

G4921.d: συν-ίστημι __1. trans., __(a) to commend, recommend: with accusative of person(s), 2Co.3:1 6:4 10:12 10:18; id. with dative, Rom.16:1 (as frequently at the beginning of a letter; Deiss., LAE, 226), 2Co.5:12; before πρός, 2Co.4:2; pass., before ὑπό, 2Co.12:11; __(b) to show, prove, establish: with accusative, Rom.3:5 5:8, 2Co.6:4; dupl. accusative, Gal.2:13; accusative and inf., 2Co.7:11 __2.…

G4922.d: συν-οδεύω to journey with: with dative of person(s), Act.9:7 (Plut., al.).† (AS)

G4923.d: συνοδία, -ας, ἡ __1. a journey in company (Plut., al.). __2. By meton., κ company of travellers, a caravan: Luk.2:44.† (AS)

G4924.d: συν-οικέω, -ῶ to dwell together: of man and wife (Hdt., al.), with dative of person(s), 1Pe.3:7,† (AS)

G4925.d: συν-οίκοδομέω, -ῶ __1. to build together or with (with dative of person(s), 1Esdras, l.with). __2. Of various materials, to build up together (Thuc., al.): metaphorically, of Christians, Eph.2:22.† (AS)

G4926.d: συν-ομιλέω, -ῶ to converse with (absol., FlJ, Bl, v, 13, 1; before μετά, Cebes, 13): with dative of person(s), Act.10:27.† (AS)

G4927.d: συν-ομορέω, -ῶ to border on: with dative, Act.18:7 (Byz.).† (AS)

G4928.d: συν-οχή, -ῆς, ή (συνέχω), __1. a holding or being held together. __2. a narrow place (Hom., al.). Metaphorical, straits, distress: Luk.21:25; καρδίας, 2Co.2:4.† (AS)

G4929.d: συν-τάσσω to prescribe, ordain, arrange: with dative of person(s), Mat.21:6 26:19 27:10" (LXX) .† (AS)

G4930.d: συντέλεια, -ας, ἡ (συντελέω), __1. in cl., a joint payment or contribution for public service; hence, generally, joint action (Plat.). __2. In late writers (Polyb., al.), consummation, completion: σ. τ. αἰῶνος, -ων (cf. Dan LXX TH Dan.12:13, al.), Mat.13:39-40, 49 24:3 28:20, Heb.9:26.† (AS)

G4931.d: συν-τελέω, -ῶ "perfective" of τελέω (cf. M, Pr., 118), __1. to complete, finish, bring to an end: Luk.4:13; pass., Luk.4:2, Jhn.2:3, WH, mg., Act.21:27. __2. to effect, accomplish, bring to fulfilment (cf. MM, xxiv): Mrk.13:4, Rom.9:28, Heb.8:8.† (AS)

G4932.d: συν-τέμνω __1. to cut in pieces. __2. to cut down, cut short: metapb., λόγον, Rom.9:28 (LXX) (Hdt., Plat., Fur., al.).† (AS)

G4933.d: συν-τηρέω, -ῶ "perfective" of τηρέω (see M, Pr., 113, 116), to preserve, keep safe, keep close: with accusative of person(s), Mrk.6:20; with accusative of thing(s), Mat.9:17; ἐν τ. καρδίᾳ, Luk.2:19 (Arist. and later writers; cf. MM, xxiv).† (AS)

G4934.d: συν-τίθημι to place or put together, in various senses. Mid., __(a) to observe, perceive; __(b) to determine, agree, covenant: with inf., Luk.22:5; before τοῦ, with inf., Act.23:20; before ἵνα, Jhn.9:22.† συν-επι-τίθημι, to help in putting on. Mid., to join in attacking (Thuc.): Act.24:9 (RV, joined in the charge).† (AS)

G4935.d: συν-τόμως, adv. (συντέμνω) concisely, briefly: Act.24:4 (for a similar ex., see MM, xxiv).† (AS)

G4936.d: συν-τρέχω to run together or with: before ἐκεῖ, Mrk.6:33; πρόσ, with accusative, Act.3:11; metaphorically, 1Pe.4:4.† (AS)

G4937.d: συν-τρίβω to shatter, break in pieces: Mat.12:20 (LXX), Mrk.5:4 14:3, Jhn.19:36" (LXX), Rev.2:27; of persons and parts of the body, to break, crush, bruise: Luk.9:39; figuratively, Rom.16:20.† (AS)

G4938.d: σύν-τριμμα, -τος, τό (συντρίβω), a fracture (Arist.; Le, l.with, al.). Metaphorical, calamity, destruction (Isa, l.with, Wis.3:3, al.): Rom.3:16" (LXX) .† (AS)

G4939.d: σύν-τροφος, -ου, ὁ (συντρέφομαι, to be brought up together) __1. prop., one nourished or brought up with, a foster-brother: Act.13:1 EV. __2. In Hellenistic usage, as a court term, an intimate friend of a king (see Deiss., BS, 305, 310 f.): Act.13:1 (cf. also MM, xxiv).† (AS)

G4940.d: συν-τυγχάνω to meet with, fall in with: with dative of person(s), Luk.8:19.† (AS)

G4942.d: συν-υπο-κρίνομαι to play a part with, dissemble with: with dative, Gal.2:13 (Polyb.).† (AS)

G4943.d: συν-υπουργέω, -ῶ to help together, join in serving: with dative instr., 2Co.1:11.† (AS)

G4944.d: συν-ωδίνω to be in travail together (Arist.): metapb. (Eur.), Rom.8:22.† (AS)

G4945.d: συνωμοσία, -ας, ή (συνόμνυμι, to conspire), [in Sm.: Eze.22:25 * ;] a conspiracy: Act.23:13.† (AS)

G4946.d: ionic Συρήκουσαι, doric Συράκοσαι, and Σῦράκοσσαι, Syracuse , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

G4948.d: Σύρος, -ου, ὁ, fem. Σύρα a Syrian: Luk.4:27, Mrk.7:26, WH, mg.† (AS)

G4949.d: Συροφοινίκισσα (Rec. -φοίνισσα), -ης, ἡ a Syropænician woman: Mrk.7:26, WH, txt., RV (cf. ἡ Φοινίκη Συρία, Diod., 19, 93).† (AS)

G4950.d: Σύρτις (L, σῦρτις), -εως, accusative -ιν, ἡ, Syrtis, the name of two large sand-banks on the Libyan coast: Act.27:17.† (AS)

G4951.d: σύρω to draw, drag: with accusative of thing(s), Jhn.21:8, Rev.12:4; with accusative of person(s), of taking to trial or punish­ment, Act.8:3; ἔξω τ. πόλεως, Act.14:19; ἐπὶ τ. πολιτάρχας (cf. 4Mac, l.with), Act.17:6 (cf. κατα-ούρω).† (AS)

G4952.d: συ-σπαράσσω to convulse completely: with accusative of person(s), Mrk.9:20, Luk.9:42 (cf. σπαράσσω).† (AS)

G4953.d: σύσ-σημον (T, συν-), -ου, τό (σῆμα), a fixed sign or signal: Mrk.14:44. (Strab., Plut., al.; condemned by Atticists, see Rutherford, NPhr., 492 f.) † (AS)

G4954.d: σύν-σωμος (Rec. συσσ-), -ον (σῶμα), of the same body: Eph.3:6 (Eccl.).† (AS)

G4955.d: στασιαστής (στασιάζω, to stir up sedition, Jdth.7:15, 2Ma.4:30 2Mac 14:6 *) = Att.. στασιώτης, a rebel, revolutionist, one who stirs up sedition: Mrk.15:7 (FlJ, al.).† συ-στασιαστής, -οῦ, ὁ, a fellow-rioter: Mrk.15:7, Rec.† (AS)

G4956.d: συ-στατικός (Tr. συν-), -ή, -όν (συνίστημι), __1. for putting together, constructive. __2. for bringing together, introductory, commendatory: ἐπιστολή (Arist., Diog. L., al.; and see MM, xxiv), 2Co.3:1.† (AS)

G4957.d: συν-σταυρόω (Rec. συσ-), -ῶ, to crucify together with: pass., with dative, Jhn.19:32; id. before σύν, Mat.27:44, Mrk.15:32. Metaphorical, of the mystical death of the Christian with Christ: Rom.6:6, Gal.2:20 (Eccl.).† (AS)

G4958.d: συν-στέλλω (Rec. συσ-), __1. to draw together, contract, shorten: of time, 1Co.7:29. __2. to wrap up: of enshrouding a body for burial (Eur.), with accusative, Act.5:6.† (AS)

G4959.d: συν-στενάζω (Rec. συσ-), to groan together or with: Rom.8:22 (with dative of person(s), Eur., Ion., 935).† (AS)

G4960.d: συν-στοιχέω (Rec. συσ-), -ῶ, to stand in the same rank or line (Polyb). Metaphorical, to correspond to: Gal.4:25 (see Lft., in l).† (AS)

G4961.d: συν-στρατιώτης (Rec. συσ-), -ου, ὁ a fellow-soldier (Plat., Xen., al.). Metaphorical, of fellowship in Christian service: Php.2:25, Phm 2 .† (AS)

G4962.d: συ-στέφω __1. to twist together: with accusative of thing(s), Act.28:3. __2. Pass., of persons, to gather themselves together: Mat.17:22 (WH, R, mg.).† (AS)

G4963.d: συ-στροφή, -ῆς, ἡ (συστρέφω), __1. a twisting together (Plat.). __2. a concourse, a riotous gathering (Polyb.): Act.19:40; σ. ποιεῖσθαι (Am, l.with), to make a compact (RV, banded themselves together): Act.23:12.† (AS)

G4964.d: συν-σχηματιζω (Rec. συσ-), (σχῆμα), to conform to (Arist.). Pass., to be conformed to, conform oneself to: Rom.12:2, 1Pe.1:14.† (AS)

G4965.d: Συχάρ (Ε, Σιχάρ), indecl., ἡ Sychar, a town of Samaria: Jhn.4:5.† (AS)

G4966.d: Συχέμ indecl. (Heb. שְׁכֶם), Shechem; __1. the son of Hamor (Gen.33:19): Act.7:16 b, Rec. __2. A city of Samaria (AV, Sychem; in LXX also sometimes Σίκιμα, -ων, as in FlJ): Act.7:16 a,b.† (AS)

G4967.d: σφαγή, -ῆς, ἡ (σφάζω), slaughter: Act.8:32 (LXX); πρόβατα σφαγῆς, Rom.8:36 (LXX); ἡμέρα σφαγῆς, Jas.5:5.† (AS)

G4968.d: σφάγιον, -ου, τό (σφαγή), a victim for slaughter: Act.7:42 (LXX).† (AS)

G4969.d: σφάζω to slay, slaughter (esp. of victims for sacrifice): ἀρνίον, Rev.5:6, 12 13:8; of persons, 1Jn.3:12, Rev.5:9 6:4, 9 18:24; ἐσφαγμένη εἰς θάνατον (RV, smitten unto death), Rev.13:3 (cf. κατα-σφάζω).† (AS)

G4970.d: σφόδρα adv. (prop. neut. of σφοδρός, excessive, violent) very, very much, exceedingly: with verbs, Mat.17:6, 23 18:31 19:25 26:22 27:54, Act.6:7; with adjectives, Mat.2:10, Mrk.16:4, Luk.18:23, Rev.16:21.† (AS)

Deiss., BS, 238 f.; MM, xxiv; DB, iv, 427a), Rom.15:28; __(b) for concealment, hence, metaphorically, to hide (Da TH Dan.9:24, Jhn.14:17): Rev.10:4 22:10; __(with) for distinction, Rev.7:3-8; metaphorically, Eph.4:30; mid., 2Co.1:22; __(d) for authentication (Est.8:8): Jhn.3:33 6:27 (cf.…

G4973.d: σφραγίς, -ῖδος, ἡ __1. a seal, signet: Rev.7:2. __2. The impression of a seal or signet, a seal (on its various purposes, see: σφραγίζω): on a book or roll, Rev.5:1-2, 5 5:9 6:1, 3 6:5, 7 6:9, 12 8:1; metaphorically, Rom.4:11, 1Co.9:2, 2Ti.2:19, Rev.9:4.† (AS)
